articles.title: Dual Activation and C–N Coupling of CO 2 and N 2 Mediated by Small Fe n + Clusters
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We present a combined experimental and theoretical study on how small iron clusters activate dinitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) under ambient conditions. Mass spectrometry shows these clusters can cleave the N≡N triple bond, producing a range of odd-nitrogen species, with Fe3N7+ and Fe4N7+ appearing as major products. Introducing CO2 into the downstream flow-tube reactor yields distinct FenNmCO+ and FenNmO+ species, indicating that the CO2 also undergoes C═O bond dissociation under this condition. Thermodynamics and kinetics analyses reveal that the formation of Fe3,4N5CO+ proceeds via C–N coupling pathways and generates a stable N2O molecule. The empty d orbitals of Fe atoms facilitate the coordination of N2 and CO2; meanwhile, not only Fen+ but also the Fe3,4N7+ clusters exhibit delocalized electrons and superatomic states. This allows the half-filled superatomic P orbital to engage in superatom–atom bonding with carbon and oxygen atoms, thereby modifying the covalent coordination and active sites for reactions with N2 and CO2. These findings advance mechanistic insight into nitrogen fixation by iron clusters─highlighting the role of electron delocalization─and point to a promising route of plasma-assisted catalytic conversion of atmospheric CO2 and N2 into value-added products under mild conditions.

articles.title: Electrolyte and Catalyst Cooperatively Control Proton Supply in Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electroreduction on CuRu at Positive Potentials
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Above 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, the hydrogen evolution reaction is thermodynamically suppressed, making this potential region attractive for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. However, in neutral and alkaline media typically used for the nitrate reduction reaction, protons for successive hydrogenation steps derive mainly from water dissociation, which becomes increasingly sluggish at more positive potentials. Proton availability thus governs the hydrogenation kinetics of nitrate and its intermediates. Using CuRu nanorods as a model catalyst, we resolve how the electrolyte and the catalyst jointly control the proton supply during NO3RR at positive potentials. Macroelectrode measurements reveal that the NO3– reduction kinetics depend on OH– concentration, and single-particle electrochemistry on a single CuRu nanorod, where ultrafast mass transport avoids local OH– accumulation, assigns this dependence to the bulk. Moreover, in situ scanning electrochemical microscopy shows that bulk OH– governs water dissociation kinetics; capacitance and potential-of-zero-charge measurements trace this to a strengthened, cation-enriched interfacial electric field, which accelerates water dissociation and sustains the proton supply at positive potentials. Building on the electrolyte-enhanced proton supply, Cu incorporation tunes the competitive adsorption between H2O-derived species and NO3– on the CuRu surface, thereby avoiding a proton oversupply that compromises the conversion kinetics. These results provide systematic insight into how bulk OH– concentration and catalyst composition cooperatively modulate proton supply, enhancing nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at HER-free potentials.

articles.title: Facile Maleimide-Hydrazine Reaction to Form Stable Bonds in Dynamic Hydrazone-Cross-Linked Hydrogels
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The hydrazone bond has been extensively used in dynamic hydrogels but is limited in applications where stability is also required. Here, we demonstrate hydrazine cross-linking with both aldehydes and maleimides under physiological conditions (pH = 7.4 and 37 °C), enabling a one-pot reaction to form dynamic hydrazone and stable hydrazinosuccinimide bonds. Using poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and hyaluronic acid (HA) functionalized macromers, hydrogel-forming reactions between maleimide and amine-containing functional groups occurred most rapidly with alkyl-hydrazine through an aza-Michael addition mechanism. Hydrazinosuccinimide cross-links also exhibited enhanced stability compared to alkyl-hydrazone and benzyl-hydrazone cross-links. Lastly, hydrazinosuccinimide cross-linked PEG-HA hydrogels were functionalized with a cell-adhesive peptide via hydrazinosuccinimide, thiosuccinimide, or benzyl-hydrazone bonds, and human mesenchymal stem cell migration depended on the cross-linker structure and dynamicity. This reaction between maleimide and alkyl-hydrazine not only expands the range of accessible properties in dynamic hydrazone-cross-linked hydrogels but also broadens the available reactions maleimide can undergo for numerous biomaterial applications.

articles.title: Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li+-binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7Li/1H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li+ in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10–4 mol·L–1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li+ over Na+ and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na+. These results establish chemically programmed host–guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.

articles.title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

Deciphering Complex Interfacial Dynamics via Operando Microbalance during Potential-Modulated Alkyne Hydrogenation
articles.abstract: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface. The results show that hydrated Na+ promotes cathodic interfacial mass accumulation, forming a cation-bridged microenvironment that enriches alkynol and limits H2 availability. Positive polarization disrupts this microenvironment, promotes product removal, and restores surface hydrogen. Based on these results, we developed an oscillating potential program (100 s at –0.9 V, 20 s at +0.5 V) to control reactant enrichment, product removal, and hydrogen availability, increasing alkenol selectivity from ∼50% to 97% while enhancing activity by 173%.

articles.title: Divergent Reactivity toward Decarboxylative Protonation or Oxidation via Single-Component Organocatalysis
articles.abstract: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.

articles.title: Exploring Liquid Metals as Dynamic Reaction Media
articles.abstract: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements. The transient geometries and electronic properties of liquid atoms within a dynamic matrix increase the possibility to align with various reactants, enabling energy-favorable adsorption patterns and reaction pathways. The catalytic properties of liquid media can be tuned by regulating the dissolved components and/or combining with other functional species. To date, a variety of bond dissociation and formation reactions, centering on C–C, C–H, C–O, C=C, C–N, and C–Cl, have been achieved using liquid metal media. The distinctive catalytic phenomena and the underlying mechanisms associated with liquid metals challenge the conventional understanding of catalysis based on solid-state catalysts. The use of liquid metal media for chemical reactions remains at an early stage, offering great opportunities for future exploration.

articles.title: Hydroxyl-Directed Anchoring and Electronic Structure of Pt–Sn on γ-Al2O3 for Propane Dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3. By hydrothermally tailoring AlOOH precursors and exploiting a topotactic phase transition, three γ-Al2O3 supports (Al2O3-AIP, Al2O3-NP, and Al2O3-NF) with distinct distributions of terminal μ1-OH and doubly bridged μ2-OH sites were prepared. Systematic characterization showed that the hydroxyl-rich Al2O3-NP and Al2O3-NF supports produced substantially smaller Pt–Sn particles than Al2O3-AIP. Spectroscopic trends suggest preferential involvement of acidic μ1-OH sites at lower precursor loadings and progressively greater involvement of μ2-OH sites as the μ1-OH sites approached saturation. The μ2-OH-enriched surfaces favored precursor anchoring associated with highly dispersed Pt–Sn clusters (∼0.6 nm) after reduction. In propane dehydrogenation at 580 °C, the μ2-OH-enriched 0.5Pt–1.3Sn/Al2O3-NF catalyst achieved an initial propane conversion of 60% while maintaining a propylene selectivity above 97%. Site-occupancy experiments and C3H6-DRIFTS further suggest that precursor anchoring involving μ2-OH sites is associated with improved Pt–Sn dispersion and weaker propylene adsorption. These results show that controlling surface hydroxyl types can regulate metal anchoring and particle growth in Al2O3-supported dehydrogenation catalysts.

articles.title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
articles.abstract: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.

articles.title: Spatial Coupling of Metal and Acid Sites via Amorphous Nb–O–Al Interfaces for Selective Polyolefin Hydrocracking
articles.abstract: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking. The catalyst comprises highly dispersed rhodium (Rh) species anchored on an amorphous NbOx-doped γ-Al2O3 support. The amorphous Nb–O–Al interfaces generate electron-deficient Nb centers that function as medium-strong Lewis acid sites, while simultaneously modulating the electronic and coordination environment of the adjacent Rh species responsible for H2 activation. The nanoscale proximity of these complementary sites facilitates the coupling of acid-mediated C–C bond transformation with the subsequent hydrogenation of reactive intermediates. When applied to the hydrocracking of low-density polyethylene under mild conditions (240 °C, 2 MPa H2), the optimized Rh/10Nb–Al catalyst achieves a liquid product space-time yield of 283 gliquid·gmetal–1·h–1 with a methane selectivity of only 0.77%. Quantitative analysis reveals a linear correlation between the density of these interfacial strong Lewis acid sites and the hydrocracking activity, thereby directly linking the catalytic performance to the interfacial structure. This study establishes interfacial engineering as a rational strategy to encode metal–acid intimacy into the catalyst architecture, thereby offering a general design principle for selective plastic-to-fuel conversion.

articles.title: Synergistic Catalysis of Single-Site Rhenium and Ruthenium Nanoclusters for Ammonia Synthesis under Mild Conditions
articles.abstract: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.

articles.title: UV Exposure and Durability of Emerging Photovoltaics: Quantifying and Reporting Outdoor UV Doses
articles.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

articles.title: Air-Stable Nickel Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform for Decoupling Structure–Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving Electrocatalysts
articles.abstract: Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.

articles.title: Bipolar Redox Molecule-Assembled Freestanding Film Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries with Excellent Thermal Adaptivity and Ultralong Life
articles.abstract: Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.

articles.title: Cation-Intercalated Mott Insulator α-RuCl3 Superlattice for Actively Tuned Optoelectronics
articles.abstract: Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by >3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.

articles.title: Controlling Redox Interplay in the Formation of Anisotropic Multimetallic Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.

articles.title: Design of Water-Resistant, Food-Grade Microneedles for Fish Injection and Underwater Cargo Delivery
articles.abstract: Aquatic foods provide around 15% of consumed animal-derived protein worldwide and aquaculture now supplies most of it. But the industry faces significant challenges in disease prevention and excessive use of antimicrobials. Vaccination, particularly for juvenile fish, can mitigate these risks, but manual and automated needle-based vaccination methods are costly, stressful, and labor-intensive. Here, a water-resistant, food-grade microneedle platform is designed to deliver cargos underwater. Silk fibroin-based microneedles are engineered to remain water resistant from minutes to hours in order to penetrate fish skin in wet conditions. To meet the requirements of different underwater applications, three microneedle morphologies─shell, solid-tip, and hollow─are developed, and their different combinations of mechanical integrity, water-resistance performance, cargo compatibility, and release kinetics are studied. The microneedles also preserve the supercoiled conformation of ⩾50% of the loaded pIHNVw-G plasmids─developed to protect fish against infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus─outside the cold chain for 4 weeks under dry conditions. In pilot animal studies, injected microneedles remain attached to zebrafish and juvenile rainbow trout while swimming. Using this food-based microneedle platform, we envision the development of tools for underwater vaccination of juvenile fish that increase aquaculture efficiencies and reduce environmental impact.

articles.title: Early Pathway Selection Precedes Conformational Locking in Protein Self-Assembly
articles.abstract: When early intermediates begin to bias subsequent pathways during protein self-assembly remains difficult to resolve experimentally because early-stage processes are transient and poorly accessible. Here, using regenerated silk fibroin as a model system, we experimentally capture and analyze an early nucleation window in which assembly pathways begin to diverge before conformational locking occurs. By combining controlled electric-field perturbation with multiscale structural characterization and coarse-grained simulations, we identify reproducible nanoscale intermediates that mediate pathway selection. Within this window, electric fields bias early assembly kinetics in a nonmonotonic manner, modulating the formation, elongation, and competition of intermediates rather than directly enforcing structure or orientation. Time-resolved measurements show that subsequent growth proceeds primarily through elongation and fusion of existing intermediates, while β-sheet formation and crystallization emerge only at later stages and serve to stabilize pathways that were biased at earlier stages. Together, we locate the emergence of detectable pathway biasing within the nucleation stage and provide a framework for understanding and guiding protein self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions.

articles.title: Human Urine–Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell Membranes Enable Personalized Transdermal Nanotherapy for Melanoma
articles.abstract: Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.

articles.title: Intracellular Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly of Peptide Nanosheets for Inflammatory Breast Cancer Therapy
articles.abstract: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a highly aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by diffuse, biologically invasive growth and poorly defined tissue boundaries, resulting in a high mortality rate even after multimodal treatment. Here, we report an intracellular polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) strategy that constructs mechanically active peptide nanosheets. Upon 365 nm UV irradiation, the photoinitiator Irgacure 2959 (I2959) initiates intracellular PISA of HisMAm in IBC cells. The corresponding nanosheets prepared in vitro exhibit a thickness of ∼30 nm and a wet-state apparent Young’s modulus of 8.02 ± 0.43 MPa. These nanosheets act through two coordinated materials-cell interactions: (i) increasing cellular viscosity and spatially associating with the actin cytoskeleton, suppressing cell migration and invasion; and (ii) accumulating in the endoplasmic reticulum and eliciting paraptosis-like cell death. In a subcutaneous IBC xenograft model, localized fiber-assisted light activation achieves 72.2% tumor growth inhibition without overt systemic toxicity. Overall, this work establishes intracellular PISA as a spatiotemporally controlled materials strategy for localized IBC treatment.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Integrated Diagnostic Platforms toward Decentralized Infectious Disease Management
articles.abstract: Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.

articles.title: Photodoping-Driven Lattice Expansion Enables Polarization Enhancement in Sliding Ferroelectric MoS2
articles.abstract: Light-matter interactions provide a powerful route to dynamically control ferroelectricity in low-dimensional materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing light-induced polarization remain elusive in sliding ferroelectrics. However, the influence of photodoped carriers on the macroscopic polarization and lattice responses remains largely unexplored. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to demonstrate the microscopic origin of the photostrictive response in rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 under carrier photodoping. The system exhibits a characteristic lattice deformation, including in-plane expansion with the magnitude of 2% under a moderate photodoping density, collectively enhancing electronic hybridization. The coupling gives rise to a substantial interlayer contraction and an increase in out-of-plane spontaneous polarization, accompanied by a softening of the interlayer vibrational mode. These results demonstrate a microscopic, nonthermal pathway for modulating ferroelectric properties and underscore the potential of lattice-engineered polarization control in two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics for advanced optoelectronic and information storage technologies.

articles.title: Recent Advances in De Novo Synthesis of Interfacial Two-Dimensional Polymers
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) integrate the molecular programmability of synthetic polymers with the reduced dimensionality and surface accessibility of atomically thin materials. Realizing their functional potential and establishing reliable structure–property relationships, however, require precise control over lattice topology, crystallinity, orientation, thickness, and defect structure. Interfacial polymerization is particularly suited to this objective because interfaces confine network formation while regulating molecular organization, reactant transport, bond-formation kinetics, nucleation, crystal growth, and defect evolution. This Review summarizes the molecular design principles underlying interfacial 2DP synthesis and compares four major environments according to whether polymerization occurs at a liquid or solid surface: air–liquid, liquid–liquid, solid–liquid, and vapor–solid interfaces. We contrast liquid surfaces, which couple dynamic confinement with transport-regulated molecular reorganization and scalable film growth, with solid surfaces, which provide adsorption, templating, and catalytic control while enabling direct mechanistic investigation at the molecular scale. We further examine how precursor organization, mass transport, crystallization pathways, stacking, and defect evolution collectively determine the structural quality of 2DPs. Particular attention is given to mechanistic insights from advanced characterization methods that directly track nucleation and domain-growth dynamics and resolve grain-boundary and defect structures from molecular to atomic resolution. Emerging electronic and stimuli-responsive devices are discussed to illustrate how framework design, structural quality, and interfacial organization translate into functional performance. Finally, we identify opportunities to advance interfacial polymerization from empirical optimization toward predictive synthesis that bridges local atomic precision with macroscopic structural uniformity.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable Elastomers
articles.abstract: Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young’s modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150–200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.

articles.title: Turning Insulators into Accelerators: Deciphering the Interfacial Ionic Conductivity Boost in Composite Solid-State Electrolytes through Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
articles.abstract: Halide solid-state electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates for all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high oxidative stability and deformability, yet their moderate ionic conductivity remains a bottleneck. While incorporating ionically insulating ZrO2 nanoparticles has been experimentally shown to enhance the ionic conductivity of Li2ZrCl6, the atomistic origin governing this interfacial phenomenon remains unclear. Here, we bridge the spatiotemporal gap in modeling complex heterostructures by developing an accurate machine-learned force field based on the neuroevolution potential, enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 heterostructures. By systematically investigating four representative low-lattice-mismatch ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 interfaces, we identify spontaneous interfacial amorphization driven by space-charge effects upon surface cleavage, trapping Li+ and leading to under-coordinated Li+ polyhedra with pronounced geometric distortion. These distorted amorphous interfacial regions exhibit markedly enhanced Li+ hopping activity, significantly outperforming the bulk lattice, provided that the local mobile Li+ density is not depleted by surface charge redistribution. This work establishes a computational framework for training validated machine-learned force fields for interfaces and provides one plausible origin for the experimentally observed conductivity boost in the insulator-conductor composites, guiding the rational design of electrolytes toward next-generation solid-state batteries.

articles.title: Visualizing Kinetic Control and Thermodynamic Selection in Nanocluster Structural Evolution
articles.abstract: It is extremely challenging to clarify the precise atomic-level evolution of nanoclusters from a dynamically trapped state to a thermodynamically selected product. Various factors play distinctly different roles in the thermodynamic and kinetic control of structural transformation reactions. In this study, we used the system Ag14(SPh)12(DPPH)4 → Ag23(SPh)18(DPPH)4 as a homologous model system, and combined single-crystal structural analysis, time-resolved electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and photoluminescence measurements for correlation analysis. Crystallographic studies revealed that the Ag23 framework could be geometrically decomposed into two substructures related to Ag14, both sharing the metal and thioimine groups, providing a structural basis for the bimolecular fusion hypothesis. Time-dependent spectroscopic techniques revealed the consumption process of Ag14 and the growth process of Ag23, while temperature-dependent experiments showed a kinetic window within which the conversion rate accelerated, but higher thermal input would promote breakage/decomposition and form Ag10. Due to the ability of ESI-MS to generate gas-phase fragments, ions containing Ag5- and Ag9 were regarded as candidate species detected by ESI, rather than confirmed solution intermediates. Therefore, the core breakthrough was not the isolated Ag14 or Ag23 nuclear numbers, but the mechanistic connection of the two structurally similar cluster states in a single reaction network and the identification of thermal activation as the key factor guiding the evolution of the cluster states.

Can Policy Uncertainty Drive the Dollar?
articles.abstract: This article reviews the risk-based literature on international arbitrage deviations, exchange rates, and countries’ borrowing costs. It synthesizes recent work identifying policy uncertainty as a key primitive in risk-based models of global finance and investment. Volatile and unpredictable policy environments alter forward-looking investors’ expectations and portfolio decisions, thereby influencing exchange rates, excess currency returns, and the cost of capital—effects especially pronounced in emerging markets. We discuss how increased global policy uncertainty can create conditions under which a policy risk premium also arises for the US dollar. We present preliminary evidence consistent with this hypothesis.

articles.title: Corporate Boards: New Thinking
articles.abstract: In the face of global challenges, corporate boards may need to think differently. In this review, I explore how the finance literature addresses the challenges boards face. I focus on a key recent challenge: how boards navigate shifting expectations about their objectives beyond shareholder value. I highlight that the literatures on boards’ stakeholder objectives and diversity overlap. This raises interesting, and important, questions about how boards can develop “new thinking” more generally. Much research remains to be done in this area. To rise to the challenge, however, finance academia may also need to think differently. Using data that measure how individual directors think, I illustrate that many factors may influence how directors think, including selection. Recognizing path dependencies in approaches and assumptions may help the field of finance continue to generate influential research on boards.

articles.title: Improving Financial Literacy: From Corporate Finance to Personal Finance
articles.abstract: This article provides an overview of the literature on financial literacy. It covers the initial measurement that created the Big Three financial literacy questions and measures of personal finance knowledge featuring 28 questions. It shows that levels of financial literacy are low and have not been improving over time. This is true not only in the United States but also in countries worldwide. These findings matter because financial literacy is conducive to savvy financial behaviors, from holding precautionary savings to planning for retirement to many other financial decisions. Financial education programs have grown exponentially over time, providing important insights into their cost-effectiveness. Personal finance courses have been added to high school and college curricula, and the evidence indicates that they are useful initiatives to improve financial knowledge and downstream behavior.

articles.title: Investor Beliefs and Expectation Formation
articles.abstract: This article reviews the literature that uses survey data to study expectation formation among investors. We begin by outlining methods for eliciting investor beliefs and summarizing key empirical patterns documented in recent work. Highlighting the persistent cross-sectional heterogeneity in expectations, we then review evidence on the determinants of beliefs, including a new analysis of belief reactions to the tariff announcement in April 2025. Next, we examine how expectations shape financial decision-making, emphasizing the systematic but muted sensitivity of outcomes to belief changes. We conclude by pointing to promising directions for future research on belief measurement, the determinants of expectations, and their implications for policy makers.

articles.title: Option Pricing, Time-Varying Volatility, and Tail Risk
articles.abstract: This article surveys recent developments and important issues in option pricing with a particular focus on time-varying volatility and tail risks. We start by briefly reviewing the most important market events, financial innovations, and theoretical developments from the 1970s to the 1990s and then focus on a more detailed review of the current state of knowledge with a discussion of open questions.

articles.title: Two Tales of Debt
articles.abstract: Recent research suggests that corporate debt contracts in the modern economy follow two common approaches: Some contracts lend against the liquidation value of separable assets, while others focus on cash flows from operations and the going-concern value of the firm as a whole. This article summarizes the key contract features and default resolution mechanisms of these two types of debt used by nonfinancial firms. Firms with abundant liquidation values and physical assets rely on the former; firms with low liquidation values and limited physical assets resort to the latter. Among large firms and those with positive earnings, total borrowing does not depend on physical assets, whereas among small firms and those with negative earnings, total borrowing remains dependent on physical assets. The evidence sheds light on the evolving nature of debt contracting and financial intermediation, with implications for economic fluctuations and growth.

articles.title: Vasomotion of Brain Arteries: Ionic Dynamics Through Systems Physiology in Health and Vascular Disease
articles.abstract: The myogenic tone and thus diameter of brain arterioles varies on multiple time scales. These variations result from coordinated contraction and relaxation of electrically coupled smooth muscle cells in the arteriole wall that drive constriction. A prominent feature is a broad-band ∼0.1 Hz rhythmicity, designated vasomotion, in the pial arterioles spanning the cortical mantle and the penetrating arterioles that nourish the capillary bed. As characterized in the murine brain, vasomotion supports propagating waves with a typical wavelength of 20 mm (a speed of 2 mm/s) that modulate perfusion with a magnitude equal to that of functional hyperemia. The spectral and spatial properties reflect the interaction of smooth muscle dynamics with the underlying neuronal drive. Possible functional roles of vasomotion are to mitigate capillary stalls and to facilitate the exchange of solutes between interstitial and cerebrospinal fluid. Indeed, loss of vasomotion has been implicated in the pathophysiology of vascular disease, such as cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

Cysteine promotes islet α-cell glucagon secretion by limiting oxidative inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels
articles.abstract: Cysteine serves as a robust α-cell secretagogue. While diabetes alters both plasma cysteine and glucagon levels, the mechanisms of α-cell cysteine action remain unclear. Here, we identified cysteine as a key regulator of islet glucagon secretion through redox control of α-cell electrical excitability. Short-term cysteine depletion markedly suppressed hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion from both human and mouse islets. Moreover, cysteine-depleted islets showed reduced hypoglycemia-stimulated α-cell calcium (Ca2+) influx. Islet glucagon secretion and α-cell Ca2+ influx rapidly normalized following cysteine restoration. Cysteine depletion also reduced α-cell voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) conductance and action potential amplitude. Importantly, reducing agents restored NaV currents and glucose control of α-cell Ca2+ handling in islets without cysteine. Together, these findings identify reductive amplification of NaV channels as a key mechanism required for hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion, highlighting cysteine as a critical regulator of α-cell redox state, electrical excitability, and glucagon secretion.

Rethinking lithium content in inorganic solid-state electrolytes
articles.abstract: Inorganic solid-state electrolytes are being developed for safer, energy-dense batteries, yet many contain nearly an order of magnitude more lithium than liquid electrolytes. This perspective proposes low-lithium-content electrolyte design and introduces a lithium-transport realization index connecting local ion motion with long-range conductivity. Evidence across existing materials shows that reduced lithium content does not necessarily sacrifice performance. The resulting design roadmap aims to preserve conductivity with less lithium, potentially easing resource, cost, and environmental burdens.

articles.title: Donor−Acceptor Engineering in Porphyrin-Based Two-Dimensional Polymers for Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Response
articles.abstract: Leveraging their extended π-conjugation, structurally tunable backbones, and superior film-forming processability, two-dimensional (2D) organic polymers have emerged as a highly promising class of materials for third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Herein, a series of porphyrin-based donor−acceptor (D−A) 2D polymer films, namely, TAPP-TAPZ, TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA, are successfully fabricated via a liquid−liquid interfacial polymerization approach. These films exhibit broad absorption profiles across the visible region alongside markedly narrowed optical bandgaps, underscoring the extensive π-electron delocalization inherent to the 2D polymeric frameworks. Femtosecond open-aperture Z-scan measurements conducted at 515 and 800 nm unambiguously reveal pronounced reverse saturable absorption in all samples. Strikingly, the TAPP-TAPZ film delivers exceptional nonlinear absorption coefficients (β) of 8.8 × 103 cm GW−1 at 800 nm and 5.2 × 103 cm GW−1 at 515 nm, values that not only substantially outperform the analogous TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA counterparts but also rival or surpass those of numerous reported covalent organic frameworks, 2D inorganic nanomaterials, and small-molecule NLO systems. Complementary density functional theory calculations ascribe this remarkable performance to the incorporation of benzothiadiazole units, which stabilize a donor−donor−acceptor (D−D−A) electronic configuration and facilitate efficient intramolecular charge transfer. Collectively, our findings establish interfacial polymerization as a robust and generalizable route for constructing ordered, defect-minimized 2D films, thereby offering actionable design principles for the development of next-generation ultrafast photonic devices.

Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples
articles.abstract: Background: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment. Methods: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF. Results: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040). Conclusions: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

Reconstructing ancient ecosystems: guanaco and marine carrion as drivers of predator-prey networks in Southern South America
articles.abstract: Understanding ancient trophic dynamics and human integration in terrestrial high-latitude ecosystems requires moving beyond traditional taxonomic lists to evaluate structural biological interactions. This study presents the first probabilistic, trait-based bipartite network reconstruction of ancient predator-prey assemblages in northern Tierra del Fuego, Southern South America, based on archeological records. By integrating a comprehensive zooarcheological dataset spanning 50 spatial-temporal contexts from the late Pleistocene through the late Holocene across steppe and forest habitats, we model trophic interactions including human subsistence strategies. In this region, dominated by grassy steppes and the forest-steppe ecotone, terrestrial hunter-gatherer societies were embedded in a complex predator-prey network in which the guanaco (Lama guanicoe) played a central role. However, the trophic structure of these interactions and how the introduction of humans as an unprecedented predator affected community-level properties is poorly understood. Our results reveal a significant chronological transformation in network architecture and diet composition. During the late Pleistocene, communities exhibited lower interaction diversity and high specialization centered around megaherbivores and multiple large predators. Following megafaunal extinction and island isolation during the mid-Holocene, the guanaco emerged as an enduring keystone herbivore and dietary anchor, while marine-derived carrion and littoral resources (mollusks and pinnipeds) provided critical energy subsidies. Humans acted as highly plastic generalist consumers, influencing network architecture across diverse habitats. In the steppe, foragers employed broad-spectrum strategies, whereas forest assemblages reflected specialized reliance on coastal resources. Ultimately, this community-level framework demonstrates that despite intense environmental shifts and insularization, the guanaco and marine necromass served as foundational trophic stabilizers, maintaining ecosystem and subsistence resilience over millennia.

articles.title: A Biodegradable Metal–Organic Framework/Oligomer Composite for Sustainable Gold Recovery and Circular Water Management
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is generating unprecedented e-waste streams rich in secondary gold resources, yet sustainable recovery strategies remain scarce. Here, we report a bioderived, environmentally degradable metal–organic framework (MOF)/oligomer composite (SU-102/pGSH) constructed via host–guest self-assembly of glutathione (GSH) within a Zr-ellagate framework. The composite integrates abundant electron-rich functional groups into a robust porous architecture, achieving a remarkable gold uptake capacity of 4385 mg·g–1, the highest reported for MOF-based adsorbents. It also exhibits outstanding selectivity in complex e-waste leachates. Mechanistic investigations reveal synergistic coordination with abundant electron-rich groups, followed by electron-transfer reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). Importantly, the spent adsorbent could degrade into benign mineral phases and natural metabolites with negligible phytotoxicity, ensuring a safe end-of-life pathway. Preliminary techno-economic analysis indicates favorable economic potential for practical implementation. By integrating efficient gold recovery with sustainable material design and end-of-life management, this work provides a viable strategy for circular water treatment.

articles.abstract: Atmospheric isotope serves as an effective source tracer for tracking the pollutants fate. Its precise source apportionment capability is constrained by the comprehensive assessment of isotope fractionation. This study aimed to propose a Computational Quantum Chemistry (CQC)-based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction (AIFP) framework. It can quantify the isotope fractionation mechanisms. This framework utilizes CQC to perform a pipeline for reaction mechanism determination, atmospheric species geometry calculation, and parameter post-processing. It integrates the isotope-substitution method with the fractionation model to establish isotope fractionation standard equations in complex atmospheric chemical systems, providing a theoretical basis for atmospheric isotope tracing. This framework was applied to investigate sulfur (34S) fractionation and sulfate (pSO42–) formation. This application developed a localized 34S fractionation parameter scheme, revealing that pSO42– pollution is driven by NO2 and TMI oxidation. These oxidants account for 58.3 ± 1.0% of its pollution, highlighting the critical role of controlling the transformation conditions of key oxidants in haze pollution mitigation. Our framework extends the atmospheric isotope application, providing a rapid and efficient isotope fractionation prediction framework.
