Enablers and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination implementation among key stakeholders in Ethiopia: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive–inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0). Results Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9–14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps. Conclusions While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia’s HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.

articles.title: Exploration of lymphoproliferative disease virus strains in wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) in Iowa, USA
articles.abstract: by Kelsey C. Smith, David Navarro, Julie A. Blanchong Wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) were nearly extirpated in the early 1900’s and extensive restoration efforts utilizing translocated wild turkeys were employed to restore populations. Although these efforts were successful, populations have again been in decline due to unknown causes. Lymphoproliferative disease virus (LPDV) was first detected in the United States in 2009. The coinciding appearance of LDPV and declining populations have led to studies in several states and provinces in North America to characterize its prevalence and distribution due to concerns about its potential role in population declines. The spread of disease agents is a common outcome during translocation programs and could be related to the spread of LPDV. Prior studies have performed phylogenetic analyses to examine genetic variation across and geographic clustering among strains. In this study we aimed to identify the diversity of LPDV strains present in wild turkeys in Iowa and if there was geographic clustering within the state or with other locations where LPDV has been detected. We sequenced a subset (n = 77) of hunter-harvested samples covering eight of the nine agricultural regions in Iowa that tested PCR positive with the viral gag gene. We performed phylogenetic analysis on 73 unique Iowan strains as well as previously catalogued strains from other regions retrieved from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank database. Overall, Iowa strains did not show geographic clustering within the state or with any other specific geographic regions. Our study demonstrated that there is a high level of genetic diversity among LPDV strains in Iowa and did not provide evidence of connection with a particular location external to Iowa as a source of introduction of LPDV to the state.

articles.title: Female sexual dysfunction in premenopausal women with diabetes mellitus in northern Nigeria: A cross-sectional study from two tertiary hospitals examining associations with glycaemic control and reproductive hormones
articles.abstract: by Fatima M. Damagum, Amina H. Hassan, Andrew E. Uloko, Hauwa A. Habeeb, Hadiza B. Damagum, Zainab A. Umar, Hassan A. Murtala, Zainab Abdulkadir, Ibrahim Y. Ibrahim, Zainab U. Ibrahim, Umar F. Abdullahi, Hamisu M. Salihu, Muktar H. Aliyu, Phylis J. Kanki, Baba M. Musa Background Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18–45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores. Results Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05–7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β −0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β −0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores. Conclusions FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.

articles.title: Frontal alpha asymmetry and instructed satisfaction-rating changes after price presentation: An exploratory pilot study
articles.abstract: This exploratory pilot study asked whether frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) recorded while a price is displayed varies with the satisfaction-rating change a consumer then makes. Twenty-one participants completed two blocks of 30 trials: view a product, give a pre-price rating (1–9), see the price, give a post-price rating, which they were instructed to change except at the scale limits. The change is described by its direction and magnitude (|Δ|, provisionally labeled Decision Momentum), two descriptions of one difference score. FAA was computed from relative alpha power at F3/F4 over 0–3 s after price onset on average-referenced data. Inference rests on 19 participants and 820 trials. The primary pooled test of the direction × magnitude interaction was inconclusive (β=−0.051, 95% CI [−0.111,0.009], p = 0.093). An exploratory block-stratified analysis found an interaction in the first block (β=−0.087, 95% CI [−0.152,−0.021], p = 0.010), although neither of its two component slopes differed clearly from zero. Support varied across specifications, and five alternative operationalizations of FAA did not reproduce it. The same model applied to the window before price onset, where the predictors cannot yet reflect the price, produced an interaction of comparable or larger size pooled and in the second block. In the first block, the direct comparison did not establish a difference between windows, and adjusting for pre-price FAA left the first-block estimate unchanged (p = 0.008); in the second block, the two windows did differ (p = 0.021), the association being present before the price and not after it. Single-trial classification of change direction showed modest performance with uncertain generalizability (ROC AUC 0.538; participant bootstrap 95% CI [0.476, 0.564]). The association is reported as hypothesis-generating; attributing it specifically to price-related processing is not supported by these data.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in exacerbating pulmonary fibrosis
articles.abstract: Background 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach. Methods IPF-related genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis combining differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate targets were obtained by intersecting IPF-associated genes with predicted 5-HMF targets. Functional enrichment analysis, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP interpretation were performed to prioritize candidate targets, while molecular docking was used to explore potential 5-HMF–target interactions. A bleomycin-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was further used to evaluate the effects of 5-HMF on fibrotic lung injury and the transcriptional expression of prioritized candidate genes. Results A total of 1,776 IPF-associated genes and 143 predicted 5-HMF targets were identified, yielding 12 overlapping candidate targets. Enrichment analysis implicated these genes in fibrosis-related pathways, including chemical carcinogenesis–receptor activation and estrogen signaling. Machine learning analysis prioritized seven core targets (CA2, CA4, ESR2, F10, HSP90AA1, PLA2G1B, and PTPRB), all of which accommodated 5-HMF in their orthosteric pockets in blind docking, albeit with weak, non-selective Vina scores (−4.5 to −5.4 kcal/mol). In vivo, 5-HMF significantly exacerbated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, as demonstrated by aggravated lung injury, increased collagen deposition, and elevated expression of Hsp90aa1, Pla2g1b, Ca4, F10, Acta2, and Col1a1. Conclusion Our findings suggest that 5-HMF may exacerbate fibrotic lung injury through multiple fibrosis-related molecular targets and pathways. These findings provide preliminary evidence for a potential association between 5-HMF exposure and the aggravation of pulmonary fibrosis, while further studies are required to determine whether 5-HMF can independently initiate fibrotic pathology.

articles.title: Knowledge and experiences of overdose among formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background Drug overdose is a leading cause of death among people released from correctional facilities, and the risk of overdose is higher among people living with HIV (PLWH). Overdose remains understudied in people in South Africa despite the high burden of HIV and hazardous opioid use. The researchers aimed to qualitatively explore how formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and OUD in South Africa understand, experience, and respond to overdose. Methods People with HIV and self-reported hazardous opioid use prior to correctional facility release or shortly after release were enrolled in a convenience sample. Twenty-three formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and opioid use in or around Tshwane, South Africa completed sequential in-depth interviews that explored medication-assisted treatment for hazardous opioid use and HIV care delivery. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using both deductive and inductive coding, with a focus on participants’ knowledge and definition of overdose, personal experiences with overdose, and responses to overdose. Results All participants used the term “overdose”, but there was no unified understanding of what constitutes an overdose or how to manage an overdose. The period immediately following release from incarceration was identified as a key moment in which overdose occurred. Pouring water onto the person overdosing was reported to be the most prevalent response strategy. Only two participants contacted or watched their peers contact the ambulance. Fear of law enforcement involvement was perceived as a barrier to calling for emergency services. Conclusion The findings identify a gap in overdose knowledge among corrections-involved people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa. There is a need to increase knowledge regarding overdose recognition and responses.

articles.title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study.Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. Conclusion In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

articles.title: Perceived quality teaching and student retention intention: The serial mediation of knowledge, skills, competencies, and student loyalty
articles.abstract: Student retention intention remains a concern for higher education systems worldwide and is relevant to institutional sustainability and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Human Capital Theory (HCT) and Expectancy–Value Theory (EVT), this study examines the direct and indirect associations between perceived quality teaching and student retention intention through students’ self-reported knowledge, skills, competencies and student loyalty. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 395 final-year students across Pakistani universities using a multistage sampling approach, with institutions selected through stratified random sampling and participants recruited via convenience sampling. The proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that perceived quality teaching is positively associated with student retention intention, both directly and indirectly through students’ knowledge, skills, and competencies and student loyalty. Significant indirect associations were identified through each mediator separately and through the proposed serial mediation pathway. These findings highlight the relevance of considering students’ perceived capability development and institutional attachment together when examining retention intention. HCT provides a rationale for the relationship between perceived teaching quality and students’ knowledge, skills, competencies, while EVT offers an interpretive perspective; however, expectancy of success and subjective task value were not directly measured. The cross-sectional design also precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. Practically, the findings suggest that faculty development, student-centered pedagogies, digitally supported teaching, and curriculum alignment with labor market needs merit consideration in institutional quality assurance. The findings provide context-specific evidence from Pakistani higher education (HE) and are relevant to SDG 4 through their focus on perceived teaching quality and students’ intentions to continue their studies. They do not establish effects on actual retention or broader educational outcomes.

articles.title: Perceptions of psychiatrists toward long-acting injectable antipsychotics: A cross-sectional survey from Fujian, China
articles.abstract: Objective This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and willingness of psychiatrists to promote long-acting injectable antipsychotics (LAIs) in Fujian Province, China, and to identify the influencing factors. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted using convenience sampling among psychiatrists attending a provincial conference. An 18-item online questionnaire was distributed via Wenjuanxing. Descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman’s rank correlation were used. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple correlations Results A total of 222 psychiatrists completed the survey, with 90 respondents (40.5%) identifying as female. The largest age group was 30–39 years (46.9%). Most participants (51.4%) had > 10 years of clinical experience, and 65 (29.3%) held senior professional titles. Most participants reported adequate knowledge of LAIs (96.4%), recognized their therapeutic value (80.2%) and favorable application prospects (87.8%), and expressed a willingness to promote LAIs (82.4%).High cost was identified as the primary barrier to clinical use (90.5%) and the most critical factor for wider adoption (88.3%). Psychiatrists with more clinical experience (>10 years) held significantly more positive attitudes regarding overall therapeutic value, willingness to promote LAIs, and support for early application (all P q q < 0.01) after FDR correction. Conclusion Psychiatrists in Fujian Province demonstrated adequate knowledge and generally positive attitudes toward LAIs. Psychiatrists’ willingness to promote LAIs was associated with knowledge level and clinical experience, but reducing the cost of drug patents may contribute to improving the prescription rates. Future efforts should focus on systematic training, academic communication, positive prescribing experiences, and policy coordination to overcome cost and stigma barriers.

articles.title: Performance analysis of MIMO-assisted HPMA networks over keyhole effect
articles.abstract: As an innovative multiple access technology, hybrid power-frequency multiple access (HPMA) effectively supports massive connectivity while eliminating the decoding complexity associated with successive interference cancellation (SIC). Concurrently, although the keyhole effect represents a critical propagation degradation that drastically reduces diversity gains in wireless channels, its impact on advanced multiple-access techniques remains largely explored. Driven by these considerations, this paper investigates a comprehensive performance evaluation of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-assisted HPMA framework deployed over keyhole Nakagami-m fading environments. Specifically, exact closed-form formulations of outage probability (OP), ergodic capacity (EC), and average bit error rate (ABER) are derived, supplemented by high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) asymptotic expansions to yield deeper engineering insights. Monte Carlo simulations verify the exactness of the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the resilience of the proposed HPMA system under realistic keyhole fading scenarios. Our findings reveal that HPMA maintains high performance under severe keyhole conditions, attaining substantial performance superiorities over standard non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), particularly regarding outage behavior and error rates. Finally, this study highlights HPMA as a promising, low-complexity, and resource-efficient radio access technology for next-generation wireless communications subjected to keyhole propagation constraints.

articles.title: Pre-service mathematics teachers’ integration of design thinking in STEM lesson plans: Insights from a qualitative case study
articles.abstract: by Rüveyda Karaman Dündar Mathematics is foundational in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. Mathematics can foster problem-solving, quantitative reasoning, modeling, and creativity across disciplines. This study explores how pre-service mathematics teachers (PMTs) in a Design Thinking (DT)-focused course integrate DT into STEM lesson planning, the factors influencing this integration, and the challenges encountered during lesson planning. 55 senior PMTs at a state university in Türkiye participated in the study. Data were collected through DT-oriented, mathematics-focused STEM lesson plans and an open-ended questionnaire and were analyzed using content analysis. Findings reveal that while many PMTs maintained mathematics as a core component in their plans, the integration of DT was often partial and unbalanced. The Define, Ideate, and Prototype phases were predominant across most plans (>80%), whereas the Empathy phase was considerably less represented, appearing in only 20.8% of plans. In contrast, while the Test phase was incorporated into more than half of the lesson plans (54.2%), its presence remained substantially lower than that of the initial construction phases, reflecting a tendency toward linear product completion rather than sustained, iterative design optimization. Participants reported difficulties aligning DT phases with learning objectives, selecting appropriate materials, and designing effective assessment strategies. Despite these challenges, PMTs strongly believed in DT’s potential to enhance student engagement, creativity, and real-world mathematical thinking. The study underscores the need for teacher education programs to provide more explicit scaffolding and practical tools to meaningfully embed all phases of DT within mathematics instruction.

articles.title: Prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension in South Asians: Evidence from a national survey of Sri Lanka
articles.abstract: Background Blood pressure(BP) control remains suboptimal worldwide. Sex-related disparities in hypertension have been reported, but data from South Asia are limited. Understanding the epidemiology and sex-related differences is essential to improve BP control. Objectives To assess the prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension among Sri Lankans. Methods We analysed secondary data from the Sri Lanka STEPS Survey 2021, a nationally representative, community-based, cross-sectional study. Hypertension was defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive use; controlled BP as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Prevalences, associations, and sex-related disparities in hypertension, undiagnosed hypertension, and BP control were assessed using logistic regression. Results Data from 4,634 adults(mean age 43.5(weighted CI 43.0–44.1) years; female 54.8 (53.1–56.5)%) were analysed. Overall, 37.2(35.5–38.9)% had hypertension, of whom 60.0(58.1–63.4) % were previously undiagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 73.6 (73.6, 69.6–77.2)% were on treatment, but only 38.0(33.0–44.20)% achieved BP targets. The rates of hypertension prevalence (p = 0.600), treated hypertension (p = 0.398), and controlled blood pressure (p = 0.819) in females and males did not differ significantly by sex. However, undiagnosed hypertension was significantly higher in males (69.4%, 65.3–73.1) than in females (53.6%, 50.1–57.0) (p < 0.001). Differences in the associations of hypertension by sex were noted; diabetes was associated only in females (p < 0.001), while wealth quintile (p < 0.001) and 24-hour urinary salt excretion (p = 0.011) were associated only in males. Overweight/obesity was shown to have a significant association with undiagnosed hypertension only in males (p = 0.017) in stratified analyses. Conclusions More than half of the hypertensives in this South Asian population were previously undiagnosed. Of hypertensives, ¾ were treated, but only 1/3 achieved treatment goals. Prevalence, treatment and control rates of hypertension were not different between females and males, but undiagnosed hypertension was more common in men. Therefore, the emphasis should be on improving the detection of hypertension, especially in men, and on treating to targets in both sexes.

articles.title: Prognostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in glioma: A meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) for the prognosis of glioma patients. Methods PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases were searched to collect literature on the relationship between SIRI and glioma prognosis from database inception to July 2026. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). STATA 15.0 and Review Manager 5.4 software were used, and random-effects models were employed with pooled hazard ratios (HR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the prognostic value of SIRI. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed. Results Eight retrospective cohort studies involving 1778 glioma patients were included, forming 12 comparison groups for OS analysis and 4 comparison groups for PFS analysis. Meta-analysis results showed that a higher SIRI was significantly associated with poorer OS (pooled HR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.34–2.38, P < 0.0001) and PFS (pooled HR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.18–1.81, P = 0.0005) in glioma patients. Subgroup analysis showed that the prognostic value of SIRI for OS was not significant in the European population subgroup, suggesting that the association may be modulated by geographic region. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the results. Egger’s test indicated publication bias in the OS analysis (P = 0.0001), but no significant bias was found in the PFS analysis. Conclusion This meta-analysis suggests that elevated SIRI is associated with poorer OS and PFS in glioma patients, although this association was not consistently observed across all subgroups, particularly in European populations. These findings highlight the need for further validation with standardized cut-off values in diverse populations.

articles.title: Retraction: In Silico identification of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitory peptides from MRJP1
Retraction: Insights into the progressive impact of high-fat-diet induced insulin resistance on skeletal muscle and myocardium: A comprehensive study on C57BL6 mice
Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship
articles.abstract: by Oxana Y. Naumova, Pavel V. Dobrynin, Griffin Litwin, Sergey Y. Rychkov, Michael P. Milham, Elena L. Grigorenko Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6–16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

articles.title: Surrogate-assisted multi-objective topology optimization design method for prefabricated large-span Suspen-Dome based on structural-mapping-method and improved-PGSA
articles.abstract: Existing optimization studies on large-span Suspen-Dome structures have mainly focused on either size optimization of the upper reticulated shell or topology optimization of the lower cable-strut system. Such a separated strategy prevents the integrated optimization of the whole structure, restricts the design space, and limits further improvement in structural performance. This study investigates the integrated optimization of prefabricated large-span Suspen-Dome structures by simultaneously considering the size, geometric configuration, and topology of the upper reticulated shell, together with the topology and cable forces of the lower cable-strut system. To ensure practical applicability, the design variables are classified into topological and size variables. The former define the structural configuration and connectivity, while the latter determine material-related properties. The optimization aims to maximize stiffness and minimize weight, subject to member slenderness, material strength, local stability, and overall structural stability constraints. An Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)-based candidate screening model is introduced to accelerate the optimization algorithm and reduce unnecessary ANSYS analyses. A partial full-stress design (PFSD) concept is proposed, in which the reticulated shell serves as a structural safety reserve. The proposed structural mapping method-improved plant growth algorithm (SMM-iPGSA) is validated through two examples. Results show that the optimized structures exhibit improved stability, more uniform stress distribution, and displacements well below the allowable limits.

articles.title: Testing the theory of planned behavior in predicting evacuation intentions during storms
articles.abstract: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely applied to predict human behavior across diverse domains; however, its application in disaster contexts remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the utility of TPB in predicting intentions to prepare evacuation plans in hurricane-prone areas. Using a quantitative approach, an online survey was administered to adults residing in Florida, yielding 816 valid responses. Attitude toward evacuation planning, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control were measured using validated Likert-scale items. Data were analyzed using Spearman’s correlation and binary logistic regression. Results indicate that all TPB constructs were significantly associated with evacuation planning intentions. Subjective norms emerged as the strongest predictor, highlighting the critical role of social influence in preparedness decisions. Attitude toward evacuation planning and perceived behavioral control also demonstrated significant positive effects, suggesting that favorable evaluations of evacuation planning and confidence in one’s ability to prepare increase preparedness intentions. The logistic regression model showed strong predictive power (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.62). These findings support the applicability of TPB in disaster preparedness research and underscore the importance of integrating social norms, perceived behavioral control, and attitude-based interventions into emergency management strategies.

articles.title: Two teams take different routes to resolve atomic collisions
articles.abstract: A tiny levitating bead records the kicks delivered by impacts from individual gas atoms. Its jitters could become the basis for precision measurements—and searches for dark matter.

articles.title: Filler and interface engineering of composite solid electrolytes: critical advances from fundamental design to practical application
Burnham urged to save England’s “doomed to fail” obesity plan

articles.abstract: Sounds Fe-nomenalNot quite. articles.title: Multisensing photoreceptors: a cross-kingdom perspective
articles.abstract: Photoreceptors are classically depicted as monochromatic switches governed strictly by light. However, emerging biophysical and structural insights reveal that these proteins act as dynamic, multisensory hubs across kingdoms of life. Drawing primarily on plant and fungal systems, where mechanisms are most extensively characterized, this review synthesizes how photoreceptors integrate ambient temperature and cellular oxidative state alongside photon flux, with cross-kingdom examples extending this framework to bacteria. Thermal energy modulates dark reversion rates, quaternary assembly, and photobody phase separation, whereas reactive oxygen species alter the photocycle and trigger structural shifts through direct redox sensing. Under a ‘stress-first’ evolutionary model, ancestral stress-sensing scaffolds could be retrofitted with chromophores via exaptation, providing a unified biophysical rationale for how cells decode complex, fluctuating environments.

articles.title: Lessons from the UN Decade: from ecosystem restoration to regenerative transformation
articles.abstract: Although restoration science increasingly considers social–ecological complexity, many restoration projects still fall short of their ecological or social goals. We argue that such failures often stem from a lack of attention to long-term social–ecological dynamics within the target system. To overcome this problem, we propose ‘regenerative transformation’ as a new paradigm to guide ecosystem restoration. Regenerative transformation foregrounds the thriving of human and other forms of life and emphasizes healthy endogenous social–ecological dynamics rather than exogenous interventions. Facilitating regenerative transformation through restoration will require changes in how restoration is conceptualized, practiced, and governed—moving from a focus on abstract targets and simple outcome indicators toward developing supportive conditions for the long-term, equitable coevolution of healthy social–ecological dynamics.

articles.title: A Chromosome Scale Genome Assembly for the Australian blue mussel Mytilus planulatus
articles.abstract: Mussels belonging to the genus Mytilus are among the world's most ecologically and economically important bivalve molluscs. Although the genus most likely originated in the Northern Hemisphere, the evolutionary history of Southern Hemisphere lineages, including the timing and number of colonisation events leading to the extant Australian populations, remains debated. Limited genomic resources have hindered the reconstruction of these evolutionary histories. In Australia, distinguishing native Mytilus planulatus from invasive Mytilus galloprovincialis is critical for biosecurity and conservation, but previous molecular approaches lacked sufficient resolution to resolve species boundaries and hybridisation patterns. Here, we present the first chromosome-scale reference genome for M. planulatus. The assembly consists of 14 chromosomes and over 51,000 annotated protein-coding genes per haplotype. Comparative analysis revealed extensive structural variation and widespread hemizygosity despite a largely conserved chromosomal organisation relative to M. galloprovincialis. Population analyses using SNPs and gene presence-absence variation in resequenced individuals confirmed previously inferred patterns of population structure and establish this reference genome as a valuable resource for future studies of genome evolution, adaptation and population genomics in Mytilus. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Recovery and Resilience Plan, EU, 2022ZRZBZ7, P2022JEEMT Australian Research Council, DP220101063

articles.title: A RecBCD-like enzyme regulates expression of bacterial defense operons in response to DNA damage
articles.abstract: Bacteria must quickly respond to stress signals including bacteriophage (phage) infection, invasion by mobile genetic elements, and other threats. DNA damage is a stress-signaling nexus in bacteria, initiating global responses such as the SOS response and triggering expression of specific defense and immune pathways through DNA damage-sensing transcriptional regulators. Here we identify a three-protein pathway termed Cerberus that senses dsDNA ends that become available during DNA damage or inhibition of the key DNA repair complex RecBCD, and controls expression of an associated defense/immune operon. The central player in Cerberus is a large peptidase-helicase-nuclease fusion protein, CerC, that is architecturally similar to the RecBC complex itself. Upon DNA damage or RecBCD inhibition, CerC binds and unwinds free DNA ends to allosterically activate its fused HExxH metallopeptidase domain. CerC specifically cleaves the adjacently encoded anti-sigma factor CerB to release its cognate sigma factor CerA, allowing CerA to mediate transcription of a defense/immune operon encoded nearby. Cerberus therefore represents a pathway that has co-opted a key DNA repair machine for DNA damage sensing, and linked that activity to transcriptional control through anti-sigma factor cleavage.

articles.title: A minimal two-residue C-terminal truncation of AID in adult-onset hyper-IgM syndrome type 2 (HIGM2)
articles.abstract: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), encoded by AICDA, facilitates class-switch recombination (CSR) and somatic hypermutation (SHM) in activated B cells. Loss of AID function causes hyper-IgM syndrome type 2 (HIGM2). While typically autosomal recessive, three C-terminal truncation variants have been reported to act in autosomal dominant manner. We describe a novel heterozygous AICDA nonsense variant, c.589G>T (p.G197*), that truncates the final two C-terminal residues of AID and results in adult-onset HIGM2. Single-cell sequencing of primary patient B cells revealed a complete block in CSR and a [~]10-fold reduction in SHM. AICDA mRNA expression was balanced between wild-type and variant alleles, yet AID protein abundance was reduced to [~]56% with normal subcellular localization. Remarkably, inducible germinal center (iGB) cultures restored CSR in purified naive patient B cells. CRISPR-Cas9 editing of healthy donor B cells confirmed that the iGB platform can rescue B cells harboring heterozygous, but not homozygous, AICDA variants. These results demonstrate that even a two-amino-acid truncation at the AID C-terminus is sufficient to disrupt its function and cause HIGM2.

articles.title: A multi-tissue RNA-seq atlas of adult medaka (Oryzias latipes) under salinity and winter-summer sampling contrasts
articles.abstract: Medaka (Oryzias latipes) is a euryhaline and eurythermal teleost widely used in genetics and environmental biology. We generated an RNA-sequencing atlas of 11 adult tissues (brain, eye, gill, heart, intestine, kidney, liver, muscle, spleen, ovary, testis) of the strain d-rR/TOKYO, sampled under two independent environmental contrasts: salinity (freshwater versus seawater) and season (winter versus summer). The freshwater and summer groups, reared indoors and outdoors under long days, provide a third contrast between laboratory and outdoor rearing. Typically, one male and one female were sampled per condition, with ten tissues taken from each individual. Ninety libraries were quantified against the medaka RefSeq transcript set (GCF_053564925.1). The resource comprises gene-level TPM and count matrices, differential expression tables for each tissue and contrast, tissue-specificity indices, human ortholog annotations, sample metadata, and a self-contained interactive browser. Because replication is limited and each condition was sampled on its own date, the differential expression tables are intended for hypothesis generation. The dataset supports studies of gene-expression plasticity and comparisons between medaka and humans.

articles.title: A multidimensional benchmark of confounder-aware differential abundance strategies for single- and multi-cohort microbiome studies
articles.abstract: Confounding is a pervasive challenge in microbiome differential abundance analysis (DAA), yet systematic benchmarks of confounder-aware DAA remain lacking. Existing benchmarks have also largely evaluated statistical methods or analytical components in isolation rather than the complete analytical strategies used in practice. We evaluated 71 single-cohort strategies spanning default and extended input configurations using 2,500 real-data-informed simulations, reference-based recovery of established biological signals and resampling-based within-dataset consistency; benchmark-prioritized strategies were further assessed for stability under systematic perturbations. We further evaluated 63 multi-cohort extensions using simulations with cohort heterogeneity and empirical datasets. Covariate adjustment improved false-discovery control at the cost of reduced sensitivity, while performance also depended strongly on the specific combination of preprocessing procedure and statistical model. Different strategies were favored across benchmark dimensions and analytical objectives. ANCOM-BC2_CSS and edgeR_CSS were favored for high-confidence, perturbation-stable inference, whereas ANCOM-BC2_count and ANCOM-BC2_TMM provided more balanced performance. In multi-cohort settings, mega-analysis provided the strongest overall balance when individual-level data were available: ANCOM-BC2_CSS_Mega and edgeR_CSS_Mega showed stronger accuracy performance, whereas ANCOM-BC2_TMM_Mega and ANCOM-BC2_count_Mega showed greater cross-cohort consistency. We implemented these findings in xConDA, an interactive web server linking analytical objectives and study designs to benchmark-prioritized, confounder-adjusted microbiome DAA workflows.

articles.title: A single-cell multimodal foundation model enables cross modality analysis between transcriptome and chromatin
articles.abstract: Most single-cell studies measure either gene expression or chromatin accessibility, and connecting the two usually requires fitting a model to each study. Here we present MUTUAL (MUltiome Transfer in a Unified Aligned Latent space), which keeps the single-cell foundation models scFoundation and EpiAgent frozen, combines their embeddings with linear summaries of each modality and learns a shared RNA--ATAC space from 3.0 million paired cells of 400 public multiome datasets. Applied without refitting to ten datasets not used for training, MUTUAL matched cells' RNA and ATAC profiles more accurately than methods fitted on other donors of the same dataset, annotated ATAC-only cells more accurately and transferred transcription-factor motif activity to RNA-only cells beyond what cell-type assignment provides. In a maturation series of stem-cell-derived islets, motif activity predicted from RNA largely reproduced the measured stage-wise changes when other libraries of the series served as the reference. MUTUAL makes public multiome data directly usable by single-modality studies.

articles.title: APR-246 and DNA polymerase theta inhibitor Novobiocinsynergize to eliminate TP53 mutant AML cells
articles.abstract: Patients with TP53-mutant myelodysplasic syndromes (MDS) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are usually elderly and frail with highly resistant malignant clones and a median survival of less than one year. The molecule APR-246 targets mutant p53 but also perturbs redox homeostasis. APR-246 showed favorable safety in a phase 3 trial in TP53 mutant MDS/AML but did not meet efficacy endpoints in combination with azacitidine (AZA), highlighting the need for more effective combination strategies. Conversion of APR-246 to the active compound MQ releases formaldehyde which generates DNA-protein crosslinks. AML cells depend on DNA polymerase theta (PolƟ) to repair such lesions and PolƟ protects cells from ferroptosis. Using a panel of isogenic MOLM13 AML cell lines each carrying a common TP53 variant, we show that the PolƟ inhibitor Novobiocin (NVB) synergizes with APR-246 to induce AML cell death. We demonstrate strong synergy with this combination in all TP53 mutant cell lines and to a lesser extent in the TP53 wildtype and null cells, indicating both p53-dependent and p53-independent mechanisms behind the synergy. APR-246 provides selectivity for TP53-mutated cells while NVB enhances p53-independent apoptosis and p53-dependent ferroptosis. Levels of ferroptosis induction correlate with the observed synergy in TP53-mutant and WT cells. Combination of APR-246 and NVB induces potent in vitro growth inhibition of primary TP53-mutated AML/CMML patient samples, with significant activity achieved at low micromolar or nanomolar concentrations of APR-246. Our findings hold promise for combination of APR-246 and NVB as a new therapeutic strategy tailored for TP53-mutated AML patients with high efficacy and low toxicity. ### Competing Interest Statement KGW is co-founder and shareholder of Aprea Therapeutics, a company that develops novel cancer therapy by targeting the DNA damage response pathway or mutant p53. KGW has previously received salary and research funding from Aprea Therapeutics. KGW is board member and shareholder of the company MyCural Therapeutics that develops novel cancer therapy by targeting the Myc protein. MMP is advisory board member for AstraZeneca, GSK and SOBI. The other authors declare no conflicts of interest. articles.title: Age-based shifts in multicellular community organization and abundance in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Cancer
articles.abstract: Aging represents a fundamental driver of cancer risk and progression, yet the mechanisms by which aging reshapes the tumor microenvironment remain incompletely understood. To interrogate how aging alters cellular and microenvironmental organization in cancer, we developed an integrated single-cell atlas of HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) encompassing 73 patients aged 18-91 years. Using a multi-layered computational framework combining NMF-based module discovery and partial correlation network analysis, we reveal that age-associated differences in tumor composition are driven primarily by selective shifts in cell type abundance and organization rather than widespread age-dependent transcriptional rewiring. We identify an age-enriched cellular community centered on basal-like squamous epithelial states linked to epithelial-mesenchymal transition, matrix-associated myofibroblast-like CAFs, and FOLR2+ macrophages, which secrete immunosuppressive and ECM-remodeling factors. Cross-dataset in-silico validation via TCGA transcriptomes, spatial transcriptomics, and mouse tumor models confirms the correlation of these cell types across patients, specific ligand-receptor usage, and increased proportions of epithelial and stromal cells in aged mouse models. Among epithelial cell-intrinsic age-associated transcriptional changes, midkine (MDK) emerges as a rare but robust tumor-derived signal linked to stromal remodeling, immunosuppression, and invasive epithelial programs. These findings reveal conserved mechanisms of age-dependent cellular reorganization in the tumor microenvironment and identify MDK and associated stromal-remodeling pathways as potential intervention points for age-stratified cancer therapy. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, R01DE031831 National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, R01DE033519 National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, 1F31DE033292 National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, 1UL1TR001430 Find the Cause Breast Cancer Foundation

articles.title: An Isogenic iPSC Model of LMNA p.R482W Recapitulates Adipocyte Dysfunction in Familial Partial Lipodystrophy Type 2
articles.abstract: Familial partial lipodystrophy type 2 (FPLD2) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in LMNA, most commonly p.R482W, and is characterized by selective loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue, severe insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. The cellular mechanisms underlying adipocyte dysfunction in FPLD2 remain incompletely understood, in part because existing in vitro models rely on patient-derived, non-isogenic cell lines or require non- physiologic transgene overexpression to achieve adipogenic differentiation. Here, we describe a CRISPR/Cas9-edited isogenic iPSC model of FPLD2 in which the heterozygous LMNA c.1444C>T (p.R482W) variant was introduced into a healthy donor-derived iPSC line. Using a transgene-free mesenchymal progenitor differentiation protocol, we generated LMNAp.R482W and isogenic control adipocytes and characterized their transcriptomic and functional phenotypes. Bulk RNA- sequencing demonstrated strong concordance in adipogenesis gene expression between genotypes during differentiation (Pearson {rho} = 0.968), yet LMNAp.R482W adipocytes exhibited significant downregulation of key adipogenic, lipid-handling, and extracellular matrix genes compared to isogenic controls. Functionally, LMNAp.R482W adipocytes showed markedly impaired glucose uptake under both basal and insulin-stimulated conditions, consistent with severe insulin resistance. Seahorse extracellular flux analysis revealed a globally quiescent metabolic state with significantly reduced oxygen consumption rate (126.5 vs. 261.5 pmol/min, p < 0.0001) and extracellular acidification rate (27.6 vs. 46.7 mpH/min, p < 0.0001). To validate these findings in human tissue, gene set enrichment analysis results from the iPSC model were compared to single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from subcutaneous white adipose tissue biopsies of individuals with FPLD2 carrying the LMNA p.R482W variant. Across 37 mutually significant pathways, 59.5% were concordant between the iPSC model and human adipose tissue, including the pathways most central to FPLD2 pathophysiology: adipogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, and inflammatory response. These findings establish this isogenic iPSC system as a faithful cellular model of FPLD2 adipocyte biology and a platform for functional characterization of LMNA variants of uncertain significance.

articles.title: Beyond Direct Binding: Serotonin Rewires Model Brain Plasma Membrane-Mediated Communication Pathways in Y4R
articles.abstract: Serotonin, an endogenous neurotransmitter, modulates pancreatic polypeptide (PP) recognition by the neuropeptide Y4 receptor (Y4R), a mechanism relevant to altered serotonergic signaling associated with metabolic disorder and anxiety. Although recent experiment demonstrates serotonin modulated PP dissociation kinetics of Y4R through membrane allostery, the molecular mechanism of serotonin induced lipidomic reorganization of the brain plasma membrane (BPM) relevant for Y4R activation is unknown. To this end, a total of 825.9 ns long all atom molecular dynamics simulations at 310 K elucidate the concentration-dependent coupling between serotonin partitioning, selective lipid reorganization, and PP binding and Y4R activation relevant intra-receptor communication in a heterogeneous, asymmetric model BPM. In the absence of serotonin, Y4R preferentially associates with the anionic lipids. Serotonin preferentially localizes at the lipid water interface over the PP binding and activation-associated regions of Y4R. At 6 mM, serotonin preferentially contacts phosphocholine species depleted from Y4R, whereas at 50 mM, phosphatidylinositol 4,5 bisphosphate dominates both microenvironments. These changes align with the selective remodeling of lipid networks, enhanced lipid chain ordering, and modest bilayer compaction. Weighted implementation of suboptimal paths analysis reveals concentration-dependent reorganization of communication pathways between experimentally implicated PP binding and activation associated Y4R residues. Collectively, these findings connects serotonin dependent selective lipid redistribution to altered intramolecular communication between Y4R residues associated with PP binding and G-protein coupling, and provide a framework for future experiments investigating membrane-mediated neuromodulation and neuronal signaling. These findings provide a basis for exploring lipid-targeted pharmacology as a complementary strategy to modulate GPCR allostery by altering membrane composition rather than directly targeting the receptor.

articles.title: Beyond a single threshold: calibration of CADD v1.7 and AlphaGenome for ACMG/AMP computational evidence across variant classes, model versions, and reference data
articles.abstract: Clinical laboratories use computational predictors as supporting evidence for or against pathogenicity under the ACMG/AMP guidelines, but this evidence is reliable only when score thresholds are calibrated. Genome-wide predictors such as CADD are often applied using a single cutoff across all variant types and model versions, and the new AlphaGenome Variant Impact score (AVI) has not been calibrated. Following a prespecified plan and the ClinGen calibration method, we calibrated CADD v1.7 and AVI on rare ClinVar missense variants. Both predictors provided moderate evidence of pathogenicity and strong evidence of benignity, and their thresholds held for variants classified after calibration. AVI performed better than CADD in each comparison and approached the missense-specific predictors. Thresholds available in 2024 gave AVI evidence in the final direction for 72.5% of the variants of uncertain significance (VUS) resolved by 2026, compared with 60.5% for CADD. Applied to 1.2 million current missense VUS, the calibrated predictors agreed on pathogenic or benign evidence for four in ten, and on strong pathogenic evidence for 186 VUS reviewed by expert panels, which can be reassessed first. Outside missense variants, the same thresholds failed, producing false-benign evidence for pathogenic noncoding variants. A change in CADD version altered the evidence level for a third of variants without improving discrimination. Our results suggest that computational evidence is most reliable within the variant class and model version in which it was calibrated. In practice, laboratories may prioritize missense-specific predictors, use AVI when a genome-wide predictor is needed, and reassess thresholds after model updates.

articles.title: Biomechanical stress in the retinal pigment epithelium surrounding laser scars in humans
articles.abstract: Purpose : The wound response of an epithelium comprises tissue-scale activation of stress fibers whose contraction regionally reconfigures the epithelium and drives closure of the wound. Recent in vitro studies have shown that similar biomechanical processes can paradoxically lead to enlargement of epithelial holes. In patients having undergone laser photocoagulation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), laser scars may expand over years. Here, to document the implication of epithelial biomechanics in the enlargement of laser scars we analyzed the dynamic changes affecting the RPE around scars in patients and performed confocal microscopy on a RPE flat-mount from a donor eye. Methods: We analyzed the image files of five patients (age 61 to 85 years) showing enlargement of laser scars in the RPE (follow-up, 13 to 60 months). In three of them, prospective imaging was performed using transscleral illumination adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO), an imaging technology enabling visualization of RPE cells. Time-lapse sequences were analyzed to track dynamic processes in the RPE surrounding scars. A flat-mounted phalloidin-labeled RPE from a human donor eye with a history of scatter photocoagulation was examined by confocal microscopy to document the distribution of stress fibers and cell metrics. Results: Time-lapse sequences showed that enlargement of laser scars was accompanied by the displacement of microscopic features in margins of atrophy. AOO imaging suggested locally coordinated displacement of mosaic of darks spots, with a generally radial or tangent direction relative to the edges of scars. Such movements were detected up to several hundred microns from the edges of scars. On the histology sample, elongated RPE cells with stress fibers forming actin cables were found along edges of scars, which formed fascicles between adjacent scars. Conclusion: Enlargement of RPE scars may be accompanied by long-lasting, largescale changes in the distribution of microscopic features in the margins of lesions. In particular, transscleral illumination AOO showed coordinated displacement of a mosaic similar to the one described for the RPE. The finding by histology of RPE cell with a tractional phenotype along edges further suggests that epithelial biomechanics contribute to such movements and may hence contribute to scar enlargement.

articles.title: CYP123, a sterol C4-methyl oxidase, acts with CYP51 to initiate mycobacterial lanosterol catabolism
articles.abstract: Mycobacteria exploit host cholesterol, both as a carbon source and as a source of catabolites proposed to modulate host immunity, but their capacity to catabolise other host sterols has not been established. Lanosterol, the first sterol intermediate of host cholesterol biosynthesis, accumulates in the activated macrophages these bacteria infect. Here we define the initiating steps of mycobacterial lanosterol catabolism, combining genomic enzymology, transcriptional profiling, mutagenesis, biochemistry, NMR and crystallography. We identify the cytochrome P450 CYP123 as a sterol C4-methyl oxidase. It is encoded with the lanosterol 14-demethylase CYP51 in a co-oriented region conserved across most Mycobacteriaceae. The region carries no binding site for the cholesterol-responsive regulators KstR or KstR2, and in M. abscessus lanosterol induces both genes while cholesterol does not. CYP123 oxidises the C4-methyl group of C14-demethylated sterols in three steps to the carboxylic acid, yet acts on neither lanosterol nor cholesterol, because Met82 excludes the C14-methylated precursor. An M82A variant binds and oxidises lanosterol. In a single reaction containing both recombinant M. smegmatis enzymes, CYP51 converts lanosterol to FF-MAS, which CYP123 then oxidises to the C4-carboxylic acid, so the two act in sequence. M. smegmatis, M. phlei and M. abscessus grow on lanosterol as a sole carbon source. Growth slows in M. smegmatis cyp123 and cyp51 mutants. Mycobacterial sterol catabolism therefore extends beyond cholesterol, and blocking the cholesterol route alone may not deprive these organisms of host sterols. Induction where lanosterol confers no growth advantage raises the possibility that the pathway also serves functions beyond carbon acquisition.

articles.title: Caspase-1 and -11 defend against environmental but not host-adapted pathogens in genetically complex mice
articles.abstract: Caspase-1 and -11 are inflammatory caspases that trigger pyroptosis, yet in most infection models they confer only a modest survival benefit. We have proposed that caspase-1 and -11 evolved primarily to defend against ubiquitous environmental microbes that have not been under selective pressure to evade them, whereas host-adapted pathogens have evolved evasion strategies. Testing this idea is complicated because the inbred mouse strains used in most infection studies carry mutations in innate immune genes: i.e., C57BL/6 (B6) mice carry a loss-of-function Nramp1 allele, and 129 mice lack functional caspase-11. Here we generated B6 x 129 F1 hybrid mice, which are gene-sufficient at both Nramp1 and Casp11, and used them to measure the fold change in lethal dose ({triangleup}LD100) caused by caspase-1 and -11 deficiency for four pathogens on the B6, 129, and F1 backgrounds. Caspase-1 and -11 conferred little or no survival benefit against the host-adapted pathogens Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella Typhimurium on any of the three backgrounds, apart from a modest benefit at the lowest S. Typhimurium inoculum in F1 mice. In contrast, caspase-1 and -11 were required to survive infection with the environmental pathogens Burkholderia thailandensis and Chromobacterium violaceum, where caspase-1 and -11 deficiency lowered the lethal dose by up to six orders of magnitude. The failure of caspase-1 and -11 against host-adapted pathogens therefore persists on a genetically robust hybrid background, supporting the view that a major evolutionary role of caspase-1 and -11 is defense against environmental microbes that have not been selected to evade them.

articles.title: Cell-in-drop genotyping detects megabase-scale loss of heterozygosity as a quantitative marker for CRISPR-Cas9 on-target toxicity
articles.abstract: Targeted DNA double strand breaks catalyzed by CRISPR-Cas9 have been demonstrated to cause megabase-scale segmental deletions and whole chromosome losses in a wide variety of mouse and human cell lines. This raises safety concerns for CRISPR-Cas9 based therapeutics and highlights the need for scalable methods to assess its on-target genotoxicity in clinical contexts. In this report, we present cell-in-drop genotyping, as a high throughput approach that combines single cell encapsulation with droplet-based PCR genotyping of endogenous polymorphisms to detect loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at a targeted chromosome without any genome manipulation. With this approach, we detected megabase scale LOH induced by Cas9 DSBs, mostly frequently by segmental loss. This approach also detected LOH from loss of a critical DNA repair factor, BLM helicase, and LOH induced by other genotoxic conditions, in particular, the chemotherapeutic drugs Paclitaxel and Mitomycin C, which were demonstrated to induce LOH by different mechanisms. A modified version of the assay also captured rare local short range LOH arising from DSB-induced interhomologue recombination. Because it requires no genome manipulation, cell-in-drop genotyping offers a practical, scalable tool for evaluating genotoxic risk of CRISPR-Cas9 and other agents in research and clinical development.

articles.title: Characterisation of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Saccharomyces jurei hybrids for oenological applications
articles.abstract: The Saccharomyces genus present as a genetically diverse set of microorganisms capable of tolerating a range of environmental stressors, demonstrating high fermentation capacity and producing interesting flavour compounds. Such diversity can be exploited in a single organism by producing interspecies hybrids, overcoming the limitations of a single species. Here, as proof of principle, we exploited a library of F12 interspecies diploid hybrids between Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Saccharomyces jurei (Sc/Sj), to identify new strains harbouring traits of oenological relevance, such as ethanol and glycerol production, superior tolerance to acetic acid, limited production of H2S, and optimal growth on fructose. Moreover, we calculated robustness across strains tested on solid media comparing the trade-off between performance on a single conditions and overall robustness. Progeny from a range of robustness values with favourable H2S production profiles were isolated for further analysis via micro and small-scale fermentations. Micro-scale fermentations in synthetic grape must containing individual wine-associated stressors were performed, and the robustness of the selected strains was confirmed. The wine characteristics of the hybrids were tested in small-scale fermentations in synthetic grape media. We found that both ethanol and glycerol production across our selected progeny matched or exceeding that from the commercial wine strain, and most hybrids produced less acetic acid and more fatty-acids, including higher quantities of associated esters. Overall, we were able to identify suitable Sc/Sj hybrids with interesting aroma profiles to develop further for wine fermentation.

articles.title: Conformation governs cellular behaviors of LRRK2 Parkinson's disease variants
articles.abstract: Gain-of-function of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is a common cause of Parkinson's disease (PD). In its autoinhibited state, the leucine-rich repeats of LRRK2 block the kinase active site, preventing substrate phosphorylation. Displacing the repeats (′unlatching′) primes LRRK2 for activity. Preferential unlatching causes increased substrate phosphorylation of the PD allele LRRK2[R1441H], but not LRRK2[G2019S]. Here, we define a large class of PD-associated ′unlatching′ mutations based on their effect on LRRK2 conformation. Unlatching mutants show increased localization to membranes, the site of LRRK2's Rab substrates. Unlatching mutants are also characterized by decreased LRRK2 S935 phosphorylation, which we define as a biomarker of conformation. This framework resolves the mechanism of variants such as I2020T, which structural studies could not predict. Overall, we establish unlatching as a unifying mechanism for most PD-linked variants and describe measurable readouts for identifying LRRK2-driven disease. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, F31NS155649 Parkinson's Foundation, https://ror.org/05mx85j86, PF-PRF-1439460 American Cancer Society, https://ror.org/02e463172, PF-25-1516576-01-PFMBB LRRK2 Investigative Therapeutics Exchange Howard Hughes Medical Institute, https://ror.org/006w34k90

articles.title: De novo design of mini-proteins as specific binders to PACAP-38, a key mediator of migraine
articles.abstract: Pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating peptide 38 (PACAP-38) is a vasoactive peptide that is attracting attention as a potential target for next-generation migraine treatments. Antibodies against PACAP-38 have recently shown promising results as a ligand trap medicine in clinical trials. In this study, we investigated the de novo design of miniproteins to evaluate the potential for developing a medium-molecular-weight drug that binds to PACAP-38. Using Bindcraft, we designed binders against PACAP-38 and identified ICLIST-2, a 63-residue peptide with affinity for PACAP-38 (KD = 26.5 nM). Furthermore, by alanine scanning and structural analysis of ICLIST-2, we determined residues that were suitable for further optimization using ProteinMPNN. This resulted in the design of ICLIST-11, which incorporates nine amino acid substitutions relative to ICLIST-2, resulting in a KD of 4.51 nM. Interaction analysis based on a structural model suggested that three mutations in ICLIST-11 may be important for enhancing affinity. Moreover, ICLIST-11 exhibits a Tm value that is 14 {degrees}C higher, and MD simulations suggest that the substitution of three residues with hydrophobic residues (E30F, M31L, and R54W) is one reason for this. In cell-based functional assays, ICLIST-11 demonstrated potent, concentration-dependent neutralizing activity against PACAP-38-induced PAC1R activation (IC50 = 10.6 nM), significantly outperforming the parental ICLIST-2. Taken together, these results provide a framework for protein drug discovery targeting PACAP-38.

articles.title: Decoding antibody-antigen recognition: the BL8 language and its application in calibrating deep learning predictions
articles.abstract: Antibodies are central to immunology and therapeutics, and understanding how they recognize antigens is essential to rational drug design. This recognition depends on the interplay of interface geometry, physicochemical interactions, sequence context, and complementarity-determining region (CDR) conformation. However, traditional analyses often oversimplify this complexity, which becomes particularly problematic when evaluating the massive and frequently overconfident structural hypotheses generated by modern deep learning models. Here, we introduce BL8, an interpretable, eight-view structural language that comprehensively parameterizes interfaces across topology, shape, interaction, CDR conformation, flexibility, interfacial area, amino-acid-pair composition, and sequence background. Using 15,396 experimental interface records from the Structural Antibody Database (SAbDab), we built a fixed reference atlas containing 1,498 discrete BL8 signatures. The atlas shows that natural interfaces occupy a diverse, long-tailed structural space in which similar geometric scaffolds can be associated with different chemical and sequence features. Furthermore, we projected 28,501 predicted complexes involving programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD), and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1), generated using AlphaFold 3 (AF3), Protenix-v2, and OpenDDE, into the reference space. Acting as a robust underlying calibration layer, BL8 successfully decoupled physical viability from native confidence illusions, revealing cross-target hallucinations and filtering out 15.3% to 20.1% of highly deceptive false-positive predictions. Crucially, by benchmarking distinct generative behaviors across models, it enabled the extraction of highly reliable, multi-model consensus out-of-distribution binding paradigms. Together, BL8 bridges foundational biophysics with large-scale computational predictions, providing an essential benchmarking framework for discovering novel mechanisms in the era of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Development of the Highly Sensitive Horse questionnaire to assess horses' sensory processing sensitivity
articles.abstract: It is well established that individuals vary in how they respond to situations, but might they also perceive their environment differently? Sensory Processing Sensitivity (SPS) is a multidimensional trait describing individual variation in the perception and response to sensory, emotional, and social stimuli. While extensively studied in humans, its presence in animals remains underexplored. We investigated whether horses might exhibit a comparable trait and developed the Highly Sensitive Horse questionnaire to assess equine SPS. A 104-item questionnaire was developed and refined using data from an online survey of 121 horses. The remaining 45 items were evaluated in an independent survey of 561 horses. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses identified a robust two-factor, 12-item structure reflecting dimensions similar to the human SPS dimensions of: ‘Overstimulation’, describing a tendency to become overwhelmed by intense or prolonged stimuli, and ‘Sensitivity to subtleties’, describing heightened perception of subtle environmental changes. The scale showed high internal consistency, excellent intra-rater and moderate inter-rater reliability. Although eSPS was associated with established behavioural traits, including fearfulness, it also explained unique behavioural variation beyond these traits. These findings suggest that horses differ in how they perceive their environment, providing a foundation to better understand equine behaviour, and opening new avenues for comparative sensory-processing research.

articles.title: Diversity in early animal communities of the Ediacaran, Avalon assemblage
articles.abstract: Diversity is an emergent property of macroecological and macroevolutionary processes. The Avalon assemblage preserves near-census snapshots of Ediacaran communities, enabling tests of the drivers of diversity. However, it remains unclear how alpha diversity varied among surfaces or whether variation reflected uneven sampling, abiotic context or biotic processes. We analysed diversity for 11,342 specimens across 22 surfaces and examined abiotic and biotic correlates. Despite compositional variation, most surfaces fell into four community types dominated by Fractofusus andersoni, F. misrai and/or Pectinifrons, Bradgatia, or upright fronds, with potential substructure within the upright-frond type, whereas Clapham's Pigeon Cove and Shingle Head communities, from the oldest and youngest formations, respectively, may indicate greater community differentiation near the sampled stratigraphic limits. Sampling effort varied widely, yet taxon-area curves showed richness was well captured on 12 of 22 surfaces, and Shannon and Simpson diversity remained consistent across sampling completeness and taxonomic treatments. Diversity showed no clear associations with locality or stratigraphic affiliation, but differed among community types and declined with increasing vertical segregation. Overall, these results suggest that, among the predominantly Newfoundland communities sampled, Avalon alpha diversity may have been shaped more by local community assembly and organisation than by broader geographic, environmental and temporal context.

articles.title: EigenBrain maps cortical molecular architecture from functional, geometric, and structural eigenmodes
articles.abstract: Neurotransmitter receptor and transporter distributions shape neural communication across the cortex and underpin mechanistic interpretations of brain function. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived eigenmodes, low-dimensional spatial patterns that capture the principal axes of cortical organization, are increasingly used to reconstruct brain maps and offer a potential route to approximating molecular topographies in large cohorts where direct measurements are unavailable. Yet whether the type of MRI data used to derive these eigenmodes determines which receptor and transporter distributions can be approximated, and which molecular systems are accessible through this approach at all, remains unknown. Using a spatial reconstruction framework applied to 23 molecular systems spanning neurotransmitter, metabolic, and pathological markers, we show that eight receptor and transporter maps, spanning serotonin, dopamine, histamine, cholinergic, and opioid markers, can be selectively approximated from functional eigenmodes but not structural or geometric ones. This selectivity also reveals that functional brain organization encodes a specific subset of neuromodulatory topographies that structural and geometric organization does not. To illustrate translational potential in clinical cohorts where molecular imaging is unavailable, we applied individual-level eigenmode decompositions of MRI data projected onto the eight validated molecular systems and detected cross-sectional differences in autism and longitudinal changes in schizophrenia. Together, these findings reveal a difference in how geometric, structural, and functional brain organization relate to molecular architecture, offering a method for approximating validated molecular profiles in population neuroimaging cohorts that lack direct molecular imaging.

articles.title: End-to-end reconstruction for cryo electron ptychographic single-particle analysis
articles.abstract: Cryo-electron ptychographic (cryo-ptycho) single-particle analysis (SPA) is a diffractive imaging method for protein structure determination. Current reconstruction workflows sequentially reconstruct a 2D phase micrograph from each scan, and then apply conventional SPA software to the resulting projections to obtain a 3D potential map. Here, we introduce End2EndPtychoSPA, an end-to-end reconstruction algorithm that directly fits a 3D electrostatic potential volume and particle poses to 4D-STEM diffraction data using a differentiable multislice forward model. On simulated haemoglobin data where the sequential route recovers initial poses, End2EndPtychoSPA with a learnable vitreous-ice layer reaches 3.22 A resolution against the ground truth (FSC 0.5), compared with 3.41 A for the sequential route. We also compare End2EndPtychoSPA with the sequential route on four published experimental cryo-ptycho SPA datasets. On apoferritin (11,552 particles), the End2EndPtychoSPA map improves agreement with an external atomic model over both our matched sequential route on the same particles and the deposited EMD-19425 half-map mean, and shifts the unmasked half-map FSC 0.143 crossing from 6.83 A to 5.99 A. On T20S, TMV and Phi92, End2EndPtychoSPA does not yet improve upon the 2D route.

articles.title: Endothelial protein C receptor is an entry receptor for Langya and related parahenipaviruses
articles.abstract: Langya virus is a zoonotic parahenipavirus with pandemic potential that causes acute febrile illness in people. We identified endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) as an entry receptor for Langya, Wenzhou, and Mojiang parahenipaviruses. A 3.1 Å cryo-electron microscopy structure reveals that Langya attachment glycoprotein engages EPCR through a site distinct from that of the ephrin binding site of Nipah G. This binding mode resembles those of protein C and a malarial adhesin, demonstrating convergent evolution. Interface substitutions abolish entry, whereas natural variation explains differential human EPCR use and predicts receptor compatibility across 26 animal species.
