These findings establish EPCR as a receptor for the Langya clade and provide a structural framework for understanding cross-species transmission and human infection potential. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Engineering and characterisation of AAVS1 FRT cell lines for inducible and dose-dependent gene expression
articles.abstract: Investigating biological function with high reproducibility requires the generation of stable cell lines that offer precise and inducible transgene expression. However, traditional methods often suffer from the limitations of random genomic integration, including unpredictable expression levels, leaky basal activity, and disruption of endogenous loci. To address these challenges, we engineered a versatile RPE1 cell line by integrating a TetOn3G-FRT cassette into the AAVS1 safe-harbour locus using CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) nickase. This platform utilises the Flp-FRT recombination system to facilitate rapid, site-specific "plug-and-play" insertion of transgenes, combined with the Tet-On 3G system for tight, dose-dependent expression control. The resulting RPE1 AAVS1 FRT8 line enables highly consistent transgene induction across independent clones, behaving as a monoclonal population. We highlight the importance of rigorous cell line characterisation through a multi-omics approach. Whole genome sequencing identified precise heterozygous integration at the target locus and de novo genomic duplications on other chromosomes. By integrating WGS with high-resolution proteomics and cell cycle analysis, we confirmed that these alterations did not significantly perturb cellular homeostasis or phenotypic fitness. This work establishes a robust and reliable platform for the efficient generation of inducible AAVS1 FRT stable cell lines, facilitating reproducible research in modern molecular biology.

articles.title: Female biases in islet cell gene expression, alpha cell number, and glucagon are present early in postnatal life
articles.abstract: Biological sex significantly affects glucose homeostasis. Sex differences in insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues play a role in this difference; however, a growing body of evidence suggests sex differences in islet cells also contribute to differential glucose homeostasis. Studies in rodent and human models have identified sex differences in alpha- and beta-cell gene expression, in islet cell composition, metabolism, and stress responses, and in circulating levels of glucoregulatory hormones. However, most of these studies used adult humans or mice, leaving the age at which these differences emerge less clear. We performed a detailed characterization of glucose homeostasis and islet biology in young male and female mice from two mouse strains widely used in diabetes research to model both Type 1 (non-obese diabetic, NOD) and Type 2 diabetes (C57BL/6J). We uncovered male-female differences in islet cell gene expression and composition, and in circulating levels of glucagon. Importantly, these differences were reproducible across both models and were present prior to diabetes-like phenotypes. Together, our data suggest sex differences in aspects of islet biology begin early in postnatal life.

articles.title: Fertilization offsets the maternal age effect on mouse oocytes provided the oviduct is not itself aged
articles.abstract: Advanced maternal age compromises oocyte quality, and it is widely assumed that these deficits are transmitted to embryos. However, because most studies rely on in vivo conception, it has been difficult to separate the effects of oocyte aging from those of an aged fertilization environment. In aging mice, we observed that the fraction of ovulated oocytes forming implantation sites after in vivo conception fell ~3.7-fold, raising the question of whether this was due to reduced fertilization, reduced embryo quality or reduced support from the aged reproductive tract. Therefore we fertilized oocytes of aged and young mice in vitro with a shared young-donor sperm preparation, holding the fertilization environment constant and removing paternal variability. Hallmarks of maternal age were largely offset following fertilization in vitro: aged oocytes produced blastocysts at rates comparable to young controls, with altered - but not deficient - cell-lineage composition and no detectable impairment in development to term (E18.5) after transfer to young oviducts. Proteomic analysis revealed that, unlike the transcriptomic signature, the proteomic age signature of oocytes was not faithfully propagated to the blastocyst: for a subset of proteins, particularly those depleted in aged oocytes, the direction of the age effect reversed between oocyte and blastocyst. Comparison with parthenogenetically activated oocytes showed this divergence to be fertilization-dependent, implicating fertilization - rather than mere embryonic cleavage - as the driver of proteomic change. Stable-isotope labelling in live embryos showed that blastocysts from aged, fertilized oocytes both synthesized more new protein and retained less maternal protein than young counterparts; neither effect was detectable after parthenogenesis. Puromycin labelling, by contrast, showed a maternal-age-associated rise in bulk synthesis regardless of route. Together, these results indicate that the maternal-age effect on the oocyte proteome is labile rather than fixed and can be offset by fertilization itself, provided the maternal environment is not itself aged. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft, https://ror.org/018mejw64, BO-2540/8-1, FU 583/7-1

articles.title: Fluidized Bed Cathodes Enable High-Rate CO2 to Formate Production and In Situ Microbial Growth
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction (eCO2RR) to formate offers a sustainable and promising route for storing renewable electricity in a microbial energy substrate. Conventional CO2 electrolyzers rely on flat electrodes with limited catalytic surface area, mass-transfer constraints, and electrolytes that are incompatible with microbial growth, preventing direct coupling of electrochemical formate production with biological conversion. Here, we developed a biocompatible CO2 electrolysis configuration that uses fluidized particles of Sn, Bi, and In as electrocatalysts to enhance CO2 to formate conversion while supporting microbial utilization in the same chamber. The fluidized configuration enabled high formate production rates up to 0.24 mmol cm2 with Faradaic efficiencies of 86 to 92%, representing a two fold improvement over static electrodes. The system also achieved a carbon conversion efficiency of 42%, approaching the theoretical limit for co-generation of formate and bicarbonate. Importantly, electrolysis was performed in a biocompatible medium that supported direct in situ cultivation of Cupriavidus necator within the cathode chamber using only electricity and CO2/O2 as fed substrates. C. necator continuously consumed electro-generated formate for 5 to 6 days under aerobic conditions, demonstrating integrated CO2 to biomass conversion. This work establishes a fluidized electrocatalytic platform for simultaneous electrosynthesis and microbial upgrading in a single reactor, providing a scalable strategy for renewable carbon fixation and sustainable biomanufacturing.

articles.title: Foreign Body Responses Adapt to Systemic Immunosuppression to Maintain Local Immune Homeostasis Through Decorin-Associated Signaling
articles.abstract: Foreign body responses (FBRs) involve complex interactions between pro- and anti-inflammatory signals that regulate the integration and function of implanted biomaterials. However, most mechanistic studies of FBRs have been conducted in healthy hosts, and little is known about how these immune responses are regulated under pathological conditions. Here, we investigated immune responses to porous polycaprolactone (PCL) scaffold implants in mice with endotoxin tolerance or aggressive breast tumors, which induce systemic immunosuppression through distinct mechanisms. Despite suppressed inflammatory activity in major organs, implanted scaffolds maintained locally immune-active environments characterized by increased pro-inflammatory immune-cell populations and elevated inflammatory mediators, including CXCL1. In migration assays, CXCL1 preferentially recruited neutrophils and enriched immune-cell populations with pro-inflammatory phenotypes among splenocytes derived from both endotoxin-tolerant and tumor-bearing mice. The extracellular matrix proteoglycan decorin, a damage-associated molecular pattern with TLR2/4-activating activity in myeloid cells, was enriched within scaffolds but reduced in major organs under both immunosuppressive conditions. Recombinant decorin promoted pro-inflammatory phenotypes in suppressive myeloid-cell populations and enhanced CXCL1 production through TLR2/4-associated signaling, suggesting a mechanistic link between decorin-mediated myeloid activation, CXCL1-dependent immune-cell recruitment, and the maintenance of local immune activity at biomaterial interfaces. Together, these findings reveal that FBRs are not merely passive inflammatory reactions to biomaterial implants but can dynamically adapt to systemic immune dysfunction to sustain local immune homeostasis. This intrinsic immunoregulatory capacity may represent an additional factor influencing the performance of immunomodulatory implants and should be considered in biomaterial design to optimize therapeutic outcomes across different applications and host immune conditions.

articles.title: From Problems to Solutions: How Self-Questions Drive Strong Scientific Reasoning
articles.abstract: Metacognition, or awareness and control of thinking, is essential for problem solving because it helps solvers select strategies for learning and decide when to enact them (planning), check their understanding in the moment (monitoring), and assess effectiveness of solutions and learning strategies (evaluating). Most studies that examine metacognition do so retrospectively, leaving a critical gap in how metacognition is used in-the-moment for problem solving. In this study, we utilized a think-aloud interview approach to capture and characterize the metacognitive skills that senior undergraduate life science students at three institution types in the United States used spontaneously while solving challenging biology problems. We found that the students (n = 39) displayed a wide variety and quantity of monitoring, some evaluating, and nearly no planning skills while creating a solution backed with high-quality reasoning. Students frequently used self-questions to monitor and evaluate their thinking. We found that self-questioning is a critical skill for generating solutions, but it only moves problem solving forward if the student asks and correctly answers the self-question out loud. This study illustrates how self-questioning and other metacognitive regulation skills provide links to bridge the gap between a student's prior knowledge and specific features of a challenging problem. Based on our student data, we conceptualized a model of metacognitive phases during problem solving with high-quality reasoning. Finally, we present a self-question scaffold to facilitate the proposed phases (planning, monitoring, reasoning, and evaluating) so educators can equip students with metacognitive and scientific reasoning tools for effective problem solving. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. U.S. National Science Foundation, https://ror.org/021nxhr62, 1942318

articles.title: Gene regulatory logic underlying the differentiation of mixed lineages in human thymic epithelial cells
articles.abstract: The thymus enacts central tolerance through thymic (TECs), which present self-antigens to developing T cells self-reactive cells, preventing autoimmunity. Human TECs include populations that express lineage-committed programs corresponding to distinct peripheral tissues, yet how they acquire these programs and whether these TEC subpopulations are genetically related and conserved in mice remain unknown. Using matched single-cell gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 126,687 human TECs, we identified 17 TEC subsets defined by their distinct expression profiles of 1,843 cell type restricted-antigens (CRAs) from 48 peripheral cell types. With a new phylogenetic reconstruction method, we show that lineage-committed TECs share a common ancestor, retain a thymus-specific mixed identity through co-expression of multiple CRA signatures, and are specified by coordinated activator and repressor regulons. We also identified a basement-membrane-collagen-rich state (BMC-TECs) with progenitor-like properties. Finally, mouse TECs shared the regulatory strategy but conserved few master transcription-factor drivers. This study mechanistically characterizes human TEC subpopulations and reveals the gene regulatory logic that leads to their distinct diversification and mixed identities in humans and mice.

articles.title: Generation of functional adipoids from human induced pluripotent stem cells
articles.abstract: Human adipose tissue models are lacking although essential for metabolic research. Traditional primary cell cultures are poorly scalable and unsuitable for drug screening or modeling of genetic disease. Conventional two-dimensional adipocyte cultures cannot withstand the long-term treatment required to mimic chronic conditions such as obesity and insulin resistance. To overcome these limitations, we developed an accessible protocol to produce three-dimensional human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived adipocyte microtissues, termed adipoids. hiPSC-derived adipoids display long-term stability and viability. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that adipoids contain mature adipocytes and adipocyte stem/progenitor cells, similar to human adipose tissue. Furthermore, hiPSC-derived adipoids contain unilocular adipocytes, exhibit stimulated lipolysis, and secrete adipokines. Thus, hiPSC-derived adipoids provide a functional, scalable and genetically tractable model to perform large-scale pharmacological screens and to investigate human metabolic disease. ### Competing Interest Statement All authors are current or former employees of Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd.

articles.title: Genomic context tunes sequence-encoded RNA processing
articles.abstract: Sequence and genomic position jointly determine RNA processing, but at native loci the two are difficult to separate. Here, we uncoupled them by integrating RNA-processing elements into endogenous transcription units at tens of thousands of mapped positions and different elements at shared positions. Genomic position dominated RNA production levels but differentially influenced RNA processing events. A cryptic polyadenylation site, used natively only upon U1 inhibition, was rarely used ectopically. In contrast, introns partially retained at their native loci remained so across thousands of ectopic positions, with a substantial fraction of transcripts reaching the cytoplasm unspliced. SON depletion reduced splicing of two such introns, preferentially near speckles. Chromatin state, GC content, and speckle proximity tuned this behavior without overriding it, and in opposite directions: speckle proximity improved the splicing of one intron and reduced that of another. Specialized introns are therefore portable modules carrying their own processing information. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Novo Nordisk Foundation, NNF22OC0073967

articles.title: HNRNPC-mediated RNA processing promotes VHL-associated excessive vasculogenesis in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome revealed from patient-derived blood vessel models
articles.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome (VHLS) is an inherited disorder characterized by excessive vascularization, which contributes to the development of hemangioblastomas and benign or malignant tumors, as well as renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and cysts in multiple organs. VHLS is caused by mutations in VHL tumor suppressor gene, which encodes a component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. Although therapeutic agents targeting hypoxia-inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF2A), which is stabilized by VHL loss and promotes tumor angiogenesis, have been approved for clinical use, their therapeutic response remains limited in RCC patients associated with VHLS. Therefore, there is an unmet need for the development of alternative therapeutic approaches independent of HIF2A. Here, we establish a human iPSCs-based model of VHLS-associated excessive vasculogenesis using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from VHLS patients and VHL-edited isogenic iPSC lines. Vascular cells (VCs) differentiated from these VHLS-specific iPSCs exhibited excessive blood vessel formation compared to healthy donor-derived VCs, leading to vascular lesion formation characterized by abundant blood vessels and abnormal cellular growth in vivo. Mechanistically, RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) were preferentially stabilized in the patient-VCs. Among these RBPs, the stabilization of heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein C1/C2 (HNRNPC), which is a substrate for pVHL-mediated protein degradation independent of HIF2A expression, was critical for the dysregulated vascularization caused by VHL inactivation in this model. These findings provide an iPSCs-derived vascular platform to elucidate VHLS mechanisms and identify HNRNPC as a potential therapeutic target for VHL-driven vascular lesion formations through an HIF2A-independent mechanism. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research from the Ministry of Education, Science, and Culture of Japan, 23K14457, 21K20668 Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED), 23bm1423010h0001, JP23bm1423018, JP23bm1323001

articles.title: Heterogeneous primary nucleation determines Aβ42 fibrilstructure.
articles.abstract: The current developments in the field of amyloid fibril structure determination has revealed multiple structures for peptides of identical sequence. This may reflect variations in sample environment or similar nucleation barriers for multiple folds. Here we investigate the influence of aggregating surface and during fibril formation from monomeric amyloid {beta} peptide (A{beta}42). The fibril structures formed in identical solutions in glass vials / bottles and PEGylated polystyrene 96-well plates display very different monomer fold within the fibrils. This is a clear indication of extremely slow homogeneous primary nucleation. Instead, heterogeneous primary nucleation at vessel walls or at the three-line interface between air, water and vessel wall dictate the outcome in each solution, where the initially formed structure is propagated through elongation and secondary nucleation. The results further imply that the conversion towards the thermodynamically stable fibril structure one is slow for A{beta}42.

articles.title: Homoplastic evolution of proximal podomere patterning across Arthropoda
articles.abstract: The jointed arthropod leg is often credited as a key innovation spurring the evolutionary success of the phylum. Across lineages, each territory of the appendage has served as the substrate for myriad adaptations and structural innovations. While much of the available data has supported a conserved suite of transcription factors responsible for the initiation and patterning of the arthropod appendage, recent works have begun to highlight instances of lineage-specific shifts in expression dynamics, particularly amongst the chelicerates, correlated both with the emergence of novel structures and developmental system drift in the specification of plesiomorphic structures. These works confound efforts to align or homologize the leg segments across arthropod lineages, an effort already challenged by ground plan differences in segment number between the subphyla. An even more unusual architecture of leg segments occurs in sea spiders (Pycnogonida), which alone among Arthropoda are considered by systematists to bear three coxae (proximal segments), in contrast to the single coxa of the remaining arthropods. Here, we examined proximal podomere patterning in the developing appendages of a sea spider and an arachnid. We find that a particular spatial arrangement of Lim1 and SoxNeuro characterizes the developing coxa and trochanter of the harvestman Phalangium opilio (Opiliones) throughout appendage formation, with RNAi depletions of Lim1 yielding deletions of coxa and trochanter. Comparison of expression patterns across taxa shows that Lim1 and SoxNeuro have a similar spatial arrangement in the harvestman and sea spider, but these suggest conflicting interpretations of leg segment homology. We show that this is attributable to homoplastic patterns of evolution in SoxNeuro across Arthropoda. Expanding our surveys of prominent PD axis-patterning transcription factors supports additional instances of homoplasy in the domains of Sp6-9 and Irx2. The pervasiveness of homoplasy in gene expression patterns demands measured skepticism of homology statements and careful comparisons of multiple patterning genes, toward achieving falsifiability in the homology of structures. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. FWF Austrian Science Fund, https://ror.org/013tf3c58, 10.55776/PAT1457924

articles.title: Identifying the source population of naturally recolonised rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) in Laokhowa-Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary, Assam, through multidisciplinary methods
articles.abstract: Megaherbivore population recovery largely depends on restoring connectivity between fragmented protected areas to facilitate natural dispersal, gene flow, and range expansion. The Indian rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) has recovered from severe population decline in the past, but several populations remain spatially restricted. Recent conservation efforts and the expansion of protected areas in Assam have coincided with natural rhino recolonization in Laokhowa-Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS). This has occurred from nearby regions of Orang NP and Kaziranga NP after the species was locally extinct in the 1980s. Identifying the source population of these recolonised rhinos is crucial for managing this emerging metapopulation. We used non-invasive genetic sampling, genetic assignment and a landscape connectivity model to investigate the origin and potential movement routes of the recolonising rhinos. We identified eight unique individuals from Laokhowa-Burhachapori WLS and assigned them to the potential source population using Bayesian and frequency-based approaches against a reference dataset of 365 individual rhinos across the rhino-bearing areas of Assam. Habitat suitability was modelled using 161 spatially thinned presence points and eight environmental variables. We applied least-cost path (LCP) analysis to assess landscape resistance between protected area nodes. All eight recolonising rhinos were assigned to Orang NP with high Bayesian assignment probabilities (q = 0.97-0.99). The connectivity model identified two least-cost pathways, with the Orang NP-Laokhowa-Burhachapori WLS linkage showing lower landscape friction than the Kaziranga NP linkage. These findings provide genetic evidence that the recolonisation occurred through natural dispersal, most likely from Orang NP, and indicate that recent landscape restoration has re-established the structural connectivity across this floodplain. Maintaining these linkages will be essential to promote natural range expansion and the long-term persistence of Indian rhinoceros in Assam.

articles.title: Immuno-Proteomic Age of Cardiovascular Etiology (iPACE) Signature Predicts Cardiovascular Risk in Elderly Patients
articles.abstract: Despite advances in clinical care, cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. While age alone is a primary risk factor for CVD, accumulating evidence suggests the immune system influences the initiation and progression of CVD pathophysiology, particularly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD). Here, using two independent cohorts of older adults, we develop a thirty-protein signature of age based on serum immune proteomics, which correlates with HFpEF and ASCVD risk and mortality (Immuno-Proteomic Age of Cardiovascular Etiology, iPACE). We find aging-related circulating immune proteins associated with ASCVD and HFpEF-specific resilience and susceptibility that may be used as potential prognostic, diagnostic, or therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Isolation and characterization of diverse Veillonella phages reveal novel lineages and distinct host interactions
articles.abstract: The human oral microbiome is diverse and home to many species of bacteria, archaea, microeukaryotes, fungi and viruses. Homeostasis in the oral microbiome is important for health and dysbiosis in these communities leads to periodontal and systemic diseases. Veillonella are gram-negative, anaerobic, lactate-fermenting early colonizers of the mouth and are abundant in healthy oral microbiomes. Although considered commensals, Veillonella serve as bridging species in dental biofilms, promoting later colonization by pathogens, with mounting evidence supporting their roles as accessory pathogens in dental caries and periodontal disease. Bacteriophages are key regulators of bacterial community composition and are important drivers of microbial diversity, evolution, and ecology of the oral environment. Despite the ecological importance of Veillonella in the oral microbiome, phages infecting Veillonella remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we report the isolation of ten phages infecting natural isolates of three Veillonella species, representing seven distinct phage genomes. These phages exhibit diverse morphologies, genome organizations, and host ranges, with infection restricted to strains within the species of isolation. Several phages establish stable lysogeny, confer resistance to superinfection, and differ substantially in spontaneous production of infectious phage progeny. Genetic analysis of resistant mutants implicates lipopolysaccharide O-antigen as the receptor for one phage. Although none of the isolated phages had close matches in existing oral virome catalogs, related sequences were detected in oral metagenomes from geographically diverse populations. Together, these findings establish an experimentally characterized collection of Veillonella phages and connect previously uncharacterized oral viral diversity to bacterial hosts and infection phenotypes.

articles.title: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy alters Schwann cell calcium homeostasis and increases peripheral nerve inflammation
articles.abstract: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-RD) affects skeletal muscle and peripheral nerves, yet the consequences of LAMA2 deficiency on peripheral nerve integrity beyond early postnatal development remain incompletely understood. We investigated sciatic nerve architecture and molecular alterations across postnatal life in hypomorphic Lama2dy2J/dy2J mice. LAMA2 localizes around the abaxonal surface of myelinating Schwann cells in control nerves. LAMA2-deficient nerves exhibited patchy regions lacking myelinated axons from early postnatal stages into adulthood, including expanded Remak bundles along with axons completely lacking normal Schwann cell ensheathment. In adult nerves, myelin infolding and reduced myelin circularity revealed abnormalities in the architecture of myelin that had formed. Bulk sciatic nerve RNA sequencing identified altered calcium-signaling and immune-related transcriptional signatures. Complementary Fura Red measurements in primary nerve-derived Schwann cell cultures demonstrated decreased intracellular calcium in LAMA2-deficient samples, while ATP-evoked responses were preserved. Older LAMA2-deficient nerves also exhibited increased CD45+CD11b+ myeloid-cell infiltration. Together, these observations extend the characterization of LAMA2-associated neuropathy into adulthood and identify calcium homeostasis and neuroimmune responses as candidate processes relevant to persistent peripheral nerve pathology.

articles.title: Leg blood flow and muscle oxygenation are reduced when exercising with loads >=40% 1RM compared to loads <=30% 1RM due to increases in contraction induced intramuscular pressure
articles.abstract: The critical occluding tension (COT) is the load at which contraction-induced increases in intramuscular pressure (IMP) collapse intramuscular vasculature and impair oxygen delivery. For knee extension resistance exercise, the COT occurs at ~30-40% 1RM, yet few studies have measured IMP alongside convective oxygen delivery. This study examined the interaction between IMP, leg blood flow, and muscle oxygenation during resistance exercise. Twelve participants completed knee extension bouts across a range of loads while vastus lateralis IMP, femoral blood flow (Doppler), blood pressure, muscle oxygenation (NIRS), and electromyography (EMG) were recorded. Mean IMP increased alongside relative load (20% 1RM=19.1(9.4) mmHg; 30% 1RM=22.4(10.4) mmHg; 40% 1RM=27.0(8.7) mmHg; 50% 1RM=31.5(11.5) mmHg; 60% 1RM=41.14(13.8) mmHg; p0.05), but different between the 20-30% 1RM and 40-60% 1RM groupings (p<0.05) (20% 1RM=2.6(1.4) times rest; 30% 1RM=1.8(0.5) fold of rest; 40% 1RM=1.4(0.6) fold of rest; 50% 1RM=1.1(0.4) fold of rest; 60% 1RM=1.1(0.5) fold of rest). Muscle oxygenation was lower at 40%, 50%, and 60% 1RM compared to 20% and 30% 1RM (p<0.05). Thus, at ≤30% 1RM exercising blood flow increased well above rest, indicating preserved microvascular perfusion, whereas at ≥40% 1RM the rise in IMP was sufficient to impair perfusion and limit blood flow increases. Exercise at or above the COT restricts convective oxygen delivery due to contraction-induced increases in IMP. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council, RGPIN-2021-04259

articles.title: Local fractal dimension as an indicator of functional reorganization in molecular interaction networks
articles.abstract: Changes in protein abundance incompletely describe how molecular perturbations reshape cellular organization. Here we introduce DIFFRACT, a framework that integrates quantitative proteomics with protein-protein interaction networks to identify reorganization through changes in local fractal dimension. Molecular associations define effective distances between connected proteins, allowing the geometry of their surrounding network neighborhoods to be compared across conditions. Analyses across four organisms (E. coli, A. thaliana, C. elegans, and H. sapiens) and three interaction resources (STRING, BioGRID, and IntAct) establish heterogeneous local scaling, while controlled perturbations demonstrate sensitivity to regional changes and invariance to uniform distance rescaling. Applied to RAVER1-deficient A549 cells, DIFFRACT identifies components associated with established RNA-regulatory functions and candidate roles in tRNA biology, mitochondrial organization and ciliogenesis. Selected RNA-regulatory and ciliary themes are not significantly enriched by abundance-ranked gene set analysis, supporting complementary information from network geometry. Selected functional annotations also recur in HEK293T cells. Guided by the ciliary predictions, we show that RAVER1 depletion increases the proportion of ciliated A549 cells 2.57-fold and increases cilium length. DIFFRACT thus connects changes in molecular network geometry to experimentally testable biological responses, extending the interpretation of proteomic perturbations beyond differential abundance.

articles.title: Long-PDE4D degradation attenuates left ventricular cardiomyocyte hypertrophic remodelling
articles.abstract: Spatial compartmentalisation enables cyclic AMP (cAMP) to regulate distinct cellular functions, yet selectively targeting disease-associated signalling remains challenging. Phosphodiesterases constrain local cAMP responses, but conventional inhibitors offer limited isoform selectivity. Here we investigate whether targeted degradation of long phosphodiesterase-4D (PDE4D) isoforms can suppress pathological growth while preserving contractile function. Using adult rat and human ventricular cardiomyocytes and human myocardial slices, we show that the proteolysis-targeting chimera KTX-184 enhances compartmentalised cAMP signalling and attenuates hypertrophic remodelling. In rat cardiomyocytes, KTX-184 increases β-adrenergic cAMP responses in the cytosol and at the plasma membrane, including T-tubule and crest regions, and enhances nuclear protein kinase A activity. In contrast, phospholamban- and ryanodine receptor-associated cAMP nanodomains, calcium transients and sarcomere shortening remain unchanged. KTX-184 prevents angiotensin II-induced hypertrophic remodelling, preserves T-tubule organisation and normalises hypertrophic marker expression. In human cardiomyocytes, it increases cytosolic cAMP responses and prevents overload-induced hypertrophy in myocardial slices. These findings identify long PDE4D isoforms as targets for spatially selective modulation of cAMP signalling and support targeted degradation as an approach to suppress cardiac hypertrophy without increasing contractility. ### Competing Interest Statement Eduardo Torres, David Stirling, Kyle Chan, and Cathy Swindlehurst are employees of Katalytic Therapeutics, which supplied the compound (KTX-184) used in this study. The remaining authors declare no competing financial interests. British Heart Foundation, RG/F/22/110081 European COST Action AtheroNET, CA21153

articles.title: Loss of stromal VEGFR2 protects against ischemic acute kidney injury by preserving the renal microvasculature
articles.abstract: Injury to the renal microvasculature, particularly the peritubular capillaries, is a defining feature of ischemic acute kidney injury (AKI). Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) signaling is a central regulator of endothelial cell survival, proliferation, migration, and vascular remodeling. Although VEGFR2 has been extensively studied in endothelial cells, accumulating evidence suggests that it is also expressed in non-endothelial cell populations, where it may regulate tissue-specific responses to injury. Here, using publicly available single-cell or single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human and mouse kidneys, we identified VEGFR2 expression in renal stromal populations. Immunostaining further detected phosphorylated VEGFR2 in the renal stroma of mouse kidneys. To determine the functional role of stromal VEGFR2, we utilized renal stroma-specific Vegfr2 KO mice. Stromal VegfR2 deletion attenuated kidney injury after renal ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI), as evidenced by reduced tubular injury, preservation of renal blood flow, decreased endothelial oxidative stress, and maintenance of the renal microvasculature. Stromal Vegfr2-deficient kidneys also exhibited increased Angpt1 and Tek levels, enhanced endothelial ERK activation, and preserved endothelial adherent junctions. Taken together, these findings reveal an unexpected role for VEGFR2 in the renal stromal lineage and highlight stromal-endothelial communication as a potential therapeutic target for preserving microvascular integrity after ischemic AKI.

articles.title: MASH-in-a-dish reveals fatty acid-driven itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is characterized by lipid-driven sterile inflammation and fibrosis that leads to liver failure and liver cancer. Metabolites are increasingly recognized as signaling molecules and regulate disease progression through cell-cell crosstalk. To overcome the challenges of studying metabolite crosstalk between different cell types in MASH livers, we developed a novel in vitro MASH model, "MASH-in-a-dish", a Transwell co-culture system of mouse hepatocyte-derived organoids (HepOrgs), Kupffer cells (KCs), and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) in a chemically defined liver co-culture medium. MASH-in-a-dish models key clinical features of clinical MASH, including steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning, inflammation and fibrosis. MASH-in-a-dish allowed for rapid and specific separation of co-cultured HepOrgs, KCs and HSCs, enabling cell type-specific metabolomics and stable-isotope fluxomics analysis. Using MASH-in-a-dish, we identified 19 MASH-associated, cell interaction-responsive metabolites and demonstrated that fatty acids, via the carnitine shuttle, drive KC itaconate production, which aggravated oxidative stress, steatosis, and cell damage in lipid-stressed HepOrgs. Inhibiting itaconate production by KC-specific Acod1 knockout in the MASH-in-a-dish system mitigated hepatocyte damage. Our results show that MASH-in-a-dish is a powerful in vitro platform to study cell-cell interactions in MASH pathogenesis and identify itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes as a novel pathogenic mechanism and a potential therapeutic target in MASH.

articles.title: MaCADEMIA: a software toolbox for single-molecule fluorescence image quantification
articles.abstract: Single-molecule localisation microscopy (SMLM) is a powerful tool in molecular and cellular biology and part of the broad umbrella of super-resolution microscopy. A distinct feature of SMLM, is its capacity for deep quantification, beyond just spatial information, to copy number, stoichiometry, molecular interaction and dynamics in living cells. The hardware required is increasingly straightforward to implement. However, complexity remains in the image analysis where much remains fragmented across specialised software tools. Here, we present MaCADEMIA (Matlab Computational Analysis of Diffusion, Emitter Molecular Intensity and Abundance), a simple yet powerful toolbox of MATLAB functions and associated documentation to enable straightforward extraction of quantitative single-molecule information. MaCADEMIA performs ensemble particle detection achieving localisation accuracies down to 0.5 pixels Root mean squared error (RMSE) across wide signal-to-noise (SNR) ranges on standardised particle tracking benchmarks, consistently matching or exceeding the performance of 14 leading methods. Our integrated workflow enables molecular counting and stoichiometry determination through stepwise photobleaching analysis, mobility measurement via mean squared displacement, colocalisaton analysis and absolute protein copy number quantification using three-dimensional cellular models.

articles.title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence has accelerated the design of structured proteins, but it remains difficult to design functional intrinsically disordered proteins because of weak structural constraints and poorly defined sequence-to-function relationships1. Activation domains (ADs), transcription factor regions that recruit coactivators, are an excellent test case for the de novo design of intrinsically disordered sequences. ADs are one of the oldest groups of functional intrinsically disordered sequences2 and designed ADs have applications in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and agriculture. We computationally generated 500,000 candidate sequences that resembled known ADs and predicted AD function with extant machine learning models, including three neural networks. From high-scoring sequences, we selected 18,750 for experimental validation in yeast. Surprisingly, >90% of the 16,770 well-measured sequences function as ADs. Sequences predicted to be active by multiple models were stronger, motivating development of a fast and accurate consensus AD predictor, MADRIGAL. A number of our designed ADs retain functionality across fungi, plants, and human cells. This work illustrates a generalizable paradigm for incorporating sequence-to-function models into the design loop to efficiently generate functional intrinsically disordered sequences. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have filed a patent covering the 14 designed activation domain sequences presented in figure 6. Patent Application No. PCT/US2026/053089 with a filing date of October 28, 2026. Its current status is pending. National Institute of General Medical Sciences, https://ror.org/04q48ey07, T32GM148378, R35GM150813, R35GM155044 National Human Genome Research Institute, T32HG000047, T32HG4725 U.S. National Science Foundation, https://ror.org/021nxhr62, IOS 2112057, IOS 2112056, IOS 2112058 Office of Biological and Environmental Research, DE-AC02-05CH11231 University of California, Berkeley, SEED Scholars Program, Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program, Rose Hill Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco, https://ror.org/00knt4f32

articles.title: Mapping Endogenous Psychedelic Chemistry: Indolethylamine N-Methyltransferase (INMT) Localizes Proximal to the Golgi Apparatus of Human Neurons
articles.abstract: N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) is a serotonergic psychedelic with a history of ethnobotanical use and emerging clinical efficacy for neuropsychiatric disorders. Following Julius Axelrod's pioneering studies showing DMT production in human tissues, DMT has been proposed as an endogenous neuromodulator because it is a serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2A R) agonist. However, the DMT-producing enzyme, indolethylamine N-methyltransferase (INMT), has not been characterized at the protein level in the human central nervous system. Here, we validated an anti-INMT antibody and used immunocytochemistry to show that INMT localizes in close proximity to other DMT biosynthetic enzymes near the cytosolic face of the cis-Golgi network in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, with immunoreactivity observed across multiple neuronal Golgi phenotypes. Notably, both DMT-like and 5-HT2A R immunoreactivity also partially localized in close proximity to the Golgi apparatus. Our results establish the first protein-level characterization of INMT in human neurons and identify the cis-Golgi network as a candidate microdomain for psychedelic tryptamine biosynthesis. We propose that INMT catalytic activity at the cis-Golgi network creates an enriched region of membrane-permeable psychedelic tryptamines that can access an intracellular 5- HT2A R pool. These findings provide new tools and insights that can inform efforts to understand the mechanism of action of psychedelics under clinical investigation and to target endogenous tryptamines therapeutically.

articles.title: Mapping, stacking and characterization of a novel resistance haplotype against GpaVvrn-virulent Globodera pallida derived from wild potato relative Solanum brevicaule
articles.abstract: Potato production is threatened by pests and pathogens. Among the most harmful are the potato cyst nematodes (PCN), including Globodera pallida . The major control measures are potato cultivars harbouring resistance genes. However, virulent nematode populations are breaking through the most broadly applied resistance genes, and therefore novel resistance genes are required to keep control of G. pallida . In this study we map a resistance locus in wild potato relative Solanum brevicaule to the bottom of chromosome 11 (42.83 - 42.85 Mb) using a k-mer based bulked segregant analysis and name the resistant haplotype GpaXIbrc . The presence of the GpaXIbrc marker in the potato genome significantly increases resistance against a GpaVvrn -virulent G. pallida population (AMPOP01). Furthermore, the GpaXIbrc haplotype was stacked with three other resistance haplotypes: GpaXItar , GpaVvrn , and GpaIXvrn . Stacking of the novel GpaXIbrc haplotype to these other resistance haplotypes resulted in a significant increase in resistance. The largest effect was seen in combinations with 'major' resistance haplotypes GpaVvrn + GpaIXvrn and GpaXItar + GpaXIbrc . To determine whether we are dealing with a novel allele, the resistance mechanism underlying the GpaXIbrc haplotype was described after performing an in vitro bioassay. The resistance mechanism was different from GpaXIspl as described in literature, which is also localized at the bottom of chromosome 11. Therefore, we conclude that we found a novel resistance allele originating from S. brevicaule . ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. AVEBE

articles.title: Mechanotransduction tuned by intermediate filaments promotes DNA repair in stiff environments
articles.abstract: High mammographic density increases breast cancer risk. Dense tissues are rich in fibrillar collagen, forming a rigid extracellular matrix around the epithelium. Although cancer initiation and progression are closely tied to DNA damage and to the DNA damage response, if and how tissue stiffness affects genome maintenance is not fully elucidated. We found that repair factor recruitment is more efficient, and that DNA breaks are repaired faster by cells on rigid substrates. Mechanistically, hemidesmosomal integrins, intermediate filaments, the LINC complex, and YAP are key mediators of this mechanogenomic response. Rigid tissue contexts favor survival of cells with DNA damage, which may lead to the accumulation of somatic mutations, as identified here with RNAseq analyses of normal breast tissue. Our findings provide new insights into how tissue rigidity influences cancer risk.

articles.title: Behavioural and neurogenetic evidence for emotion primitives in the fruit fly Drosophila from an open field test
articles.abstract: Emotions are based on evolutionarily conserved building blocks (‘emotion primitives’) that are present across mammals. Whether these building blocks are found in insects is largely undefined. Here, we employ the open field test (OFT) in Drosophila and focus on wall-following and total walking activity as behavioural indicators of emotion-like states. Wildtype and transgenic flies were subjected to various conditions prior to behavioural testing. The results indicate that wall-following and total walking activity are independent measures that are modulated, with generally increased wall-following observed under aversive stimuli and decreased values under positive conditions, independent of the time of day. The effects of genetic manipulation of selected neuromodulatory systems support their role in modulating emotion-like states in Drosophila. Activation of reward-related neurons decreased wall-following while inhibition increased it. Moreover, treatment with ethanol or diazepam produced predictable changes in behaviour. Our findings suggest that Drosophila shares conserved core emotion-like building blocks with vertebrates, and show that wall-following and total walking activity in the OFT can serve as a reliable indicator of emotional valence and arousal in the fruit fly. This positions Drosophila as a powerful genetic model to dissect the neuronal and neurochemical substrates of emotion primitives.

articles.title: Glycolipid MPIase is essential for the TAT (twin-arginine translocation) pathway
articles.abstract: TAT (twin-arginine translocation) is a preprotein translocation system dedicated to membrane translocation of prefolded proteins in plants and bacteria. The TAT translocon, consisting of the TatABC subunits, drives translocation using proton motive force. However, there have been no reports on the successful reconstitution of the TAT system. In this report, we show that MPIase, a glycolipid that has been known to catalyze membrane protein integration, is essential for the TAT system. Our findings in recombinant Escherichia coli demonstrate that overproducing TatABC increases MPIase levels, and that depleting MPIase results in TAT precursor accumulation in the cytosol. Furthermore, co-reconstitution of MPIase with TatABC revealed the translocation activities of TAT substrates in a proton motive force-dependent manner. This is the first successful reconstitution of the TAT system and will be advantageous for understanding its mechanisms.

articles.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection
articles.abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. In this study, we interrogate the programmable landscape in macrophages to find regulatory panels that determine the precise polarization state that a macrophage is driven to. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. Using our computational pipeline, we identify combinatorial panels of epicentric regulatory factors (RFs) for each polarization state. We demonstrate that a set of three RFs, that is, CEBPB, NFE2L2, and BCL3, is sufficient to change the polarization destination from M1 to M2. siRNA knockdown of the 3-RF-set in THP1-derived M0 cells, despite exposure to an M1 stimulant, significantly attenuated the shift to M1 phenotype and instead increased the expression of M2 markers. Single knockdown of each RF also showed a similar trend. The siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 3-RF-set rendered the macrophages hyper-susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection, demonstrating the importance of these factors in modulating immune responses. Overall, our results provide insights into the transcriptional mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization and identify key RFs that may be targeted to modulate immune responses.

articles.title: Quantifying microbial fitness in high-throughput experiments
articles.abstract: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. What are the consequences of these different fitness statistics, and is there a best way to quantify fitness in a given context? Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.

articles.title: Simplifying principles underlying the highly complex peptide motif of the promiscuous chicken MHC class I molecule, BF2*21:01
articles.abstract: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. Understanding the impact of these promiscuous generalists and fastidious specialists is of considerable interest. The promiscuous BF2 molecule from the chicken B21 haplotype, BF2*21:01, binds a wide range of peptides by remodelling the peptide-binding site, allowing co-variation of the anchor residues at peptide positions P2 and Pc-2, and binding of an anchor residue at Pc. Using in vitro refolding assays with peptides and peptide libraries, determining thermostability and crystal structures, and analysing a chicken B21 cell line by immunopeptidomics, we found that BF2*21:01 will accommodate many possible combinations at P2 and Pc-2, as well as several hydrophobic amino acids at Pc. However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P2 and Pc-2 as well as at P3 and Pc-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.

articles.title: A Retrospective Real-World Assessment of Motor Status After Stroke Using a Home-Based Brain-Computer Interface
articles.abstract: Background: Upper extremity impairment persists in many stroke survivors, and few treatments are effective for severe chronic deficits. Brain-computer interface (BCI) therapy, which pairs decoded motor-intention-associated electrophysiology with sensory feedback, has improved upper extremity impairment in randomized trials, including in patients with severe paresis. Whether these benefits translate to routine care has rarely been evaluated. This study examined upper extremity motor recovery through 1 year among patients prescribed at-home BCI therapy in clinical practice. Methods: This retrospective observational study included adults who were prescribed the IpsiHand System, an electroencephalography-based BCI, through a commercial US home therapy program, had a baseline Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer (UEFM) assessment, and averaged >1 session per week through their last assessment. Occupational therapists administered the UEFM by video every 4 weeks. The primary outcome was UEFM change from baseline to week 12. A mixed model for repeated measures estimated change through week 52, with multiple imputation sensitivity analyses for missing data. Results: Of 452 patients included in analyses (mean time since stroke, 5.4 +/- 5.4 years), mean baseline UEFM was 20.1 +/- 14.6, with 333 patients (73.7%) having severe motor impairment (UEFM 0-28). At week 12, mean UEFM change was 4.3 points (95% CI, 3.7-4.9; P<0.001), and 31.7% achieved the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 5.25 points. Mean change reached the MCID at week 16 (5.6, 95% CI [4.8, 6.4]). Model-estimated change in UEFM continued to improve through 1 year, being 6.1 (95% CI, 5.5-6.8) at week 24 and 8.1 (95% CI, 6.8-9.4) at week 52. Conclusions: Among regular users of at-home BCI therapy in routine care, most of whom had severe chronic impairment, UEFM scores improved by 12 weeks, reached MCID by 16 weeks, and continued to increase through 1 year. At-home BCI therapy merits evaluation in randomized trials with follow-up beyond 12 weeks.

articles.title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
articles.abstract: Background. Testing and deploying medical AI systems at scale already results in more outputs than clinicians can review, and the use of large language models (LLMs) as judges is growing rapidly. Decision-only models, cheap and fast models that return structured probabilities rather than text, offer a potentially scalable option for that goal. Methods. In an OSF pre-registered evaluation, we tested TypeSafe Jev 1.13 as a judge on tasks from five validated clinical benchmarks: rubric grading (HealthBench), planted clinical errors (When Rubrics Fail), risk in AI-written clinical documents (MedVAL), counseling ratings and failures (CounselBench) and physicians' preferences between answers (Real-POCQi). Comparators were expert raters' agreement with each other, OpenAI Decisions, GPT-6 Luna, a proposed hybrid team combining decision models and a cheap LLM and, as frontier comparators, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. The main outcome was plain agreement with the expert label. Results. The test comprised 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls. Jev's agreement with expert labels averaged 64.7% over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US$1.46; per judgment, it cost 1/34 of Sol's price and 1/152 of Opus's. A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev's least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit. Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Conclusions. Across more than 200,000 model calls, a decision-only model was non-inferior to two frontier judges on most tasks at a small fraction of their cost and time, while reporting how sure it was of every call. With local cutoffs and expert oversight of omissions and clinical documents, judging every output of a deployed medical AI system becomes more affordable.

articles.title: A personal network analysis of health-advice seeking and dietary influence in a rural community
articles.abstract: Health advice circulates through everyday relationships. The sources of informal health authority are less clear: the adviser's knowledge and conduct, or their network position. We examine personal network data from 89 adults in a rural community (1,625 respondent-contact relationships). We distinguish contacts consulted for health advice from contacts who tried to change the respondent's eating, model both relations with multilevel and penalised regressions, and test their differences. Both relations are embedded in frequent, close, and commensal ties and point to contacts more educated than the respondent. We find no characteristic that is more strongly associated with one relation than with the other. Health advice seeking also correlates with co-residence, the marital relationship, and responsibility for cooking. Respondents perceive their advisers as healthier, but advisers' own reports give no evidence of healthier diets or lower body mass. Informal health authority here is constituted by relational position (intimacy, domestic food work, and a contact's higher education relative to the respondent). We find no evidence that it rests on demonstrated conduct. Interventions that work through nominated advisers should not assume that being consulted implies expertise. Our design is cross-sectional and single-site. Future dyadic and longitudinal studies should test whether advice is followed.

articles.title: Allostatic load as a potential pathway linking exposomic risk to early-onset cancer: a matched case-control study in the All of Us Research Program
articles.abstract: Background: Early-onset cancer (EoC) incidence is rising worldwide, yet risk models built on isolated exposures or rare pathogenic variants capture little of the cumulative environmental burden experienced by younger adults. Allostatic load (AL), the cumulative physiological burden of chronic stress, can be measured from routine laboratory values and vital signs and is a candidate biological pathway linking environmental exposures to carcinogenesis. Methods: We conducted a 1:4 matched case-control study nested within the NIH All of Us Research Program, including 7,550 participants and 1,510 cancers diagnosed before age 50, of which 298 were exposome-related (the primary outcome). We derived an exposomic risk score (ERS) from 12 survey-based measures and an eight-component AL score from electronic health record data, and used mediation analysis to estimate the proportion of the ERS-EoC association operating through AL. Results: A higher ERS was associated with higher AL ({beta}=0.18 standard deviations [SD] per SD; 95% CI 0.16-0.20), and each SD increase in AL was associated with 21% higher odds of EoC (odds ratio 1.21; 95% CI 1.15-1.28). For exposome-related EoC, AL mediated 17.0% (95% CI 7.4-49.5%) of the association between the ERS and EoC, with significant total, direct, and indirect effects that were robust to lag, scoring, and age-adjustment sensitivity analyses. Across all EoC, the proportion mediated was 48.8% (95% CI 21.2-186.5%). Conclusions: AL is a candidate biomarker and potential pathway through which cumulative environmental burden relates to EoC, warranting prospective validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
articles.abstract: Background: Young onset dementia is frequently misdiagnosed, particularly where neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorders (PPD) overlap. Plasma biomarkers measure current pathology, whereas polygenic risk scores (PRS) capture lifelong genetic risk. Whether PRS derived from late-onset and population samples transfer to young-onset presentations, and how they relate to plasma biomarkers, is unknown. Methods: We studied 687 participants of European ancestry from the Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders (MiND) Study, a prospective young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort: 195 healthy controls (HC), 283 PPD, 55 Alzheimers disease (AD) and 154 non-AD neurodegenerative disease (oNDG). PRS for AD, a cross-disorder psychiatric factor (PSY), frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia and Parkinsons disease were computed with PRS CS, excluding the APOE locus. Plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 were available for 332 participants. Models were adjusted for age, sex and APOE e4 dose. Results: Relative to HC, the AD PRS was associated with AD (OR 1.69 per SD, 95% CI 1.17-2.45) but not PPD (0.95, 0.77-1.16). The PSY PRS showed the reciprocal pattern (PPD 1.29, 1.05-1.58; AD 1.00, 0.72-1.40). No PRS was associated with any plasma protein. In distinguishing PPD from oNDG, NfL was the strongest discriminator (OR 2.15, 1.62-2.83). The AD PRS was also associated with oNDG (1.38, 1.11-1.71), without improving discrimination (AUC 0.764 for NfL alone versus 0.773 combined). Conclusion: In young onset presentations, AD and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration. Their combined diagnostic value requires evaluation in larger, longitudinal pre-clinical cohorts.

articles.title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
articles.abstract: Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subject's own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.

articles.title: Brownfield land and emergency hospital admissions in England: a small-area ecological study using contamination hazard score as an exposure proxy
articles.abstract: Background: Empirical evidence on the health impacts of brownfield land (previously developed land that may be contaminated) remains limited, mainly due to poorly defined exposures and pathways. Here we assessed associations between an area-level contamination hazard score and emergency hospital admissions across England, using the score as a proxy for the potential contamination associated with brownfield land. Methods: We used Lower-layer Super Output Area (LSOA)-level population-weighted contamination hazard scores in Bayesian hierarchical models to examine the risk of emergency hospital admission (age-sex standardised, 2010-2019) with a primary diagnosis of i) all-cause (excluding external causes), ii) respiratory diseases, and iii) cardiovascular diseases (CVD). Models were adjusted for deprivation, population density, tobacco expenditure, greenspace, urbanicity, and ethnicity, and included spatially structured and unstructured random effects to account for residual spatial autocorrelation between neighbouring areas. Stratified analyses assessed potential effect modification by deprivation, urban/rural classification, and region. Results: We included 42,875,231 admissions for all natural causes, 6,657,050 for respiratory diseases, and 4,393,461 for CVD across 32,844 LSOAs in England. LSOAs with higher contamination hazard scores showed a non-linear decreasing trend in relative risk (RR) for all health outcomes. Spatial variation was evident, with stronger negative associations in urban and the least deprived LSOAs, while rural and more deprived LSOAs showed weaker associations or greater uncertainty. Region-specific analyses demonstrated inverse associations for all outcomes in London and for all natural causes and respiratory admissions in the North West and East of England. Other regions showed no consistent pattern across outcomes. Conclusion: Higher contamination hazard scores were associated with lower emergency hospital admission risks. This suggests that areas with a greater legacy of potentially contaminating land uses do not necessarily experience poorer contemporary population health. The inverse associations may partly reflect subsequent remediation and urban regeneration, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

articles.title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson's Disease
articles.abstract: Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinson's disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brain's cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a 'vertical' trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel 'lateral trajectory' in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D™ (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM ('Vertical' target) or its lateral efferent bundle ('Lateral' target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D™ algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: Comparing Machine Learning Methods for Detecting Caregiver Burden in Transcribed Conversations with Clinicians
articles.abstract: Dementia caregivers' elevated burden is associated with earlier patient institutionalization and greater caregiver morbidity, yet no standardized, objective method exists for detecting burden during routine clinical encounters. We compared four machine learning and AI approaches for detecting caregiver burden in de-identified caregiver-clinician transcripts from the COPE in PACE study using Zarit burden scores. A naive baseline predicting burden in every transcript achieved precision/F1 = 0.40/0.57. LLM prompting achieved precision/F1 = 0.43/0.60. Weak supervision achieved precision/F1 = 0.48/0.58. The fully supervised model, trained on sentence-level labels with only 1.1% burden-positive sentences, achieved precision/F1=0.19/0.25; this result is not directly comparable because of different labels and units of analysis. LLM prompting modestly outperformed weak supervision and naive baseline without fine-tuning, while class imbalance limited fully supervised sentence-level classification. Larger annotated corpora and refined labeling strategies are needed for clinical deployment.

articles.title: Constructing expert models of adolescent vaping behaviour: A mental models study
articles.abstract: Research on vaping prevention messages has predominantly examined adolescents’ perceptions of and responses and the research exploring how experts’ perspectives is limited. Expert knowledge is crucial for conceptualising the risk phenomenon and its key causal mechanisms, uncertainties, and issues that are relevant to address in evidence-based communication strategies. This study therefore explored how professionals and experts conceptualise and understand adolescent vaping behaviour, including its perceived causes and drivers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with a purposive sample of 12 experts from medical research, addiction science, public health prevention, and adolescent-oriented practice in Norway. Data collection and analysis were informed by the mental models approach to risk communication. The analysis identified an expert-derived mental model/influence diagram of adolescent vaping behaviour. Across expert domains, vaping was understood as a multifactorial phenomenon emerging from interacting biological, psychological, and social factors operating across multiple system levels. The first theme describes vaping initiation as a socially embedded and often intermittent practice shaped by identity development, peer belonging, and low perceived harm. The second theme captures how vaping is enabled, sustained, and legitimised through interacting drivers operating across social, structural, commercial, and regulatory contexts. The third theme focuses on reinforcement processes, whereby nicotine dependence and emotional coping mechanisms contribute to more sustained use. According to these expert accounts, adolescent vaping is sustained and legitimised through broader processes of normalisation operating across multiple societal levels. The expert perspectives identified in this study suggest that comparative risk framings of e-cigarettes as less harmful than cigarettes, and the social functions of vaping within adolescent peer cultures, may be important considerations in the development of risk communication targeting adolescents.

articles.title: Decision-Making Under Stress, Biological Stress Responses, and Risk for Suicidal Behavior in Young Adults
articles.abstract: Background: Stress may influence decision-making processes relevant to suicidal behavior, yet few studies have examined risky decision-making and expected value (EV) sensitivity under stress longitudinally among young adults at elevated suicide risk. Methods: Participants included 233 young adults (18-30 years) with recent suicide attempts (n=55), suicidal ideation (n=59), psychiatric controls (n=71), and healthy controls (n=48). Hair cortisol concentration, circulating inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, IL-10, IL-1ra, TNF-alpha), Stressful Cups Task, and clinical measures were assessed at baseline, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups. Results: Participants with a history of suicide attempts showed greater reductions in risky choices under stress over time compared to healthy controls. Greater reductions in EV sensitivity under stress relative to neutral conditions predicted subsequent suicidal behavior. Higher C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with fewer risky choices under both neutral and stress conditions, while higher interleukin-6 (IL-6) was associated with fewer risky choices under neutral conditions. Higher interleukin-10 (IL-10) was associated with greater reductions in risky choices under stress relative to neutral conditions over time. No significant associations were observed for hair cortisol concentrations (HCC). Conclusions: Stress-related changes in risky decision-making and reduced EV sensitivity may contribute to vulnerability to suicidal behavior. These findings highlight the importance of assessing decision-making under stress and examining inflammatory processes as potential mechanisms underlying suicide risk.

articles.title: Deep learning grading of Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images: a weighted soft-voting ensemble of convolutional and transformer networks
articles.abstract: Background: Schistosomiasis morbidity still persists in China despite extensive progress towards elimination of new and active infections. Diagnosis of liver fibrosis related to Schistosoma japonicum remains challenging due to the subjective nature of ultrasound grading and the shortage of experienced sonographers in endemic counties. Methods: We developed a deep learning model that grades schistosomal liver fibrosis from a single B-mode ultrasound image without manual delineation of a region of interest. We used 2,921 images from 2,921 adults (aged 18-88 years, median age 54 years; 46.4% female) from a schistosomiasis hospital in Jiangxi Province, China, between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 12.9%, 34.6%, 32.4% and 20.2% had grade 0, 1, 2 and 3 fibrosis, respectively. Fibrosis grades were based on the clinical ultrasound record and re-evaluation by an experienced radiologist according to the Chinese Handbook of Schistosomiasis Control; discordant cases were reviewed by a second radiologist and resolved by consensus. Predictions from four neural networks with different architectures (ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T) were combined by weighted soft voting, with weights derived from validation performance. Results: For the four-grade task this model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184-0.8856), an accuracy of 0.8500 (0.8136-0.8818) and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9187 (0.8983-0.9373) on a fixed test set of 440 images. For detecting significant fibrosis (grade 2 or 3; test-set prevalence 0.530), sensitivity was 0.9700, specificity was 0.9179, positive predictive value was 0.9300, negative predictive value was 0.9645, and AUROC was 0.9817. The ensemble achieved a higher macro-F1 than each individual backbone. Every ensemble misclassification was to an adjacent grade; no image with severe fibrosis was classified as no or mild fibrosis, or vice versa, whereas each individual backbone made 1-4 errors spanning two or more grades. Conclusions: The model may provide an automated aid for Schistosoma japonicum-associated fibrosis grading and could potentially support screening and follow-up in endemic areas after external validation.

articles.title: Delayed-centrifugation blood collection tube for remote blood biomarker assessment
articles.abstract: Introduction: Plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and amyloid-{beta} 42 (A{beta}42) are advancing toward clinical use for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but their reliability can be impacted by preanalytical handling. Although alternative collection tubes with distinct stabilization strategies --P100 (protease inhibitor) and HEMAcollect (hemolysis/platelet-activation minimization) --have been developed to stabilize plasma proteins, how well they preserve these markers remains unresolved; we therefore compared both against fresh standard EDTA tubes. Methods: In 40 participants, plasma p-tau217 and A{beta}42 were measured (Lumipulse) in paired fresh EDTA, P100, and HEMAcollect samples after 5-day ambient storage. We assessed concentration change, rank-order preservation (Spearman {rho}), percentage difference, and diagnostic classification under the p-tau217/A{beta}42 ratio and p-tau217 alone.
