These results establish sulfide-interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

articles.title: Re(I)‐Based Molecular Actuator‐Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
articles.abstract: The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen‐dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor (Re1@NMs) that integrates a three‐dimensional rhenium(I)‐based molecular actuator (Re1) with glucose oxidase (GOx)‐powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx‐catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered Re1, screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose Y‐axis motif undergoes E/Z photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano‐photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model, Re1@NMs‐mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor‐infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage‐associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal‐complex‐based three‐dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor‐microenvironment‐adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

articles.title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
articles.abstract: Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS2. Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn2+ photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g−1. Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

articles.title: Submolecular Selenium Enables Low‐Pressure and Recyclable All‐Solid‐State Li–Se Batteries
articles.abstract: All‐solid‐state lithium‐selenium (Li–Se) batteries offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their practical deployment is hindered by sluggish solid‐state redox kinetics, large volume fluctuations, and unstable solid‐solid interfaces, particularly under low stack pressure. Here we report a submolecular Sex cathode by converting crystalline cyclo‐Se8 into amorphous single‐atom and short‐chain Se (Sex, x < 4) species anchored on graphene (Sex@G), which increases the electronic conductivity from 6.3 × 10−5 to 13 S cm−1 and Li+ diffusivity from 1.7 × 10−14 to 2.0 × 10−11 cm2 s−1. Meanwhile, a Li2O‐nanoshell‐modified sulfide solid electrolyte is designed to stabilize the interface against both Li metal and Se cathode. As a result, all‐solid‐state Li–Se batteries deliver the theoretical capacity of 673 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and retain 86% capacity over 2800 cycles at 3 C under 8 MPa, with stable operation down to −30°C. All‐solid‐state Li–Se pouch cells further achieve an energy density of 420 Wh kg−1 and 94% capacity retention after 300 cycles under 2.5 MPa. Post‐mortem analysis reveals that the submolecular Sex species are not only structurally preserved but also recyclable after electrochemical cycling within the solid‐state reaction environment. This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low‐pressure, recyclable, and high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries.

articles.title: Incorporating reef condition into conservation planning to meet place‐based biodiversity outcomes under the Global Biodiversity Framework
articles.abstract: To achieve Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Target 3, the selection of protected areas must consider the condition of ecosystems at sites in addition to the GBF 30% area target. Implementing this consideration for coral reef ecosystems is challenging because data describing condition are patchy and limited. Thus, there is uncertainty in how effective coral reef condition data are for informing conservation priorities. To address this uncertainty, we evaluated whether including ecosystem condition data changed conservation priorities when the objective was to protect reefs and implement Target 3. We tested multiple static and modeled temporal coral reef condition datasets for the Great Barrier Reef and found that including reef condition significantly altered spatial planning priorities (p < 0.001), with effects varying according to the condition indicator used. Almost half of the reefs prioritized for protection when condition metrics were included became low priority when they were excluded. Ignoring information about condition missed conservation targets for ∼22% of reef habitats once condition measures were included, highlighting how presence‐only approaches can overestimate conservation benefits by treating lower‐condition reefs as equal contributors to biodiversity protection. These differences in priority areas highlight the need to develop and use effective condition metrics for designing marine protected area systems for coral reefs globally. Making such data available and usable for managers and practitioners is a priority for coral reef conservation. Incorporación de la condición de los arrecifes a la planeación de la conservación para cumplir con los resultados de sitio bajo el Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad Resumen Para alcanzar la Meta 3 del Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad (GBF) de Kunming‐Montreal, la selección de áreas protegidas debe tener en cuenta el estado de los ecosistemas en los distintos emplazamientos, además del objetivo del GBF de cubrir el 30% de la superficie. Aplicar esta consideración a los ecosistemas de arrecifes de coral supone un reto, ya que los datos que describen su estado son pocos y están fragmentados. Por lo tanto, existe incertidumbre sobre la eficacia de los datos sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral a la hora de establecer prioridades de conservación. Para abordar esta incertidumbre, evaluamos si la inclusión de datos sobre el estado de los ecosistemas modificaba las prioridades de conservación cuando el objetivo era proteger los arrecifes y cumplir la Meta 3. Analizamos varios conjuntos de datos estáticos y temporales modelados sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral de la Gran Barrera de Coral y descubrimos que la inclusión del estado de los arrecifes alteraba significativamente las prioridades de planificación espacial (p <0.001), con efectos que variaban según el indicador de estado utilizado. Casi la mitad de los arrecifes que se consideraban prioritarios para su protección cuando se incluían los indicadores de estado pasaban a tener baja prioridad cuando se excluían dichos indicadores. Cuando ignoramos la información sobre el estado, no se alcanzaron los objetivos de conservación en aproximadamente el 22% de los hábitats de arrecifes una vez que se incluyeron las medidas de estado, lo que resalta cómo los enfoques basados únicamente en la presencia pueden sobreestimar los beneficios de conservación al considerar que los arrecifes en peor estado contribuyen en igual medida a la protección de la biodiversidad. Estas diferencias en las áreas prioritarias ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de desarrollar y utilizar métricas de estado eficaces para diseñar sistemas de áreas marinas protegidas para los arrecifes de coral a nivel mundial. Poner dichos datos a disposición de los gestores y profesionales, y garantizar que sean utilizables, es una prioridad para la conservación de los arrecifes de coral.

articles.title: Climate‐Driven Distribution Modeling of the Glacial Apollo Butterfly (Parnassius glacialis) for Biodiversity Conservation
articles.abstract: Understanding how climate change affects insect distribution is critical for biodiversity conservation, particularly in the case of range‐restricted and ecologically sensitive species. The glacial Apollo, Parnassius glacialis (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae), is a high‐altitude butterfly of notable scientific and esthetic value, yet its ecological response to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we model the current and future distribution of P. glacialis across China and identify key environmental drivers shaping its habitat. We developed an ensemble species distribution model using 45 occurrence records and 10 bioclimatic variables, integrating outputs from multiple algorithms to enhance predictive robustness. Temperature—particularly seasonal variation—emerged as the strongest determinant of habitat suitability, followed by precipitation. At present, suitable habitats are concentrated in northern, southwestern, and eastern China. However, projections under future climate scenarios reveal a marked reduction in suitable range, with the habitat centroid shifting to lower elevations in Hubei Province. The direction and extent of this shift vary among scenarios, highlighting the species' vulnerability to both climatic and socioeconomic trajectories. These findings raise urgent conservation concerns, suggesting that P. glacialis may face significant habitat loss and range contraction under projected climate conditions. We recommend the establishment of targeted protected areas, the integration of insect responses into climate adaptation policies, and the implementation of long‐term ecological monitoring. This study provides crucial insights into climate‐driven range shifts in high‐altitude butterflies and underscores the broader need for adaptive conservation strategies in a warming world.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Exonic SSR‐Containing Genes in Three Diving Duck Species Reveals Shared Functional Themes
articles.abstract: Simple sequence repeats (SSRs) are ubiquitous components of eukaryotic genomes that contribute to genome evolution, genetic variation, and gene regulation. Although genome‐wide SSR landscapes have been extensively characterized across vertebrates, the cross‐species distribution and functional associations of exonic SSR‐containing genes remain poorly understood, particularly in non‐model birds. To address this knowledge gap, we performed a comparative analysis of chromosome‐level genome assemblies from three diving duck species (Aythya ferina, Aythya marila, and Netta rufina) to investigate genome‐wide SSR patterns and the cross‐species sharing and functional characteristics of exonic SSR‐containing genes. Comparative analyses of genome‐wide SSRs revealed pronounced interspecific variation in SSR abundance and repeat composition, whereas exonic SSR abundance showed more similar values after normalization by total annotated exon sequence length. Cross‐species comparison identified 4336 exonic SSR‐containing genes shared among all three species, greatly outnumbering the species‐specific gene sets. Functional enrichment analyses identified four broad functional themes associated with these shared genes: (i) gene transcription and epigenetic regulation, (ii) protein homeostasis and the ubiquitin–proteasome system, (iii) development, differentiation and morphogenesis, and (iv) stress response and cellular maintenance. The most significantly enriched categories were associated with transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, RNA processing, and epigenetic regulation, whereas autophagy‐ and other cellular‐maintenance pathways indicated additional associations with stress‐response processes. These functional associations should be interpreted cautiously because they may be influenced by cross‐species annotation limitations and gene‐architecture differences. Collectively, our results reveal distinct patterns for genome‐wide and exonic SSRs distribution among the three diving duck species and identify shared functional associations of genes containing exonic SSRs. These findings provide a comparative genomic framework for future investigations of exonic SSRs in waterfowl and other non‐model vertebrates.

articles.title: Comparison of the Population Genetic Structures of Borrelia Virulence Gene ospC and a Putatively Neutral Intergenic Spacer
articles.abstract: Borrelia afzelii, a major causative agent of Lyme borreliosis in Europe, exhibits high polymorphism of the outer surface protein C (ospC) gene, which facilitates evasion of the vertebrate immune response. Its extensive polymorphism has been hypothesized to result from balancing selection imposed by host immunity, which predicts reduced population genetic structure at ospC relative to neutrally evolving genomic regions. To test this prediction, we genotyped ospC and the rrs–rrl intergenic spacer (IGS) in B. afzelii samples from questing Ixodes ricinus ticks and bank voles (Clethrionomys glareolus) sampled across nine populations in Poland between 2020 and 2024. Among‐population differentiation was consistently lower at ospC than at IGS, and while IGS exhibited a significant isolation‐by‐distance pattern, no such signal was detected for ospC. Collectively, these findings support the hypothesis that balancing selection maintains ospC polymorphism and counteracts geographic differentiation, with implications for the evolutionary epidemiology of Lyme borreliosis in Europe.

articles.title: Do Harbour Porpoise Mortality Records Reflect Living Population Structure? A Matrix Population Model Diagnostic
articles.abstract: Effective conservation of marine mammals depends on reliable demographic information, yet acquiring such data for highly mobile cetaceans is challenging. Harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena) are widely used as sentinel species, but much of what is known about their demography comes from stranding and bycatch records. While invaluable, these data may be filtered by drift, detection, reporting effort and age‐specific vulnerability. We developed a matrix population model (MPM)‐based diagnostic framework to quantify how observed stage compositions in mortality datasets deviate from asymptotic demographic expectations. Using a stage‐structured MPM parameterised from published vital rates, we derived the stable stage distribution (SSD) and compared it with age‐class distributions from 10,863 harbour porpoise strandings (of 16,181 total records) in Danish and North Sea waters, bycatch and mixed‐mortality records, and hunting captures from Greenland and Denmark. Deviations from SSD, and from the composition expected among deaths, were assessed using goodness‐of‐fit tests, distance metrics, and tests of the juvenile proportion. Strandings showed strong and consistent departures from SSD expectations, with juveniles markedly over‐represented across spatial and temporal scales. Juveniles remained over‐represented relative to the composition expected among deaths under baseline rates, and the departure from the living population was robust to variation in vital rates. Divergence from the asymptotic stage structure was moderate to strong, varied across space, and increased significantly over time in 2 of 6 regions. Bycatch, mixed‐mortality, and hunting captures showed comparable SSD divergence, indicating that juvenile‐heavy mortality composition is not an artefact of stranding sampling alone. Our results show that harbour porpoise stranding, bycatch, and even hunting data should not be assumed to be demographically representative of living populations. Separating sampling bias from higher juvenile mortality needs independent estimates of juvenile survival.

articles.title: Moult Timing as a Measure of Condition in a Northern Hemisphere Ungulate
articles.abstract: Many vertebrates that live in seasonal climates moult once or twice a year, with the effect of refreshing worn coat or plumage, increasing insulation or improving camouflage. The timing of moult may be in response to a variety of cues, but because it is costly, it is also likely to reflect the health and wellbeing of individuals, here referred to as their condition. Using the individually‐monitored red deer from the Isle of Rum, in which summer and winter coats are easily distinguished, we (a) test for traits that are predictive of moult timing, (b) explore traits that moult timing is predictive of and (c) analyse covariances between moult timings and calving dates at the individual, annual and residual level. We show that adult female moult timing in July and November is associated with age, reproductive status and parasite burden, and has been getting earlier over time in November. A female's moult timing also predicts the overwinter survival of herself and her current calf as well as her future fecundity. Moult timing varies among individuals and years. Covariances between calving dates and the timing of each moult shed light on the temporal patterns of condition within individuals and across years, for example, across years, winter moult covaries with the following calving date but not the summer moult that occurs shortly after. The timing of moult appears to be a non‐invasive measure of condition. Monitoring moult timing across years at the population level may shed light on year‐to‐year variation in population health and variation within populations is likely indicative of the relative conditions among individuals. Increased knowledge of population and individual condition may be of benefit for ungulate population management and conservation.

articles.title: Raptor Models Alter Rodent Behavior During Acorn Dispersal
articles.abstract: The relationship between rodents and oak trees has attracted considerable attention. The interaction spans a wide range of outcomes, from extreme predation, in which rodents consume acorns, to forms of collaboration that approach mutualism. Acorn characteristics and the behavior of rodent species within the oak habitats are among the factors shaping this interaction. This study examines the influence of third species on rodent–oak interaction by using raptor models. The main objective is to determine whether raptors in the treetops can deter rodents from feeding on acorns, thereby reducing acorn dispersal. To achieve this objective, we monitored acorns' dispersal by four rodent species, Algerian mouse, wood mouse, common vole, and garden dormouse, in 10 m × 10 m semi‐wild enclosures with oak trees in the four corners, two of them with raptor models. Beneath the 4 oaks, 60 acorns, 15 acorns per tree, were provided daily for 15 days, and the acorns in situ consumption and dispersal were tracked to determine whether the presence of raptor models altered the dispersal by any of the rodent species. The results show that species that are actively involved in acorn dispersion through transport (Algerian mouse, wood mouse) modify their behavior in response to the presence of raptor models in the treetops. The garden dormouse also modifies its behavior, although this species does not transport or bury acorns; however, it does move them around on the surface and consumes most of the acorns whole by preying on them. Therefore, it does not participate in the acorn dispersion process. The common vole typically occupies open habitats without oaks and does not modify its behavior, probably because raptor models are not perceived as a threat.

articles.title: Sex, Age, and Skull Morphology Effects on Eye Size and Refractive Errors in Reindeer
articles.abstract: Eye size influences captured light and visual resolution and is used as an indicator of the relative importance of vision. Although vision‐related sexual dimorphism is subtle among vertebrates, Cervids exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body size, antler development, and reproductive strategies. We tested the hypothesis that male reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) with larger skeletal dimensions would have larger eyes and narrower binocular overlap but similar refractive errors compared to females. We collected skull morphological, ocular biometric, and refractive error data from 69 semi‐domesticated reindeer (0.5–12.5‐year‐old; 27 females, 42 males) living year‐round under extreme high‐latitude seasonal variation in photoperiod in south‐central Norway. The relationships between eye size, mandible length, interorbital distance, and orbital diameter were analyzed, and binocular overlap and anterior blind zones were calculated. Eye size increased with measures of skull size, while refractive error remained minimal across all ages. Although male calves had significantly larger mandibles and interorbital distances, their orbital diameters were the same as in female calves. However, in adults, males also had larger orbital diameters. After controlling for differences in skeletal measures, males were found to have relatively smaller eyes than females, whereas binocular overlap and blind zones were similar. These findings demonstrate vision‐related sexual dimorphism in reindeer.

articles.title: Social Behaviour Drives Gut Microbiome Community Assembly Among Wild Long‐Tailed Macaques (Macaca fascicularis) in Thailand
articles.abstract: The ‘social microbiome’ conceptualises gut microbial communities as ‘islands’ of host social organisation. Yet, in comparison to broader aspects of social organisation such as animals' group membership and composition, the impact of inter‐individual differences in sociality on microbiome community ecology remains less well studied. Among a wild but human‐provisioned group of long‐tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis), we assessed the relative effects of individuals' sociality, compared to their demographic characteristics, anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors, and microbe‐microbe associations, on the relative abundance and co‐occurrence of bacterial taxa. Bipartite network analysis showed that bacterial communities among macaques were nested rather than segregated or modular structures. Several ‘core’ bacterial genera were found across all macaques, but other ‘non‐core’ bacteria were found only in a few macaques suggesting that their occurrence/abundance may be influenced by transient environmental factors. Joint Species Distributions Models showed that macaques' sociality, particularly their dominance rank and their connectedness or centrality within their social grooming network, had the strongest impact on taxa abundance, followed by their demographic characteristics, and finally their exposure to both anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors. Phylogenetically distant taxa were more likely to co‐occur within the same macaque hosts than phylogenetically related taxa. These findings confirm that microbiome communities are strongly influenced by the social status and connectedness of individual hosts. Nevertheless, the finding that some taxa were more prevalent among high‐ranking or well‐connected macaques, while others were more prevalent among low‐ranking or socially peripheral macaques, warrants further investigation into how individual differences in social microbiomes might affect their health and fitness. Future studies, through the collection of behavioural and microbial data on additional macaque groups, may provide further insights into the relative effects of animals' social organisation and social behaviours on microbiomes.

articles.title: The Human‐Imprinted Regional Species Pool: Functional Trait Patterns of Commercial and Established Plants
articles.abstract: Urban plant communities assemble from a regional species pool shaped by both ecological processes and horticultural trade, yet how these two forces jointly structure its functional composition remains poorly understood. We characterized the potential regional species pool of Switzerland by compiling 5295 vascular plant species spanning herbs, shrubs, and trees and comparing established species (wild‐established only), commercial species (horticulturally available only), and overlapping species (both). Using a trait database covering life‐history strategies, morphology, environmental preferences, and human use, we examined functional trait space using principal component analysis and quantified functional richness, dispersion, and originality. We further tested which traits were associated with wild establishment among non‐native species and invasive status among overlapping species using Firth logistic regression. Commercial species were unevenly distributed across growth forms, dominating among trees (67.9%) and shrubs (59.7%) but less represented among herbs (17.9%). Functional differentiation was strongest along an environmental niche axis, with commercial herbs associated with drier conditions and commercial woody species with warmer conditions. Commercial species consistently had the lowest functional richness, dispersion, and originality across all growth forms. Wild establishment was associated with multiple environmental, reproductive, and ecological traits, whereas invasive status was associated with warmer temperature preference and anthropogenic tolerance, although the latter analysis was exploratory. These results indicate that commercial availability creates a functionally selective pool of species that may influence later urban community assembly. By shaping the functional possibilities available before local assembly occurs, horticultural trade may therefore leave an important human imprint on urban biodiversity, with potential downstream consequences for ecosystem functioning and trophic interactions.

articles.title: Unveiling the Ongoing Expansion of Bullheads of the Genus Ameiurus (Actinopteri: Siluriformes) in the Dnipro River Basin, Ukraine: New Distributional Records and Genetic Diversity
articles.abstract: Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. We employed an integrated framework combining laboratory molecular analysis (mtDNA COI barcoding) with field‐based morphological scoring via Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC). Sampling was conducted across multiple riverine networks within the catchment to evaluate whether range expansion is driven by natural downstream dispersal or human‐mediated pathways. A total of 66 specimens from six sampling localities were analysed, yielding 66 COI sequences. Phylogenetic reconstruction consistently recovered two discrete, high‐support clades corresponding to A. nebulosus and A. melas, a topology consistently supported across multiple distance‐based and phylogeny‐based delimitation methods. These results document the continued range expansion of both species in the Dnipro River basin, including the first molecularly confirmed occurrence record of A. melas in this basin, previously known only from the Southern Buh and Danube basins. Genetic analysis revealed five COI haplotypes per species, most of which are new to Ukraine, a pattern consistent with multiple independent introduction events or the retention of standing genetic variation from diverse source populations. DAPC profiling identified body colouration, pectoral spine serration, anal fin membrane pigmentation, and gill raker count as the most robust diagnostic traits for reliable field delimitation. The observed lack of isolation‐by‐distance and the allopatric establishment of both species in adjacent water bodies support a ‘jumpy’ colonisation pattern driven by unauthorised human‐mediated translocations rather than natural dispersal. This study provides a scalable, integrated framework to resolve taxonomic ambiguities in cryptic or plastic invasive fish populations. Our findings establish an ecological baseline for range forecasting and risk assessment of Ameiurus in European inland waters, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated molecular monitoring at the leading edges of freshwater biological invasions.

articles.title: Deciphering the Interfacial Chemistry Governing Oriented Zinc Electrodeposition in Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
Interfacial Fe-O-Ni electron bridges endow single-atom Fe-N-C catalysts with superior oxygen redox performance

Low-Frequency Lattice Dynamics and Zinc Storage in an Intrinsic SnBi4Te7 van der Waals Superlattice

Shorebird Flyways Under Global Change: Governance for a Shifting World
Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
articles.abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio‐temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio‐temporal variation. Recent research extends STMs by also estimating density responses to habitat conditions at nearby locations using a “spatially distributed lag” (SDL) that averages habitat conditions in the vicinity of samples. Here, we extend the SDL by incorporating insights from diffusion‐enhanced STMs to simultaneously estimate spatially distributed and time‐lagged responses to nearby and past habitat conditions (a “spatio‐temporal distributed lag” STDL). We then use summer bottom trawl survey data from the eastern Bering Sea (1982–2024) to measure whether spatial and/or temporal lags are parsimonious when predicting population density from temperature anomalies for six ecologically important fishes. Results show that time‐lagged responses are parsimonious, positive, and substantial (correlation of 0.20–0.83 per year) for five species, and that density responses to temperature anomalies also diffuse outward over time for four species at 30–53 km per year. A self‐ and cross‐test simulation experiment shows that model selection can identify the appropriate model and that parameter estimates are approximately unbiased. We therefore conclude that temperature carryover effects arise in marine fishes and implement the method in the R package sdmTMB so that future studies can estimate nonlocal and time‐lagged responses when measuring density responses to habitat.

articles.title: Beyond the ground state: a spin-resolved reaction network for oxygen evolution reaction on NiOOH
Non-covalent aggregation as a general strategy to activate dipole-forbidden transitions for visible-to-red-light H2 evolution
Trees rely on both root‐based ‘do‐it‐yourself’ and mycorrhizal‐based ‘outsourcing’ adaptations to shifting soil nutrient availability during forest stand development
articles.abstract: This study shows that stand development decreases soil nitrogen and phosphorus availability and results in a shift from nitrogen limitation to phosphorus limitation. In response, there was a clear transition from trees depending more on root nutrient scavenging to trees relying more on both nitrogen scavenging by ectomycorrhizal fungi and root phosphorus mining as stands developed. Abstract Soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability generally decrease with forest stand development, yet how tree species acclimate to this decline remains largely unclear. The functional coordination hypothesis proposes that trees concurrently improve leaf nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to cope with nutrient deficiency. Conversely, the resource limitation hypothesis posits that trees prioritize either strategy, as simultaneous employment of both strategies is resource costly. To test these conflicting hypotheses, we leveraged a chronosequence of Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica stands with six age classes ranging from 16‐ to 62‐year‐old. We measured a comprehensive set of 70 plant and soil variables including needle nutrient retranslocation and resorption, and root architectural, morphological, physiological and mycorrhizal traits to assess the response of needle nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to changes in stand nutrient status. Stand development reduced soil N and P availability and caused a shift from N to P limitation as evidenced by increasing needle N:P ratios and decreasing N:P‐acquisition enzyme ratios. There was no evidence of N or P retranslocation from old to young needles, and nutrient resorption efficiency was independent of soil nutrient availability, indicating that adjustments of needle nutrient recycling contribute little to mitigating nutrient deficiency. Root length density decreased exponentially with stand development, whereas cord‐forming ectomycorrhizal fungi (EMF), root phosphatase activity and rhizosphere effects on plant‐available soil P logarithmically increased, implying a shift from root nutrient scavenging to combined EMF nutrient scavenging and root P mining. Synthesis. Our findings suggest that tree species do not necessarily rely on both improved recycling and acquisition to acclimate to soil nutrient scarcity with stand development. However, trees can simultaneously depend on physiological adaptations of absorptive fine roots themselves, as well as on a constrained selection of EMF. This reveals that complex sets of adaptations, both root‐based ‘do‐it‐yourself’ and mycorrhizal‐based ‘outsourcing’, can be effectively used by trees to cope with changes in soil nutrient availability.

articles.title: A Stable Terminal Mercury Hydride and Its Reactivity To Form Mercury–Metal Bonds
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Organomercury hydrides are typically encountered as unstable intermediates in organic transformations. These compounds are conventionally thought to be intrinsically unstable and have eluded isolation in the condensed phase. Here, we report the synthesis, isolation, characterization, and reactivity of an unexpectedly stable arylmercury hydride using a sterically encumbering fluorenyl-hydrindacene scaffold. The arylmercury hydride readily reacts with metalloradicals and metal hydrides to form bimetallic complexes containing unsupported mercury–metal bonds. These results suggest that the instability of mercury hydride compounds is not due to an intrinsic weakness of the mercury–hydrogen bond, but rather their propensity to undergo bimetallic reactions that result in mercury–mercury bond formation.

articles.title: Brain Transcriptomic Changes Associated With the Socially Regulated Behavioural Specialisation of Ant Queens
articles.abstract: Insect societies are characterised by a reproductive division of labour between queens that monopolise egg production and workers that perform all non‐reproductive tasks. The queen specialisation in egg laying is typically considered to be constitutive and independent of environmental conditions, but this common assumption was recently challenged by the finding that the presence of workers both induces and maintains the queen specialisation in several species of ants. However, the molecular changes that translate worker presence into queen behavioural specialisation remain unknown. To investigate the transcriptomic basis of the socially regulated specialisation of ant queens, we produced 93 individual brain transcriptomes from queens of the black garden ant Lasius niger that were experimentally maintained in different social environments. Our transcriptomic analyses revealed that 123 genes were differentially expressed between the brains of queens maintained with and without workers. These genes were enriched for processes related to brain energy metabolism and neuronal plasticity and signalling. By investigating the response of selected genes of interest to further manipulations of the social environment, we identified four candidate genes that fully mirrored the queen behavioural changes. Specifically, their expression changes in response to worker presence were reversible and they did not respond to mere cues of the worker presence. These candidate genes included the transcription factor Krüppel‐homologue 1 and other genes in the juvenile hormone and insulin signalling pathways, both known to regulate multiple aspects of division of labour in social insects. By producing a robust, well‐replicated and well‐controlled investigation of the transcriptomic basis of the behavioural specialisation of ant queens, this study provides a better understanding of the emergence and maintenance of reproductive division of labour in insect societies.

articles.title: Relationships Among MHC Diversity, Parasites and Secondary Sexual Colouration
articles.abstract: Sexual selection via honest (costly) signals of fitness can generate patterns in immunogenetic diversity at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). MHC diversity explains variation in immunocompetence—and therefore fitness—thus impacting the ability to generate honest signals. Differences in guppy (Poecilia reticulata) colour patterns can be driven by opposing selection pressures of predation and female mate choice, but the effect of parasitism has received less attention. By studying 21 wild guppy populations in Trinidad, we sought to quantify covariation among parasitic Gyrodactylus spp. infections, male sexual ornamentation (orange and black colouration) and genetic variation at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) at both individual and population levels. We found population level support for a correlation between MHC diversity and Gyrodactylus prevalence, including an overall association between MHC supertype composition and prevalence. At the individual level, supertype (functional) diversity again emerged as a more informative measure than allelic richness alone. Predation was associated with Gyrodactylus prevalence and orange, but not black, colouration. Notably, some of these relationships differed between the individual and population levels. Further, much of this variation was explained by processes acting at a broader geographic scale within river drainages, which comprise divergent guppy lineages. These findings suggest that evolutionary history and processes such as genetic drift and gene flow contribute substantially to these relationships, but that ecological variation (i.e., predation) interacts with these processes. Our findings indicate that multi‐trait relationships between colour, immunogenetic diversity and infection are best examined within their broader evolutionary and ecological contexts.

articles.title: High-Contrast Broadband Optical Edge Detection by Low-Loss Geometric Phase Gratings
articles.abstract: Optical edge detection is emerging as a key technique in image processing owing to its merits of large-scale and real-time operation. However, achieving both broadband and high-contrast functionality remains challenging. While broadband optical edge detection has been demonstrated using nanograting-based geometric phase (GP) gratings, the relatively low image contrast limits their effectiveness. Here, we demonstrate high-efficiency nanopore-based GP gratings by ultrafast laser writing in silica glass, enabling high-contrast and broadband edge detection. A maximum contrast of 0.97 is achieved at 515 nm, approaching the theoretical limit of unity. We further show that the edge detection contrast and spatial resolution are influenced by the period of the GP gratings. Moreover, the nanopore-based GP gratings exhibit broadband performance from 450 to 2000 nm and support both one-dimensional and two-dimensional edge detection. Finally, we demonstrate edge detection capability in complex environments, e.g., through water or silicon at appropriate wavelengths.

articles.title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
articles.abstract: Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

articles.title: Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
articles.abstract: Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.

articles.title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

articles.title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
articles.abstract: During liver regeneration, EGF upregulates PRMT1, leading to increased asymmetric arginine dimethylation at R81 of SKP1. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation.

articles.title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
articles.abstract: DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
articles.abstract: Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

articles.title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
articles.abstract: Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.

articles.title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
articles.abstract: Volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms.

articles.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI
Aligning auxin supply to developmental demand in adventitious rooting
articles.abstract: The dose–time program of adventitious root (AR) formation. Summary Adventitious root (AR) formation is the developmental process that makes vegetative propagation possible, underpinning forestry, horticulture, and the clonal multiplication of elite and hard‐to‐propagate genotypes. Despite a detailed understanding of auxin's stage‐specific roles across the rooting program, propagation practice still treats auxin supply as a quantity to set rather than a profile to match. We argue that this produces a temporal mismatch between auxin supply and developmental demand: the available evidence shows that exogenous auxin availability frequently declines before the stages it should support are complete, particularly in slow‐to‐root and recalcitrant species, where developmental timelines are longest. New delivery tools, such as slow‐release conjugates, encapsulation systems, and selective auxin agonists, now make time‐structured delivery profiles feasible, but realizing their potential requires a different starting point. Rather than optimizing auxin dose empirically against rooting outcome, the field should characterize the spatiotemporal auxin demand curve across AR stages and design delivery profiles to match it. We outline the conceptual framework for this shift and the experimental approaches now available to support it.

articles.title: Aridity reshapes leaf and root trait dispersion through distinct microbial pathways
articles.abstract: Piecewise structural equation model and decomposition of standardized effects. Summary Aridity is a primary driver of plant community assembly, yet most trait-based studies focus on mean traits rather than trait dispersion. Soil microbes may mediate plant responses to aridity, but whether leaf and root trait dispersion responds to aridity through shared or distinct microbial pathways remains unclear. Using 535 species-by-plot records (247 species) along an aridity gradient in north-west China, we quantified four leaf and four root traits, soil properties, microbial diversity and composition, and microbial carbon use efficiency. We tested whether aridity differentially regulates leaf vs root functional dispersion (FD is ), and whether these responses are associated with different microbial predictors. Leaf traits shifted more consistently with aridity and were more tightly linked to environmental variation than root traits. Leaf FD is negatively correlated with CUE, whereas root FD is negatively correlated with fungal diversity and bacterial community composition. These associations weakened toward less arid sites. Structural equation modeling further showed that leaf FD is linked primarily to microbial functioning, whereas root FD is linked more strongly to microbial diversity and composition. Our results reveal that aridity reshapes trait dispersion through organ-specific plant–microbe pathways, highlighting that predicting dryland community responses to increasing drought must treat above- and belowground traits separately.

articles.title: Fruit color and size provide reliable signals of macronutritional rewards for seed dispersers
articles.abstract: Here, we reveal that fruit color and size traits signaled macronutrient reward specifically relating to bird‐, mammal‐, and mixed‐dispersed dispersal syndromes. Birds prioritize fruit color, while mammals prioritize fruit size to achieve optimal macronutritional reward, and these signal‐mutualist relationships are shaped by associated disperser traits, demonstrating co‐evolutionary mechanisms driving adaptive differentiation of fruit morphological and macronutrient traits. Our findings connect classical dispersal‐syndrome research with more recent developments in signal theory, trait‐matching theory, optimal foraging theory, and nutritional geometry theory, thus advancing the seed disperser mutualism paradigm. Summary Fruit color and size provide vital cues for determining seed dispersers' preferences; however, any consistent underlying link between these traits and fruit macronutritional rewards remains to be established by large‐scale analyses. We collated a global database comprising 2626 observations of 1626 fruiting plant species from 460 global sites to test whether fruit color and size traits do indeed consistently signal macronutritional rewards to frugivores. We found that consistent fruit color and size signaled macronutrient reward specifically relating to bird‐, mammal‐, and mixed‐dispersed dispersal syndromes. Lipids were the predominant macronutrient in black, blue, red, orange, and yellow fruits with birds (27.24%), whereas sugar predominated in mammal‐dispersed fruits (72.55%). Fruits dispersed by mammals (25.55 mm) were consistently larger than those dispersed by birds (10.17 mm) regardless of fruit color, and total macronutrient mass per fruit increased with fruit size. These signal‐mutualist relationships are shaped by associated disperser traits, demonstrating co‐evolutionary mechanisms driving adaptive differentiation of fruit morphological and macronutrient traits. By integrating the disperser syndrome hypothesis and signal theory with nutritional geometry theory and trait‐matching theory, our study expounds the role of seed disperser selective preferences in the evolution of fruit traits, thus advancing the seed disperser mutualism paradigm.

articles.title: Rethinking RNAi efficiency: the role of fungal lifestyle in HIGS and SIGS success
Rice bZIP11 acts as a transcriptional repressor that negatively regulates photosynthesis in response to nitrogen deficiency
articles.abstract: Phenotypes of 43‐d‐old wild‐type (WT), Osbzip11‐KO, and OsbZIP11‐OX seedlings grown under control N and low N conditions. Summary Nitrogen (N)‐deficiency responses, which are closely linked to plant biomass and crop yield, differ between plant tissues. A previous in silico analysis suggested that four transcription factors, including OsbZIP11, play vital roles in the gene regulatory network governing N‐deficiency responses (NDRs) in rice roots. To investigate the role of OsbZIP11 in NDRs, the phenotypes, functional responses, and gene expression of rice plants that either lacked functional OsbZIP11 or overexpressed OsbZIP11 were analyzed. Contrary to expectations, OsbZIP11 function showed an overwhelmingly stronger association with photosynthetic gene expression than with any other physiological process, including the expression control of N‐related genes. OsbZIP11 directly suppressed numerous photosynthetic genes as a transcriptional repressor. N deficiency increased OsbZIP11 expression in shoots, consistent with N deficiency‐reduced photosynthetic activity. Furthermore, removing functional OsbZIP11 and OsbZIP11 overexpression produced opposite effects on the expression of genes involved in the light‐dependent reactions of photosynthesis and carbon dioxide fixation, as well as on growth and grain yield. These findings indicate that OsbZIP11 is a critical factor responsible for N deficiency‐induced decreases in photosynthesis in rice and provide new insights into the mechanism underlying the coordination of C and N acquisition. まとめ 植物のバイオマスや作物の収量と密接に関連する窒素(N)欠乏応答は、植物組織によって異なる。これまでに計算科学的手法により、OsbZIP11を含む4つの転写因子が、イネの根における窒素欠乏応答を制御する遺伝子調節ネットワークにおいて重要な役割を果たしていることが示唆されていた。 窒素欠乏応答におけるOsbZIP11の役割を解明するため、機能的なOsbZIP11を欠くイネおよびOsbZIP11遺伝子を過剰発現させたイネの表現型、機能的応答、および遺伝子発現を解析した。 予想に反して、OsbZIP11の機能は、窒素関連遺伝子の発現制御を含む他のいかなる生理的プロセスよりも、光合成関連遺伝子の発現と圧倒的に強い関連性を示した。OsbZIP11は転写抑制因子として多数の光合成関連遺伝子の発現を直接的に抑制しており、また、窒素欠乏による光合成活性の低下と一致して、地上部におけるOsbZIP11遺伝子の発現量は窒素欠乏により増加した。さらに、機能的なOsbZIP11の除去とOsbZIP11遺伝子の過剰発現は、光合成の光依存反応や二酸化炭素固定に関与する遺伝子の発現、ならびに生育や穀粒収量に対して、正反対の影響をもたらした。 これらの知見は、OsbZIP11がイネにおける窒素欠乏による光合成低下を担う重要な転写因子であることを示しており、植物における炭素と窒素の獲得の協調的制御を司るメカニズムに関する新たな知見を提供するものである。

articles.title: Thermal acclimation as an emergent property of economically optimal photosynthesis
articles.abstract: Observed vs modelled relationships between (a) T opt and growth temperature and (b) normalised A opt and growth temperature for different species. Summary Leaf-level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis (T opt) increasing with growth temperature (T growth). We investigated how this behaviour emerges in the P model, a primary production model based on eco-evolutionary optimality hypotheses. We evaluated the P model estimates against experimental data for three herbaceous species grown at different temperatures and examined mechanisms underlying the responses of T opt and the photosynthetic rate at T opt (A opt). The model yields a realistic increase in T opt with T growth and a peaked relationship between A opt and T growth. These responses emerge largely from adjustment of the stomatal sensitivity parameter ξ, which determines the internal-to-ambient CO2 ratio (c i : c a) and its sensitivity to vapour pressure deficit. Rubisco kinetics (K) does not acclimate in the model, but its temperature dependence enters acclimation through optimality, mainly via ξ, shifting T opt. The decline in A opt at high growth temperatures, often attributed to heat stress, reflects the narrowing gap between T opt and T growth because the T opt shift has a slope below one. The P model provides a mechanistic explanation for observed trends in T opt and A opt and a scalable approach for representing biochemical and stomatal acclimation in land-surface models.

articles.title: 24-hour time-use behaviors and maternal depressive symptoms during early pregnancy: Compositional data analysis
articles.abstract: Background: Previous research suggested that modifiable health factors such as physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep (i.e., 24-hour time-use behaviors) were potential intervention targets to improve antenatal depressive symptoms. However, most previous studies examine one behavior at a time, ignoring their co-dependence. The aim of this study was to examine the association between 24-hour time-use behaviors and depressive symptoms during early pregnancy. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis using baseline data from the Health and Behaviors in Transition (HABIT) trial. Pregnant participants with pre-pregnancy body mass index [≥]25 kg/m2 wore a wrist-worn ActiGraph for seven consecutive days to estimate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), light physical activity (LPA), inactivity (IA), and sleep. We used compositional data analysis with an isometric log-ratio transformation to examine associations with depressive symptoms, quantified by the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), adjusting for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and cohabitation status. G-computation was applied to estimate the marginal mean of depressive symptoms at specified durations of each behavior, with the remaining time reallocated proportionally among the other behaviors. Results: A total of 255 participants with median EPDS score of 5.0 (IQR, 2.0-8.0) had geometric mean 24-hour behaviors of MVPA = 75.5 min/day (5.2%), LPA = 311.2 min/day (21.6%), IA = 593.9 min/day (41.2%), and sleep = 459.4 min/day (31.9%). 24-hour time-use behaviors were not significantly associated with EPDS scores, and marginal mean EPDS scores showed minimal changes (MVPA 10 min: 6.51 (95% CI 4.22, 9.64) vs 40 min: 5.97 (95% CI 5.03, 6.97); sleep 300 min: 5.41 (95% CI 4.56, 6.22) vs 480 min: 5.81 (95% CI 5.23, 6.39)). Conclusions: In this relatively active pregnant population, 24-hour time-use behaviors were not associated with depressive symptoms. Future research can examine later trimesters or other populations that are more sedentary or more depressed.

articles.title: Agreement of abdominal palpation with point-of-care ultrasound for hepatosplenic organomegaly: a cross-sectional, population-based study in schistosomiasis-endemic settings of rural Uganda
articles.abstract: Background: Ultrasound is commonly used to assess hepatosplenic morbidity in schistosomiasis, but access may be limited in resource-constrained settings. Abdominal palpation is simple and inexpensive, yet its clinical value and diagnostic performance for detecting ultrasound-defined organ enlargement remains uncertain. We evaluated standardised abdominal palpation against point-of-care ultrasound in a schistosomiasis-endemic setting in rural Uganda. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study in January-February 2024 of 3177 participants aged 5-92 years from Pakwach, Buliisa and Mayuge districts in the SchistoTrack cohort. Trained nurses who also had midwifery skills performed standardised liver and spleen palpation, assessing palpability, extension, consistency and tenderness. Palpation agreement was assessed against point-of-care B-mode ultrasound performed by sonographers with organ dimensions classified using height-standardised internal reference values. We estimated sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and Cohen's {kappa} for palpation against ultrasound-defined liver and spleen enlargement and assessed associations between liver consistency and tenderness, and schistosomal periportal fibrosis examined from ultrasound. Results: Spleen palpation had high specificity (98.4%), with sensitivity ranging from 10.9% for moderate splenomegaly to 48.6% for severe splenomegaly. There was strong agreement with ultrasound for severe splenomegaly ({kappa}=0.57) though weak agreement for moderate splenomegaly ({kappa}=0.14). Liver palpation had high specificity (97.7%) but very low sensitivity (3.4-7.3%) and minimal agreement with any hepatomegaly found from ultrasound ({kappa}=0.02-0.04). Among participants with a palpable liver, schistosomal periportal fibrosis was more frequent in those with firm/hard than soft liver consistency (53.3%, n=24/45 vs 8.6%, n=3/35; {chi}2=17.64, p<0.001); while tenderness was not associated with schistosomal periportal fibrosis. Nurses additionally identified clinically relevant findings, including umbilical collaterals, abdominal swelling, and abdominal or hypochondrial pain and tenderness. Conclusions: Standardised abdominal palpation cannot replace ultrasound for comprehensive detection or exclusion of hepatosplenomegaly. Nevertheless, severe ultrasound-defined splenomegaly was more readily detected by palpation, while liver consistency and other clinical findings provided information beyond organomegaly. In schistosomiasis-endemic settings with limited access to ultrasound, further research is needed to assess building capacity for abdominal palpation and how it can be combined with clinical information to increase clinical suspicion while possibly informing low-cost strategies for triage and referral.

articles.title: Applications of large language model in general practice: a qualitative interview study with professionals and patients
articles.abstract: Background: Workload is increasing in general practice. Large language models (LLMs) are a promising tool that could relieve part of this workload. However, existing studies offer little insight into how professionals and patients want specific LLM applications to be implemented in practice. Objectives: This study aimed to prioritize a broad range of LLM applications in general practice and identify the benefits, risks, and requirements of each application. Methods: We conducted semi-structured one-on-one interviews with 12 general practitioners (GPs), 7 GP assistants, 6 practice nurses, and 6 patient representatives in the Netherlands between October and December 2025. To guide the interviews, we developed a list of 21 LLM applications derived from literature, existing tools, and GP input. Application were divided into 5 categories: administrative tasks, pre-consultation and triage, clinical decision support, management of (chronic) diseases, and patient interaction and communication. Participants discussed and prioritized each application. Transcripts were analyzed with a combined deductive and inductive approach. Results: Priorities for LLM applications differed by group: GPs favored clinical decision support, assistants favored triage, and practice nurses and patient representatives favored chronic disease management. The most prioritized applications were summarizing consultations and triage and urgency classification (high priority 18/31; 58%), followed by clarification of medical information around the consultation (14/31; 45%). The qualitative analysis revealed three recurring considerations when applying LLMs for different tasks. First, participants questioned whether an LLM is needed, as simpler or existing tools may suffice. Second, they questioned whether LLMs relieve workload or create extra work. Third, a possible benefit on workload has to explicitly be weighed against risks such as mistakes, reduced personal care and accessibility, and negative effects on professionals. Conclusions: Professionals and patients see potential for LLM support across many areas of general practice. Realizing this potential requires three steps: critically assessing whether an LLM is the right tool, establishing that it relieves workload, and designing applications so that their benefits outweigh the risks. Our application-level prioritization and analysis provide a starting point for assessment and design.

articles.title: Copper Catalyzed Highly Enantioselective B–H Insertion of α-Alkynyl-α-silyl Carbenes for the Synthesis of Chiral Propargylic gem -Silylboranes
articles.abstract: Chiral gem-silylboronates represent a class of pivotal gem-dimetallic reagents in organic chemistry. Despite various synthetic methods emerged recently, the structural diversity of gem-silylboronates remains largely confined to alkyl-, (hetero)aryl-, and alkenyl-substituted variants; notably, alkynyl-substituted counterparts have remained largely underexplored. Herein, we report a Cu(I)/chiral bisoxazoline-catalyzed asymmetric insertion of α-alkynyl silyl carbenes into B–H bonds, affording a series of propargyl chiral gem-silylboronates and thus expanding the repertoire of organo-gem-dimetallics. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and diverse downstream transformations, demonstrating significant synthetic utility. Furthermore, mechanistic experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the reaction proceeds via a concerted carbene insertion into the B–H bond, which likely serves as the rate-determining step. The enantioselectivity arises mainly from the shielding of the carbene Re face by the aryl groups on the oxazoline indenyl moiety, directing borane attack to the Si face, with additional enhancement from π–π interactions between the pyridine and indene rings. This work provides an efficient approach to chiral propargyl gem-silylboronates, further enriching the structural diversity and synthetic potential of chiral organosilicon–boron chemistry.

articles.title: Sub-nanofluidic Photochemical Membrane with Catalytically Active Channels for Solar Ammonia Synthesis
articles.abstract: Solar-driven conversion of N2 and H2O into ammonia under ambient conditions offers an alternative to the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, yet current advances are largely limited by material-focused strategies that insufficiently address coupled transport and interfacial reaction processes. Herein, we report a sub-nanofluidic photochemical membrane with catalytically active channels that integrate light harvesting, catalytic activation, and mass transport within a unified architecture for solar ammonia synthesis. The membrane consists of ZnIn2S4 atomically thin sheets and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) quantum monolayers, forming ordered sub-nanometer channels that are intrinsically catalytic. This design establishes a confined reaction environment in which nanofluidic transport, gas–liquid interfacial regulation, and charge carrier dynamics are synergistically coupled. In particular, the combination of hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces and sub-nanofluidic-engineered serpentine flow pathways enhances reactant accessibility, residence time, and photon utilization, thereby overcoming diffusion and activation limitations typical of conventional photocatalytic systems. With these merits, the membrane achieves an ammonia production rate of 4.39 μg cm–2 h–1 (2.48 mmol gcat.–1 h–1) with ∼70% ammonia selectivity and maintains stable operation over 48 h of continuous testing. The achieved ammonia production rate compares favorably with those of reported photocatalytic platforms and some electrocatalytic N2 fixation systems. This work introduces a catalytically active nanofluidic channel paradigm for solar-driven N2 fixation and highlights the importance of material-transport co-engineering in bridging the gap between nanoscale catalytic design and device-level performance for chemical synthesis.

articles.title: Subnanometer Ni@Fe Catalysts Enable High-Performance and Stable Oxygen Evolution of WO3 Photoanodes
articles.abstract: NiFe-based catalysts are highly active for the oxygen evolution reaction, but their precise fabrication on photoanodes at subnanometer scale for accelerating charge transport and maximizing active sites remains a challenge. Herein, we report a facile approach to deposit trimesic acid (TA) coordinated subnanometer Ni@Fe hydroxides (Ni-TA-Fe) on nanoporous WO3 photoanodes. This WO3/Ni-TA-Fe photoanode exhibited a record photocurrent density of ∼2.4 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE under AM 1.5 G irradiation (100 mW cm–2) with an enhanced stability, which is much higher than that of pristine WO3 photoanodes. Comparative experiments, characterizations, and density functional theory calculations revealed that the subnanometer Ni catalyst layers could effectively inhibit the dissolution of W atoms from the surface lattice and promote the structural stability of the WO3 photoanode during PEC water oxidation. Furthermore, the strong coordination and electron-trapping capability of TA could efficiently promote charge redistribution in Fe catalyst layers, resulting in the activation and transformation of surface Fe sites into high-valence Fe4+ species for significantly improving the OER activity. This work provides the viable pathway to active and durable bimetallic catalysts to achieve high-performance and stable PEC water splitting.

articles.title: Transference Number of Electrolytes at Infinite Dilution
articles.abstract: Understanding ion transport in the limit of infinite dilution is necessary for predicting the performance of electrochemical devices. While transport properties like ionic conductivity and diffusion coefficient can be readily extrapolated to zero concentration, establishing a reliable approach for determining the cation transference number with respect to the solvent velocity, t+0, remains a challenge. To address this challenge, we introduce an approach based on Newman's concentrated solution theory and fundamental dilute-limit constraints. We validate the approach using experimental data for a poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)/ sodium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NaTFSI) electrolyte and derive a simple quadratic equation relating t+0 to readily measurable transport properties. Our approach has the potential to provide more accurate models of concentration gradients and limiting current in electrochemical systems, thereby improving their use in design and optimization.

articles.title: Ultralow Deposition Potential and Antisite-Boosted Diffusivity of Li3Ga2 Anode for All-Solid-State Batteries
articles.abstract: Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10–8 cm2 s–1). The high Li atomic diffusivity primarily originates from moderate Li/Ga antisite mixing, stabilizing the anode-solid electrolyte interface and enabling a high critical current density of 24 mA cm–2 in ASSLBs. Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.

articles.title: Third-Eigenmode Atomic Force Microscopy for Resolving Solvation Structures and Structural Defects in Organic Semiconductor Films under Ambient Conditions
articles.abstract: Organic semiconductor molecules are key elements for the development of next-generation flexible and lightweight electronic devices. Their performance is largely governed by molecular arrangement within thin films, whereas environmental sensing is governed by surface functionality and mediated by the interfacial structure at the solid–gas interface. However, experimental tools capable of accessing such information with molecular-scale resolution remain scarce. Here, we employ third-eigenmode atomic force microscopy (AFM) with moderately compliant cantilevers to directly probe the interfacial solvation structure of the liquid layer formed at the interface between small-molecule organic semiconductor thin films and the ambient gas environment. This approach also enables true molecular-resolution imaging across molecular steps, providing detailed insight into interplanar molecular organization and crystal growth mechanisms. Overall, our results establish third-eigenmode AFM as a versatile methodology for high-resolution characterization of molecular packing and for elucidating the relationship between surface functionality and interfacial structure in organic semiconductor materials.

articles.title: X-ray Crystallography of a Nanobody/JAM-1 Complex Informs Barrier Weakening and Enhanced Drug Permeability in a Cellular Blood–Brain Barrier Model
articles.abstract: For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.
