By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In2O3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 1018 cm−3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 1010∼1011 cm−2·eV−1. We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement‐mode transistors with sub‐3 nm channels, featuring near‐zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate‐stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high‐performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next‐generation nanoelectronics.

articles.title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis, resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis. Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

articles.title: Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer
articles.abstract: Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge‐transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi‐hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge‐transfer energetics. Using a sulfur‐rich amorphous CoReS2+x cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi‐hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron‐deficient interfacial state. This adsorption‐driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first‐principles calculations. The resulting a‐CoReS2+x/CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass‐derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi‐adsorbate‐induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy‐conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.

articles.title: Near‐Infrared Imaging of H2O2 in Plants With Nanosensors Under Environmentally Changing Conditions
articles.abstract: Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion, and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H2O2. Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H2O2 sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ∼1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EB–NS, 900–955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (∼641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind‐induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H2O2 monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single‐channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress‐induced H2O2 under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference‐resistant optical sensing and advances field‐deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.

articles.title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt‐Free Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
articles.abstract: Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li+ transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi0.948Al0.045Te0.007O2 containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and c‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li+ migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g−1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.

articles.title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
articles.abstract: Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard‐to‐access environments, while providing integrated self‐sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next‐generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath‐core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near‐infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load‐bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real‐time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self‐sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

articles.title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen (1O2) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of 1O2. Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

articles.title: Bismuth–Sulfur Engineered Zero‐Valent Iron Prioritizes Chloramphenicol‐Class Antibiotics Dechlorination Over Hydrogen Evolution and Nitro Reduction
articles.abstract: Chloramphenicol (CAP) and florfenicol (FF), as chloramphenicol‐class antibiotics, often coexist in wastewater, where chlorine substituents largely determine their toxicity. Although zero‐valent iron (ZVI) is a promising reductive remediation material, its poor chemoselectivity and preferential electron consumption by hydrogen evolution (HER) and nitro‐reduction severely limit the detoxification of chlorinated moieties. Herein, we develop bismuth–sulfur co‐intercalated ZVI (Bi‐S‐ZVI) to reduce CAP+FF co‐contaminants, achieving enhanced nitro‐reduction (22–74‐fold), dechlorination (175–419‐fold), and low HER. Notably, the dechlorination selectivity (defined as the ratio of FF dechlorination to CAP nitro‐reduction) increased from 0.3%–2% to 39%, and Bi‐S‐ZVI enabled a distinct pathway where dechlorination preceded nitro‐reduction in the ‐NO2/‐Cl co‐substituted CAP molecule. Mechanistically, Bi2S3 and Bi0 are the dominant contributors to the reactivity and dechlorination selectivity of Bi‐S‐ZVI, respectively. Bi2S3 couples galvanically with Fe0 to generate a built‐in electric field and creates Fe–S–Bi charge‐transfer channels to accelerate electron transport. Bi0 selectively associates with ─Cl as a halogen‐bond acceptor. Bi2S3 and Bi0 synergistically suppress HER by increasing surface hydrophobicity and hindering atomic hydrogen recombination, while Bi2S3 further disrupts the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network. This work provides a cost‐effective and scalable strategy for selective reductive remediation, overcoming the reactivity–selectivity–stability trade‐offs of existing iron materials.

articles.title: Bright Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots via Organic Dication Compensatory Doping
articles.abstract: Tin halide perovskite quantum dots (THP QDs) are promising alternatives to their lead analogs for red and near‐infrared emission. However, cation vacancies cause strong p‐doping, limiting the photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of quantum‐confined THP QDs. Low formation energies of charged cation vacancies hinder doping control through stoichiometry alone, while effective aliovalent doping strategies for extrinsic control of carrier concentrations remain lacking. Here, we establish organic dications, such as ethylenediammonium (EN), as effective electron‐donor dopants for THP QDs. Aliovalent A‐cation substitution compensates the p‐character, enhancing the PLQY by over two orders of magnitude. CsSnI3‐EN QDs ranging in size from 4 to 16 nm emit beyond 750 nm with PLQYs up to 38%. Enhancements extend to various dications and hybrid FASnI3 QDs. The pristine, hole‐doped THP QDs exhibit a size‐dependent infrared absorption band arising from valence‐to‐valence intraband transitions, which disappears upon compensatory EN doping. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals increased core‐level binding energies for all three perovskite constituents, consistent with a Fermi level shift of approximately 0.1 eV away from the valence band. Density functional theory calculations corroborate this finding and elucidate the defect equilibria. These results establish organic dications as donor dopants for near‐infrared emissive THP QDs.

articles.title: Engineering Rapid Payload Release Rate in 1,6‐Elimination Processes of Self‐Immolative Linkers
articles.abstract: Stimuli‐responsive prodrugs form the foundation of targeted medicine. These compounds, once activated at the site of interest, release their bioactive payload, often through elimination from self‐immolative linkers (SILs). However, payload release rates from activated SILs can vary widely depending on the SIL's (electronic) structure. Low release rates do not compete with diffusion of the activated prodrug from the target site, which compromises the spatial resolution and diminishes the practical utility. Here we report a new strategy to engineer the payload release rate from SILs through the introduction of cation‐stabilizing substituents, which yields an up to 104‐fold improvement in rate constant compared to the reference SIL. Relating the DFT‐computed stabilities of an ion pair intermediate with the first order rate constants for self‐immolation revealed a strong correlation, providing a robust rational basis for our strategy. Furthermore, we discovered that lipophilicity of the SIL‐payload conjugate is a key, and hitherto overlooked, factor affecting the rate, based on which we propose a new model for the overall payload release reaction. Lastly, we show the practical utility of our strategy, through demonstrating the superiority of our SILs in releasing the anticancer drug palbociclib and studying radiation‐dependent enzyme inhibition and cell‐cycle alteration.

articles.title: Engineering Steric‐Hindrance‐Guided Crystalline Vacancies in a Scalable Pillared‐Layer Nickel‐MOF for Efficient Gas Uptake and Separation
articles.abstract: Engineering local vacancies in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) presents a promising route to high‐performance gas adsorption/separation, yet conventional defect engineering often yields statistically distributed vacancies. Here, we report a steric‐hindrance‐programmed strategy to construct periodically ordered vacancies in pillared‐layer LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H2O via de novo synthesis by changing pyrazine linkers in a full‐pillared reference TJE‐1 to bulkier triethylenediamine ligands, resulting in missing‐pillars to produce potential vacancies in a regularly staggered interlayer fashion. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction unambiguously identifies the alternating pillar/vacancy arrangement, and digestion 1H NMR supports overall stoichiometry. Removing capped water molecules converts LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H2O into LIFM‐Ni‐3 with complete exposure of the open‐metal Ni2+‐sites, reshaping the local pore to form a contracted Window‐I and an enlarged Window‐II bearing open‐metal sites for molecular accessing and binding. LIFM‐Ni‐3 enables efficient separation processes: adsorbing SF6 at Window‐II with 2.64 mmol g−1 uptake at 0.1 bar while excluding N2, and purifying CH4 by removing minor C2H6/C3H8 from natural gas with an exceptional productivity of 13.5 mmol g−1. This represents a rare example that features simultaneously high capacity and selectivity by overcoming capacity–selectivity trade‐off, and combines favorable low‐pressure capture with fast apparent uptake responses. The scale‐up experiment testifies reliability of this pillar‐displacing approach for mass production and scalable gas separation.

articles.title: Flexible‐Ligand Rigidification Enables Anti‐Thermal‐Quenching Emission and Cryogenic Afterglow in Antimony‐Based Hybrid Bimetallic Halides
articles.abstract: Limited by the flexible and dynamic natures of organic ligands, designing organic‐inorganic hybrid halides with robust luminescence at elevated temperatures remains a critical challenge. Herein, we demonstrate that rigidifying flexible urea‐type ligands within bimetallic hybrid chlorides provides an effective route to anti‐thermal‐quenching (ATQ) self‐trapped‐exciton (STE) emission and cryogenic afterglow in a single crystalline platform. A family of zero‐dimensional hybrid bimetallic chlorides, [RE(DEU)6]SbCl6 (RE = La, Ce, Eu, Gd, Tb, Y, Lu; DEU = N,N‐diethylurea), is synthesized via low‐temperature solution evaporation. All compounds exhibit broadband STE emissions with high photoluminescence (PL) quantum yields (90.24%–95.32%) and pronounced ATQ luminescence. Temperature‐dependent spectroscopy and structural analyses reveal exceptionally strong electron‐phonon coupling combined with a hydrogen‐bond‐locked, weakly expanding lattice, which together suppress thermally activated PL quenching. Moreover, the DEU network underpins blue prompt emission and green afterglow at cryogenic temperatures, enabling dual‐channel exciton management between organic DEU parts and inorganic [SbCl6]3− centers. Radius‐encoded tuning across the RE3+ series links ionic size, lattice rigidity, and ATQ performance, highlighting the role of the RE3+ ions as an effective structure‐rigidity‐property tuner rather than just a structural linker. This work establishes a flexible‐ligand rigidification paradigm for designing thermally resistant and multifunctional Sb‐based hybrid luminescent materials.

articles.title: Inside Back Cover: Direct Observation of Radical‐Mediated Oxide‐to‐Alloy Transformation in Solution Under Pulsed Laser Irradiation
articles.abstract: In the Research Article e8536600, Joonghan Kim, Tae Wu Kim, Myong Yong Choi, and co‐workers reveal how pulsed laser irradiation converts NiCo2O4 into NiCo alloy. Time‐resolved in situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and DFTB molecular dynamics show facile hydrogen atom transfer from ethanol to lattice oxygen, whereas entropy‐driven oxygen release requires transient local temperatures near 1000 K, set by laser fluence.

articles.title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
articles.abstract: Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1, COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H+/4e–ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3. The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm−2, outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

articles.title: Molecular Glue Degraders of TEM β‐Lactamases by Periplasmic Protease DegP
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is one of the most serious challenges to global health, yet the development of new molecules with novel mechanisms of action to combat resistance is lacking. In this study, we report the discovery of molecular glues that recruit TEM‐family β‐lactamases to the bacterial protease DegP for degradation. β‐Lactamase inhibitor tazobactam was found to accelerate degradation of TEM β‐lactamases by DegP, which was further enhanced by linkerless incorporation of dipeptide motifs enriched among DegP substrates. The resulting molecular glue degraders showed improved synergy with β‐lactam piperacillin against resistant Escherichia coli compared to tazobactam, as well as good pharmacokinetic properties for oral dosing. Collectively, this work establishes periplasmic targeted protein degradation as a promising new mechanism for combating β‐lactamase resistance.

articles.title: Photocatalytically Generated Nitrate Radicals Drive Decomposition of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
articles.abstract: Nitrate radicals (NO3•) generated in irradiated aqueous TiO2 suspensions at acidic pH drive decomposition of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The key role played by NO3• is demonstrated by the dependence of the reaction rate on the initial concentration of nitrate ions and by scavenging tests. The amount of nitrate ions remains constant during the process, indicating its catalytic behavior. The existence of nitrate radicals under the given conditions is here for the first time directly demonstrated by time‐resolved transient absorption spectroscopy. The process achieves ∼90% degradation of PFOA in 9 h with ca. 57% fluoride liberation. Theoretical results suggest that nitrate radicals trigger water‐mediated hydrogen atom transfer from the protonated PFOA, followed by decarboxylation and hydroxylation to the corresponding alcohol (experimentally detected), which eventually evolves to shorter‐chain intermediates. The proposed process represents the first proof of concept of the reactivity of NO3• with PFAS, but more importantly may be of practical relevance when coupled with the acidic regeneration of adsorbents currently used for remediation of water effluents containing PFAS.

articles.title: Radiation‐Triggered Catalytic Decaging in Living Mice
articles.abstract: Precise spatiotemporal control over chemical reactivity in living systems remains a formidable challenge, especially within deep tissues where light‐based methods suffer from limited penetration. Here, we present a γ‐radiation‐mediated catalytic decaging (γ‐RCD) strategy that harnesses hydrated electrons generated during low‐dose γ‐radiation to activate palladium catalysts, thereby initiating a catalytic cycle for the efficient release of functional molecules. Unlike conventional radiation‐triggered decaging, which relies on primary radiolytic species and suffers from inherently low yields, γ‐RCD achieves catalytic amplification, significantly enhancing radiochemical efficiency with G‐values up to 25.8‐surpassing existing radiation chemistries by at least 20‐fold. We demonstrate the versatility of γ‐RCD in remotely activating fluorophores, as well as prodrugs with minimal radiation input. The selective activation of caged bioactive compounds in tumor‐bearing mice leads to potent antitumor effects and the translational potential of the γ‐RCD strategy. By integrating catalytic amplification with clinically relevant γ‐radiation, γ‐RCD opens a new avenue for precision medicine, functional biomaterials, and radiation‐responsive therapeutics.

articles.title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
articles.abstract: Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g−1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g−1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

articles.title: The Elusive [B(ReO4)4]− Anion in the Non‐Centrosymmetric Crystal Structure of K[B(ReO4)4]
articles.abstract: The reaction of KReO4 with B2O3 in molten Re2O7 results in the formation of a colorless crystalline powder of K[B(ReO4)4]. The single‐crystal structure determination reveals a non‐centrosymmetric structure (space group I4¯${\mathrm{\bar{4}}}$), containing the hitherto unknown [B(ReO4)4]− anion. This anion presents the first example of a monomeric anion with boron as a central atom coordinated by four perrhenate anions forming B─O─Re bonds. The compound has been further characterized by Raman spectroscopy, with additionally DFT calculations to assign the vibration modes. Moreover, the absence of inversion symmetry has been proven by second harmonic generation (SHG) measurements.

articles.title: Visible Light Accelerates Ultralow Electric Field‐Induced Switching of Antipolar‐to‐Polar Orders in Photoactive Ferroelectric
articles.abstract: Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) have emerged as intriguing electroactive materials due to their unique merits arising from electric field-induced switching of antipolar-to-polar phases. For molecular AFEs, however, a high electric field strength is required to switch antipolar dipoles in adjacent sublattices because of complex intermolecular interactions. Herein, we propose visible-light irradiation as a feasible strategy to accelerate electric field-induced switching of antipolar-to-polar states in a photoactive AFE perovskite, (benzylammonium)2(ethylammonium)BiI6, with an ultralow coercive field. It is a multiaxial ferroelectric with large spontaneous polarization of 3.5 µC cm−2. The cooperation of organic cation dynamics and inorganic octahedral distortion induces stepwise symmetry breaking in (benzylammonium)2(ethylammonium)BiI6, described by the point-group sequence m-2/m-3m-3¯$\bar{3}$m. Strikingly, visible light accelerates its electric field-induced AFE-to-ferroelectric switching; it shows near-room-temperature AFE behavior in the dark even under a high electric field, whereas visible-light irradiation enables field-induced ferroelectricity at an ultralow coercive field (E c = 0.8 kV cm−1, merely 1/39 of that in the dark). Nanoscale piezoresponse force microscopy studies further confirm this light-accelerated polarization modulation, resembling an optical writing/reading memory process. This work provides a new pathway to modulate ferroic orders toward electronic device applications.

articles.title: How Tumor Cells Colonize the Most Protected Organs
articles.abstract: Immune privilege, or the capacity of specific tissues to actively limit immune responses, cannot be reduced to passive exclusion. The brain, eye, testis, and placenta each maintain this state through specialized physical barriers, resident immunosuppressive cell populations, and suppression of antigen presentation. Tumor cells metastasizing to these organs co-opt the same molecular programs that immune-privileged tissues evolved to protect themselves, turning biological safeguards into metastatic sanctuaries. The pattern points to selection rather than chance: The cells that thrive are those able to evade specialized immune programs and breach site-specific barriers. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling, liquid biopsy, and preclinical modeling have now provided the tools to interrogate these ecosystems with previously unavailable resolution. Here, we review the biology of immune-privileged metastatic niches, advances in their detection and molecular profiling, and the therapeutic strategies emerging from this understanding, with an emphasis on molecularly guided treatment over tissue-of-origin classification.

articles.title: Unmasking Cellular Plasticity from Development to Cancer by Lineage Tracing
articles.abstract: Cellular plasticity, a hallmark of normal development, is frequently co-opted by cancers to drive heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Deciphering these dynamic processes requires lineage-tracing technologies capable of recording cellular ancestry. This review outlines the methodological evolution from widely used site-specific recombinase tools to high-resolution, single-cell DNA barcoding. The integration of lineage tracing with single-cell multiomics and spatial transcriptomics now enables the construction of dynamic atlases that link cellular history to molecular state and microenvironment. Key insights reshaping cancer biology include the frequent polyclonal origin of early lesions followed by Darwinian selection toward monoclonal dominance, the revelation that cancer stem cells represent dynamic and plastic states rather than fixed entities, and the identification of specific cellular states critical for metastasis. This synergistic framework provides a powerful means to delineate the rules of tumor evolution, opening new avenues for predicting cell fates and designing strategies to target the roots of malignancy.

articles.title: Are We Going to the Dogs? Human Disease Phenotypes in Canines
articles.abstract: Companion dogs are increasingly recognized as translational models for studying human physiology and disease. Unlike conventional or genetically engineered laboratory models, dogs are outbred, immunocompetent animals that spontaneously develop complex diseases whose pathogenesis and environmental exposures commonly overlap with those of humans. These distinctive features create opportunities to study mechanisms of disease, progression, and therapeutic responses under conditions that more closely resemble clinical reality. This review highlights evidence for the translational relevance of canine models across multiple therapeutic areas. We further discuss how advances in genomics, transcriptomics, spatial biology, and in vitro and in silico model systems are expanding the translational utility of canine models for applications in human medicine. Although important species differences must be carefully weighed, dogs represent a uniquely valuable comparative model for elucidating disease mechanisms, informing drug development, and accelerating the translation of scientific discoveries to human medicine.

articles.title: Control of Diaphragm Muscle in Health and Disease
articles.abstract: Unique to mammals, the diaphragm muscle (DIAm) is the major pump muscle for breathing. The DIAm is a skeletal muscle composed of different fiber types with different mechanical and fatigue properties. Neural control of the DIAm is mediated by recruitment of motor units (MUs), each comprising a phrenic motor neuron in the cervical spinal cord and the set of muscle fibers (of a single type) it innervates. Thus, by recruiting different MU types, a range of motor behaviors can be accomplished. To support breathing, which is a sustained behavior, fatigue-resistant slow (type I fibers) and fast (type IIa fibers) MUs are recruited. However, the DIAm also subserves short duration, higher-force airway clearance, and voiding behaviors that require recruitment of more fatigable fast (type IIx/IIb) fibers. Importantly, in disease conditions, these fatigable DIAm MUs are more vulnerable, while fatigue-resistant MUs are more resilient.

articles.title: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila
articles.abstract: In the aging Drosophila brain, Orb2 amyloids required for long-term memory undergo structural remodeling, shifting from translation-promoting assemblies to destabilization-resistant, translation-deficient states. Rebalancing Orb2 toward youthful, translationally active assemblies improves memory in old flies.

articles.title: A competitive PDLIM1-USP14 axis destabilizes ACTN4 to disturb the invasive homeostasis of trophoblast in preeclampsia
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by insufficient extravillous trophoblast (EVT) invasion, but the cytoskeletal mechanisms restraining EVT motility remain unclear. TMT-based placental proteomics identified the cytoskeletal adaptor PDLIM1 as markedly upregulated in PE. In primary trophoblasts and cell lines, PDLIM1 depletion remodeled the actin cytoskeleton and enhanced migration and invasion, whereas trophoblast-restricted Pdlim1 overexpression impaired trophoblast invasion and placental development in mice. Mechanistically, PDLIM1 bounds the rod domain of α-actinin-4 (ACTN4) and competitively displaced USP14, limiting ACTN4 deubiquitination and shifting ACTN4 toward RNF38-associated K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover. Importantly, placenta-targeted chondroitin sulfate A-binding nanoparticles delivering Pdlim1 short hairpin RNA (shRNA) alleviated PE-like maternal and fetal phenotypes in mice. Collectively, these findings define a PDLIM1-USP14-ACTN4 proteostatic axis controlling trophoblast invasive homeostasis and identify PDLIM1 as a potential therapeutic target in PE.

articles.title: A hyper-IgM2 AID mutation limits IgH break formation but preserves affinity maturation
articles.abstract: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) drives antibody diversification through class switch recombination (CSR) and somatic hypermutation (SHM). Humans with an AID mutation deleting the last nine amino acids (AIDR190X) develop hyper-IgM syndrome with defective CSR but variable SHM, suggesting that the C terminus plays a marked role in CSR. To model this putative separation-of-function mutation, we generated an AicdaR190X knock-in mouse. These mice show a severe CSR defect and a moderately reduced but ongoing SHM. Mechanistically, the severe CSR defect correlates with defective recombination of double-strand breaks in immunoglobulin switch regions. Strikingly, fusion of AIDR190X to a catalytically inactive AID restores CSR, indicating that the C terminus mediates a non-catalytic function for recombination. This mouse model of the human R190X mutation demonstrates that the AID C terminus is indispensable for CSR and also contributes to efficient SHM, providing insight into the mechanistic basis of hyper-IgM immunodeficiency.

articles.title: Clusterin, through exercise-mediated liver-heart crosstalk, promotes heart regeneration after myocardial infarction
articles.abstract: Loss of cardiomyocytes drives cardiac remodeling and ultimately leads to heart failure, highlighting the need to promote cardiac regeneration. Exercise has been known to enhance cardiac repair and stimulate cardiomyocyte proliferation; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that exercise-induced exerkine clusterin mediates the pro-regenerative effects of running plasma on cardiac repair and cardiomyocyte proliferation following myocardial infarction (MI). Cardiac-specific Clu knockout attenuated, whereas clusterin overexpression enhanced, post-MI cardiac regeneration. Recombinant clusterin administration promoted heart regeneration in adult mice after MI. Mechanistically, clusterin activated NF-κB via proteasome-dependent IκBα degradation through direct binding with IκBα. Furthermore, the liver was identified as the major source of exercise-induced circulating clusterin; hepatocyte-specific Clu knockdown abolished the stimulatory effect of exercise plasma on cardiac regeneration. This study reveals a liver-heart crosstalk mechanism by which exercise-induced clusterin promotes cardiomyocyte proliferation, positioning clusterin as a potential therapeutic target for post-MI heart failure.

articles.title: Conserved disordered regions and ubiquitin-binding motifs within HUWE1 contribute to substrate targeting plasticity
articles.abstract: E3 ligases confer substrate specificity within ubiquitin-dependent pathways. However, the pleiotropic HECT-type E3 ligase HUWE1 targets a biochemically and structurally diverse set of substrates through mechanisms that remain largely unknown. We develop a combinatorial cell-based system integrating global proteomics, proximity labeling, and reporter assays to systematically interrogate HUWE1 sequence features that enable substrate targeting. We define a robust HUWE1 activity signature consisting of putative substrates that accumulate upon HUWE1 impairment across multiple cell lines. By re-expressing a panel of HUWE1 deletion mutants, we find that both the largest intrinsically disordered region and the conserved ubiquitin-binding motifs contribute to substrate targeting. Structural modeling and domain analysis further suggest that HUWE1 achieves targeting plasticity through multivalent interactions, engaging both disordered and structured regions within its substrates. Together, our findings establish a framework for understanding how large, modular E3 ligases exploit intrinsic disorder and multivalency to shape their substrate repertoires.

articles.title: Influenza virus antagonizes self-sensing by RIG-I to enhance viral replication
articles.abstract: Innate immune sensors must finely distinguish pathogens from the host to mount a response only during infection. RIG-I is a cytoplasmic sensor that triggers a broad antiviral response in response to sensing foreign RNAs. Here, we show that RIG-I not only binds viral RNAs but is activated by host RNAs. These are primarily non-coding RNAs transcribed by RNA polymerase III. They are benign under normal conditions but become immunogenic during influenza virus infection, where they signal via RIG-I to suppress viral replication. These RNAs are also bound by influenza virus nucleoprotein (NP), which normally functions to encapsidate the viral genome. NP interacts with RIG-I via an RNA bridge and antagonizes sensing of self-RNAs to counter innate immune responses. Overall, we demonstrate that self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.

articles.title: MHC II-expressing bone marrow megakaryocytes are noncanonical antigen-presenting cells and activate CD4+ T cells ex vivo
articles.abstract: While professional antigen-presenting cells drive adaptive immunity, atypical cell types can fulfill this role in the bone marrow. Megakaryocytes (MKs) are canonically recognized for platelet production, but recent studies indicate functional heterogeneity and immune potential. We found that ∼20% of bone marrow MKs express major histocompatibility complex (MHC) II and co-stimulatory receptors CD80, CD86, CD40, and CD83. These MKs process and present antigen to activate T cells ex vivo in an MHC II-dependent manner. MK/T cell interactions induced TGF-β1 secretion and promoted induced regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation. Toll-like receptor (TLR) stimulation of MKs elicited modest Th1-associated responses, including IFN-γ and TNF-α production, without robust Th17 differentiation. Immunopeptidomics confirmed peptide occupancy of MK MHC II in vivo. Using MK-targeted MHC II deletion, we observed altered TLR responses and reduced bone marrow TGF-β1. Together, these findings identify MHC II+ MKs as noncanonical antigen-presenting cells with potential roles in regulating CD4+ T cell responses within the bone marrow niche.

articles.title: Machine learning-assisted Repli-Histo labeling reveals distinct transcription-dependent constraints on chromatin motion in living cells
articles.abstract: Genomic DNA is wrapped around core histones to form nucleosomes, which are organized in cells from euchromatin to heterochromatin with distinct genome functions. Although transcription is known to shape chromatin behavior in live cells, it remains unclear how different transcription systems act across chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments. We develop machine learning-assisted Repli-Histo labeling to classify euchromatin and heterochromatin classes (classes IA, IB, II, and III) and combine it with single-nucleosome imaging in living human cells. Nucleosome motion is progressively constrained from euchromatin to heterochromatin. RNA polymerase II inhibition by THZ1, DRB, or α-amanitin increases nucleosome motion in euchromatic classes IA and IB and in heterochromatin around nucleoli, but not at the nuclear periphery. In contrast, RNA polymerase I inhibition by CX-5461 selectively increases nucleosome motion in Class III heterochromatin around nucleoli. Our study reveals that Pol II and Pol I transcription shape chromatin behavior in distinct chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments.

articles.title: Macrophages iron out cancer cells’ vulnerability
articles.abstract: Surviving despite accumulating toxic metabolites inside the cell is a defining feature of cancer evolution. In the current issue of Cell Reports, Eric Cheung and coworkers identify a mechanism that enables the survival of malignant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells through the sequestration of reactive iron.1.

articles.title: Pot1a maintains mesenchymal stem cell niche function to support hematopoietic stem cells
articles.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) maintain their function through interactions with niche cells in the bone marrow. We previously demonstrated that protection of telomeres 1a (Pot1a), a shelterin component, maintains HSCs and neuron-glial antigen 2-expressing (NG2+) mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) by suppressing DNA damage response (DDR) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. However, the role of Pot1a in leptin receptor-expressing (LepR+) MSCs, a primary HSC niche component, remains unclear. LepR-specific Pot1a knockout mice showed decreased LepR+ MSC numbers, increased DDR and ROS production, reduced HSC quiescence, and impaired long-term hematopoietic reconstitution. In contrast, cell-permeable Pot1a enhanced the hematopoietic-supporting function of LepR+ MSCs. Pot1a deficiency reduced pleiotrophin (Ptn) expression, whereas Pot1a overexpression increased its expression. These findings suggest that Pot1a preserves LepR+ MSC function by limiting stress-associated changes, maintaining MSC numbers, and regulating hematopoietic-supportive factor expression, including PTN.

articles.title: Rheb in central amygdala somatostatin neurons regulates chronic itch and anxiety-like behaviors
articles.abstract: Chronic itch represents a significant clinical challenge that substantially impairs patients' quality of life, yet its underlying neural circuit and molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that somatostatin-expressing (SST) neurons in the central amygdala (CeA) are activated and functionally required in a mouse model of diphenylcyclopropenone (DCP)-induced chronic itch. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed upregulation of Ras homolog enriched in brain (Rheb) within DCP-TRAPed CeA SST neurons. Notably, Rheb knockdown suppressed the hyperexcitability of CeA SST neurons and alleviated chronic itch-related scratching and anxiety-like behaviors in DCP-treated mice. Conversely, Rheb overexpression promoted scratching and anxiety-like behaviors in naive mice. Collectively, these findings delineate a Rheb-regulated CeA SST neuronal mechanism that contributes to chronic itch-related scratching and anxiety-like behaviors, highlighting a potential molecular target for therapeutic intervention in chronic itch.

articles.title: Transcriptional and functional profiling reveals a dynamic continuum of beta-cell activation states
articles.abstract: A central question is whether beta-cells respond uniformly to glucose. Using phospho-S6 as an activation marker, this study shows that beta-cells are recruited sequentially as glucose concentrations increase. Recruitment is spatially organized, with high-threshold cells predominantly located in the islet core. Transcriptomic profiling indicates functional heterogeneity among beta-cells. A low-threshold subset is characterized by enhanced stress resilience necessary for sustained secretion. An intermediate subset, enriched for calcium-signaling and vesicle-excitatory genes, modulates postprandial glucose excursions. The high-threshold subset specializes in high-capacity protein synthesis and insulin secretion to manage glucose peaks. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that these functional subsets form a continuous spectrum rather than discrete subpopulations. This division of labor is adaptable; under high-fat diet-induced metabolic demand, islets undergo remodeling with a global reduction in activation thresholds and a shift toward high-capacity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify a beta-cell hierarchy that balances metabolic resilience with secretory demand to maintain glucose homeostasis.

articles.title: Engineered receptor-biased IL-2–drug immunoconjugates selectively expand Tregs and suppress effector cells for autoimmune therapy
articles.abstract: Li et al. identify Y31-20K-KU, a receptor-biased, site-specifically PEGylated IL-2-mTOR inhibitor immunoconjugate that selectively expands Treg cells, suppresses effector T cell activation, and ameliorates autoimmune inflammation in preclinical models.

articles.abstract: Weak yet cooperative C–H⋯X hydrogen bonds support C–H···X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks. This Review summarizes their assembly, structural regulation, representative applications, and future challenges.

articles.title: Red List Index of Western Palearctic freshwater fishes
articles.abstract: The Red List Index (RLI) is a key indicator for global biodiversity targets, but its application to freshwater fishes has been limited by infrequent reassessment and sparse monitoring data. To address this gap, we developed the first comprehensive RLI for freshwater fishes of the Western Palearctic (Europe, West Asia, and North Africa), based on two comparable global assessment rounds. We reconciled taxonomy, classified category changes as nongenuine (reflecting taxonomic revision or improved knowledge) or genuine, and calculated RLIs with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. Of 1,157 native, described species, 727 (63%) had two comparable assessments and formed the index. The RLI declined across the region (−2.4%), with subregional declines ranging from −0.8% in West Asia to −7.1% in North Africa; genuine declines outnumbered improvements by approximately 6:1 and included losses to extinct in the wild or possibly extinct. Most species showed no change or a nongenuine change. The main constraint on the trend was not data deficiency (eight species) but the absence of a comparable earlier assessment for 337 species recently assessed. Of these species, the assessments showed that 163 were threatened and concentrated in West Asia, and coverage was lowest in West Asia (51%) and for small‐bodied, range‐restricted families. The index should therefore be read as a regional benchmark and not as a test of the RLI's sensitivity because the true number of genuine changes that should have occurred is unknown. Building on this analysis, we developed a prioritized, data‐informed agenda for strengthening future iterations: completing a second assessment of the already‐threatened species currently outside the trend, focusing the resurvey on under‐covered subregions and families, and matching monitoring technique to taxon. Documented recoveries show that targeted conservation can reverse declines, often in data‐poor areas, but without such effort, both decline and recovery of these faunas will be detected slowly. Índice de la Lista Roja de peces de agua dulce del Paleártico occidental Resumen El Índice de la Lista Roja (RLI) es un indicador clave para los objetivos mundiales de biodiversidad, pero su aplicación a los peces de agua dulce se ha visto limitada por la escasa frecuencia de las reevaluaciones y la escasez de datos de seguimiento. Para subsanar esta carencia desarrollamos el primer RLI exhaustivo para los peces de agua dulce del Paleártico occidental (Europa, Asia Occidental y el norte de África), basado en dos rondas de evaluación global comparables. Conciliamos la taxonomía, clasificamos los cambios de categoría como no genuinos (que reflejan una revisión taxonómica o un mayor conocimiento) o genuinos, y calculamos los RLI con intervalos de confianza del 95% obtenidos mediante el método bootstrap. De las 1,157 especies autóctonas descritas, 727 (63%) contaban con dos evaluaciones comparables y formaron parte del índice. El RLI disminuyó en toda la región (–2.4%), con descensos subregionales que oscilaron entre el –0.8% en Asia Occidental y el –7.1% en el norte de África. Los descensos genuinos superaron a las mejoras en una proporción de aproximadamente 6:1 e incluyeron pérdidas por extinción en estado silvestre o posible extinción. La mayoría de las especies no mostraron cambios o presentaron un cambio no genuino. La principal limitación de la tendencia no fue la falta de datos (8 especies), sino la ausencia de una evaluación anterior comparable para 337 especies evaluadas recientemente. De estas especies, el RLI reveló que 163 se encontraban amenazadas y concentradas en Asia occidental, y que la cobertura era menor en esta zona (51%) y para el caso de las familias de pequeño tamaño y área de distribución limitada. Por lo tanto, el índice debe interpretarse como un punto de referencia regional y no como una prueba de la sensibilidad del RLI, ya que se desconoce el número real de cambios genuinos que deberían haber ocurrido.…

articles.title: From Passive Drift to Olfactory Detection? A Late‐Stage Oceanic Juvenile Hawksbill's 9000‐km Journey Across the Western Indian Ocean
articles.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the transition of juvenile sea turtles from oceanic to neritic habitats remain poorly understood, as the oceanic stage is rarely observed directly. Here, we report a 201‐day satellite track of a juvenile hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata, curved carapace length of 38 cm) that traveled 9129 km from the Mozambique Channel to Huvadhu Atoll, Maldives. Current reanalysis data indicate that 74% of this distance resulted from passive transport by regional ocean currents. However, upon approaching within 50 km of the atoll, the turtle showed a marked, active course correction, swimming against weak currents while positioned downwind and downstream of the atoll, a low‐lying landform (~1 m above sea level) that would have been invisible by eye at such a distance. This pattern raises the possibility of olfactory detection of the atoll and provides, to our knowledge, a first indication of olfactory‐based island detection guiding habitat recruitment in a juvenile turtle, a mechanism previously documented only in breeding females. This track suggests a potential two‐scale process of oceanic‐to‐neritic habitat transition: a broadly stochastic oceanic phase shaped by passive dispersal, followed by fine‐scale, sensory‐guided settlement once the turtle nears a suitable habitat.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Phylogeography of the Proboscis Monkey (Nasalis larvatus) Reveals Riverine and Coastal Population Structure Across Eastern Borneo
articles.abstract: The proboscis monkey (Nasalis larvatus) is an endangered colobine endemic to Borneo, largely confined to mangrove, peat-swamp, and riverine forest and capable of swimming across the rivers and tidal channels that structure its habitat. How this riparian specialization influences the spatial distribution of genetic diversity across the species' range in Indonesia has not been characterized. We sequenced the mitochondrial control region from 32 individuals collected at 11 localities throughout North and East Kalimantan and combined them with published data from Sabah and Pulau Kaget. Twenty-six haplotypes (Hd = 0.986; π = 0.029) are divided into three haplogroups, with their geographic distributions only partially separated. AMOVA revealed significant population differentiation (Φ ST = 0.275, p = 0.018). Differentiation among localities was more accurately explained by least-cost distance calculated over a combined riverine–coastal network than by straight-line distance, supporting the idea that gene flow predominantly occurs along riparian and coastal corridors rather than crossing land. A haplotype found in Sembakung, Nunukan, and Sabah indicates mitochondrial continuity across the Indonesia–Malaysia border. The Pulau Kaget reserve population clusters with East Kalimantan rather than forming a separate southern lineage. Neutrality tests indicate a demographic expansion in the late Pleistocene within the most prevalent haplogroup. Calibrated Simias–Nasalis distances place the split between these sister genera in the Pleistocene (~0.74 Ma). These findings reveal regionally distinct and transboundary mitochondrial lineages, which should guide conservation efforts for this endangered primate.

articles.title: Nationwide Tracking of A‐Lineage Spread in Western Honey Bees Using Haplotype Sharing, Local Ancestry Mapping, and Migration Inference
articles.abstract: Understanding the spatial dynamics of genetic ancestry is essential for elucidating historical and contemporary patterns of gene flow among populations. Honey bees in the United States have a 400‐year history of importation, management, and adaptation to diverse environments. Genetic diversity is a key factor for colony health and resilience. Notably, the most genetically diverse populations in the country originate from the invasive A‐lineage (Africanized or ‘Killer’ honey bees). In this study, we leveraged a nationwide community‐science platform to assemble an extensive genomic dataset of U.S. honey bee populations and used it to ask how this invasive lineage is spreading across the country and how its spread has impacted honey bee genetic diversity nationwide. Using RFMix, we assigned local ancestry across the genome to capture fine‐scale ancestry patterns and applied TreeMix to genome‐wide allele frequency data to infer directional gene flow among U.S. populations. Our analyses revealed patterns consistent with a strong northward migration, with major source populations in southern states such as Texas (TX), Arizona (AZ), and Florida (FL), and primary targets in northern states including Michigan (MI), New York (NY), and Vermont (VT). Covariance estimates indicated strong genetic connectivity, particularly from TX and AZ. Spatial visualization of migration edges highlighted key routes of A‐lineage expansion. Together, these results provide the first genome‐wide evidence for a nationwide spread of A‐lineage ancestry in the U.S., offering insights to guide breeding strategies and predict the future dynamics of honey bee genetic diversity.

articles.title: Plant Conservation Genetics Advocates for a Green List
articles.abstract: Our definition of a green list is rooted in the art of safeguarding plant genetic resources and relies on the ability to compile all the tools and information on conservation plans and management activities with the goal of de‐listing any taxon of special concern from the red lists.

articles.title: Resource‐Related Interactions Between Wolverines and Brown Bears in Scandinavia
articles.abstract: Ongoing recovery of large carnivore species into their former ranges increases the occurrence of interactions among them. The recovering Scandinavian wolverine (Gulo gulo) population has recently expanded southwards and is increasingly overlapping with the core of the brown bear (Ursus arctos) range. Both species are facultative scavengers that feed on moose (Alces alces) carcasses, which are an important resource all year round for wolverines and seasonally for bears. Reliance on the same resource may lead to interactions. We monitored five GPS‐collared wolverines in central Sweden to investigate feeding sites with food remains and determine bear activity. In addition, we used motion‐triggered cameras to monitor wolverine and bear activity at three wolverine rendezvous sites (i.e., temporary sites where females keep cubs) and at a recently bear‐killed adult moose carcass. We found 115 wolverine feeding sites, of which 25 (22%) showed signs of bear activity. At 24 sites we found remains from adult moose carcasses, five presumably bear‐killed of which two were fresh (< 1 week). Based on GPS‐data, wolverines repeatedly used these recently bear‐killed moose for periods ranging from a few hours to multiple days. Bear activity was documented at two of the three presumed rendezvous sites used by a female wolverine with cubs. Camera data also documented repeated visits by at least three different wolverines at the presumed bear‐killed moose carcass, including visits short before and after bear activity at the site. Our results illustrate that wolverines and bears overlap and share food resources, potentially leading to direct and/or indirect interactions. These observations suggest that co‐occurrence between these two species create both feeding opportunities and potential risks for wolverines, which deserves further research.

articles.title: Taxon‐Specific Loss in Scleractinian Living Coral Area Following a Bleaching Event Is Linked to Reef Structural Decline in the Central Red Sea
articles.abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasing in frequency and intensity worldwide, triggering coral bleaching events. While colony and community scale consequences of bleaching have been well documented, its consequence on reef structural complexity remains comparatively less studied. Using Structure‐from‐Motion (SfM), colony fate tracking of hermatypic scleractinians, and a cross‐scale, sequential approach, this study linked in situ thermal stress to coral colony‐scale bleaching and mortality and reef‐scale structural change during the 2023 bleaching event in the central Saudi Arabian Red Sea. Taxon‐specific bleaching thresholds were consistent with regional bleaching alert levels; however, ecological risk varied substantially among reefs. We further support that the relationship between thermal stress and change in reef‐building coral colony area is taxon‐dependent, and that bleaching‐driven coral mortality can rapidly alter reef structural complexity, with potential consequences for ecosystem function. This study represents the first mechanistic assessment of coral resilience across biological scales in the central Red Sea, and provides new insight into reef structural persistence under accelerating climate change.

articles.title: The Synergy Between Deterministic and Neutral Processes Drives Turnover‐Dominated Beta Diversity of Non‐Volant Small Mammals in the Western Tianshan Mountains, China
articles.abstract: Exploring multifaceted beta diversity, including its turnover and nestedness components, is crucial for elucidating the drivers of community assembly. Arid mountain ecosystems, with their strong environmental filtering and fragmented habitats, serve as a useful model system for testing how these drivers interact across multiple dimensions of diversity. Here, we compared taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic beta diversity in non‐volant small mammal communities across environmental gradients in arid areas of the western Tianshan Mountains, China, and inferred the associated community‐assembly processes. Species turnover predominantly structured beta diversity across all three dimensions. Decomposition of multifaceted beta diversity revealed a consistent pattern: functional dissimilarity was highest, followed by taxonomic and phylogenetic dissimilarity. Hierarchical partitioning identified elevational distance as the most significant factor influencing beta diversity and its turnover component, and nestedness was driven by multiple factors. We also confirmed a significant distance–decay relationship for overall community dissimilarity and its turnover component. Moreover, analyses of community‐assembly mechanisms suggested a synergistic interaction between deterministic and neutral processes, whereby the influence of environmental filtering weakened while that of limiting similarity strengthened as elevational distance increased. Collectively, these findings clarify the patterns and drivers of beta diversity in arid montane regions and provide a practical basis for biodiversity conservation in Central Asian mountain ecosystems.

An insight into molecular identification and DNA barcoding of bamboo: current status, challenges, and future prospects
articles.abstract: IntroductionBamboo exhibits a complex taxonomy due to polyploidy, hybridisation, and long flowering periods, which complicate species identification. Traditional morphological taxonomy often struggles with limited diagnostic traits and considerable phenotypic variability, leading to taxonomic ambiguities and misinterpretations. The convergence of similar traits among unrelated species further complicates phylogenetic classification. To address these challenges, integrative taxonomic approaches are needed to combine morphological, molecular, and ecological data for accurate bamboo classification. This review synthesises the current status, recent advances, and emerging trends in molecular identification and DNA barcoding of bamboo, highlighting their potential to improve taxonomy, conservation, and the sustainable utilisation of bamboo genetic resources.MethodTo provide a framework for the review, a scientometric analysis was performed using bibliographic records.ResultsThe review suggests that no single marker or combination of markers can currently serve as a universal barcode across bamboo. The performance of commonly used markers such as ITS, matK, rbcL, psbA-trnH, rps16-trnQ, and alternative plastid regions provides valuable insights into species identification. Comparative evidence indicates that barcode performance is strongly marker- and lineage-dependent. These markers have improved plant taxonomy by providing more reliable species identification than traditional morphological methods.DiscussionDNA barcoding has been effectively used to understand complex species relationships and identify cryptic species that are difficult to distinguish morphologically. Furthermore, next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies have transformed genomic data acquisition, enabling species discrimination. Integrating machine learning with DNA barcoding further improves species identification accuracy and shows promise for improving conventional methodologies in bamboo systematics. However, the application of ML and NGS in bamboo is still in its early stages and will require substantial work on bamboo databases to achieve greater accuracy.

articles.title: The intermediate social resilience hypothesis: a testable framework linking animal sociality to population resilience under environmental change
articles.abstract: Sociality can improve access to information, cooperation, collective defense, parental care, collective decision-making, and social buffering, but it can also intensify competition and pathogen transmission, spread outdated information, and create dependence on particular partners, roles, or traditions. In this article, we propose the Intermediate Social Resilience Hypothesis (ISRH), which predicts that, under specified conditions, population resilience may be greatest at an intermediate value of a defined social dimension. We do not rank all animal societies on a single universal scale. Instead, low, intermediate, and high values must be defined within a measurable dimension, such as group size, cohesion, network connectivity, cooperative effort, or reliance on social information, and within a biologically comparable system. Resilience must likewise be specified as resistance, recovery, temporal stability, or persistence under a defined form and scale of environmental change. The distinctive contribution of the ISRH is not simply the recognition that sociality can generate both benefits and costs, but the explicit prediction that their balance can, under identifiable conditions, produce a testable intermediate maximum in population resilience. An intermediate optimum is expected only when social benefits initially increase but eventually saturate, whereas one or more relevant social costs continue to rise. Environmental harshness, variability, unpredictability, and the flexibility, modularity, redundancy, or multilevel organization of social systems may shift, flatten, or eliminate this relationship. The hypothesis generates two falsifiable predictions that can be tested through comparative, longitudinal, experimental, phylogenetic, network, and population-monitoring approaches. By integrating behavioral ecology, social evolution, resilience theory, and conservation, the framework explicitly recognizes the multidimensional nature of animal social systems while providing explicit criteria for distinguishing support for the ISRH from monotonic, threshold, flat, or context-dependent alternative relationships.

articles.title: When wildlife damage threatens livelihoods: why national park residents consider a transition to tourism
articles.abstract: Wildlife damage is often expected to push national park residents toward new sources of income, but the appraisals that turn damage into a willingness to move into tourism remain unclear. Drawing on protection motivation theory and questionnaire data from 513 residents in and around the Wuyishan City section of Wuyishan National Park, China, this study distinguishes perceived tourism adaptive efficacy from tourism self-efficacy and examines how these two beliefs relate to intentions to shift household livelihoods toward tourism. Greater perceived wildlife damage was related to stronger threat appraisal of traditional livelihoods. Residents who perceived greater livelihood threat also reported stronger transition intentions and were more likely to view tourism as a workable livelihood alternative. However, no clear relationship emerged between livelihood threat and tourism self-efficacy, although both adaptive efficacy and self-efficacy were positively related to transition intention. As a moderator, perceived tourism development opportunity was more relevant to adaptive efficacy than to self-efficacy. When residents perceived greater tourism opportunities, the positive relationship between livelihood threat and adaptive efficacy was stronger, as was the corresponding indirect relationship with transition intention. In contrast, perceived opportunity made little difference to the relationship involving self-efficacy. These findings suggest that livelihood threat was associated with greater perceived usefulness and feasibility of tourism without a corresponding association with residents’ confidence in their own ability to engage in tourism activities. Policies aimed at encouraging livelihood diversification in national park communities may therefore need to combine the creation of tourism opportunities with training, skills development, and other forms of support that strengthen residents’ capacity to participate.

articles.title: Mitochondrial DNA abundance is a determinant of immunogenic cell death in cancer
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial stress can trigger either immunogenic or apoptotic cell death. Tanaka et al. find that mitochondrial DNA abundance, shaped by oncogenic KRAS signaling and mitophagy, determines the immunological outcome of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization, providing a mechanistic basis for targeting mitochondrial stress to augment antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Host seasonal trophic strategies linked to dietary‐microbiota coupling: A potential mechanism mediating the coexistence of sympatric small rodents
articles.abstract: This study reveals that host trophic strategy, not shared seasonality, drives gut microbiota plasticity in sympatric rodents. Herbivorous voles show tight diet–microbiome coupling; granivorous gerbils exhibit functional stability. This highlights gut microbiota as a potential key mechanism for niche differentiation and coexistence. Abstract The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host‐specific gut microbiota responses. We compared the herbivorous Brandt's vole (Lasiopodomys brandtii) and the granivorous Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus), two sympatric rodent species with divergent trophic strategies inhabiting the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. By integrating plant DNA metabarcoding, gut microbiota profiling and microbial functional output analyses across seasons, we investigated seasonal dietary–microbiome associations. Our results revealed that although seasonal dietary variation affects the composition of the host gut microbiota, the taxonomic and functional plasticity of gut microbiota is strongly influenced by host trophic strategies. Brandt's voles maintained a fermentation‐oriented microbiota tightly coupled with seasonal shifts in Poaceae and Cyperaceae intake, exhibiting coordinated changes in microbial taxa, short‐chain fatty acid production and cellulase activity. In contrast, Mongolian gerbils exhibited substantial seasonal dietary turnover between Chenopodiaceae and Caragana plants, while maintaining comparatively stable microbial functional outputs, suggesting metabolic buffering. Host trophic strategy, rather than shared environmental seasonality, is related to the strength and functional consequences of the coupling between diet and microbiome. Our results emphasize the gut microbiome as a potential key mechanism underlying trophic niche differentiation and ecological coexistence in wild mammalian communities.
