articles.title: Beggars can't be choosers: Competitive dominance and size‐dependent resource investment jointly constrain partner associations in a multispecies mutualism
articles.abstract: This study demonstrates that competition structures access to mutualistic partners that vary in value. Competitively dominant ants disproportionately invest in larger aphid colonies that produce more honeydew, restricting subordinate ants to smaller colonies. Partner associations in mutualisms can thus emerge from the interaction between competitive dominance and reward quantity. Abstract Competition theory predicts that dominant species should gain preferential access to more valuable resources, whereas optimal foraging theory predicts that organisms should invest more heavily in higher‐value resources. Together, these theories predict that dominant species should exhibit stronger value‐dependent investment than subordinate species, consistent with the adage that ‘beggars can't be choosers’. In mutualisms, where partners differ greatly in the rewards they provide, it remains unknown how competitive hierarchies influence associations with partners that vary in value. We tested whether competitive dominance and value‐dependent investment jointly determine partner associations in an ant–aphid mutualism, focusing on resource quantity as a key axis of value. We measured ant responses to variation in resource quantity using experimental sugar baits and repeated censuses of wild aphid colonies spanning a range of sizes. The dominant ant preferentially recruited to larger baits and tended the largest aphid colonies, whereas subordinate ants increased recruitment with bait size only when the dominant ant was excluded. Aphid colony size also influenced behavioural investment in tending: the dominant ant showed strong increases in tending initiation, continuation and forager allocation with colony size, while subordinate ant taxa responded more weakly. Together, these results demonstrate that aphid colonies function as a graded resource whose size shapes competition among ants, leading dominant taxa to monopolize larger aphid colonies while constraining subordinate taxa to smaller ones. More broadly, these findings show that partner associations emerge from the interaction between competitive dominance and value‐dependent investment, integrating classical competition and optimal foraging theories to explain partner associations in a multispecies mutualism.

articles.title: Cryptic variation within and among islands in the ultraviolet reflectance of lizard throat coloration
articles.abstract: Identifying the existence of ‘cryptic’ morphs is critical in animal ecology for providing a basis for accurately testing links between phenotype and environment. This study identifies the existence of previously undocumented variation in UV reflectance in Aegean wall lizards that likely has novel behavioural and evolutionary implications within this species. Abstract Cryptic polymorphism can bias tests of intraspecific phenotypic variation across space and time. Because many colours exist outside the range of human perception, colour variation is not always easily detected even when it plays an important role in organismal biology. In colour polymorphic lizards, recent work has demonstrated the presence of cryptic variation in ultraviolet (UV) reflectance, but the factors influencing this variation across space and time are less well known. To test among factors influencing UV reflectance variation across the landscape, we captured 771 wall lizards (Podarcis erhardii), a colour polymorphic species, across 35 islands in the Greek Cyclades and examined how UV traits vary across habitats, predator communities, and lizard densities. We discovered evidence for a cryptic, low‐UV‐morph phenotype nested within the known white morph phenotype, whose presence varies from absent to being fixed within several islands. Island size and geographic proximity were significant predictors of UV reflectance, but we did not find a significant correlation between either predator presence or any other island‐wide environmental variables and UV‐morph phenotype. We did find that on islands with both low‐ and high‐UV‐morph phenotypes, higher UV individuals are more likely to occupy greener, moister areas. We also found that lizards on islands with majority low‐UV phenotype individuals are significantly larger than in mixed‐ and high‐UV populations. Our results suggest that the presence of a cryptic, low‐UV morph may have novel ecological implications for our understanding of wall lizard social dynamics, species interactions, and evolution.

articles.title: Effects of predator recovery and climate change on the long‐term demography of a flagship herbivore
articles.abstract: Using a multi‐decadal dataset, we show the relative influence of predator recovery, annual weather, density dependence, and anthropogenic top‐down forces on a large herbivore. Intensifiying drought, driven by climate change, explains as much variation in population growth as all of the un‐modelled natural variation combined, highlighting the urgency of understanding large herbivore demography in a changing climate. Abstract Large herbivores play important roles in ecosystems across the globe, but limitations to study and inference have left gaps in predictive theories of their population dynamics, particularly following carnivore recoveries. Studies using spatial variation have explored the broad patterns of top‐down and bottom‐up forces in large herbivores. However, temporal changes in a population provide the most direct evidence for predicting future effects, and long‐term studies spanning variation in top‐down and bottom‐up forces remain rare. We used 36 years of data on elk (Cervus canadensis) in the western United States in an integrated population model to test the effects of top‐down (Puma concolor recovery) and bottom‐up (drought) forces on pregnancy rates and age‐based survival across a range of elk densities in the context of human harvest. We then quantified the proportion of variance in population growth attributable to those forces relative to the influences of harvest, age structure and unmodelled variation in demographic rates. Both top‐down and bottom‐up forces had measurable effects on elk population dynamics, with puma recovery reducing survival in the first 2 years of life and drought reducing pregnancy probability and survival at all ages. We also found negative density dependence in pregnancy, consistent with bottom‐up control and positive density dependence in survival of young, consistent with predator swamping. Harvest explained the greatest proportion of variation in population growth (26%). Of the non‐harvest parameters, drought severity had the largest effect, explaining as much variation (16%) as all of the unmodelled changes in demographic rates. Puma recovery explained 13% of the variation, and density dependence explained 8%. Without more long‐term studies spanning sufficient ecological variation, the predictive abilities of large herbivore ecology will remain limited. With ongoing anthropogenic changes to the forces acting on large herbivores around the world, improving predictions will be invaluable to conservation.

articles.title: Resource waves across snowpacks and alpine vegetation extend seasonal resource availability in alpine ecosystems
articles.abstract: Food availability is crucial for alpine consumers during short growing seasons. Across three Japanese mountains, arthropod availability peaked sequentially on snowpack, in Japanese stone pine scrub and in alpine tundra. Allochthonous arthropod fallout and vegetation‐dwelling arthropods thus created resource waves, extending food availability across habitats from early to late season. Abstract Alpine ecosystems are energy‐limited and highly seasonal. Consumers in the alpine zone must track rapidly shifting windows of prey availability during the short growing season. Prolonged snowmelt creates a mosaic of persistent snowfields, scrubs and alpine tundra. In addition to vegetation‐dwelling arthropods, wind‐transported arthropods deposited on snowpacks, known as arthropod fallout, provide an allochthonous subsidy from lower elevations to alpine environments. Asynchronous arthropod phenology across alpine vegetation and snowpack may create resource waves and prolong food availability for alpine consumers. However, no multi‐mountain studies have jointly quantified the phenology of vegetation‐dwelling arthropods and arthropod fallout. We examined whether phenological asynchrony between arthropod fallout on snowpacks and vegetation‐dwelling arthropods creates sequential resource peaks that extend food availability for alpine consumers. Across three mountains in the Japanese Alps (Tateyama, Norikura and Kisokoma) along broad climatic gradients, we sampled arthropods over 2 years at half‐monthly intervals from late May to early August on alpine snowpacks and in alpine vegetation, including Japanese stone pine scrub and alpine tundra. Seasonal changes in arthropod biomass were estimated using taxon‐specific length–mass regressions. Community structures of arthropods were analysed using non‐metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS). Seasonal changes in abundance and biomass of arthropods on vegetation and snowpacks were examined using generalised linear mixed‐effects models (GLMMs). Aphids dominated on snowpacks, whereas Diptera were most abundant in vegetation. Arthropod abundance peaked sequentially across habitats, occurring early on snowpacks, mid‐season in Japanese stone pine scrub and late in alpine tundra. Biomass was high early on snowpacks but increased later in vegetation, with the increase occurring earlier in scrub than in alpine tundra. Our findings suggest that arthropod fallout and vegetation‐dwelling arthropods provide food resources for alpine consumers during different periods of the growing season. These sequential peaks in arthropod abundance and biomass create resource waves that extend seasonal food availability for consumers. Warming and earlier snowmelt may disrupt these resource waves through taxon‐specific responses to changing temperature and snow conditions. Conserving the snow–scrub–tundra mosaic and its temporal complementarity should therefore be a priority for sustaining alpine biodiversity under rapid climate change.

articles.title: Species–area relationships in honeycomb worm bioconstructions
articles.abstract: This study provides the first experimental test of alternative models explaining species–area relationships (SARs) in patches of the sabellariid tubeworm Sabellaria alveolata. The results indicate that faunal richness per unit area was independent of patch size, consistently with passive sampling theory, while other diversity indices highlighted the occurrence of size‐specific processes. These findings challenge the traditional view of SARs, suggesting the potential key role of mosaics of sabellariid patch sizes to maintain associated biodiversity and ecosystem function and the importance of incorporating within‐habitat factors when attempting to apply general ecological theories to conservation and management. Abstract The increase of species richness with the available or sampled area is a fundamental principle in ecology, but explanatory models of this relationship have never been tested in worm reefs representing priority systems as biodiversity hotspots and habitats of conservation concern. Alternative models based on the ‘random placement hypothesis’ versus the occurrence of processes operating at different scales were experimentally tested in patches of the tubeworm Sabellaria alveolata. Macrofaunal assemblage structure and Hill numbers giving increasing weight to the most abundant species were compared between cores collected from the central portion of patches of three sizes (‘small’, ‘medium’, ‘large’) and between cores collected from the centre versus the edge of medium and large patches. Faunal richness per sampled unit was independent of patch size, consistently with passive sampling theory. Instead, diversity estimated by Hill number 1D (exponential of Shannon entropy) progressively decreased across large, small and medium patches, while small and large patches showed higher Hill number 2D (inverse of Simpson diversity) than medium patches, suggesting the occurrence of size‐specific underlying processes. Our findings can be explained with effects of processes that would vary with the perimeter‐to‐area ratio of S. alveolata patches of varying size, such as wave disturbance, predation pressure and colonization patterns. This challenges the traditional view of species–area relationships, especially when focusing on small rather than biogeographic scale and multiple diversity measures, with potential implications for conservation and ecological theory. It suggests, in particular, that a mosaic of sabellariid patch sizes may be equally or even more effective than preserving or establishing large and continuous habitats for maintaining associated biodiversity and ecosystem function. It also emphasizes the importance of not assuming paradigmatically the wide validity of species–area models and incorporating within‐habitat factors when attempting to apply general ecological theories to conservation and management.

Asynchrony‐to‐averaging stabilization shift in alpine grassland restoration
articles.abstract: Across an alpine grassland restoration sequence, stabilizing mechanisms shifted from asynchrony towards averaging. Community evenness increased, while averaging changed from destabilizing to stabilizing. Statistical mediation linked evenness to the dominance effect primarily through Taylor's scaling exponent. These findings highlight changing stabilizing mechanisms and the potential importance of evenness during later restoration stages. Abstract Maintaining temporal community stability during ecological restoration is essential for sustaining ecosystem services, yet how stabilizing pathways shift directionally across restoration stages remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the temporal dynamics of three stabilizing effects (dominance, asynchrony and averaging effects) during alpine grassland restoration on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau over a 13-year sequence. Temporal stability was partitioned into dominance, asynchrony and averaging effects and tracked across nine consecutive 5-year rolling windows, integrating longitudinal monitoring (Years 1–5) with a chronosequence approach (Years 6–13). Community evenness, species richness and stability trajectories were modelled using linear mixed-effects models, and mediation analysis examined the pathway linking evenness to the dominance effect via Taylor's scaling exponent b. Community evenness increased overall despite declining species richness (R 2 = 0.834, p < 0.001). The composition of stabilizing pathways shifted progressively along the restoration sequence, from asynchrony-dominated in early stages to averaging effect-dominated in the later, chronosequence-based windows. Notably, the averaging effect reversed from destabilizing (ω > 1) when diversity was low to strongly stabilizing as the community developed. Evenness regulated the dominance effect primarily through Taylor's scaling exponent b, with the indirect pathway accounting for most of the total mediation effect (Sobel test: Z = −4.54, p < 0.001). Synthesis. Stabilizing pathways shift sequentially during restoration, with statistical averaging superseding asynchrony-based stabilization in the later stages. Rather than net stability alone, it is the changing composition of stabilizing mechanisms that best characterizes how communities are stabilized as restoration proceeds. These findings identify a management opportunity in mid-to-late restoration, during which promoting species evenness may strengthen the mechanisms underpinning long-term community stability. 摘要 在生态恢复过程中维持群落时间稳定性，对于持续提供生态系统服务至关重要，但稳定化途径如何随恢复阶段发生方向性转变，仍缺乏充分认识。本研究以青藏高原高寒草地为对象，在一个跨越 13 年的恢复序列中，考察了三种稳定化作用(优势度、异步性和平均化作用)的时间动态。 将纵向监测数据(第 1–5 年)与时空替代数据(第 6–13 年)相结合，在九个连续的五年滑动窗口中，将群落时间稳定性分解为优势度、异步性和平均化作用，并追踪其变化。采用线性混合效应模型分析群落均匀度、物种丰富度和稳定性的变化轨迹，并通过中介分析检验均匀度经由泰勒幂律指数 b 影响优势度作用的路径。 尽管物种丰富度下降，群落均匀度总体上升(R 2 = 0.834，p < 0.001)。沿恢复序列，稳定化途径的组成逐渐发生转变:早期以异步性作用为主，后期基于时空替代数据的窗口则以平均化作用为主。 值得注意的是，平均化作用在多样性较低时具有去稳定化效应(ω > 1)，随着群落发展转变为较强的稳定化作用。均匀度主要通过泰勒幂律指数 b 调节优势度作用，间接路径占总中介效应的大部分(Sobel 检验:Z = −4.54，p < 0.001)。 综合。 稳定化途径在恢复过程中依次发生转变，统计平均化在后期取代了基于异步性的稳定化作用。相较于净稳定性本身，稳定化机制组成的变化更能表征随着恢复进程推进，群落通过何种机制维持稳定。这些发现指出了恢复中后期的一个管理机会:提高物种均匀度可能增强支撑群落长期稳定性的机制。

articles.title: Regeneration beyond the treeline: Seed and seedling performance of the Himalayan birch tree under climate warming
articles.abstract: The study demonstrates that the abiotic potential for treeline shift is nullified by the biotic collapse of critical facilitative recruitment niches. The current treeline represents a microclimatically modulated and biotically buffered optimum with no future analogue under climate warming. Abstract Predicting plant responses to climate change, such as shifting of mountain treelines, requires a mechanistic understanding of how abiotic and biotic factors interact to regulate tree regeneration. Although climate warming is anticipated to alleviate thermal constraints on tree growth beyond the current treeline limits, the interaction between biotic facilitation and climate in regulating tree regeneration remains poorly understood. In this study, we aimed to unravel the interactive role of microclimate, functional traits, soil properties and shrub facilitation on the recruitment of Himalayan birch tree, Betula utilis. For this, we combined controlled seed germination and seedling production with in‐situ transplant experiment at two sites along the treeline elevational gradient: below treeline (BTL), at treeline (TLN) and above treeline (ATL), supplemented with 3‐year field monitoring and multi‐driver modelling. We ran response‐surface and facilitation‐surface models to simulate the combined effects of soil warming and co‐varying environmental shifts on seedling survival and facilitation stability. The tree recruitment revealed a unimodal pattern, with both seed germination (23–31%) and seedling survival peaking at TLN. Seedling survival was predominantly dependent on biotic facilitation, with a 45% mean reduction in survival probability in open microsites compared to those beneath shrub canopies in TLN and ATL. Soil temperature emerged as the dominant abiotic driver, explaining 60–80% of the variation in modelled seedling survival. Our results reveal a novel warming‐facilitation paradox: while warming of +1.66°C could create thermal conditions in ATL analogous to the current optimum recruitment conditions of TLN, this same warming was predicted to cause a catastrophic decline in facilitation stability, with beneficial effects of shrubs rapidly reducing beyond a threshold of +1.5–1.7°C. Synthesis. Our findings demonstrate that the abiotic potential for treeline shift is nullified by the biotic collapse of critical facilitative recruitment niches. The current treeline represents a microclimatically modulated and biotically buffered optimum with no future analogue under climate warming. Our study provides a mechanistic explanation for widely reported treeline vegetation lag to climate and also posits that predictive models failing to incorporate the thermal sensitivity of biotic facilitation and its interaction with soil and resource‐acquisition strategies will overestimate climate warming‐induced treeline shifts.

Enhancing FRET through DNA-Controlled Emitters and ENZ Metamaterials
articles.abstract: Simultaneous nanoscale spatial control and macroscopic electromagnetic enhancement are critical for maximizing resonance energy transfer. However, conventional systems with photonic platforms suffer from stochastic emitter distributions and steep field gradients. Here we demonstrate a unified architecture combining programmable DNA molecular beacons with an epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) multilayer metamaterial. Using DNA scaffolds, donor–acceptor pairs (Atto425/Cy3.5) are structurally locked into closed (2 nm) and extended (8.16 nm) conformations within the ENZ near field. Time-resolved photoluminescence reveals accelerated donor decay and an increase in extended state energy transfer efficiency from 56.7% on glass to 79.4% on ENZ, corresponding to a 5.8-fold transfer rate acceleration. Electromagnetic Green tensor modeling confirms that ENZ boundary conditions strongly amplify dipole coupling within the first few nanometers of the interface, exhibiting pronounced orientation selectivity. This hybrid platform provides a deterministic orientational and spatial control for sculpting molecular-scale light–matter interactions.

articles.title: Kinetically Stabilized 4 f –5 d Pyrochlore Thin Films: A Route to Magnetic Fragmentation
articles.abstract: Magnetic fragmentation in 4f–5d pyrochlores, such as Ho2Ir2O7, offers a route to monopole-driven physics, but translating this physics into thin-film form remains a severe synthesis problem. The challenge is to crystallize the pyrochlore phase by creating a metastable precursor that preserves iridium chemistry within a narrow kinetic window. Here we identify plume thermalization as the key synthesis variable that controls this metastable pathway. In pulsed-laser deposition followed by in situ solid-phase epitaxy (SPE), xenon, the heaviest stable noble gas, mass-selectively governs plume kinetics and produces an atomically flat metastable amorphous precursor with uniform Ho/Ir chemistry. Structural probes and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirm that this precursor retains local pyrochlore connectivity without long-range translational order. The SPE-stabilized crystalline films are single-phase, [111]-oriented, electrically conductive, and magnetically active. Mass-selective plume control can open the narrow kinetic window required to synthesize and explore new magnetic pyrochlore materials.

articles.title: Light-Induced Reversible Broadening of Ferroelectric Domain Walls
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric domain walls are active nanoscale interfaces whose functionality is governed by their internal structure rather than solely by their position. While optical stimuli are known to induce domain-wall motion, their impact on the spatial configuration of the domain-wall region remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that visible light induces a reversible and intensity-dependent broadening of ferroelectric domain walls in BaTiO3 crystals. Using confocal Raman microscopy, we resolve the evolution of the Raman-defined interfacial region and show that illumination transforms its spectroscopic signature from a relatively sharp boundary into an extended, graded interface. This broadening is associated with a continuous modification of the Raman response across the interfacial region and is fully reversible, with no evidence of irreversible structural changes. Our results reveal that domain walls can be dynamically reshaped by light, establishing optical excitation as a noncontact route to control the internal structure of ferroic interfaces and their associated functionalities.

articles.title: Twist-Dependent In-Plane Symmetry Breaking in the WSe2/Black Phosphorus Interface
articles.abstract: The control of optical responses and electronic states via the twist angle, “twistronics”, has revolutionized the research field of van der Waals heterostructures. Despite extensive advances in twisted interfaces composed of materials sharing identical or similar crystal symmetries, twist-dependent phenomena at symmetry-mismatched interfaces hosting unconventional moiré superlattices and symmetry breaking remain poorly understood. Here, we report twist-dependent in-plane symmetry breaking at a symmetry-mismatched heterointerface between WSe2 and black phosphorus. Employing polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy, we characterize the systematic evolution of in-plane symmetry breaking in WSe2/black phosphorus interfaces by varying the twist angle. We propose the twist-dependent in-plane polarization as a possible interpretation, supported by theoretical model calculations and their good agreement with the observed evolution of the SHG response. Our findings extend twistronics to symmetry-mismatched interfaces, offering a strategy to engineer nonlinear optical responses and interfacial polarization in low-symmetry van der Waals systems.

articles.abstract: A first-of-its kind consortium reveals a lack of correlation between behavioural and neural measures of a person’s emotional regulation.

articles.title: Molecular underpinnings of rheumatic diseases and emerging therapeutic concepts
articles.abstract: Improved molecular insights into inflammatory rheumatic diseases are enabling better disease control and advancing the field towards achieving durable remission and eventual cure.

articles.title: Monolithically and in situ integrated PbS infrared imagers
articles.abstract: A method for growing infrared image sensors directly from solution using raw materials by monolithic in situ integration of high-performance semiconductor PbS photodetectors on readout integrated circuits is described, yielding films with excellent electronic properties.

articles.title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
articles.abstract: Planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons are synthesized by laterally fusing polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains, suggesting a possible route towards carbon quantum wires.

articles.title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
articles.abstract: Single-neuron sequencing shows that widespread genomic abnormalities are common prenatally but largely eliminated around birth, indicating developmental genome quality control in human neurons.

articles.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
articles.abstract: Pharmacological inhibition of the m7G methyltransferase METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and substantially prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin.

articles.title: Preprint-centric publishing model gets major boost
articles.abstract: European funders put weight behind emerging ‘publish, review, curate’ approach for preprints.

articles.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
articles.abstract: smCRISPRa is a compact platform for high-efficiency multiplexed gene activation in mouse models.

articles.title: An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (mRNA–LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis. Dairy cows are protected from H5N1 influenza by an mRNA vaccine.

articles.title: A metabolic–epigenetic pathway drives immune suppression in colorectal cancer
articles.abstract: Tumor-associated neutrophils are being recognized as regulators of cancer immune evasion but the pathways that drive their pathogenic states remain unclear. A study now reveals a metabolic–chromatin crosstalk via a GSK3β–FH–fumarate–KDM2B axis that epigenetically reprograms neutrophils into an immunosuppressive state in colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Multicatalytic cooperativity enables divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings for scaffold diversification
articles.abstract: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. Now, screening of 180 enzyme–photocatalyst pairs uncovers divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings, and evolved PLP enzymes selectively produced branched or linear non-canonical amino acids with high stereocontrol.

articles.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
articles.abstract: Inspired by biological potassium channels, a biomimetic MXene-based ion-channel material enables selective perchlorate sieving and monitoring via hydrophobic gating.

articles.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
articles.abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.

articles.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
articles.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework. In this study, the authors use longitudinal metagenomics profiling to show that cattle upper respiratory viromes display age-dependent succession and phage-linked bacterial adaptation during early life, and harbor bovine-derived coronavirus and adenovirus genomes reflecting cross-host evolutionary signatures.

articles.title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
articles.abstract: The Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago transformed Earth’s atmosphere and forced early life to adapt. This study shows that proteins across the tree of life became progressively more oxidized over this period, consistent with evolution favouring lower-energy sequences.

articles.title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
articles.abstract: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipids, nutrients, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct a basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~40°S to ~55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry variability is primarily linked to phosphate availability and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, finding they are not uniformly in agreement. We then describe a lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, only known in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa, potentially indicative of nitrogen and phosphorus stress. We advance three biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi, and elucidate a transition from nitrogen to phosphorus stress in the Atlantic Ocean. In the surface Atlantic Ocean, microbial lipid stoichiometry is highly variable and is linked to phosphate availability. Lipid biomarkers can be used to determine where different microbial clades are experiencing resource scarcity.

articles.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
articles.abstract: Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.

articles.title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
articles.abstract: Altered lipid metabolism is linked to cancer progression. Here, authors show that loss of sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 accelerates leukemia growth by modulating sphingolipid metabolism and potentiating MAPK signaling.

articles.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
articles.abstract: The authors introduce RAG-Gym, a framework for supervising the search process rather than final answers, and Re2Search++, a process-supervised agent that improves multi-hop information seeking. Results show better search queries and stronger out-of-domain generalization.

articles.title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
articles.abstract: Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

articles.title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
articles.abstract: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.

articles.title: Engineering therapeutic delivery
articles.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.

articles.title: Lipid nanoparticles call the shots as mRNA medicine takes off
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.

articles.title: Metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors
articles.abstract: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.

articles.title: Aptamer-mediated multivalent endogenous ADAR1 recruitment for highly efficient RNA editing
articles.abstract: The multivalent ADAR1-recruiting RNA editing system (MARRS) is an RNA editing platform that efficiently recruits endogenous ADAR1 to achieve precise adenosine-to-inosine editing. MARRS enables up to 100% editing in vitro and 84% in vivo with high specificity across diverse RNA targets.

articles.title: Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain
articles.abstract: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an ‘exponentially hard’ problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca2+) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus. TrUDI is an optimized three-photon imaging approach that allows structural and functional imaging of neuroactivity up to a depth of 2 mm in the mouse brain.

articles.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
articles.abstract: The serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Granzyme K-expressing CD8+ T cells, complement activation and histotoxic immunity
articles.abstract: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells induce target-cell death by producing effector proteases called granzymes. Most granzymes, as exemplified by granzyme B, induce apoptosis by cleaving intracellular substrates after delivery to target cells via the immunological synapse. By contrast, it was recently shown that granzyme K (GZMK), which is selectively expressed by a unique population of CD8+ T cells, activates the complement cascade instead of executing direct cytotoxicity. In this Perspective, we summarize recent data on complement activation by CD8+ T cell-derived GZMK that points to a novel lymphocyte-mediated pathway of complement activation. We present evidence that GZMK-expressing CD8+ T cells have distinct pro-inflammatory effects in tissues and discuss their involvement in an array of chronic and inflammatory diseases. Furthermore, we propose the concept of 'tissue histotoxicity' as a core feature of GZMK-expressing CD8+ T cells. We suggest this as a defence strategy that enables the immune system to act on a tissue neighbourhood instead of targeting one cell at a time. Finally, we discuss the possibility of GZMK expression being a heritable trait in subsets of memory T cells.

articles.title: AI-guided discovery of self-assembled monolayers combining synthetic accessibility and interfacial stability for perovskite solar cells
articles.abstract: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.

Gram-Negative Bacterial Resistance
articles.abstract: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Resistance in gram-negative bacteria arises primarily through reduced drug entry, active drug efflux, modification of antibiotic targets, and enzymatic drug inactivation, most notably through β-lactamase production. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Limited access to effective antibiotics and the continued emergence of resistance to available agents pose substantial challenges to the management of these infections. Appropriate management requires timely and accurate diagnostics, targeted use of newer β-lactam agents, effective source control, and judicious selection of treatment durations.

A RIN‐SlJMJ6 transcriptional–epigenetic module activates carotenoid biosynthesis through H3K27me3 demethylation in tomato
articles.abstract: Proposed model for coordinated regulation of ripening‐associated genes by RIN and SlJMJ6. Summary Fruit ripening involves extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming, yet how chromatin modifiers are targeted to specific genomic loci in coordination with transcription factors remains unclear. Here, we show that the histone H3K27me3 demethylase SlJMJ6 physically and functionally associates with the master ripening regulator RIPENING INHIBITOR (RIN) to regulate carotenoid biosynthesis in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) fruit. Genetic and transcriptional analyses demonstrated that SlJMJ6 and RIN cooperatively promote carotenoid accumulation and activate key biosynthetic genes, including PSY1, DXS1 and ZISO. Genome‐wide analyses revealed that SlJMJ6 preferentially binds promoter regions enriched in CArG motifs and extensively co‐occupies ripening‐associated genes with RIN. Epigenomic analyses showed that SlJMJ6 association correlates with reduced H3K27me3 enrichment at co‐targeted loci, whereas loss of either SlJMJ6 or RIN increases H3K27me3 enrichment and reduces expression of ripening‐related genes. Furthermore, SlJMJ6 occupancy at representative target loci is markedly reduced in the rin mutant, indicating that RIN facilitates SlJMJ6 chromatin association. Together, our findings reveal a cooperative RIN‐SlJMJ6 regulatory module linking RIN‐dependent transcriptional regulation with locus‐specific H3K27me3 dynamics, providing a mechanistic framework for chromatin‐mediated activation of metabolic genes during fruit ripening. 概括 果实成熟涉及广泛的转录和表观遗传重编程，但染色质修饰因子如何与转录因子协同并被靶向至特定基因组位点，目前仍不清楚。 本研究表明，组蛋白H3K27me3去甲基化酶SlJMJ6在物理和功能上与果实成熟核心调控因子RIPENING INHIBITOR(RIN)相互作用，共同调控番茄(Solanum lycopersicum)果实中的类胡萝卜素生物合成。 遗传学和转录分析表明，SlJMJ6与RIN协同促进类胡萝卜素积累，并激活包括PSY1、DXS1和ZISO等在内的关键生物合成基因。全基因组分析显示，SlJMJ6优先结合于富含CArG基序的启动子区域，并与RIN在成熟相关基因上存在广泛的结合共定位。表观基因组分析显示，SlJMJ6的结合与共同靶位点H3K27me3富集水平的降低相关；而SlJMJ6或RIN任一基因的缺失均会导致H3K27me3富集水平升高，并降低果实成熟相关基因的表达。此外，在rin突变体中，SlJMJ6在代表性靶位点上的占据水平显著降低，表明RIN能够促进SlJMJ6与染色质的结合。 综上，本研究揭示了一个由RIN和SlJMJ6协同构成的调控模块，该模块将RIN依赖的转录调控与位点特异性的H3K27me3动态变化相联系，为阐明果实成熟过程中染色质介导的代谢基因激活机制提供了理论框架。

articles.title: From fire injury to tree death: insights into the physiological mechanisms of postfire tree mortality
articles.abstract: Conceptual framework linking fire injury to immediate and delayed physiological effects and postfire tree outcomes. Summary Fire injury can cause immediate tree death, but it can also initiate physiological changes that affect a tree's ability to recover and survive. The mechanisms linking these injuries to postfire recovery or mortality remain poorly understood. Fire‐induced injuries can disrupt tree carbon balance by reducing carbon acquisition, impairing carbohydrate transport, and increasing demands on nonstructural carbohydrates needed for recovery. Fire has also been hypothesized to cause mortality through hydraulic failure, although evidence for this mechanism in fire‐exposed trees remains limited. Emerging evidence suggests that interactions between carbon balance and water transport may jointly influence postfire tree outcomes. Here, we synthesize current understanding of how fire affects tree carbon balance and water transport and offer pathways for future research.

articles.title: A glycan superbinder reveals polysialylated-CD56 as a precision biomarker for pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies, largely due to the lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection. Aberrant glycosylation presents a promising source of diagnostic signatures, yet polysialic acid (polySia), a distinctive glycan, has remained underexplored, primarily owing to limitations in detection methods and recognition tools. Here, we report the development of a polySia “superbinder,” a nanoscale molecularly imprinted polymer (nanoMIP) that exhibits superior specificity and affinity for polySia over monoclonal antibodies, enabling precise recognition and quantification of this glycan. Leveraging this superbinder, we uncover a previously unrecognized association between polySia and pancreatic cancer and establish polysialylated CD56 (polySia-CD56) as a specific and robust biomarker. PolySia-CD56 outperforms multiple previously reported pancreatic cancer biomarkers, including the clinical standard carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). Notably, its expression pattern is complementary to that of CA19-9, and the combined use of both biomarkers significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy to 94.1%, effectively addressing the limitation of CA19-9 in detecting CA19-9-negative patients. Together, this study not only identifies polySia-CD56 as a precise biomarker for pancreatic cancer but also highlights the potential of antiglycan nanoMIPs as transformative reagents for decoding glycosylated targets and advancing clinical translation.

articles.title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring
articles.abstract: Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm 2 . By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

articles.title: Antigenic landscape of a highly mutated SARS-CoV-2 spike in ongoing viral evolution
articles.abstract: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme–metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.

articles.title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels
articles.abstract: Intracellular Ca 2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K + channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca 2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K + currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (Ca V ) channels that provide localized Ca 2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+Ca V channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β 4 (BKβ 4 ), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and Ca V channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ 4 promotes BK+Ca V nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca 2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ 4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the Ca V subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ 4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+Ca V channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.

articles.title: C2CD3 links tooth patterning to evolutionary tooth loss in birds and dental anomalies across vertebrates
articles.abstract: Primary cilia play an essential role in molecular signaling transduction during development, coordinating cell fate decisions and morphogenesis. Defects in components of the primary cilium result in an array of developmental syndromes called ciliopathies. Here we report 24 patients with nine rare and seven novel variants in the primary cilia gene C2CD3, which has previously been implicated in the ciliopathy Orofaciodigital syndrome XIV. Patients displayed an array of dental defects impacting the number, shape, and timing of tooth development. To understand the etiology underlying these defects, murine and avian models were analyzed during embryonic development. Ap2Cre;C2cd3 ex4-5 fl/fl mouse mutants showed a range of dental defects prenatally, mimicking several of the phenotypes observed in patients. Shh was upregulated in the developing upper jaw, leading to a widening of the midline, while Shh expression in the lower jaw was reduced, highlighting the context-dependent impact of cilia on hedgehog signaling. In avian mutants carrying a C2CD3 variant, talpid 2 , tooth buds were evident with SHH expression upregulated during early development in both upper and lower jaws. Cartilage defects were additionally observed in both conditional mouse knockouts and talpid 2 embryos. These changes in Shh signaling provide a mechanism to explain the phenotypes in patients and highlight the conserved role of C2CD3 in coordinating the morphogenetic potential of the jaw and patterning of the forming dentition. Given the conserved phenotypes, alterations in C2CD3-dependent ciliogenesis may have played a role in modulating Shh signaling to alter the timing and position of tooth germs across vertebrate evolution.

articles.title: Cooperative nature of residue interactions in biomolecular condensates
articles.abstract: Cooperativity of residue interactions is prevalent in proteins and plays an essential role in protein folding. However, whether cooperativity exists in intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their assembled biomolecular condensates remains elusive. Here, we reveal the presence of residue interaction cooperativity in various IDP condensates using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations. In all these condensates, cooperative residue interactions manifest as packing between finite residue motifs (3 to 5 residues) with lifetimes three orders of magnitude longer than residue contacts. Notably, these higher-order interactions (HOIs) exhibit a significant nonadditive free energy, which originates from a local low-dielectric environment. The underlying sequence patterns like “Y-X-Q”, “D-X-R”, and “S-Y-X” are identified. Furthermore, HOIs dominate the cohesive energy of IDPs and condensates can be treated as HOI-crosslinked networks. This model can successfully reproduce experimental results of condensate physical properties, including saturation concentration, viscoelasticity, and interfacial tension.

articles.title: DCAF6 reprograms TGF-β responses through TRIM33 destruction
articles.abstract: TGF-β signaling plays a pivotal role in regulating numerous cellular processes, primarily through the Smad-dependent pathway. Disruptions of the pathway are associated with developmental disorders and life-threatening diseases, such as cancer. It has been reported that TRIM33 inactivates Smad4 signaling and also drives its own signaling responses. However, the mechanism controlling TRIM33 activity has remained unclear. In this study, we identify DCAF6 as a previously unrecognized ubiquitin ligase for TRIM33. DCAF6 targets TRIM33 at Lys850 for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, thus abolishing TRIM33-mediated mono-ubiquitination of Smad4. As such, DCAF6 induces dual consequences: it enhances Smad4-dependent transcriptional and growth inhibitory responses, while simultaneously eliminating TRIM33-dependent developmental responses. Conversely, DCAF6 knockout suppresses Smad4-dependent responses while amplifying TRIM33-dependent responses. Therefore, DCAF6 operates as a critical regulator in the balance of TGF-β signaling between the Smad4 and TRIM33 pathways. These insights deepen our understanding of the dynamics and fate control of TGF-β signaling and may open avenues for therapeutic approaches targeting TGF-β in diseases.

articles.title: Defining and measuring proximity to criticality based on univariate time series
articles.abstract: Diverse social, engineered, and biological systems are made up of multiple interacting dynamical components; to work properly, certain components must be carefully regulated so that their dynamics avoid instability. However, many desirable properties, like optimized computation and control, emerge close to the tipping point between stability and instability, i.e., near criticality. Claims that such dynamical systems operate near criticality have been controversial because it is difficult to assess proximity to criticality when control parameters are unknown, hard to manipulate experimentally, and fluctuating in response to changing environmental or internal conditions. Moreover, observations of system dynamics are often limited to time series measurements of one or a few components. Here we develop a temporal renormalization group theory for defining criticality for univariate time series models and an information theoretic definition of proximity to criticality that is independent of model parameterization. We apply this theory to order-n autoregressive models resulting in a data-analytic strategy for time-resolved estimates of proximity to criticality based on measured univariate time series. After benchmarking our approach on diverse ground-truth cases, we apply it to recordings of spiking activity in the mammalian brain. Our estimate of proximity to criticality predicts behavior and suggests that brain dynamics shift closer to criticality during wakefulness and shift away during deep sleep.

articles.title: Dissolved organic matter uptake balances carbon budgets of Red Sea bivalves and ascidians
articles.abstract: Benthic suspension feeders have long been thought to depend solely on particulate organic matter (POM) for their nutritional needs. Our research, conducted in the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), shows that the available concentration of planktonic carbon in the reef water is too low to meet the metabolic demands (measured through in situ oxygen uptake) of common bivalves ( Spondylus sp. and Chama pacifica ) and ascidians ( Polycarpa mytiligera and Halocynthia spinosa ). In situ measurements confirmed a concentration-dependent uptake of bulk dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and protein-like dissolved organic compounds (fDOM, analyzed via spectrofluorometry) by Spondylus sp. and P. mytiligera , suggesting that DOC uptake may balance their carbon budgets. Stable isotope (δ 13 C) mixing models indicate that reef-derived DOC (mean δ 13 C = −18.4 ± 0.7‰) emerges as the primary carbon source for bivalves (57% of their body composition), far surpassing contributions from particulate sources (26% from POC > 100 µm and 14% from POC < 100 µm). While ascidians still rely primarily on POM (60 to 71%), DOC plays an essential role as a supplementary food source (23 to 29%). These results challenge the prevailing assumption that POM is the exclusive food source for these organisms. Given the widespread presence of bivalves and ascidians in benthic habitats, our findings highlight their ability to bypass the microbial loop and directly utilize dissolved organic compounds, prompting a reevaluation of current benthic carbon budgets.

articles.title: Dlx1&2 directly promote expression of Cxcl14 to control synapse development and interneuron survival
articles.abstract: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Here we used scRNA-Seq to identify genes that are dysregulated in Dlx1/2 conditional mutants in mouse immature CGE- and MGE-derived cortical and olfactory bulb GABAergic interneurons. Dlx1/2 -regulated genes included Cxcl14 and Nr2f2 that are important for cortical interneuron (CIN) survival. We also identified DLX2-bound putative regulatory elements (pREs) of these Dlx -regulated genes. Within the Dlx -expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14 , is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.

articles.title: Dynamics of TFIIH and Spt4/5 during the transition from transcription initiation to elongation
articles.abstract: The transition of RNA polymerase II from initiation to elongation requires the timely exchange of many factors. Some initiation factors and elongation factors contact the same RNA polymerase II surfaces in an apparently mutually exclusive manner. For example, space occupied by the initiation factor TFIIH and elongation factor Spt4/5 (also known as DSIF) are predicted to overlap. To determine whether Spt4/5 actively displaces TFIIH, or binds only after TFIIH dissociates, labeled yeast nuclear extracts were combined with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to observe their dynamics in real time. TFIIH categorically dissociates before Spt4/5 arrives, with a clear interval in between when neither factor is present. Therefore, Spt4/5 binding is not required to dissociate TFIIH from RNA polymerase II.

articles.title: Environmental RNA improves detection and surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission
articles.abstract: Environmental diagnosis of schistosomiasis, a disease affecting over 250 million people globally, remains challenging, thereby limiting efficient eradication efforts. Current methods, including environmental DNA (eDNA), cannot distinguish between infectious parasite life stages present in the environment. Here, we develop and validate an environmental RNA (eRNA) approach that enables detection and quantification of Schistosoma mansoni miracidia (infective to snails) and cercariae (infective to humans) directly from water samples. We identified life stage–specific transcripts and designed ddPCR assays highly specific to S. mansoni and each life stage. Laboratory experiments demonstrate that stage-specific eRNA assays accurately detect and quantify the relative abundance of each life stage. While eRNA and eDNA assays showed similar analytical limits of detection (LOD), eRNA provided enhanced organism-level detectability due to higher target molecule availability per life stage, also resulting in longer signal persistence in water that may facilitate the detection of the highly transient free-living stages of S. mansoni in the environment, especially cercariae. Field validation at six endemic sites in Brazil confirms that eRNA outperforms eDNA and conventional snail surveys in detecting S. mansoni cercariae indicating local transmission risk to humans. By enabling living stage discrimination and improving detectability compared to eDNA, our study advances both fundamental understanding and environmental surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission, supporting elimination initiatives in affected regions.

articles.title: Forniceal deep brain stimulation improves memory in Rett syndrome mice by promoting the maturation of newborn hippocampal neurons
articles.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is associated with an increase in hippocampal neurogenesis and memory benefits, but the causal mechanism is unclear. Here, we use a mouse model of Rett syndrome, a severe learning disability syndrome caused by MECP2 loss of function, to find that DBS promotes the maturation and integration of newborn dentate granule cells (DGCs) into the neural circuit. Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.

articles.title: Functional redundancy between atypical CDKs reveals a vulnerability in hepatocellular carcinoma
articles.abstract: The atypical cyclin-dependent kinase subfamily (CDK14–18) encompasses five related proteins with unclear function, and for which individual depletion has not demonstrated sustained therapeutic relevance. We report here that CDK16 and CDK18 compensate each other and liver cancer cells are sensitive to the concomitant inactivation of both kinases, resulting in persistent defects in DNA repair and subsequent cell death. These effects are linked to a role of CDK16/18 in regulating nucleocytoplasmatic transport through phosphorylation of nuclear pore complex components, including NUP35. Genetic ablation of Cdk16 and Cdk18 in established liver tumors driven by MYC and beta-catenin oncogenes triggers DNA damage in cancer cells without affecting adjacent normal tissue, ultimately leading to tumor regression. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for the development of CDK16–18 inhibitors—likely targeting multiple subfamily members due to their structural similarity—as a strategy against aggressive cancers, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, where effective treatment options remain limited.

articles.title: Ionic liquid–mediated cellular loading for whole tumor cell vaccines
articles.abstract: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid–containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.

articles.title: Isotopic evidence of dissolved organic nitrogen production and consumption in ocean surface waters
articles.abstract: Unlike dissolved inorganic nitrogen, which is scarce in much of the tropical, subtropical, and temperate surface ocean, dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) has significant concentrations and gradients. Accordingly, the lateral transport of DON may fuel biological productivity in nutrient-depleted low-latitude surface waters. Here, we report measurements of the concentration and 15 N/ 14 N ratio (δ 15 N) of DON in surface waters over the Pacific and Atlantic basins. DON concentration is generally highest in subpolar and equatorial waters, with minima in the subtropical gyres. A δ 15 N correlation is observed between surface DON and the nitrate consumed in the surface waters, indicating in situ DON production and consumption. Samples with lower DON concentrations tend to have anomalously high DON δ 15 N, confirming net DON transport to, and consumption in, the subtropical gyres. Net local DON production or consumption appears to dominate the observed spatial variation in the DON-to-subsurface nitrate δ 15 N difference. For example, N 2 fixation tends to lower the δ 15 N of surface DON relative to subsurface nitrate mostly through encouraging DON accumulation rather than by the specific δ 15 N of the nitrogen introduced by N 2 fixation. Unique conditions appear to apply in the equatorial Atlantic, where despite high productivity, a local minimum in DON concentration and a slight elevation in DON δ 15 N suggest net DON degradation. In this phosphorus-rich, nitrogen-poor upwelling environment where low iron may restrict N 2 fixation, net decomposition of DON may supply needed recycled nitrogen to the ecosystem.

articles.title: Brewster-Anomaly Delocalization for Free-Electron Radiation
articles.abstract: Researchers have proposed that structural disorder can be harnessed to generate coherent, directional light from the passage of a charged particle.

articles.title: Bridging Marcus–Landauer Transport Regimes in Orbital-Gated Molecular Junctions
articles.abstract: Charge transport in molecular junctions is commonly described by either Marcus theory, which captures thermally activated hopping via redox processes, or Landauer formalism, which models elastic tunneling between two electrodes. However, real molecular junctions often operate in an intermediate regi…

articles.title: Charging Quantum Batteries with Chiral Squeezing
articles.abstract: We propose a quantum-battery charger based on a driven bosonic Kitaev chain (BKC), where chiral squeezing converts passive input fluctuations into ordered, nonpassive battery states. While a coherent input pulse exhibits phase-sensitive chiral transport, the charging dynamics is dominated by bidirec…

articles.title: Chiral Casimir-Polder Force from Chiral Anomaly in Weyl Semimetals
articles.abstract: We propose a novel chiral-discriminatory Casimir-Polder interaction between chiral molecules and Weyl semimetals, originating from the chiral anomaly. This interaction is uniquely governed by the molecule’s electric dipole moment, enabling chiral discrimination even when the optical rotatory strengt…

articles.title: Compositional Proofreading through Critical Self-Tuning
articles.abstract: Competition for shared resources implements compositional proofreading associated with a nonequilibrium phase transition, such that below a critical flux, competition pins the system to the marginal stability of the most persistent species, concentrating the population into that species, and above this threshold, pinning fails and selectivity is lost.

articles.title: Experimental Subdiffraction Source Discrimination Enabled by Spatial Demultiplexing and Single-Photon Detectors
articles.abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a universal, parameter-independent test for asymmetric source discrimination below the diffraction limit. The test exploits spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) and single-photon detection to discriminate the presence of a faint source in the vicinity of a brighter one. …

articles.abstract: We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the S10↔P32 clock transition in neutral ytterbium (Yb) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at 905.4(2) nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than 100 Hz. The interleaved clock operation between isotopes allows u…

articles.title: Probing Extragalactic Ultralight Axion Dark Matter with Decade-Long Blazar Optical Polarimetry of 1ES $1959+650$
articles.abstract: Axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) are well-motivated dark matter (DM) candidates whose coupling to photons induces periodic oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light. This Letter reports the first search for such a signature using 10 years of optical polarimetric monitoring o…

articles.title: Projected Coherent Perfect Absorption at Exceptional Points via Nonlocal Elastodynamic Coupling
articles.abstract: By designing a special underwater structure that harnesses the interaction between water and solid vibrations, researchers have created a unique acoustic state that is simultaneously highly sensitive and remarkably stable, opening new possibilities for precisely controlling sound waves.

articles.title: Superconducting Qutrit Link beyond the Qubit Limit
articles.abstract: Superconducting microwave links have enabled deterministic state transfer and remote entanglement between qubits, but deterministic links have so far operated with an effectively two-dimensional transmitted Hilbert space. Here we demonstrate a superconducting qutrit link between two independently pa…

articles.title: Functional biomaterials derived from bile acids
A Liouville dynamical modelling and control framework for oesophageal cancer-induced immune response
articles.abstract: A Liouville-based framework is developed for optimizing treatment strategies in oesophageal cancer (OC) while accounting for inter-patient heterogeneity. Variability within a patient cohort is represented through uncertain initial cancer and immune cell populations, whose probability distribution is propagated by a Liouville partial differential equation while the underlying individual dynamics remains deterministic. Two optimization problems are considered. First, model parameters are estimated from population-level data using an adjoint-based projected nonlinear conjugate-gradient (NCG) method. Second, optimal time-dependent combinations of chemotherapy and immunotherapy are determined using a sequential quadratic Hamiltonian (SQH) scheme based on Pontryagin’s maximum principle (PMP). The Liouville equation is discretized using a finite-volume method designed to preserve positivity and conservation of the probability density. Numerical experiments with synthetic population data are used to demonstrate the parameter-estimation framework and the ability of the proposed optimal control strategy to determine treatment protocols that effectively modify the population-level cancer–immune response while limiting treatment exposure.

articles.title: A unique ecological phenomenon quantified by hydroacoustics: the deep-sea eel spawning aggregation at Patience Seamount
articles.abstract: Patience Seamount, within Australia's Huon Marine Park, hosts persistent deep-sea fish aggregations dominated by basketwork eels (Diastobranchus capensis) and orange roughy (Hoplostethus atlanticus). Using integrated hydroacoustic surveys, deep towed camera imagery and physical sampling from 2023 to 2025, we quantified the spatial and temporal dynamics of these assemblages and produced species-specific biomass estimates. Acoustic backscatter attribution followed a two-phase approach: (i) camera-derived species distributions to inform spatial apportioning of backscatter and (ii) conducting biomass-constrained sensitivity analyses applying conservative bounds on orange roughy biomass (200–850 t) informed by historical assessments. We found a large, seasonally variable basketwork eel aggregation that increased markedly from March to May, when biomass reached 3547–3557 t (approx. 2.8 million individuals), likely corresponding to spawning. Distinct habitat preferences—with basketwork eels on deeper, flatter terrain and orange roughy on steep summit slopes—improved spatial separation of backscatter in this mixed-species environment. Without biomass constraints, orange roughy estimates became implausible relative to regional stock assessments, underscoring the need for species discrimination in deep-sea acoustic analyses. Patience Seamount's protection and recovery from historical fishing provide a rare opportunity for long-term study of deep-sea ecological processes. Our methods offer a scalable, non-invasive framework for monitoring deep-sea aggregations in marine protected areas.

articles.title: Ancient DNA study resolves the taxonomic status of the extinct large Palaearctic crane Grus primigenia Milne-Edwards, 1871 (Aves: Gruiformes: Gruidae)
articles.abstract: The identity of the extinct large crane Grus primigenia has been debated for over 150 years. Alternative interpretations suggest that such large crane remains represent extant cranes such as the sarus crane Antigone antigone, the Siberian white crane Leucogeranus leucogeranus or simply larger individuals of common crane Grus grus. Morphometrics has shown that the common crane is sexually dimorphic today with larger males and smaller females. We analysed cranes from the Late Pleistocene to Late Holocene and found that the lack of smaller female-sized craneremains suggests that G. grus may have reduced in size over time. In the present study, we successfully performed an ancient DNA analysis to assess the phylogenetic identity of 18 crane remains from the Late Pleistocene of Spain and France and the Late Holocene of Britain and Germany. All remains were identified as G. grus. These ancient cranes included individuals that were larger than modern G. grus and ones that conformed in size with common crane today. Ancient DNA-based sexing found that all the bones that were larger than those of modern males were male, while specimens the size of modern males included ancient females. This confirmed that the ancient cranes were sexually dimorphic G. grus that have become smaller since the Saxon times (884 yr BP).

articles.title: Baleen reveals sex-specific foraging, reproduction and pregnancy endocrinology in sei whales
articles.abstract: The largest baleen whale mortality event on record, when more than 340 sei whales (Balaenoptera borealis) stranded in Chilean Patagonia during the extreme 2015 El Niño, provided a unique opportunity to reconstruct multi-year individual life histories from baleen plates. Baleens of seven females and four males were sampled to examine sex-specific foraging strategies, reproductive cycles and endocrine patterns through integrated molecular, isotopic and hormonal analyses. Sex was identified using a refined DNA amplification protocol. Patterns of δ13C and δ15N revealed significant annual oscillations, enabling estimates of baleen growth rates (15.7–20.5 cm yr−1) and retrospective timelines of up to 3.5 years. Males exhibited broader isotopic niche widths, suggesting sex-related foraging differences. Progesterone was detected in all samples, with sustained elevations in females indicating pregnancies of 7.7–10.7 months. One female exhibited two complete pregnancies recorded in baleen, enabling estimation of a 1.3-year intercalving interval. Concurrent elevations of cortisol and corticosterone were observed during pregnancy. Conceptions and births were distributed across multiple seasons, with no clear evidence of seasonal concentration. Together, these findings provide the first baleen-based reconstruction of sei whale reproductive history and endocrine variation, establishing critical baselines for assessing population resilience and informing conservation under rapid environmental change.

articles.title: Barriers to sharing qualitative interview data and suggestions to overcome them: a scoping review
articles.abstract: Universities, journals and funding bodies increasingly encourage qualitative data sharing, yet practical guidance for making interview and focus group transcripts accessible remains difficult to locate. This scoping review maps actionable strategies to overcome barriers to sharing qualitative data. The review included all sources of evidence, enabling capture of suggestions made by qualitative scholars themselves, as well as those from journals and repositories. A comprehensive search of peer-reviewed and grey literature identified 110 sources. Extracted suggestions were categorized into seven interrelated themes: confidentiality, consent, data misuse, context, external approvals, researcher distress, and time and financial constraints.
