These findings are consolidated into a table-based tool to guide researchers toward the most practical resources for each barrier. The review highlights the diversity and complexity of qualitative data sharing, the absence of systematic evaluation of strategies and the importance of avoiding one-size-fits-all data sharing expectations. By providing a structured, accessible resource, this work aims to support researchers in ethically, effectively and confidently sharing qualitative data, while informing funders and institutions developing open data policies.

articles.title: Calibrated term presence modelling for CCUS patent abstracts: a case study with variational autoencoders and retrieval baselines
articles.abstract: Patent codes may lack granularity when carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) inventions combine climate and chemical engineering concepts. We evaluate term presence models on 10 603 English patent abstracts through document completion, calibration and cooperative patent classification (CPC) prefix retrieval. We compare two variational autoencoders (VAEs), a product of the experts latent Dirichlet allocation model, a unigram prior, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), PatentSBERTa and PaECTER. With a target masking rate of 50 per cent for positive terms, TF-IDF nearest neighbours give the best ranked completion. The direct Bernoulli VAE ranks slightly above the negative binomial to Bernoulli VAE (NB VAE), while the latter has lower expected calibration error (ECE). Conditional posterior predictive draws retain positive rank associations for document and term counts, but the NB VAE and direct Bernoulli VAE predict 1.47 and 1.63 times the observed positive count, respectively. PaECTER and the TF-IDF representation after singular value decomposition (SVD) give the strongest CPC prefix retrieval, while VAE probabilities could support inspectable term screening.

articles.title: Can optimal caching models predict changes in diurnal feeder use patterns in black-capped chickadees ( Poecile atricapillus )?
articles.abstract: Many birds collect and store food for later use, a behaviour known as caching. Theoretical models predict that caching effort is concentrated in a single peak during the day, though the precise timing of that peak depends on multiple factors. We studied diurnal patterns of feeder used in a population of 50 individually marked black-capped chickadees (Poecile atricapillus) in late summer. We used total daily feeder visits (1 visit ≈ 1 sunflower seed) as a proxy for caching intensity because daily feeder visits (range 11–339 feeder visits per bird per day) often exceeded the required intake of about 45 sunflower seeds for chickadees at this time of year, consistent with a wide range of caching effort. Patterns of feeder use were always bimodal, and increases in hourly feeder visits occurred throughout the day with increased total daily feeder visits, however, the greatest relative increase in feeder visits was during midday. Post hoc analyses revealed that this population-level effect was driven by individual differences; some chickadees increased morning feeder visits with increasing total daily feeder visits, while others increased midday or end-of-day feeder visits. Future work should investigate drivers of these individual differences, including the role of interference competition.

articles.title: Can you feel meaning? Spirituality involves stronger sensorimotor associations with abstract concepts
articles.abstract: Understanding abstract phenomena is a fundamental human need. Emerging evidence increasingly points to the multidimensionality of abstract knowledge representations, with theories emphasizing the importance of both embodied and linguistic influences. In the present paper, we argue that the strength with which embodiment is associated with abstract concepts is moderated by cultural beliefs about ontological meaning. Specifically, we predicted that self-identified spirituality—a belief system guided by an experiential approach to understanding reality—contributes to greater sensorimotor associations with abstract concepts. As hypothesized, across four studies (n = 729; in the USA and the UK), Western spiritual beliefs involved stronger sensorimotor associations for highly abstract compared to concrete concepts. Importantly, religious beliefs that conceptually overlap with spirituality did not contribute to these associations. Altogether, individual differences in belief systems guide people's conscious attendance to sensorimotor features when thinking about abstract concepts, with spiritual individuals likely feeling the meaning of words through linking abstract thought with bodily experiences.

articles.title: Condition-associated modulation of melanin-based skin pigmentation in juvenile Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
articles.abstract: Melanin-based pigmentation in vertebrates has often been regarded as a stable trait, inexpensive to produce and highly heritable. Accumulating evidence, however, links melanin patterns to behavioural, physiological and endocrine variation. In salmonids, eumelanin-based skin spottiness has been associated with stress responsiveness and coping style, but it remains unclear to what extent environmental challenge induces within-individual state-dependent changes in spot expression. Here, we examined whether feeding dynamics during acclimation to novelty are associated with longitudinal changes in visible skin spot density in juvenile Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), in which dark patterns are expressed through eumelanin-containing melanophores. Fish were transferred from group rearing to individual housing, inducing transient feeding suppression followed by large inter-individual variation in feeding recovery and growth. Although visible spot density declined overall, the magnitude and direction of change varied among individuals and covaried with feed intake, growth and condition factor. Individuals with higher feed intake and growth, and smaller declines in condition factor, exhibited reduced spot loss and, in some cases, increased spot density, whereas lower-performing individuals showed larger reductions. Pre-existing spot patterns predicted post-transfer performance. These findings suggest that salmonid skin spots track resource acquisition and coping capacity, consistent with regulated phenotypic plasticity in condition-associated visible pigmentation.

articles.title: Correction to: ‘A polycarboxylic/ether composite polymer electrolyte via in situ UV-curing for all-solid-state lithium battery’ (2020) by Wang et al.
Do carnivorous plants exploit prey perceptual bias? A case study in Drosera finlaysonii with yellow-green traps
articles.abstract: Perceptual biases—disproportionate sensory responses to specific stimuli—are widespread in animals and can be exploited by predators to attract prey. However, this mechanism has not been rigorously tested in carnivorous plants. We investigated whether the yellow-green traps of Drosera finlaysonii (Droseraceae) exploit hemipterans’ preference for yellow to yellow-green stimuli that strongly activate green relative to blue photoreceptors. Using multispectral imaging, we quantified trap brightness and modelled the green-to-blue photoreceptor activation ratio (G/B ratio) of hemipteran prey. We characterized the taxonomic composition of prey captured by D. finlaysonii and deployed adhesive models differing in brightness and G/B ratio. We then compared arthropod assemblages between plants and models, and taxon-specific capture numbers among models. D. finlaysonii traps were brighter and had higher G/B ratios than sympatric graminoid leaves. Hemiptera were a major prey component, although their relative abundance varied between years. Yellow models, with the highest G/B ratio, captured more hemipterans than other colour models. However, arthropod assemblages captured by D. finlaysonii differed from those captured by yellow models, with proportionally more dipterans and fewer hemipterans. Thus, a high G/B ratio may contribute to hemipteran attraction and capture but cannot alone explain the overall prey assemblage in D. finlaysonii.

articles.title: Dynamic backgrounds enhance the confusion effect
articles.abstract: Natural environments are generally dynamic; examples of background motion include changes in illumination and moving physical features, such as wind-blown foliage or flowing water. Experimental evidence suggests dynamic backgrounds can impede predation by masking the movement of a target, but the interaction between background motion and the movement of prey in groups has not been investigated. Dynamic backgrounds could potentially enhance the confusion effect, the phenomenon whereby locating and/or tracking a single target among similar individuals (‘distractors’) becomes less successful owing to difficulty in discriminating this target from its conspecifics. We investigated whether dynamic backgrounds contribute to the confusion effect by impeding accurate tracking of a target among distractors. We hypothesize that any effect would be greatest when the temporal properties of the background's movement match those of the moving objects. In two experiments, human surrogate ‘predators’ tracked a single target among distractors, moving unpredictably, on backgrounds that drifted coherently in a given direction. Tracking was generally poorer when backgrounds and objects moved at more closely matched speeds, probably owing to temporary masking of prey target movement and subsequent difficulty in re-locating the target among distractors. Our findings identify a role for dynamic backgrounds in defending against predation.

articles.title: Ecological role of Acropora palmata for its associated species in barrier reefs
articles.abstract: Acropora palmata is a key branching coral in the Caribbean, contributing to reef complexity and providing habitat for diverse species. In recent decades, its abundance and distribution have declined, highlighting the need to better understand its ecological role. Visual surveys along linear transects in the Limones and Picudas reefs (Quintana Roo, Mexico) identified macrofaunal species associated with A. palmata and evaluated their interactions to assess habitat use. A total of 81 species were recorded, 34 of which were shared between both reefs. The recorded groups included fish, crustaceans, polychaetes, echinoderms and molluscs. Species composition was similar across both reefs, despite the particular characteristics of each reef. The structure of A. palmata was found to generate spatially heterogeneous areas that function as habitat, refuge, feeding sites and territorial spaces at the colony level. Although the colony-specific area influenced species abundance, no effect on size was detected. These findings indicate that, at the colony scale, A. palmata provides microhabitats that support diverse assemblages across different reef conditions. This suggests a lack of functional redundancy in the region: Acropora cervicornis, its only structural analogue, mainly shelters small-bodied taxa and has become even more depleted, leaving A. palmata’s habitat role without a substitute.

articles.title: Endosymbiotic Regiella insecticola reduce mummification in native and transinfected aphid hosts but do not prevent reproductive damage post parasitism
articles.abstract: Some bacterial endosymbionts of aphids can reduce mummification rates following attack by parasitoids, yet these endosymbionts can remain at a low frequency in populations even when parasitoids are present. The endosymbiont Regiella insecticola is uncommon in the major pest aphid Myzus persicae despite providing apparent protection against parasitoid attack. Here, we consider population-level effects associated with Regiella in its native M. persicae host as well as Regiella transinfected into pest Rhopalosiphum padi (oat aphids) and Diuraphis noxia (Russian wheat aphids), focusing on two parasitoids (Diaeretiella rapi, Aphidius colemani). We consider their impact not only on mummification rates but also on fecundity of non-mummified aphids that have been stung by wasps as detected by a qPCR assay to detect parasitoid DNA, with experiments simulating a single parasitoid attack event. Regiella produced a sharp decrease in mummification rates of their native and transinfected hosts, but aphids with Regiella that were stung (successful oviposition confirmed by molecular analysis) and not mummified showed low reproduction. The combination of these effects meant we did not detect major differences in the population size of infected and uninfected aphids. These results highlight the importance of considering multi-trait effects when assessing the impacts of endosymbiont infections and predicting the outcome of endosymbiont–host–parasitoid interactions.

articles.title: Environmentally friendly novel macromolecular leveller imidazole-pentaerythritol glycidyl ether with high electroplating performance
articles.abstract: In this study, a novel environmentally friendly leveller, imidazole-pentaerythritol glycidyl ether (IMDPGE), which is free of sulfur (S) and other pollutant elements, was developed by chemical synthesis for blind-hole filling in acidic copper electroplating. The chemical structure of IMDPGE was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. The molecular properties of IMDPGE were investigated through quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, and its levelling performance was predicted accordingly. The electrochemical characteristics of IMDPGE, as well as its interactions with the accelerator bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS) and the suppressor propyleneoxide (PO)-ethylene oxide (EO)-propylene oxide (PO), named PEP (EPE), were evaluated using galvanostatic potential transient measurements, cyclic voltammetry and linear scan voltammetry. The results demonstrated that IMDPGE exhibited strong polarization capability, which persisted even in the absence of SPS. Additionally, a kinetically controlled competitive adsorption existed between IMDPGE and SPS, while a synergistic inhibitory effect was observed between IMDPGE and EPE. The blind-hole filling performance of IMDPGE was verified through electroplating experiments. For the optimized EPE-SPS-IMDPGE additive system, a filling rate of 90.7% and a surface copper thickness of 7.7 µm were achieved after electroplating at a current density of 2 A dm–² for 30 minutes.

articles.title: Epidemiological trajectory of Mpox in Brazil, 2022–2025: evidence of geographic consolidation and syndemic burden
articles.abstract: Mpox has transitioned from outbreak to sustained transmission in Brazil, a country with high ecological and social connectivity. We analysed the epidemiological trajectory of mpox during 2022–2025 using 14 475 laboratory-confirmed cases reported by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. Our findings indicate geographical consolidation of transmission, with the highest incidence observed in the southeast and midwest regions. The epidemic disproportionately affects men (93.0%), particularly young adults, with transmission primarily associated with networks of men who have sex with men (69.1%). A substantial burden of co-infections was identified: 47.1% of reported cases occurred in persons living with HIV and 30.8% had syphilis. Clinically, most patients presented with cutaneous manifestations (91.3%). These findings highlight the convergence of epidemiological and social determinants shaping mpox transmission in Brazil. Strengthening integrated surveillance systems and ensuring equitable, stigma-free access to prevention and care are critical to reducing transmission and mitigating the risk of broader dissemination.

articles.title: Evolutionary dynamics of a four-stakeholder ecosystem for misinformation governance on short-video platforms
articles.abstract: Misinformation governance on short-video platforms depends on strategic interaction among online media, netizens, platforms and government regulators, but platform decisions are often treated as exogenous in two- and three-party models. We develop a quadripartite evolutionary game model to examine these interactions under bounded rationality. Equilibrium analysis and numerical simulations identify the stable strategy profiles and the conditions under which they emerge. Under the baseline parameters, the system has a unique asymptotically stable profile. Platforms adopt active governance, media report without verification, government regulators apply loose supervision and netizens assess information rationally. Parameter analysis shows that higher platform traffic revenue, a greater probability of insider refutation, and larger credibility and reputational losses accelerate convergence to this profile. Strict supervision can alter the transient evolutionary path and accelerate convergence under the benchmark conditions, but it is not part of the stable profile. Within the model, active platform governance and user rationality are the principal stabilizing factors, while government supervision plays a complementary role. These results provide a modelling basis for coordinating platform, user and regulatory responses to misinformation in short-video ecosystems.

articles.title: Expanding the Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry reference library for North American mammals: new collagen fingerprints from extinct and extant taxa
articles.abstract: Robust zooarchaeological analysis of Pleistocene-Holocene faunal assemblages is fundamental for reconstructing past environments, species distributions, human subsistence and faunal turnovers in North America. However, faunal remains from archaeological and palaeontological sites are commonly highly fragmented or modified, often precluding morphological identification and limiting the information they can provide about faunal communities and their relationships with human populations and changing climates. Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) provides an effective biomolecular means of overcoming this limitation, enabling the identification of unidentifiable bone fragments, but its resolution depends on the availability of empirically validated reference datasets, which remain incomplete for North American fauna. Here, we expand the North American ZooMS reference library by characterizing and validating collagen peptide markers for 22 extant and extinct mammal taxa across four mammalian orders: Artiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Carnivora and Rodentia, integrating Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry fingerprinting with Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry peptide sequencing to provide sequence-level validation of diagnostic peptide markers. The resulting markers enable robust family-level discrimination across a range of taxa with genus- or species-level identification possible for several groups. This expanded reference framework enhances the taxonomic resolution and applicability of ZooMS across North American faunal assemblages, supporting its use for advancing archaeological, palaeontological and conservation-related research on the continent.

articles.title: Extragroup interactions are not related to cognitive performance in a group-living passerine
articles.abstract: Sociality, in particular group-living, can present many challenges to individuals and is widely thought to influence the development and evolution of cognition. However, support for the effect of sociality on cognition is mixed, and it has recently been suggested that an entire axis of sociality has been overlooked—extragroup interactions. Extragroup interactions (those that occur with a heterospecific or conspecific individual outside of the focal individual's group) present informational challenges that may favour certain cognitive phenotypes, such as discrimination, assessment and categorization. We quantified the rates of two types of extragroup interactions (intergroup and interspecific interactions) in adult Western Australian magpies (Gymnorhina tibicen dorsalis) and compared these to individual performance across a battery of four cognitive tasks. We also investigated whether response to playback of intruding conspecifics (an assessment of quantity discrimination abilities) was related to intergroup interaction rate. We hypothesized that greater involvement in extragroup interactions would be positively related to cognitive performance; however, we found no support for this. We did identify a relationship between intergroup interaction rate and response to playback, with individuals involved in more intergroup interactions exhibiting a greater difference in response to one and three calling extragroup conspecifics. Our findings suggest that extragroup interactions experienced in adult life do not influence performance in food-based cognitive tasks, but research on individuals during the developmental stage is needed to rule out an effect of extragroup interactions on cognitive development.

articles.title: Latent variable modelling of condition and reproductive investment in Gryllus vocalis field crickets
articles.abstract: ‘Condition’ is often used to describe the underlying state or quality of an individual and is expected to influence traits essential for fitness. Variation in condition is therefore expected to contribute to differences in reproductive investment. However, both condition and reproductive investment are complex and multi-dimensional, making them difficult to quantify comprehensively. Instead, they are typically inferred using measurable traits, which may capture only limited aspects of these constructs. Herein, we use structural equation modelling to integrate multiple proxy measurements, quantify the influence of underlying condition and reproductive investment on proxies and examine the relationship between condition and reproductive investment. Using Gryllus vocalis field crickets, we constructed sex-specific models to account for differences in reproductive strategies and trait expression between males and females. Both models identified proxies that were significantly influenced by condition and reproductive investment, although the strength of this influence varied across traits, suggesting that some proxies are better indicators than others. Both models also revealed significant positive relationships between condition and reproductive investment. Overall, our results demonstrate that condition positively influences reproductive investment, while revealing that commonly used proxies vary in how well they reflect these underlying constructs.

articles.title: Mechanistic ODE modelling of ovarian tumour microenvironment dynamics under hesperidin exposure
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer progression is driven by complex interactions among tumour, immune, stromal, metabolic and angiogenic processes. Although hesperidin exhibits anti-cancer and immunomodulatory activities, its integrated effects on the tumour microenvironment (TME) remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a mechanistic ODE-based framework integrating tumour growth, immune regulation, macrophage polarization, cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling, hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)−1α/ vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-dependent angiogenesis, glucose–lactate metabolism and redox signalling within a hypothetical ovarian TME centred on PA-1 cells. Simulations across multiple hesperidin concentrations predicted dose-dependent suppression of tumour growth, reduced HIF−1α accumulation, angiogenesis, ECM stiffening and lactate production, accompanied by enhanced anti-tumour immune activity. Local one-at-a-time (OAT) and global Sobol’ sensitivity analyses identified tumour growth kinetics, CAF–ECM interactions, metabolic regulation and selected hesperidin-response parameters as principal determinants of system behaviour. Although not calibrated for quantitative prediction, the proposed framework provides mechanistic insight into how hesperidin-mediated perturbations propagate through interconnected tumour–immune–stromal networks. The model should be regarded as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating platform supporting future experimental validation of hesperidin-mediated mechanisms in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Messy eaters and scavenger hunts: the community ecology of scavenging interactions in a rockpool ecosystem
articles.abstract: Carcasses are valuable resources to those scavengers able to access them. While some generalist foragers are poorly equipped to process carcasses themselves, they may exploit the actions of others by feeding on tissues that the latter expose or detach. Carcasses also attract opportunistic predators, which can target other smaller scavengers, as well as feeding on the carcass itself. We studied these interactions using field-based experiments in a rockpool ecosystem. First, we showed that greater numbers of small fishes and mysids were attracted to areas where scavengers, primarily hermit crabs (Pagurus bernhardus), were feeding on mussel carcass baits compared to treatments where inaccessible carcasses or no-carcass controls were presented. We termed these secondary scavengers, since we did not see them feeding on the carcass directly. Second, we saw predators attack scavengers more frequently in trials where carcasses were present than where they were absent. They also approached stimulus chambers containing aggregations of hermit crabs more often than empty controls. Nonetheless, predator interactions were, overall, infrequent. For these smaller scavengers, carcass-foraging may be a trade-off between access to a sizeable food resource and competition, and sometimes heightened predation risk, from larger scavengers.

articles.title: No association between body dissatisfaction and attentional bias towards lower-weight bodies in a non-clinical sample of women: an eye-tracking study
articles.abstract: Body dissatisfaction is a key risk factor for psychiatric illnesses and is a modifiable target. Previous gaze-tracking research suggests that body dissatisfaction is related to greater attentional bias towards lower-weight bodies. Here, we aimed to partially replicate and extend previous work to verify this association by using realistic body stimuli and a validated scale of body dissatisfaction. Sixty, mostly young, women from the general population underwent eye-tracking while viewing picture pairs of women's bodies morphed to lower and higher weights. Attentional bias was measured as percentage fixation duration, fixation count and first fixations on lower-weight compared to higher-weight bodies. There was weak evidence that all women fixated for longer on lower-weight bodies, and that participants with higher body dissatisfaction spent less time fixating on lower-weight bodies, contrary to our hypotheses and to previous findings, but this effect was not robust to adjustment for age and body mass index. This lack of replication suggests this association is not robust in non-clinical populations. Instead, an overall bias towards lower-weight bodies could contribute to higher levels of body dissatisfaction and risk of mental health problems in younger women. Future studies measuring attentional biases in realistic settings and in clinical populations with eating disorder symptoms are needed.

articles.title: Osteohistological analysis reveals unusual bone tissue patterns in Temminck's ground pangolin ( Smutsia temminckii )
articles.abstract: Temminck's ground pangolin is one of Africa's most threatened mammals, yet little is known about its skeletal biology. This study provides the first osteohistological analysis of its limb bones, documenting patterns of growth, remodelling and skeletal reinforcement. Limb bones exhibit extensive cortical remodelling, with substantial portions of the cortex being composed of compacted coarse cancellous bone, endosteal bone and secondary osteons, together with abundant resorption cavities. Growth marks occur in all elements, but the absence of outer circumferential lamellae and persistence of open vascular canals indicate continued growth and a lack of skeletal maturity despite the presence of up to four annual growth cycles. Extensive skeletal reinforcement occurs throughout the limbs, although elements employ distinct osteohistological patterns. Comparison with the aardvark reveals alternative pathways of skeletal reinforcement, with ground pangolins showing relatively greater secondary remodelling in the hind limb. Ground pangolins are further distinguished by abundant, incompletely infilled resorption cavities extending into the middle and outer cortex, suggesting an unusual pattern of intracortical remodelling. The exceptionally low basal metabolic rate of S. temminckii may contribute to these patterns, although this relationship remains to be tested. These findings provide new insights into the skeletal biology of this poorly studied mammal.

articles.title: Pygmy blue whale feeding drives greater nocturnal than diurnal song production
articles.abstract: Effective management of threatened and migratory species requires monitoring of critical behaviours, such as foraging. Passive acoustic monitoring can provide cost-effective, long-term observations on the relative abundance of vocal animals across large spatial scales. However, linking specific sounds to behavioural contexts can be challenging, especially for cryptic and aquatic species. This study combined passive acoustic and biologging data to explore whether observed periods of greater nocturnal than diurnal song production were linked to feeding by eastern Indian Ocean pygmy blue whales, Balaenoptera musculus brevicauda. The proportion of time available for singing was modelled as a function of geographical region, diel period and the presence or absence of feeding dives with generalized linear mixed models, based on 130.1 days of diving data. Top-ranked models indicated less time was available for singing during diurnal feeding periods compared to nocturnal feeding periods and non-feeding periods during the day and night. These findings suggest that diurnal feeding by pygmy blue whales reduces the time available for song production. Therefore, greater nocturnal than diurnal song production may provide an acoustic indicator of population-level feeding activity for pygmy blue whales between the Perth Canyon and offshore of the northwest shelf of Western Australia.

articles.title: Qualitative study reveals perceived barriers and facilitators of preregistration in animal research
articles.abstract: Preregistration—the prospective registration of hypotheses, methods and analyses plans—is a promising tool in promoting transparency, rigour and reproducibility in science. However, its adoption remains low, particularly in animal research, and little is known about factors influencing its uptake. We explored researchers' experiences and views on preregistration, identifying perceived facilitators and barriers, and gathering suggestions to improve its use. Within a larger cross-sectional mixed-methods project, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 Swiss-based researchers involved in animal research and thematically analysed independently by two researchers. Preregistration was described as uncommon in animal research, with views varying by prior experience. Researchers with preregistration experience reported more positive views, whereas those without were more critical. Main barriers included administrative burden, time constraints, limited flexibility and perceived incompatibility with exploratory research. Reported benefits comprised improved study planning, adherence to good research practices and increased transparency. Suggestions to improve uptake involved training, institutional support, integration with the existing authorization procedure and maintaining voluntary participation. Preregistration in animal research remains uncommon and is shaped by prior experience. Addressing barriers through training, institutional support and structural integration may broaden its adoption.

articles.title: Remotely seeing is believing: how trust in cyber-physical systems evolves through virtual observation
articles.abstract: We study how passive virtual observation of cyber-physical systems (CPS) can affect human trust in those systems. We perform this study via a newly developed novel web application that enables researchers to show pre-recorded or live video feeds to groups of users in a synchronized fashion. Users are able to provide real-time feedback on these videos via affect buttons and a free-form chat interface. We evaluate our application via a quantitative user study (N≈80) involving videos of CPS, such as autonomous vehicles (AVs), performing positively or negatively. Using data collected from user responses in the application, as well as customized survey instruments assessing different facets of trust, we find that human trust in CPS can be affected by remotely observing the behaviour of such systems—without ever encountering them in person.

articles.title: Reproductive plasticity in the lizard Ameiva ameiva across distinct climatic domains in Brazil
articles.abstract: The Neotropical lizard Ameiva ameiva is widespread in Brazil, occurring in contrasting climatic regimes that can shape its reproductive tactics. Here, we compared reproductive traits of three populations from equatorial, tropical wet–dry and tropical equatorial domains using museum specimens to evaluate geographic variation in reproductive tactics. We examined male and female reproductive tracts macro- and microscopically to characterize individual and population-level reproductive cycles. Males produced sperm year-round, and most individuals remained in recrudescence or spermiogenesis. Females showed follicular growth and oviductal changes that tracked vitellogenic stages and seasons, revealing population-specific adjustments. Mating coincided with vitellogenesis and ovulation in all populations, and the presence of mating plugs and stored sperm may indicate that females can produce multiple clutches per reproductive season. Together, these patterns show that A. ameiva exhibits a continuous reproductive cycle at the individual level but a seasonal, semi-synchronous cycle at the population level. Temporal differences among populations, particularly in the timing of vitellogenesis and mating, thus demonstrate reproductive plasticity that may contribute to the species's ability to persist across diverse and changing environments.

articles.title: Responses of Glossina pallidipes tsetse fly to geosmin, 2-pentanol and carbon dioxide odour cues
articles.abstract: Tsetse flies exhibit varying host preferences when seeking blood meals. Volatile organic compounds from preferred hosts such as buffalo and cattle have been used to develop the 3-n-propylphenol, 1-octen-3-ol, p-cresol and acetone (POCA) attractant blend, but its attraction is only about 25% of that of natural hosts, necessitating improved attractants. This study evaluated laboratory and field behavioural responses of Glossina pallidipes to geosmin, hexanal, 2-pentanol and carbon dioxide (CO2), compounds known to elicit strong responses in other insects. Laboratory two-choice olfactometer assays showed dose-dependent attraction to all tested compounds, with significantly more flies choosing treatment arms than control arms (p < 0.05). Field responses to geosmin and CO2 were validated using a randomized Latin square design, in which traps baited with either odour captured significantly more tsetse flies than unbaited control traps (p < 0.05). These findings identify geosmin, 2-pentanol and CO2 as promising odour cues for enhancing POCA attractant blends for G. pallidipes. Incorporating these compounds into existing odour-bait systems could improve the effectiveness of environmentally friendly and cost-effective tsetse control strategies.

articles.title: Sailing to Gondwana: multiple waves of spinosaurid dispersal to the southern continents
articles.abstract: Spinosaurid theropods exhibited a relatively widespread distribution during the Cretaceous Period; however, biogeographical analyses have been limited, largely owing to their fragmentary nature and uncertainties in spinosaurid phylogeny. We conducted a biogeographical analysis of Megalosauroidea, with a focus on Spinosauridae, using the R package ‘BioGeoBEARS’ on multiple phylogenetic trees to test their probable dispersal patterns. The best-fit models suggest that spinosaurid evolutionary history was influenced by geodispersal followed by narrow and widespread vicariance, as well as regional sympatry between co-occurring taxa. Within Spinosauridae, we find at least two distinct dispersals from Europe into Africa and South America, as well as at least one dispersal from Europe into Asia. Based on existing climate model data, spinosaurids generally appear to occur in high mean annual temperature semi-aquatic environments (approx. 26.1–33.1°C) with relatively minimal seasonal variation (approx. ±8.46°C), which may have influenced their dispersal capability, as these preferences appearmore constrained compared with those of other medium-to-large theropods. These results imply a more limited biogeographical distribution for Spinosauridae compared with other clades, which may be owing to climatic dispersal barriers and environmental factors.

articles.title: Smart insect trap: insect identification and classification using iNaturalist and ChatGPT
articles.abstract: Insect identification is crucial for sustainable agriculture and pest control, as it helps determine the pest type, reduces human labour, and decreases reliance on pesticides. However, there are a number of challenges associated with AI-based insect identification and classification, such as the lack of reliable data sources, imbalanced datasets and difficulty of annotation. Our paper offers a practical solution to these challenges using online platforms. Specifically, we coordinate multiple AI tools in an agentic-AI-style workflow: iNaturalist's computer vision model identifies the insect, ChatGPT determines whether it is a pest and the result drives a low-cost robotic trap. This approach is particularly accessible for non-experts, as it does not require extensive knowledge of machine learning or computer vision, and each component can be upgraded as better AI tools emerge. The system was further validated through field testing using images collected under real agricultural conditions. The results show our method is able to identify and differentiate insect species with sufficient accuracy. Our approach would be more accessible, reliable and efficient than traditional methods and can be used to identify a wider range of insect species.

articles.title: Swainson's thrushes vary singing behaviour across ambient noise gradients and rapidly adjust songs in response to experimental traffic noise
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic noise pollution has a variety of negative consequences for animals, with observed effects ranging from physiological processes to community structures. Sound waves from anthropogenic noise can mask animal signals, creating challenges for animal communication. Songbirds have been observed to combat noise pollution by changing their song rate, duration, frequency or amplitude, with different species employing different strategies. We examined whether Swainson's thrushes (Catharus usulatus) adjust their songs under different traffic noise regimens using both population-level surveys and individual-level noise playback experiments. Swainson's thrushes' introductory note frequency varied with background traffic noise levels across the surveyed population, but other song parameters did not. When confronted with realistic levels of experimental traffic noise playback, individual thrushes rapidly changed the acoustic features of their songs, increasing the duration of their songs and adjusting the frequency parameters of the introductory notes before quickly returning towards baseline levels after the noise playback ended. Together, these results suggest that Swainson's thrushes adjust their singing to reduce acoustic masking in noisy areas and further indicate that some songbirds might continually assess ambient noise levels and only adjust their signals when necessary.

articles.title: The effects of estuary salinization on benthic assemblages: a richer and treacherous future
articles.abstract: Estuarine salinization is emerging as a major consequence of climate change, yet its long-term ecological effects on tropical benthic assemblages remain poorly understood. Using nearly two decades of monitoring across three tropical estuaries, we evaluated temporal changes in benthic macroinfauna structure along their salinity gradients. We tested whether salinization would increase richness, change assemblage composition and cause shifts in benthic invertebrate distribution along the estuarine gradient. In two estuaries (Jaguaripe and Subaé) richness increased over time. Multivariate analyses showed that salinity remained the primary driver of benthic structure. Although some homogenization has occurred in middle and upper estuary zones in recent years, we found no consistent evidence that lower and middle estuarine taxa expanded landward. One estuary (Subaé) exhibited weaker temporal trends, possibly owing to historical contamination masking salinity effects. Our findings highlight that estuarine benthic assemblages are indicators of salinization, and increasing richness does not necessarily imply ecological improvement. Shifts in salinity regimes may compress estuarine zones, threaten oligohaline assemblages and alter ecosystem functions. Long-term monitoring, especially in tropical estuaries where climate extremes and human pressures are intensifying, is essential to detect tipping points and guide adaptive management and conservation strategies.

articles.title: The evolution of group size and kin structure in complex societies
articles.abstract: Molecular and pedigree data reveal substantial variation in genetic relatedness within social groups across animals. Yet kin selection theory typically treats relatedness as a fixed parameter rather than an emergent property of group dynamics. We develop a demographically explicit model in which group size fluctuates through births, dispersal, mortality and floater immigration. Residents and potential joiners resolve conflict over membership, with joining probabilities set by inclusive-fitness effects at demographic equilibrium. Membership control jointly shapes group size distributions, stability and relatedness. Under insider control, unrelated outsiders are admitted primarily to small, low-productivity groups, so mean relatedness rises with group size and stays high in larger groups. Groups are most stable near the per capita productivity optimum, with equilibrium sizes slightly above it. Low fecundity relative to resident mortality increases floater reliance, promoting mixed-kin groups and reducing relatedness. Under outsider control, groups grow larger by admitting unrelated floaters, and relatedness remains low. By treating kin structure as an emergent outcome of demographic processes and membership decisions rather than a fixed parameter, our framework links relatedness to the processes that form and regulate social groups, offering new insight into the evolution of sociality.

articles.title: Types of statistical arguments in empirical research in psychology
articles.abstract: Numerous solutions have been proposed to address the problem of statistical misuse and misunderstanding in research in psychology. This might have diverted attention from how or whether scientists are actually engaging in statistical reasoning by arguing about and with statistics within the context of the reasoning involved in empirical research in their written papers. In this paper, we studied statistical reasonings in psychological research papers. Specifically, we inductively coded arguments of 42 papers from seven highly cited psychology journals. With these data, we formed a partial, empirical typology with which we described different types of statistical arguments used in the literature. Papers, and their statistical arguments, in empirical psychology can be interpreted as possessing a ‘legal’ nature. Common arguments, such as statistical significance, are often used as a tacit and concise way of certifying that a claim, including conclusions, is empirically and statistically substantiated under the social standards of good research in our field. However, approval of research based on certifications may hinder the exposition and clarity of statistical arguments.

articles.title: Under pressure: personality, behavioural and physiological responses to handling in captive Addax nasomaculatus antelopes
articles.abstract: Animal personality refers to consistent behavioural differences among individuals across time and contexts. Knowledge of personality in ruminants, particularly non-domesticated species, remains limited. The study aimed to assess personality in a herd of Addax nasomaculatus antelopes (n = 25) living in a zoo, via a questionnaire, and to examine its relationship with handling responses under captive conditions. Personality was assessed using a 20-item questionnaire rated by observers across three contexts (Feeding, Neutral and Handling). Handling responses were measured via surface temperature, feeding and locomotor behaviour (pre- and post-handling), exit velocity and faecal cortisol metabolites. Data were analysed using exploratory factor analysis and linear mixed models. Four personality dimensions were identified: ‘Active/Unpredictable’, ‘Aggressive/Excitable’, ‘Bully’ and ‘Confident’. These traits were associated with distinct handling responses, indicating consistent interindividual variation in stress responses. Specifically, individuals scoring higher in ‘Aggressive/Excitable’ showed higher exit velocity and lower surface temperature, whereas those scoring higher in ‘Active/Unpredictable’ and ‘Bully’ showed lower exit velocity, higher surface temperature and increased grazing after handling. No association was found between personality and faecal cortisol metabolites. These findings expand the limited knowledge on non-domestic ruminants and have implications for improving captive management and conservation programmes.

articles.title: Variation and adaptation in the mechanical properties of primate molar tooth enamel
articles.abstract: Tooth enamel is a durable tissue with mechanical properties (stiffness and hardness) that vary throughout the teeth of primates with implications for dietary adaptation. Typically, estimations of tooth strength rely on averaged values of mechanical properties, which relegates variation within the crown that may be important for testing functional hypotheses. Here, we measured the mechanical properties of enamel in a taxonomically broad sample of primates and used generalized additive models to describe variation as gradients from the enamel-dentine juncture (EDJ) to the tooth surface. We found a sharp reduction in enamel stiffness at the EDJ and overall lower stiffness in the crown cervical margin across the sample. These regions are predicted to be vulnerable to fracture propagation during mastication, which reduced stiffness would help to mitigate. High hardness was identified at the cusp tips, consistent with increased wear resistance at the tooth surface. Large-bodied and hard-object feeding primates exemplified these patterns in our dataset. Our results suggest that mechanical properties in enamel vary to accommodate the maintenance of high strength throughout the cusp while simultaneously protecting vulnerable regions within from failure. This variation likely constitutes a key dietary adaptation with important implications for understanding dental function in medical and evolutionary contexts.

articles.title: Violent shaking versus a bicycle trailer ride: experimental comparison of kinematics in infant injury scenarios
articles.abstract: Fatal traumatic head injury in infants is regularly inflicted by a perpetrator, with head injury from shaking trauma (IHI-ST) being a major type. In IHI-ST, perpetrators violently shake an infant back-and-forth, whipping its head back-and-forth. Courts often debate whether shaking caused injuries or whether an alternative accidental scenario raised by the defendant did, like a bumpy bicycle-trailer ride. Head and torso kinematics of an infant dummy (six-week-old) during bicycle-trailer rides across bumps with different heights and slopes were recorded at different speeds. The validity of this alternative scenario was investigated by comparing it with violent shaking kinematics. Trailer ride conditions substantially affected the magnitude of dummy accelerations, velocities and neck flexion. Even for the highest speeds and steepest/highest bumps, head motion was less rotational than during violent shaking. While sagittal peak head linear accelerations were of similar magnitude, head angular accelerations in the trailer were less than half those during violent shaking. The head's median instantaneous radius of rotation was around 12 times shorter during shaking, indicative of greater rotational motion. Because of differences in kinematics, differences in the exposure duration, and the lack of injury thresholds between both scenarios, determining the resulting differences in injury risks requires further research.

articles.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
articles.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

articles.title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
articles.abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm 2 ) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

articles.title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
articles.abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

articles.title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
articles.abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

articles.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)—a major product of NTP oxidation—not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

articles.title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4 for reductive photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn 2 S 4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, H 2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

articles.title: Bioinspired soft enteroscopic robot for intestinal locomotion, steering, and intervention
articles.abstract: Diagnosing and treating small intestinal disorders such as bleeding, inflammatory bowel disease, and tumors present challenges because of limited access to this anatomical compartment. We present BIOSENTER, a bioinspired soft enteroscopic robot for deep procedures in the small intestine that addresses locomotion, steering, and intervention constraints of existing soft robotic systems. BIOSENTER features a hollow cylinder architecture comprising a linearly deformable soft pneumatic actuator as the body, two radially expandable soft pneumatic actuators wrapped with kirigami sleeves as the head and tail, a central hollow channel for accessory endoscopic tools, and a control box for navigation. Inspired by snake locomotion, the robotic body incorporates a fiber-reinforced actuator with four embedded inflatable chambers, enabling steering and axial expansion. The dynamic kirigami sleeves generate an anchoring force of ∼1.5 newtons on intestinal mucosa while requiring substantially less radial expansion than the corresponding nonkirigami configuration. A reinforced central channel supports tool passage for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. The control box enables locomotion and steering at autonomous speeds of ∼100 millimeters per minute in vitro and ∼43 millimeters per minute in tissue-covered tubing. BIOSENTER successfully navigated the collapsed, tortuous small intestine for 2 meters in 11 minutes, with gentle forward pushing forces of 2.2 to 6.4 newtons in pig studies. In vivo pig studies demonstrated technical feasibility of tissue biopsy, localized fluid delivery as a model for future drug administration, and real-time visualization of the deep intestine, without macroscopic overdistention or visible tissue damage under the tested conditions.

articles.title: Robot autonomous agency by any other name
articles.abstract: The humorous new science fiction novel Valet: A Novel philosophizes about robots gaining free will, but in real life, they may already have it.

articles.title: The Mars 2020 OnBoard Planner: Increasing autonomy mission productivity of the Perseverance rover
articles.abstract: Operators of planetary rovers, under strict energy and thermal constraints, face substantial challenges in maintaining high levels of rover productivity because of conservative ground-based planning and long communication latencies. In October 2023, to overcome these limits and increase science return, the Mars 2020 mission deployed OnBoard Planner into Perseverance rover operations. OnBoard Planner uses artificial intelligence constraint–based search to dynamically construct and modify activity schedules on board, adapting to real-time changes in rover state and martian environmental conditions. By replacing conservative ground predictions with real-time resource tracking, the system dynamically adjusts heating durations, reclaims unused schedule margin, and inserts opportunistic activities when extra resources become available. Here, we report on OnBoard Planner’s performance on Mars across more than 2 years of surface operations. The results demonstrate that OnBoard Planner increased discretionary rover activity by 10.5% overall while also improving the thermal and temporal conditions for certain types of scientific observations. Furthermore, the system achieved these productivity gains without increasing ground operations timelines. These findings are part of why OnBoard Planner has successfully become a standard part of Mars 2020 operations and demonstrate how dynamic onboard autonomy can enable resource-efficient operations for complex robotic systems in deep-space environments.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

articles.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition
articles.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A–positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

articles.title: Brain-sensing synNotch–CAR T cells enable precise targeting and clearance of diffuse midline glioma in multiple preclinical models
articles.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 (“B-SYNC”), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 (“B-SYNC–B/I”) similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC–B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory–like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

articles.title: Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses
articles.abstract: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8 + T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ + T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

articles.title: Keratinocyte-derived CHI3L2 reprograms phospholipid metabolism to promote skin inflammation in psoriasis
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: MIF-CD74 orchestrates synovial macrophage metabolic-inflammatory reprogramming by ENO2 interaction to drive osteoarthritis pathogenesis
articles.abstract: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Through integrative analysis of time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing in murine synovium and spatial transcriptomics of human OA tissues, we identified a pathogenic CD74 + macrophage subset that expands in OA and localizes at the synovial-cartilage interface. This subset exhibits a proinflammatory, nonclassical polarization and displays a metabolic dependency on glycolysis. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). This interaction orchestrates a feed-forward signaling axis wherein CD74/ENO2 facilitates the nuclear translocation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin dimers, which coactivate glycolytic and inflammatory gene programs, thereby sustaining a metabolically driven inflammatory state. Genetic ablation of CD74 in myeloid cells or its pharmacological blockade mitigated synovitis and cartilage degradation in murine OA models. To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74 + macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

articles.title: T cell–mediated depletion of intratumoral regulatory T cells using a CCR8xCD3 T cell–engaging bispecific antibody (TCB) promotes antitumor immunity in preclinical mouse models
articles.abstract: T cell–engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. T reg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating T reg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)–mediated T reg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing T reg cells in a T cell–mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral T reg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti–PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of T reg cells.

articles.title: Cryo-EM structure of the Arabidopsis thaliana V-type ATPase
articles.abstract: Khamina, Wunsch et al. use a bacterial effector protein to isolate and determine the structure of V-ATPase from an important model plant. The structure reveals posttranslational modifications that are specific to the plant enzyme, and interactions with an activity-modulating protein similar to interactions described previously for mammalian and fungal V-ATPases.

articles.title: AI bots swamped UK government consultation on vape restrictions, analysis suggests
articles.abstract: An overwhelming proportion of responses to the UK government’s consultation on creating a smoke-free generation and restricting disposable vape sales were generated by AI bots, an analysis suggests.1The AI generated responses were mainly targeted at opposing restrictions on disposable vape sales.Researchers from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the University of Bath said that the number of AI responses—and the consistency of their opposition to government restrictions—“suggest a coordinated campaign” to swamp the consultation.The government consultation, which took place in 2023, sought public feedback on a range of proposals, including making it illegal to sell tobacco products to anyone born from 1 January 2009 and placing restrictions on vape packaging, presentation, and flavours.2The new analysis, published in the journal Tobacco Control,1 examined publicly available data and freedom of information requests.Its researchers noted several limitations to their findings, including their inability to independently verify the bot detection methods...

articles.title: AI recommends vastly more expensive treatment than physicians, analysis suggests
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems suggest medical tests and treatment plans that are more than three times as expensive as those recommended by doctors, a study has found.1A small head-to-head evaluation by Israeli and US researchers analysed how 24 AI systems responded to 200 real outpatient and emergency department clinical notes.These notes were sourced from MTSamples, a public collection of deidentified US format clinical notes contributed by practising clinicians.Each AI system received the notes as they were recorded by the treating physician. The AI then produced its own assessment and plan, which was compared with the physician’s plan documented in the original notes.Orders from both plans were priced at 2026 Medicare rates. New medicines were counted rather than priced.Publishing their findings in the New England Journal of Medicine,1 the researchers found that the primary reason AI treatment plans were more expensive was because the algorithms suggested more diagnostic tests, medications, and...

articles.title: Jackdaw: The false promises of another gas field
articles.abstract: Global temperatures will increase 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.1 What once seemed unthinkable is now undeniable. But how much global temperatures increase beyond 1.5°C is still up to us. With current policies, global warming is heading towards a 2.8°C increase within this century.1 The 2026 Planetary Health Check finds that seven of the nine planetary boundaries, our life support systems, have been breached.2This is the backdrop against which the UK government approved the Jackdaw gas field. While alarm bells are going off around the world, it gave the green light to more drilling for more fossil fuels—to more emissions, more harm, and more injustice.The government is selling this decision as an act of pragmatism: protecting jobs, supporting people through the cost of living crisis, and ensuring that homes are kept warm through the winter using locally sourced fossil fuels. But Jackdaw will have no meaningful effect on any of this. An...

articles.title: Management of chronic pain secondary to temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials
articles.abstract: In this article by Liang Yao and colleagues (BMJ 2023;383:e076226, doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-076226, published 15 December 2023), errors in fig 3 and the data supplement have been corrected.In fig 3, an editorial error had led to minus signs being omitted from the upper 95% CI values for the mean differences in pain relief. In the data supplement, there had been errors in the 95% confidence intervals for the indirect evidence estimates for pain relief.These were reporting errors rather than errors in the underlying NMA models or estimates, and so these corrections do not change the NMA effect estimates, the GRADE certainty ratings, or the Guideline Panel’s recommendations arising from the review.

articles.title: Should doctors be on social media?
articles.abstract: Consultant geriatrician Elena Mucci had no idea what Instagram was before creating an account, on the advice of her trainees, at age 45.
