A comparative legal analysis of migratory bird conservation along the African–Eurasian flyway
articles.abstract: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African–Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. Using purposive sampling and comparative legal analysis, we examined how international conservation conventions and EU directives have been translated into national legislation and implemented in practice. Our findings revealed a fragmented conservation governance system in which enforcement consistently lags behind legal commitments, contributing to continued biodiversity loss, including the 78% decline in the European turtle dove (Streptopelia turtur) since 1980. Across diverse legal and institutional settings, cultural traditions, economic incentives associated with hunting tourism, and lobbying pressures have repeatedly weakened compliance and enforcement. Although legal penalties range from modest administrative fines to criminal sanctions, inconsistent enforcement limits their deterrent effect. By identifying common patterns across multiple jurisdictions, we identified the institutional factors that sustain implementation gaps and argue that narrowing these gaps will require stronger political commitment, greater enforcement capacity, and explicit recognition of wildlife crime as a serious conservation and environmental offense. Análisis jurídico comparativo de la conservación de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta afro‐euroasiática Resumen A pesar de décadas de acuerdos internacionales destinados a la conservación de la biodiversidad, cada año se siguen matando ilegalmente millones de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta migratoria afro‐euroasiática, especialmente en el Mediterráneo, lo que supone un desafío persistente para los esfuerzos de conservación a nivel mundial. Comparamos los marcos jurídicos de diez países para determinar cómo han surgido los vacíos de aplicación entre la legislación en materia de conservación y su cumplimiento. Usamos un muestreo intencional y un análisis jurídico comparativo para examinar cómo se han transpuesto a la legislación nacional y se han aplicado en la práctica los convenios internacionales de conservación y las directivas de la UE. Nuestros resultados revelaron un sistema de gobernanza de la conservación fragmentado, en el que la aplicación de la ley va sistemáticamente a la zaga de los compromisos legales, lo que contribuye a la pérdida continua de biodiversidad, incluida la disminución del 78% de la tórtola europea (Streptopelia turtur) desde 1980. En diversos contextos jurídicos e institucionales, las tradiciones culturales, los incentivos económicos asociados al turismo cinegético y las presiones de los grupos de interés han debilitado repetidamente el cumplimiento y la aplicación de la ley. Aunque las sanciones legales van desde modestas multas administrativas hasta sanciones penales, la aplicación inconsistente limita su efecto disuasorio. Cuando identificamos patrones comunes en múltiples jurisdicciones, logramos determinar los factores institucionales que perpetúan las deficiencias en la aplicación de la normativa y sostenemos que, para reducir dichas deficiencias, es necesario un compromiso político más firme, una mayor capacidad de aplicación de la ley y el reconocimiento explícito de los delitos contra la fauna silvestre como infracciones graves en materia de conservación y medio ambiente.

articles.title: A framework to assess trajectories of societal and biological extinction
articles.abstract: Threatened species that are societally extinct, which refers to the loss of a species’ presence in human societies, are less likely to receive conservation attention, potentially resulting in their biological extinction going unnoticed. However, little is known about the process and forms of such extinction. Thus, we aimed to quantitatively demonstrate the concept of societal extinction. We hypothesized that societal extinction leads to reduced conservation efforts for the affected species, which may, in turn, be associated with their biological extinction. We developed a framework for the trajectories between societal and biological extinction that involves four corner states and nine pathways of societal presence that can be characterized using quantitative metrics. A case study was conducted using Google Trends data for species listed on the 2020 Japanese Red List, together with information on private‐sector contributions to conservation. Notably, more than half of the species remained societally threatened, meaning they were close to societal extinction. In contrast, conservation efforts, such as tax donation schemes and nonmonetary corporate contributions, were primarily directed toward societally extant (particularly prevalent) species that were consistently searched over time. A small number of biologically extant species were nevertheless societally threatened, suggesting a potential divergence between the biological and societal status of species. Thus, species that are not only biologically but also societally threatened should be prioritized as targets for public conservation efforts, as they are less likely to receive sufficient support from the private sector. To inform future research efforts, we also summarized data on the societal presence of a selection of species from multiple perspectives beyond Google Trends. Un marco de trabajo para evaluar las trayectorias de la extinción biológica y social Resumen Las especies amenazadas que se encuentran en situación de extinción social, término que hace referencia a la pérdida de la presencia de una especie en las sociedades humanas, tienen menos probabilidades de ser objeto de medidas de conservación, lo que podría dar lugar a que su extinción biológica pase desapercibida. Sin embargo, se sabe muy poco sobre el proceso y las formas que adopta dicha extinción. Por ello, nuestro objetivo fue demostrar cuantitativamente el concepto de extinción social. Planteamos la hipótesis de que la extinción social conduce a una reducción de los esfuerzos de conservación para las especies afectadas, lo que, a su vez, podría estar asociado a su extinción biológica. Desarrollamos un marco para las trayectorias entre la extinción social y la biológica que incluye cuatro estados extremos y nueve vías de presencia social que pueden caracterizarse mediante métricas cuantitativas. Se llevó a cabo un estudio de caso utilizando datos de Google Trends sobre las especies incluidas en la Lista Roja de Japón de 2020, junto con información sobre las contribuciones del sector privado a la conservación. Cabe destacar que más de la mitad de las especies seguían amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que significa que se encontraban cerca de la extinción social. Por el contrario, los esfuerzos de conservación, como los programas de donaciones fiscales y las contribuciones corporativas no monetarias, se dirigieron principalmente hacia especies socialmente existentes (especialmente prevalentes) que fueron buscadas de forma constante a lo largo del tiempo. No obstante, un pequeño número de especies biológicamente existentes se encontraban amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que sugiere una posible divergencia entre el estado biológico y el social de las especies.…

articles.title: Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone application
articles.abstract: Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade remains a major conservation challenge and is increasingly shifting to online marketplaces where monitoring is difficult. To address this gap, we used real‐world images from online platforms, enforcement seizures, and market inspections to develop a deep‐learning object detection framework to identify products derived from three highly traded species: elephant, pangolin, and tiger. Our dataset of 39,941 images included both wildlife products and visually similar nonwildlife items, reflecting real enforcement complexity. We used cross‐entropy and asymmetric focal loss functions to train Faster Region‐based convolutional neural network (Faster R‐CNN) models and compared species‐specific and multispecies training strategies. The best‐performing model, trained with cross‐entropy on all species combined, achieved an overall accuracy of 84.2%, with high performance for pangolin (93.6%) and tiger (90.3%) and moderate performance for elephant (71.1%). Although asymmetric focal loss increased recall, it substantially reduced precision. We deployed the optimized model in a prototype smartphone application, potentially usable in real‐world settings for monitoring online images. With an independent test set, the application achieved 91.3% accuracy and an F‐score of 0.86. These results demonstrate the potential of object detection models to support scalable, real‐time monitoring of wildlife trade and enable the rapid triage of suspicious posts, regulatory compliance, and conservation decision‐making. Detección del comercio en productos derivados de especies amenazadas mediante aprendizaje automatizado y aplicaciones en teléfonos inteligentes Resumen El comercio ilegal e insostenible de fauna silvestre sigue siendo un importante reto para la conservación y se está desplazando cada vez más hacia los mercados en línea, donde resulta difícil llevar a cabo una vigilancia eficaz. Para enfrentar esta carencia, utilizamos imágenes reales procedentes de plataformas en línea, incautaciones realizadas por las fuerzas del orden e inspecciones de mercado para desarrollar un marco de detección de objetos basado en el aprendizaje profundo, con el fin de identificar productos derivados de tres especies muy comercializadas: el elefante, el pangolín y el tigre. Nuestro conjunto de datos, compuesto por 39, 941 imágenes, incluía tanto productos de fauna silvestre como artículos no silvestres visualmente similares, lo que refleja la complejidad real de la labor de las fuerzas del orden. Utilizamos funciones de entropía cruzada y de pérdida focal asimétrica para entrenar modelos de red neuronal convolucional basada en regiones más rápidas (faster R‐CNN) y comparamos estrategias de entrenamiento específicas para cada especie y multiespecíficas. El modelo con mejor rendimiento, entrenado con entropía cruzada sobre todas las especies combinadas, alcanzó una precisión global del 84.2%, con un alto rendimiento para el pangolín (93.6%) y el tigre (90.3%), y un rendimiento moderado para el elefante (71.1%). Si bien la pérdida focal asimétrica aumentó la recuperación, redujo sustancialmente la precisión. Implementamos el modelo optimizado en una aplicación prototipo para teléfonos inteligentes, que podría utilizarse en entornos reales para la supervisión de imágenes en línea. Con un conjunto de datos de prueba independiente, la aplicación alcanzó una precisión del 91.3% y un índice F de 0.86. Estos resultados demuestran el potencial de los modelos de detección de objetos para facilitar una vigilancia escalable y en tiempo real del comercio de fauna silvestre, así como para permitir la rápida clasificación de publicaciones sospechosas, el cumplimiento normativo y la toma de decisiones en materia de conservación.

articles.title: Diplochorous Seed Dispersal of Rafflesiaceae by Fruit‐Consuming Squirrels, Rats and Treeshrews, Then Seed‐Burying Dung Beetles
articles.abstract: Understanding seed‐dispersal of Rafflesiaceae species is essential to conserve this extraordinary family of parasitic plants. We present evidence supporting diplochorous seed dispersal, involving primary endozoochorous dispersal by small mammals, followed by secondary exozoochorous dispersal by dung beetles. Methods employed included in situ live capture of small mammals in traps, placed over developing Sapria himalayana fruits, in situ observations of dung beetles handling the small dung pellets of primary dispersers and ex situ experiments with both dispersers. Dung pellet analyses (number, weight, expulsion time and ratio of undamaged to broken seeds) indicated that the most capable primary seed dispersers were the nocturnal rat Maxomys surifer (among four species studied) and, during daytime, the squirrel Dremomys rufigenis and, to a lesser extent, the treeshrew Tupaia belangeri. Dispersal distances were likely to encompass multiple host Tetrastigma spp. (lianas). Dung beetles served as secondary dispersers. They removed all faecal pellets of primary dispersers from the soil surface within 24 h, burying them up to 7 cm deep. The beetles also released seeds from the faecal matrix by microphagy, enabling the seeds to come into intimate contact with hosts' fine roots and root hairs, through which infection likely occurs. Forty‐one beetle species (including seven new species) were involved, with Ochicanthon thai and Onthophagus lindaae being the most abundant. Further research throughout the distribution of Rafflesiaceae species, particularly in the Philippines, regarded as a centre of Rafflesia diversity, is likely to add to primary and secondary disperser diversity.

articles.title: Disentangling the Drivers of Fish Community Variation in a Highly Urbanized Estuary Based on Hierarchical Modeling of Species Communities (HMSC)
articles.abstract: Biodiversity conservation and management in highly urbanized estuaries have garnered widespread global attention. However, the environmental response mechanisms of fish communities in these estuaries remain poorly understood, hindering their ecological health and sustainable development. Here, we utilized Hierarchical Modeling of Species Communities (HMSC), a burgeoning and powerful framework, jointly investigating how the species occurrences, species traits, and spatiotemporal structure of fish communities respond to environmental variables in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). It exhibited seasonal variation in species composition, taxonomic diversity, functional diversity, and functional‐space occupancy of fish communities, and several CWM traits showed directional seasonal shifts. Furthermore, the HMSC framework showed that environmental filtering was the primary driver of the spatiotemporal dynamics in fish community. Salinity, pH, and phosphate were identified as key environmental drivers of species distributions and trait‐mediated responses. Functional traits showed contrasting responses along the phosphate gradient, whereas habitat‐level residual species associations revealed distinct positive and negative co‐occurrence patterns that reflect shared environmental filtering rather than stochastic assembly. The study elucidates the environmental response mechanisms of fish community dynamics by integrating taxonomic and functional diversity perspectives, offering new insights into the assembly of estuarine fish communities.

articles.title: Synergistic multi-site passivation with a CF 3 -featuring small-molecule additive for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells
articles.abstract: Defect passivation and crystallization regulation are critical for achieving efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, developing a single additive capable of simultaneously optimizing energy-level alignment, suppressing ion migration,...

articles.title: A physics-guided virtual probe for anode potential estimation via target-label-free sim-to-real adaptation
Electronic coupling at bimetallic Ni-Co sites enables reversible Li2O2 formation and decomposition in lithium-oxygen batteries
Analysis of the spatiotemporal pattern and driving mechanism of ecological restoration in the Kubuqi Desert
articles.abstract: The health of desert plant life is closely linked to the stability of the local ecological equilibrium, where both human actions and shifts in climate serve as primary influences on environmental security. This research examined the temporal and spatial variations in vegetation NDVI and climatic elements within the Kubuqi Desert between 2000 and 2023. It utilized partial correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and the geodetector method to uncover the underlying drivers of NDVI dynamics. Additionally, the study applied an ARIMA model to forecast the NDVI trajectory for the upcoming five-year period. The findings indicated that: (1) Plant life in the Kubuqi Desert has experienced substantial enhancement, with more than 80.61% of the region demonstrating a highly notable upward trajectory in NDVI; nonetheless, the general vegetation is projected to display slight anti-persistence going forward. (2) Annual precipitation, annual average high temperature, and annual average low temperature all showed an increasing trend. (3) Land transfer mainly occurred among barren land, cultivated land, and grassland, with the conversion from barren land to grassland accounting for 15.49%. (4) Precipitation and high temperature are key factors affecting NDVI distribution, with a 2–3month lag effect on NDVI. (5) Vegetation NDVI will show an increasing trend over the next five years. This study will provide certain data support for vegetation restoration strategies in the Kubuqi Desert.

articles.title: Correction to ‘Microbial richness and composition independently drive soil multifunctionality’
A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2hi Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease
articles.abstract: Our understanding of how commensal-specific CD4+ T cells respond to intestinal inflammation is limited. Pedersen et al. define the phenotypic diversity of human CD4+ T cells recognizing a defined Bacteroidales epitope across disease settings. This revealed a TMIGD2hi Th17 phenotype that expands in inflamed tissue. More broadly, this work underscores the malleability of microbiota-specific T cells during inflammatory bowel disease.

articles.title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond
articles.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a system to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. Mancuso and colleagues discuss how HBCXs enable in vivo interrogation of human-specific brain cell biology, neuroimmunology, disease modeling, and genetic risk and their potential for functional genomics, therapeutic discovery, and preclinical assessment of cell-based therapies for central nervous system disorders.

articles.title: Regulating carrier transport and oxychloride interphase formation by increasing configurational complexity in solid-state halide electrolytes
articles.abstract: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

articles.title: Following the rules? Different thermal and temporal life‐stage responses of biometrics across four decades in a songbird population
articles.abstract: Using biometric data collected over 33 years in a Mediterranean population of Great tits we reveal a dynamic phenotypic mosaic where long‐term trends decouple from immediate thermal effects. By integrating life‐stage sensitivities, we show how ontogenetic buffering and life‐history trade‐offs contribute to shape avian responses to a changing climate. Abstract Global warming is widely associated with changes in body size and shape, with these variations typically framed within the context of Bergmann, Allen and the Temperature‐Size rules. However, evaluating phenotypic change only against these rules can limit our understanding of how immediate plastic reactions to temperature interact with long‐term trends. Also, phenotypic responses may differ among life stages, due to their different thermal sensitivity and life‐history role. We examined body size and shape variations across life stages in a Mediterranean great tit (Parus major) population monitored over four decades, during which mean annual temperatures increased by approximately 1.7°C. Adults were the life stage most responsive to temperature and their mass declined by 0.84% for every 1°C of warming, while wing length shortened. Instead, tarsus length, a measure of structural size, increased with temperature in both nestlings and adults at a comparable magnitude, consistent with Allen's rule. Nestling mass near fledging showed no thermal response. Among reproductive traits, clutch size tended to decrease with temperature without reaching statistical significance and egg mass showed no thermal response, yet total clutch mass, an integrated measure of reproductive output, declined significantly with warmer laying temperatures. Long‐term temporal trends did not consistently mirror these thermal effects. Adult mass declined across the study period, matching the direction of its thermal response, whereas adult tarsus length shortened over time despite lengthening with temperature. Wing length and nestling mass both remained stable. Egg mass declined and clutch size increased across the study period, despite their lack of thermal response. These results demonstrate that while warming can proximately affect body size, long‐term temporal trends can be decoupled from immediate thermal effects, and that mass and structural size do not necessarily vary together. This creates an underappreciated mosaic of phenotypic responses across life stages and generations, with potential consequences for fecundity, morphology and fitness. Our findings highlight the importance of integrating ontogenetic perspectives into evolutionary ecogeographic theory and raise questions about which ‘rules’ will govern the trajectories of avian populations under climate change.

articles.title: Design Cu/AAl2O4 (A = Mg, Ni, Mn) catalysts with superior H2 generation efficiency for methanol steam reforming (MSR): suppressing CO formation by tuning A-site cation in spinel support structure
Direct synthesis of polycarbonate diols from flow CO2 and 1,6-hexanediol over BaO-modified CeO2 catalyst
Drought legacies weaken resistance and plant‐mycorrhizal associations but not recovery
articles.abstract: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates. Abstract Drought legacies can shape how grasslands respond to increasingly frequent climate extremes, yet their influence on future resistance and recovery remains unclear, particularly in mesic grasslands, where productivity is strongly linked to precipitation availability. Using a long‐term field experiment, we tested how zero, one or two prior experimentally imposed extreme droughts influenced grassland resistance to a subsequent 4‐year extreme drought (2018–2021) and recovery after drought in 2022. We quantified above‐ground net primary productivity and species composition, as well as plant functional traits and arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal colonization of the dominant grasses at the site, to evaluate above‐ and below‐ground legacy effects. Differences in productivity resistance among drought‐legacy treatments were small during the first three drought years and became evident only in the final, most severe drought year, when resistance was lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts. However, above‐ground productivity recovered to similar levels across all treatments in 2022, demonstrating substantial short‐term recovery despite contrasting drought histories. The dominant grass, Andropogon gerardii, exhibited higher specific leaf area and greater leaf production during the recovery year, indicating increased investment in rapid resource capture and regrowth. Additionally, AM fungal colonization of A. gerardii declined with repeated drought exposure and remained lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts even after above‐ground productivity recovered. In contrast to these traits and below‐ground changes, species composition, including richness, evenness, turnover and absolute cover, remained stable across all treatments and years. Synthesis: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates.

articles.title: Fuego en el cerebro: cómo puede surgir la psicosis cuando el cuerpo se ataca a sí mismo
Meds are often the go-to for dementia patients. Is there a better way?
Li-associated cation redistribution and structural reversibility in honeycomb-ordered sodium ruthenates
Non-equilibrium fluctuations in the corrosion process
articles.abstract: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.

articles.title: Polymer coordination enables alloying-free synthesis of stable α-FAPbI3 thick films for real-time X-ray imaging
articles.abstract: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.

articles.title: An AI‐based and coding‐free integration for forest Leaf Area Index calculation
articles.abstract: Seasonal and spatial variations in Leaf Area Index (LAI, or plant area index, PAI) are challenging to delineate in tropical forests because the changes are often too subtle to be reliably detected. Many existing DHP software tools offer one‐click processing of all images using auto‐threshold segmentation (e.g. HemispheR, HemiPy and Hemisfer), but they produce results with large discrepancies. Some software (e.g. CAN‐EYE) requires manual tuning of each image, making large‐scale analysis impractical. We analysed 19,044 images from four tropical forest subtypes and found that using coding‐free AI software to process hemispherical images can significantly improve the consistency of canopy‐sky segmentation, thereby improving the detection of temporal and spatial variation of PAI. The results show that replacing the auto‐threshold segmentation with AI substantially reduced inter‐software disagreement, with the mean inter‐software range for PAI decreasing from 4.31 to 1.19, and delineating correct seasonal and spatial patterns. CAN‐EYE could identify the correct seasonal patterns but produced less accurate results than the CAN‐EYE‐AI integrated approach due to subjective bias. The high consistency achieved after AI integration enables reliable cross‐site and temporal comparisons. As users can combine the AI segmentation with other DHP software, our integrated, affordable and coding‐free method offers wide applicability and high consistency of PAI measurements, facilitating the advancement of tropical forest monitoring and research.

articles.title: Every scientist a modeller? The promise and peril of AI‐assisted mechanistic models
articles.abstract: Mechanistic models, expressed as simulations that can be run and visualised, are a powerful way to understand biological and other systems. Building them, however, requires formulating mathematical or rule‐based descriptions and translating them into working code, skills that many ecologists and other disciplinary researchers do not have. Generative AI can now perform much of this translation, making mechanistic modelling accessible to researchers, educators and students previously excluded by its technical demands. But delegating this translation to AI also carries real risks: modelling assumptions can become hidden, plausible but incorrect code can pass unnoticed, and the skills and critical habits that model building once developed may never form. We examine the benefits and risks of using generative AI as a modelling companion at each stage of model development (conceptual specification, formalisation, implementation and exploration), drawing on recent experimental evidence on AI‐assisted learning and on a worked predator–prey example built with AI, with a rule‐based epidemic model as a parallel case. At each stage we identify where consequential decisions are silently delegated to the AI and set out practical mitigations that keep human judgement engaged without requiring the technical skills AI has made optional: specifying the conceptual model explicitly before engaging AI, having the AI translate its formalisation back into plain language, testing the implementation against outcomes known from domain knowledge and designing the interface to support interrogation. This new opportunity is substantial: researchers, educators and students who understand their systems but have never been able to build models of them are now able to explore these systems mechanistically, testing how components interact and how the system responds to conditions it has not yet experienced, questions that correlative approaches alone cannot answer. Used carelessly, AI risks eroding modelling skill for little lasting benefit, but used deliberately, in the ways set out here, it opens a new pathway to mechanistic understanding without removing the critical thinking the old technical barrier once enforced.

articles.title: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery
articles.abstract: Semen carries extracellular RNA that shapes early embryonic development, but how it reaches sperm is unclear. Mallen et al. show that amyloid fibrils in seminal fluid bind RNA, enter sperm, and deliver their cargo to the zygote at fertilization, where chaperones release it for translation.

articles.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation
articles.abstract: Viral RNA genomes fold into networks of compact structures, so their RNA sequences do more than carry genetic code. Hann et al. review how viral RNA structures control viral gene expression, replication, and immune evasion, revealing viruses as simple model systems for regulatory principles that also shape human gene expression.

articles.title: The 9-1-1 complex protects ssDNA gaps in BRCA2-deficient cancer
articles.abstract: Grimsley et al. demonstrate that the 9-1-1 complex safeguards BRCA2-deficient cells from lethal ssDNA gap accumulation by suppressing PRIMPOL-dependent gap formation, restraining EXO1 degradation, and promoting POLζ-mediated filling. This identifies an ATR-independent 9-1-1 role in post-replicative repair and establishes gap length as a key determinant of repair pathway choice.

articles.title: A compact bio-inspired 3D conical spiral RF energy harvester for self-powered sensing
Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
articles.abstract: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

articles.title: Correction to “Nanoconfined Polymer Dot Reactors for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Diverse Metabolites and Point-of-Care Diagnosis”
Giant Resistance Switching Ratio Exceeding 106 through a Reversible 2D–3D Structural Phase Transition in Nonequilibrium (Pb1– x Sn x )Se Thin Films
articles.abstract: Control and switching of electrical resistance in semiconductors are important for high-performance electronic devices. Here, we realize giant resistance switching in nonequilibrium (Pb1–xSnx)Se films through a reversible structural transition between three-dimensional (3D) rock-salt (RS)-type and two-dimensional (2D) GeS-type phases. The solid-solution films were fabricated by reactive solid-phase epitaxy of SnSe/PbSe bilayers followed by rapid thermal quenching. Se-flux annealing of the PbSe template suppressed Pb precipitation, enabling chemically homogeneous, single-phase nonequilibrium RS-type films up to x = 0.58. Increasing the Sn content from x = 0.43 to 0.58 systematically increased the 2D–3D structural transition temperature and enhanced the resistance switching ratio to 4.9 × 106, far exceeding those of representative transition-metal oxide thin films (∼102–104). The giant resistance switching originates from the nearly complete transformation (∼98%) of the conductive 3D phase into the high-resistance 2D phase. These results establish crystal-dimensionality switching as a promising new mechanism for high-performance electronic switching devices.

articles.title: Long-Range Single-Molecule Transport and Assembly at Liquid Nitrogen Temperatures
articles.abstract: The bottom-up construction of functional matter from individually positioned atoms and molecules requires deterministic control over capture, transport, and assembly on surfaces. Although atomic manipulation is well established, extending comparable control to molecules remains challenging due to their complex internal degrees of freedom and surface interactions. Here, we demonstrate controlled single-molecule transport and assembly at liquid nitrogen temperatures using a scanning tunneling microscope. We designed a molecule with an intrinsic electric dipole moment, enabling efficient noncontact manipulation via electrostatic coupling to the tip. This strategy allows stable long-range translation and the programmable formation of defined dimers and larger assemblies. Systematic mapping of the operational parameter space, supported by first-principles calculations, identifies an electrostatic driving mechanism governing motion. Our approach shifts molecular nanomachine research from demonstrations under extreme cryogenic conditions to positional control under experimentally more accessible temperatures, establishing a practical platform for programmable molecular-scale engineering.

articles.title: Programming-Current-Induced Mechanism Crossover Enables Reconfigurable Memory Window in In2Te3 Selector-Only Memory
articles.abstract: Selector-only memory (SOM), which integrates threshold switching and data storage within a chalcogenide layer, is a promising high-density memory technology, yet the regulation of memory characteristics and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that programming current (Ip) regulates the competition between composition-driven and trap-associated switching processes in amorphous In2Te3 devices. Decreasing Ip from 10–2 to 10–4 A reversibly changes the positive-read threshold voltage (Vth) ordering from Vth, SET > Vth, RESET, yielding an inverted memory window of up to 1.53 V, to Vth, SET < Vth, RESET, with a conventional memory window of ∼0.5 V. Cross-sectional energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals state-dependent In/Te redistribution at high Ip, consistent with composition-mediated modulation of conductive pathways. At low Ip, atomic redistribution is suppressed and trap-associated transport modulation is enhanced, with extracted trap depths of 0.51 eV (SET) and 0.63 eV (RESET), establishing Ip as a means of modifying SOM memory characteristics without complex engineering.

articles.title: Spontaneous Nanoscale Wiggling in Cleaved WTe2
articles.abstract: Structural deformation of crystal lattices has emerged as a powerful pathway to engineer and boost electronic properties through lattice geometry. However, realizing ultrafine structural modulations remains challenging without external strain imposed by substrates, prestrain, or artificial patterning. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy, we show that the cleaving process spontaneously induces nanoscale wiggling in 1T′-WTe2 without such external strain sources. Furthermore, scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals pronounced electronic reconstruction and spatially resolved spectral modulations between the top and valley regions of the wiggling. Combined with first-principles calculations, our results show that this wiggling substantially modifies the local electronic structure relative to the unstrained flat region, suggesting electronic structure reconstruction driven by spontaneous lattice deformation. These findings establish spontaneous nanoscale wiggling as a self-formed structural modulation for local electronic-structure engineering in strain-sensitive low-symmetry layered materials.

articles.title: Stacking-Order-Dependent Electronic Properties of MoTe2/WSe2 Moiré Bilayers
articles.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré bilayers have realized a wide range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena. The physics in these materials is often sensitive to the interlayer stacking order. Polarization-resolved optical second harmonic generation (SHG) is the most used technique for stacking order characterization but unverified for most heterobilayers. Here we calibrate the optical SHG for angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers by the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). We directly compare the transport and magnetic properties and the electronic phase diagram for two distinct stacking orders. With the calibrated stacking order assignment, we clarify the interpretation of earlier results, including the nature of the Chern insulator, mechanism of an electric-field-tuned metal–insulator transition at half band filling, and the Kondo lattice physics. Our work provides a consistent picture of the relation between the stacking order and the electronic properties of MoTe2/WSe2 moiré bilayers.

articles.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
articles.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca II triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profiles characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85–145019.95, a new gas-disc system that exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 R ⊙ to 0.34 R ⊙ and from 0.54 R ⊙ to 1.93 R ⊙ . We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

articles.title: Retention of primordial atmospheres through giant impacts
articles.abstract: Giant impacts help rocky planets retain hydrogen-rich atmospheres because accreted mass increases atmospheric gravitational binding more than collisional heating drives atmospheric loss. This may explain the bimodal radius distribution of exoplanets.

articles.title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table
Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
articles.abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

articles.title: A CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation
articles.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit . Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro–myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

articles.title: The EMPROR’s new groove
articles.abstract: Two studies shed new light on macrophage origins. Perivascular macrophages derive from extraembryonic erythromyeloid progenitors arising at a newly discovered hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface and a related population of adult bone marrow progenitors.

articles.title: The maternal–fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors
articles.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R + erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4 + CSF1R − Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4 + nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal–fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

articles.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
articles.abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

articles.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models

articles.title: Reconstructing Cenozoic grasslands in North America and western Eurasia: evidence for cold‐season grasses from 3D phytolith morphology
articles.abstract: Pie charts illustrate the composition of fossil grass silica short‐cell phytolith (GSSCP) assemblages at investigated fossil sites in the United States and Türkiye and representative 3D meshes of classified phytoliths. Summary Pooideae, the largest grass subfamily, radiated in the Northern Hemisphere from the Paleocene onward and today dominates cold‐season and high‐altitude grasslands. Fossil phytolith assemblages suggest pooid‐rich ecosystems during the Oligocene–Miocene, but the lack of quantitative phytolith identification has limited reconstruction of early grassland composition and ecology. We combined 3D geometric morphometrics of grass silica short‐cell phytoliths (GSSCPs) with machine‐learning classification and phylogenetically informed climate modelling. A dataset of modern GSSCPs was used to classify Eocene–Miocene phytoliths from Türkiye and the US Great Plains and reconstruct paleoclimate. 3D GSSCP morphology distinguished modern grass subfamilies and tribes. Fossil assemblages contained mainly phytoliths assigned to Bambusoideae and Pooideae (including Poeae I and II). In modern grasses, Crenate and Polylobate phytolith dimensions correlated with temperature and precipitation. Fossil Crenates and Polylobates yielded climate estimates warmer and wetter than today. Ancestral state reconstructions indicated milder winter conditions at early Pooideae nodes, with cold tolerance arising early. Major temperate grass lineages (Poeae I and II) were established earlier than previously recognized, and Pooideae‐rich grasslands were present by the Oligo‐Miocene under warmer, wetter climates than today. These findings demonstrate the value of 3D phytolith morphometrics for interpreting early grassland evolution.

Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
articles.abstract: Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.

articles.title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.

articles.title: [Comment] Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?
articles.abstract: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis
articles.abstract: BackgroundNational cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system.MethodsWe identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded. We developed an analytical framework of 12 elements and 76 sub-elements, aligned with WHO, International Cancer Control Partnership, and Union for International Cancer Control guidance and validated it through a modified two-stage Delphi process (online survey of 67 experts; triangulation workshop with 31 participants). PRISM comprised document ingestion (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), policy analysis with retrieval-augmented generation (Llama 4 Scout, 109B), and semantic quality assurance. PRISM was validated against masked dual-expert ratings for six purposely selected NCCPs, then applied to all NCCPs. Scores were normalised to 0-5 and medians compared across World Bank income group and WHO region.FindingsWe identified 50 NCCPs that met the inclusion criteria. Median overall comprehensiveness was 2·78 (IQR 2·25-3·09), with high comprehensiveness classified as 4·0-5·0, moderate as 2·0-3·9, and low as 0-1·9. Europe (2·96; 2·78-3·35) and lower-middle-income countries (2·97; 2·48-3·15) had the highest medians; the western Pacific (2·21; 1·78-2·87) and low-income countries (2·05; 1·94-2·22) had the lowest. Element-level medians were highest for implementation (4·17; 3·54-4·38), health services (3·89; 2·63-4·19), and governance and organisation (3·67; 3·35-3·98), and lowest for financing (1·88; 1·00-2·69), outcomes (1·83; 1·33-2·33), and threats (2·19; 1·72-2·34). Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less.InterpretationOur analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.FundingHarvard University.

Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

articles.title: Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors
articles.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.
