This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.

articles.title: PARP1 directly disassembles nucleosomes to regulate DNA repair
articles.abstract: Verma, Zhu, et al. show that PARP1 promotes NAD+-dependent eviction of H2A-H2B dimers, generating oriented hexasomes with increased DNA accessibility. The H2A C-terminal tail supports this remodeling activity, linking PARP1-dependent nucleosome disassembly to cellular responses to DNA damage.

articles.title: Oxygen-framework stabilization and stress-relief engineering via Mo/Ca co-substitution for durable sodium layered oxide cathodes
Breaking the Activity–Stability Trade-Off in Electrochemical NO2– Reduction to NH3 over a Robust Fe3C/CN Catalyst
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrite reduction coupled with plasma nitrogen oxidation offers a promising route for ambient ammonia synthesis, yet simultaneously achieving high activity and stability remains challenging owing to high kinetic barriers and catalyst deactivation. Here, we develop a robust hybrid electrocatalyst for active and durable nitrite reduction to ammonia by leveraging Fe3C nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (Fe3C/CN). As a benefit from strong interactions between Fe3C and CN, this hybrid catalyst delivers a high faradaic efficiency of 89.6% at −0.7 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (vs RHE) and a record ammonia yield rate of 16 956.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.9 V vs RHE, along with no apparent performance decay over 1000 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential for sustainable electrochemical ammonia production. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergistic effect between Fe3C nanoparticles and a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix enhances catalytic performance by optimizing reactant adsorption, water dissociation, and promoting reaction kinetics.

articles.title: Decoupling Josephson Coupling and Supercurrent Nonreciprocity in Twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 van der Waals Junctions
articles.abstract: The microscopic origin of supercurrent nonreciprocity in van der Waals Josephson junctions remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of twist-angle engineering. Here, we investigate twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 vertical Josephson junctions with controlled crystallographic alignment and clean interfaces. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly determines the twist angle and interface quality. While Josephson coupling exhibits a pronounced twist-angle dependence, the supercurrent diode efficiency remains small and shows no systematic angular dependence. In contrast, enhanced diode responses emerge in weakly coupled junctions with reduced transparency and interfacial disorder. Deliberate interface degradation further enhances the diode efficiency to nearly 30% and produces irregular magnetic-field dependence. These results demonstrate a clear decoupling between Josephson coupling and supercurrent nonreciprocity, indicating that interfacial disorder rather than twist-angle-controlled momentum matching plays a dominant role in the observed diode response. Our findings establish an important benchmark for understanding nonreciprocal superconducting transport in van der Waals Josephson devices in the future.

articles.title: Engineering a Dynamic Alloy–Fluoride Interface via a Co-Placement Gas-Phase Strategy for Stable Lithium Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy-density energy storage systems, but suffer from uneven Li nucleation and unstable interfaces. Here, a scalable coplacement gas-phase reaction strategy is developed to construct an adaptive alloy–fluoride interface on nickel mesh current collectors, enabling one-step in-situ formation of a uniform Ni3Sb/NiF2 layer. The lithiophilic Ni3Sb alloy effectively lowers the lithium nucleation barrier and guides uniform lithium deposition. Upon cycling, NiF2 is transformed into a LiF-rich interphase, which stabilizes the electrode/electrolyte interface and homogenizes Li+ flux. The combined interface enables durable and uniform Li plating/stripping under long-term cycling. Consequently, the Ni3Sb/NiF2-modified anode achieves stable cycling for over 2600 h in symmetric cells and delivers 83.1% capacity retention after 240 cycles in LiFePO4 full cells with a high areal capacity of 10 mAh cm–2. This work provides a facile and scalable strategy for engineering multifunctional interfaces toward practical LMBs.

articles.title: An enriched methane D/H ratio in the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS
articles.abstract: JWST spectra of interstellar object 3I/ATLAS reveal an enhanced D/H ratio in methane compared with measurements of Solar System objects. The high value is comparable with that calculated for pre- and protostellar regions, indicating a primitive origin.

articles.title: An intertwined short and long γ-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
articles.abstract: GRB 160425A emitted two sub-bursts in short succession with differing properties, indicative of two distinct progenitor types: collapsar and stellar merger. This event raises questions about γ-ray burst progenitor scenarios.

articles.title: Apparent magnetic field decay in a solar flare from Zeeman splitting of the Mg I 12.32-µm line
articles.abstract: AIMS mid-infrared spectroscopy of the Mg I 12.32 µm line during an X1.5 flare reveals magnetic field weakening beneath impulsive-phase ribbons via Zeeman splitting. These changes may arise from an elevated line-formation height or local magnetic redistribution.

articles.title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
articles.abstract: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d 1 geometry stabilizes a 4 d z 2 –5 s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times ( T 1 ) up to 87 ms and dephasing times ( T m , T m CPMG ) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.

articles.title: Cytokine circuits in CNS homeostasis and disease
articles.abstract: In their Review, Becher et al. discuss how selected cytokine networks preserve, destabilize and restore central nervous system integrity.

articles.title: GutPath links immune archetypes and single-cell landscapes in the infected gut
articles.abstract: A single-cell gene expression atlas, spanning six phylogenetically diverse infections, reveals pathogen-specific reprogramming of the intestinal epithelium and a novel Yersinia-induced enterocyte state that is spatially linked to tissue pathology.

articles.title: Bispecific dual T cell agonist invikafusp alfa in solid tumors: the phase 1/2 START-001 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress 2026, in a phase 1/2 trial in participants with solid tumors, invika, a first-in-class bispecific agonistic antibody that selectively targets the prevalent Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, was well tolerated, enabling the selection of a recommended phase 2 dose for further testing, and showed a preliminary efficacy signal in both immunologically hot and cold tumors.

articles.title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
articles.abstract: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10−5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies. A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

articles.title: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026, in a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating an off-the-shelf lymph node-targeting peptide vaccine in patients with mutated KRAS pancreatic cancer within 6 months of standard curative intent therapy, the primary endpoint of disease-free survival was not met, but prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant disease-free survival benefit in the vaccine arm for patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative disease and in those without prior radiation treatment.

articles.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
articles.abstract: A patient-facing conversational AI showed promising feasibility and safety in a single-center primary care setting, providing a basis for larger-scale evaluation.

articles.title: The human microbiome and chronic disease: ten strategic priorities for research and public health
articles.abstract: The human microbiome has emerged as one of the most consequential frontiers in biomedical science. An international group of leading microbiome scientists, convened by the US Department of Health and Human Services, presents a strategic vision for realizing its potential to transform public health.

articles.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
articles.abstract: This Analysis benchmarks segmentation methods across different datasets and presents Nextflow, a pipeline for standardized method selection for spatial transcriptomics.

articles.title: NanostarDB: an interactive knowledgebase for standardized annotation, discovery and reuse of nucleic acid nanostructure designs
articles.abstract: The lack of standardized reporting and annotation of nucleic acid nanostructures limits reproducibility, interoperability and the efficient reuse of published designs. NanostarDB is a community-driven knowledgebase that standardizes nucleic acid nanostar designs through persistent identifiers, structural annotations, and integrated computational tools for design exploration, analysis and reuse, and is compliant with principles of findability, accessibility, interoprability and reusability (FAIR).

articles.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. Here we introduce an approach to immuno-isolate EVs from neurons and glia based on protein surface markers. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

articles.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
articles.abstract: This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

articles.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
articles.abstract: Conventional quantum error correction requires repeated measurements and real-time feedback, which are technically complex. An autonomous implementation that eliminates these while beating the break-even point is demonstrated in a trapped-ion system.

articles.title: Maxwell’s demon with memory
articles.abstract: Maxwell’s demon may produce work using the information it obtains by measuring the system as fuel. Now, it is shown that the amount of produced work increases if the demon takes information about the dynamical correlations of the system into account.

articles.title: Particle collisions on a quantum computer
articles.abstract: Elementary particle physics rests on the discovery of particles produced in high-energy collider experiments. Now, a model collision above the threshold for particle production has been simulated on a quantum computer.

articles.title: The physical chemistry behind porous liquids
articles.abstract: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.

articles.title: Understanding porous liquids
articles.abstract: Becky Greenaway, Associate Professor (Reader) and Royal Society University Research Fellow at Imperial College London, talks to Nature Synthesis about developing automated high-throughput experimentation to design porous liquids as well as persistent challenges in the field.

articles.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy
articles.abstract: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL. In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria. A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups. Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

articles.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy — Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial
articles.abstract: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9. In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed. In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred. In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

articles.title: Embryonal degreening and seed longevity require plastid LEA proteins
articles.abstract: Working model of how plastidial LEA proteins aid the remodelling of photosynthetic structures during degreening of Arabidopsis seed embryos. LEA42 and LEA48 support thylakoid proteostasis and membrane remodelling in embryonal cells during late seed maturation by maintaining a local physicochemical environment compatible with protein turnover and membrane re‐organisation. ATP synthase F1 subunits, ClpP4 and HSP90‐5, as pinpointed as potential LEA interactors by proteomic approaches, are highlighted as candidate molecular entry points. Summary Seeds enable plant embryos to endure extended periods and environmental extremes. Orthodox seeds acquire desiccation tolerance during maturation, before metabolic quiescence. Coordinated thylakoid disassembly and Chl degradation lead to embryo degreening, a hallmark of orthodox seed maturation. While degreening is hormonally controlled, our understanding of the molecular players involved and its physiological significance remains incomplete. By serendipity, we observed a stay‐green seed phenotype in an Arabidopsis thaliana mutant lacking two LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) proteins, LEA42 and LEA48, which we identified as the most abundant LEA proteins in seed mitochondria and plastids. Using lea48xlea42 as a model for impaired LEA function in seed mitochondria and plastids, proteomic, transcriptomic and transmission electron microscopy analyses indicate incomplete thylakoid degradation. Freshly harvested lea48xlea42 seeds were unaffected in germination but were impaired in germination after high‐temperature/high‐humidity ageing. Genetic complementation with specifically targeted LEA expression in either mitochondria or chloroplasts revealed that seed longevity support is associated with plastidial, but not mitochondrial, LEA. Light exposure of mature seeds (‘light storage’) reduced longevity, providing a physiological framework for embryo degreening. Our data identify a role for LEA proteins in remodelling seed plastids before maturation drying and highlight LEA‐dependent embryo degreening as a decisive contributor to seed longevity. Zusammenfassung Samen ermöglichen Pflanzenembryonen, lange Zeiträume und extreme Umweltbedingungen zu überdauern. Orthodoxe Samen erlangen während der Reifung und vor dem Eintritt in einen metabolischen Ruhezustand Trocknungstoleranz. Der koordinierte Abbau von Thylakoiden und Chlorophyll führt zur Entgrünung des Embryos, einem charakteristischen Merkmal der Reifung orthodoxer Samen. Obwohl die Entgrünung hormonell reguliert wird, ist unser Verständnis der daran beteiligten molekularen Komponenten und ihrer physiologischen Bedeutung bislang unvollständig. Durch Zufall beobachteten wir unvollständig entgrünte Samen in einer Arabidiopsis thaliana Mutante, der zwei LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) Proteine, LEA42 und LEA48, fehlten. Diese identifizierten wir als die am häufigsten vorkommenden LEA‐Proteine in den Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen. Wir verwendeten lea48xlea42 als Modell für eine beeinträchtigte LEA‐Funktion in Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen. Proteomische und transkriptomische Analysen sowie elektronenmikroskopische Daten deuteten auf einen unvollständigen Abbau der Thylakoide hin. Frisch geerntete lea48xlea42‐Samen zeigten keine Beeinträchtigung der Keimung. Nach Alterung der Samen bei hoher Temperatur und Luftfeuchtigkeit war die Keimfähigkeit jedoch verringert. Die genetische Komplementation durch gezielte LEA‐Expression entweder in Mitochondrien oder Chloroplasten zeigte, dass der Beitrag zur Samenlanglebigkeit mit plastidären, nicht jedoch mit mitochondrialen LEA‐Proteinen verbunden ist. Die Lichtexposition reifer Samen (‘Lichtlagerung’) verringerte ihre Langlebigkeit und liefert damit einen physiologischen Erklärungsrahmen für die Entgrünung des Embryos. Unsere Daten zeigen eine Rolle von LEA‐Proteinen bei der Umstrukturierung von Samenplastiden vor der Austrocknung während der Reifung.…

articles.title: Field generation of triparental sugar beet plants through polyspermy‐induced three‐parent breeding
articles.abstract: Polyspermy, the fertilization of an egg by two sperm cells, can generate viable triparental offspring in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. To explore the potential for three‐parent breeding in a crop species, male‐sterile sugar beet plants were grown alongside genetically distinct pollen donors carrying dominant, traceable selection markers. Progeny carrying genetic signatures from two fathers were identified and subjected to further genetic analysis. The combined detection of paternal markers from two pollen donors and an additional chromosome set confirms the triparental origin of these plants, demonstrating the potential for three‐parent breeding in sugar beet under field conditions.

articles.title: Leaf‐to‐root ROS signaling recruits rhizosphere Bacillus: a synbiotic mechanism for rice adaptability under foliar Cd stress
articles.abstract: Foliar cadmium (Cd) exposure triggers systemic reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling from leaves to roots in rice, accompanied by calcium (Ca2+) responses, increasing root membrane permeability and promoting the exudation of L‐valine (Val) and L‐leucine (Leu). These amino acids enhance chemotaxis and root colonization by beneficial Bacillus strains. The recruited Bacillus promotes leaf lignification, enhances rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress, and reduces grain Cd accumulation. Combining Val and Leu with Bacillus as a synbiotic further strengthens these beneficial effects and improves rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress. Summary In paddy fields near mining sites or transport corridors, elevated foliar cadmium (Cd) exposure is an emerging threat to rice (Oryza sativa) production. While rice recruits beneficial rhizosphere microbes against environmental stress, how this recruitment is coordinated under foliar Cd stress remains elusive. We assessed physiological responses to foliar Cd exposure in 26 rice cultivars and characterized rhizosphere bacterial communities and root exudates in six representative cultivars. Foliar Cd reduced leaf biomass by 6–29% and induced pronounced oxidative stress. In parallel, this foliar stress reshaped the rhizosphere microbiota, with consistent enrichment of Bacillus. This microbial shift was accompanied by increased root exudation of L‐valine and L‐leucine, which was associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and increased root membrane permeability. Crucially, these amino acids promoted chemotaxis and root colonization by the representative Bacillus strains SRS50 and SRS107, selected from 11 candidates among 241 rhizosphere isolates, whereas colonization was reduced in ROS‐deficient mutants. Functionally, application of a ‘synbiotic’ (amino acid‐Bacillus combination) reduced grain Cd concentrations by 40.5–43.3%, associated with Bacillus‐induced leaf lignification. These findings highlight a plant–microbe feedback loop that contributes to rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress.

articles.title: Ten rules for identifying horizontal gene transfers in deep plant phylogenies
articles.abstract: Deep‐level clustering in the GH32 gene family is unsupported and is not robust to the alignment substitution matrix or the rooting method. Summary Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is one of the most intriguing aspects of genome evolution, challenging classical views of vertical inheritance. Growing genome availability across the tree of life offers opportunities to discover HGT, yet recent reanalyses suggest many reported cases may not withstand scrutiny. Detecting ancient transfers is especially difficult, as phylogenetic signal erodes over time and analytical choices strongly shape conclusions. Here we propose 10 practical rules for evaluating HGT in deep plant phylogenies, organised around three themes: genomic foundation, rigorous analytical framework, and biological interpretation. A reliable genomic foundation requires excluding contamination, verifying genomic integration, and avoiding biased taxon sampling. Rigorous phylogenetics is essential, as deep phylogenies are sensitive to alignment parameters, substitution model, rooting strategy, and branch support. We illustrate this with three glycosyl hydrolase families: for GH9 and GH32, analytical choices can eliminate apparent HGT signals entirely, while GH18 shows why complex, multi‐domain families resist confident inference. Finally, HGT signatures demand cautious, biologically plausible interpretation. Recurrent gene duplication, loss, and domain shuffling commonly produce HGT‐like patterns and should always be considered as alternatives. Our rules offer a pragmatic checklist helping authors and reviewers distinguish robust HGT from artefacts, fostering more reliable evidence on HGT in plants.

articles.title: Chirality-Resolved Spectroscopy of Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon States in Multiband ${\mathrm{FeTe}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Se}}_{x}$ Superconductors
articles.abstract: Terahertz magneto-optics is established as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations, providing dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.

articles.abstract: The discovery of directional and robust wave manipulation has become a crucial goal in the field of science and technology. Topological pump, as an efficient form of directed energy transport protected by nontrivial topology, has been intensively studied in condensed matter and materials physics. Co…

articles.title: Electronic Transport in Hexagonal-Boron-Nitride-Encapsulated Graphene Limited by Remote Phonon Scattering
articles.abstract: We study the impact of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) phonons on the electrical resistivity of hBN-encapsulated graphene. While encapsulation yields high-mobility devices, the surrounding hBN itself introduces remote scattering from polar optical phonons, whose role in standard resistivity measuremen…

articles.title: Entangling Ions with Engineered Light Gradients
articles.abstract: A high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate based on engineered light gradients in a trapped-ion chain.

articles.title: Quantum Advantage for Sensing Properties of Classical Fields
articles.abstract: Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.

articles.title: Toward Complete Characterization of Topological Insulators and Superconductors: A Systematic Construction of Topological Invariants Based on Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
articles.abstract: A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.

articles.title: Physics for plays, not for work
articles.abstract: Nilanjan P. Choudhury left physics for a corporate software job, then returned to it for playwriting.

articles.title: An autonomous macrophage-nociceptor mechanosensory relay drives chronic visceral pain
articles.abstract: Visceral pain in ulcerative colitis is conventionally attributed to inflammatory cascades, though whether immune cells directly transduce mechanical cues into nociceptive signals remains unclear. Here, we show that the mechanosensitive channel Piezo1 in tissue-resident CX3CR1 + macrophages directly drives colitis-associated visceral hypersensitivity. Piezo1 triggered calcium influx and nuclear factor κB nuclear translocation that occupied the Ngf promoter to induce nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis. This macrophage-derived NGF remodeled and sensitized the peripheral terminals of TRPV1 + nociceptive afferents in neuroimmune units. Using a minimally inflammatory intracolonic zymosan model, we found that this Piezo1-NGF-TrkA axis functions as a direct mechanosensory relay largely independent of cytokine cascades. Genetic deletion of Piezo1 or Ngf in resident macrophages, or Ntrk1 in TRPV1 + neurons, abolished visceral hyperalgesia in both inflammatory and noninflammatory models. These findings reveal tissue-resident macrophages as autonomous mechanical sensors that establish a direct, parallel pain transmission pathway to sensory nerves during disease.

articles.title: ILC2-derived IL-9 promotes eosinophil-mediated antitumor activity
articles.abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) regulate tissue immunity, yet their roles in tumor control remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined analyses of human sequencing datasets with genetic ablation mouse models and adoptive transfer experiments to identify that glucocorticoid-induced tumor necrosis factor receptor (GITR) engagement on tumor-infiltrating group 2 ILCs (ILC2s) induced activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) and robust interleukin-9 (IL-9) production, exceeding the modest coinduction of IL-5 and IL-13. ILC2-derived IL-9 promoted intratumoral eosinophil accumulation by enhancing survival, tissue retention, and cytotoxicity through tumor-induced IL-9 receptor expression. Eosinophil ablation abolished GITR-mediated tumor control, whereas adoptive eosinophil transfer restored it. This IL-9–eosinophil pathway suppressed tumor growth in the absence of adaptive lymphocytes. In human datasets, IL-9 and eosinophil signatures were associated with favorable prognosis in melanoma and lung adenocarcinoma. These findings define an innate pathway linking ILC2s to eosinophil-mediated tumor immunity and support GITR agonism as a therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Competition for specialty training eases for UK graduates after law change
articles.abstract: Competition for NHS specialty training posts eased substantially for UK graduates in 2026, official data show.This follows new legislation to prioritise UK medical graduates over international medical graduates (IMGs) for posts in response to concerns about increasing competition.1The BMA, which pushed for the law change, welcomed the figures.The NHS figures show that overall there were 39 387 applicants for 10 682 posts across all training levels in 2026, or 3.69 per post.2But this fell to 1.86 per post for the priority applicant group—mostly UK graduates—who benefited from the Medical Training Prioritisation Act, which officially became law in March.Data show that applicants in the priority group—UK and Irish graduates and those from other European Economic Area (EEA) countries with which the UK has an agreement—accounted for around half of all applicants and applications to specialty training in 2026 (19 908 of 39 387).3Priority applicants filled 96% of all core training year...

articles.title: Ebola: Nigeria announces first Bundibugyo case, as numbers continue to rise in Kenya and DRC
articles.abstract: Nigeria has announced its first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), becoming the fifth country to be affected by an outbreak that has left thousands dead.Officials said that the patient is a woman who had travelled from Uganda. She began feeling unwell and sought care at a private clinic in Abuja on 11 October and was confirmed positive for BVD on 20 October.It is the first Ebola case in Nigeria in 12 years.The infected woman is currently in isolation and receiving care, said the World Health Organization, which added that investigations continue to establish the likely source of her infection and reconstruct her full travel and exposure history.1So far, 44 of her contacts have been identified and are now being monitored, the Nigerian Ministry of Health has said.Meanwhile Kenya recorded its first BVD infection earlier this month after a citizen travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through...

articles.title: Five AI tools for prostate cancer screening are recommended by NICE
articles.abstract: Five AI tools that can help identify prostate cancer “more accurately” on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans will be made available to doctors, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has announced.NICE has recommended that the technologies be used in the NHS to help detect prostate cancer on MRI while further evidence on their use and accuracy is generated. The tools “are designed to help radiologists by highlighting areas on a prostate MRI scan where cancer might be present,” it said.NICE concluded that the technologies “have the potential” to improve the accuracy and consistency of prostate MRI interpretation, particularly in settings without specialist expertise. But it added that further evidence was needed to understand how the tools would perform in routine NHS practice.Independent experts, while welcoming the announcement, said that the evidence on AI use must also consider how the algorithms could contribute to overdiagnosis.The technologies will be...

articles.title: Measles: “Stagnant” vaccine coverage has led to global resurgence, analysis finds
articles.abstract: Significant global progress towards eliminating measles has been lost since 2020 because of “stagnation” in global vaccine coverage, a new analysis suggests.1Researchers said that this had led to a resurgence in the disease and that “urgent action” was needed to restore routine immunisation.The study assessed measles incidence, mortality, disability adjusted life years, and vaccine coverage among children under 5 years of age across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023.The researchers found that, from 1990 to 2019, global measles incidence and mortality declined “substantially” by around 80% and 90%, respectively. This reflected “decades of progress” in routine immunisation, surveillance, and outbreak response, the researchers said.But the trajectory reversed after 2020, as incidence and mortality rebounded with 40% and 12% increases, respectively, from 2019 to 2023.The resurgence coincided with covid-19 related disruptions to immunisation programmes, health systems, and global health financing. By 2023 the study estimated 15.6 million measles cases...

Meanwhile, 1 in 10 reception aged children have obesity.“Successive governments have failed to address the scale of the...

articles.title: What happens when there is no duty of care?
articles.abstract: The Court of Appeal has now settled the legal question arising from the tragic death of Sridharan Suresh: the General Medical Council (GMC) does not owe doctors an actionable common law duty of care when exercising its statutory fitness-to-practise functions.1 The judgment is legally important, but it should not be mistaken for an answer to the wider question raised by Suresh’s death.The question is not simply whether the GMC owes a legal duty of care; it is what responsibility a regulator should assume when it exercises powers capable of profoundly affecting the psychological wellbeing, professional identity, and future of the doctor being investigated.This distinction matters because the GMC itself recognises the potential harm. It has previously stated that “the impact of receiving a complaint can be great for doctors” and has introduced personalised contact, a single point of contact, changes to communications, and other measures intended to reduce that impact....

articles.title: [Articles] Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

articles.title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression
articles.abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group
articles.abstract: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC.MethodsMASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete.FindingsBetween Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24).…

Genome-wide human T cell screens: barriers and design
articles.abstract: Liu et al. enabled genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screening of primary human T cells in vivo and identified P2RY8 and GNAS through complementary readouts. We discuss how context shapes perturbation effects, and how readouts guide prioritization, with implications for T cell engineering in solid tumors.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cells: towering ambitions, shaky foundations
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been a feature of stem cell research since the early 1990s. Despite long-standing questions concerning the identity, characteristics, physiological functions, and potential therapeutic uses of these cells, MSC studies are now published more frequently than those of any other stem cell type. Over the past decade, this increase in the MSC literature is attributable almost entirely to publications by scientists in China. Reviewing the history and present state of MSC research, we explore why this might be and propose steps that stakeholders in China and other countries might take to address what has become one of the more perplexing developments in contemporary stem cell research.

articles.title: Dependency grammar remains the simplest theory of grammar: a reply to Fujita
articles.abstract: In the original article [1], I claimed that dependency grammar is the simplest theory of grammar. All theories of grammar have rules for connecting words together to make larger units. In dependency grammar, these connections are directly between words. In phrase structure grammars, there is slightly more structure than in dependency grammar, consisting of nonterminal categories for the connected elements, such as the noun phrase and the verb phrase. I argued that these two alternatives are somewhat interchangeable.

articles.title: Evidence supports constituency-based syntax, movement, and unpronounced elements
articles.abstract: Gibson advocates dependency grammar [1], contrasting it with constituency-based accounts that posit movement and phonologically null (unpronounced) syntactic elements [2,3]. Dependency grammar represents sentence structure through word-to-word relations, whereas constituency-based accounts represent sentence structure by grouping words into larger hierarchical constituents. Movement accounts for cases in which a constituent appears in one position but is interpreted in another. For example, in ‘Who did you call?’, ‘Who’ appears sentence-initially but is interpreted as the object of ‘call’; this is analysed as movement from the object position to the sentence-initial position.

articles.title: An IL-21R STAT hypomorph circumvents functional redundancy in germinal centre responses
articles.abstract: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21REINS) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21REINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.

articles.title: Correction: Targeted degradation of aberrant tau in frontotemporal dementia patient-derived neuronal cell models
Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain
articles.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.

articles.title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI
articles.abstract: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral–caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.

articles.title: Modulation of human dorsal root ganglion neuron excitability by Nav1.7 inhibition
articles.abstract: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.

articles.title: Morphology and ultrastructure of pharyngeal sense organs of Drosophila larvae
articles.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.

articles.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis suppresses protective Th17 responses during infection
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. Here, we identify factors suppressing Th17 responses during primary infection. We demonstrate that the lack of Th17 induction is independent of route and duration. Next, using Tbx21-deficient mice, we show that Mtb drives a Th1 response that is only partially protective and limits Th17 cell production in an IFN-γ-independent manner. We further reveal that the ESX-1 type VII secretion system and lipid phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) suppress Th17 responses. Infection with ESX-1 or PDIM mutants results in significantly increased Th17 T cells and IL-17A cytokine in the lungs, and infection of IL-17A-deficient animals partially restores virulence of ESX-1 and PDIM mutants. Although the ESX-1 secretion system and lipid PDIM elicit type I IFN, which can suppress Th17 differentiation, we find that suppression of Th17 is independent of type I IFN. Instead, ESX-1 and PDIM suppress production of IL-23, a cytokine that promotes Th17 differentiation, in dendritic cells found in mediastinal lymph nodes during Mtb infection. These findings define a new function of the ESX-1 secretion system and PDIM in Mtb virulence, a long-standing question in tuberculosis research.

articles.title: The new paradox of women’s health research
articles.abstract: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women’s health.

articles.title: Disentangling Static and Dynamic Contributions to the Urbach Energy in Mixed Sn–Pb Perovskites
articles.abstract: Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.

articles.title: Electrostatic Contributions of the Extended Environment and Local Catalytic Effects in Bipolar Membranes
articles.abstract: Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.

articles.title: Insoluble π –d -Conjugated Small Molecules Featuring p -Type Ligands Enable All-Organic Dual-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.

articles.title: Low-Cost Iron/Manganese-Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Sustainable Na-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.

articles.title: Three-Dimensionally Fibrillated Inorganic Composite Anion Exchange Membranes for Ampere-Scale Hydrogen Production
articles.abstract: Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.

My Life as a Structural Scientist
articles.abstract: In this autobiography, I describe my childhood and early education and summarize structural biology research in nucleic acids and proteins and my work with the Protein Data Bank.

articles.title: Power Electronics Conversion Systems and Control
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.

articles.title: Assessing the Implementation of the Nonprofit Hospital Community Benefit Program: 15 Years Post–Affordable Care Act
articles.abstract: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 (“Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals”). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.

articles.abstract: Sulfur-assisted oxidative coupling of methane (SOCM) provides a direct route for methane conversion to ethylene over transition-metal sulfides (TMSs), with sulfur-rich surface environments involved in methane activation and ethylene formation....

articles.title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
articles.abstract: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

articles.title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
articles.abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

articles.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
articles.abstract: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

articles.title: Genetic dissection of rapid proteolysis identifies TXNDC15 as a key factor of ERAD and lipid homeostasis
articles.abstract: ER-associated protein degradation is central to organelle homeostasis, yet many regulatory components remain unknown. Liu et al. exploit the rapid turnover of short-lived proteins to identify TXNDC15 as a noncanonical MARCHF6-dependent ERAD factor that links proteostasis to lipid homeostasis, illustrating how rapid proteolysis can uncover hidden metabolic regulatory circuits.

articles.title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3
articles.abstract: Zhang et al. show that gut microbial inositol phosphate metabolism transduces feeding cues into intestinal diurnal rhythms through histone deacetylase 3. This pathway activates PGC-1α and enhances nutrient absorption during feeding, promoting juvenile growth during undernutrition but exacerbating obesity during overnutrition.

articles.title: Targeted lactate depletion via gluconeogenesis by engineered hepatocyte-based micronanorobots for radiosensitization and immune activation
articles.abstract: Fan et al. develop CXCR4-engineered hepatocyte cytoplasts integrated with Au-Pt nanorobots to deplete tumor lactate through gluconeogenesis. Lactate depletion suppresses repair-associated lactylation and impairs MRN-mediated DNA repair, while Au-Pt catalysis amplifies radiation-induced damage. This metabolic remodeling simultaneously alleviates immunosuppression and promotes systemic antitumor immunity.

articles.abstract: The authors introduce a programmable synthetic biology framework for tissue construction from hiPSCs through subtractive multicellular engineering. By selectively removing undesired cells during development via synthetic apoptosis circuits, this approach enhances tissue maturation and refines morphogenesis across organoid and embryoid models.

articles.title: Identical-location electron microscopy for the discovery of heterogeneous catalysts' dynamics at the single-particle level
articles.abstract: Identical-location electron microscopy enables particle-resolved tracking of structural evolution, providing deep insights into catalyst stability and the structure–function relationship beyond what ensemble-averaged analysis can offer.

articles.title: Cu-Based Versatile p-d Bimetallic Catalysts for Efficient CO2 Reduction Reaction via Orbital Matching Mechanism
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Among various electrocatalysts, copper-based materials occupy a central position due to their unique capability for *CO adsorption and dimerization; however, they still face severe challenges, including high overpotentials and limited product selectivity. Orbital engineering, particularly the construction of p-d bimetallic systems through the introduction of p-block metals, has emerged as a pivotal approach to surmounting the performance bottlenecks of Cu-based catalysts. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in copper-based p-d bimetallic catalysts designed via orbital engineering for efficient CO2 reduction reaction. We provide an in-depth discussion on the modulation mechanisms of p-block metals on the performance of Cu active centers from three key dimensions: electronic effects, geometric effects, and microenvironment regulation. Furthermore, we summarize the primary challenges currently facing the field of p-d orbital matching and offer perspectives on the rational design of future CO2 reduction catalytic systems that possess high activity, stability, and energy efficiency, aiming to provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for the large-scale application of green energy conversion technologies.

articles.title: Dual-Dynamic Sacrificial Networks Enable Durable and Reprocessable Epoxidized Natural Rubber Elastomers
articles.abstract: Conventional elastomer networks can provide mechanical stability but offer limited capacity for network rearrangement and reprocessing. In this work, a sulfur-rich oligomeric crosslinker (S-VBGE) was introduced into epoxidized natural rubber (ENR) to construct a filler-free dual-dynamic network containing reversible hydrogen-bonding associations and sulfur-containing dynamic structures. The optimized ENR-SV15 formulation reached a tensile strength of 14.84 MPa and a toughness of 85.07 MJ·m−3. Based on three independent fatigue crack growth measurements, its apparent fatigue threshold was 310 ± 14 J·m−2, compared with 41 ± 1 J·m−2 for ENR-0. Temperature-dependent stress relaxation and reprocessing experiments indicate thermally activated network rearrangement, while variable-temperature FTIR supports the thermal responsiveness of the hydrogen-bonding associations. Together, these results show that balancing reversible associations, sulfur-containing dynamic structures, and network constraints can improve crack growth resistance while retaining solid-state reprocessability in dry ENR elastomers.

articles.title: Understanding the Dynamics of Zinc Deposition/Dissolution Processes in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries by In Operando Electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance with Dissipation
articles.abstract: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. Using a three-electrode configuration under a constant overpotential of ± 100 mV, current density, mass change, and dissipation were simultaneously monitored in real time. A comparison between the measured mass change (ΔMf) and the theoretical Faradaic mass (ΔMq) reveals that both electrolyte anion identity and concentration strongly affect Zn redox behavior. Zn(ClO4)2 promotes the formation of rigid, highly reversible Zn deposits, although accompanied by hydrogen evolution, whereas concentrated Zn(OTf)2 forms viscoelastic interfacial layers, consistent with the accumulation of alkaline byproducts and the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). ZnSO4 exhibits intermediate behavior with improved reversibility at higher concentrations. Complementary analyses of Coulombic efficiency and mass-per-electron (MPE) further show that concentrated Zn(ClO4)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes provide more reversible Zn deposition/dissolution than Zn(OTf)2. Ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations corroborate this picture by resolving the anion-dependent interphase chemistry and the underlying solvation and hydrogen-bond structures, respectively. These findings provide mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent Zn interfacial chemistry and demonstrate the capability of in operando E-QCMD for elucidating Zn redox processes in AZIBs.

articles.title: π-Bridge-Driven Design of Donor-π-Acceptor Organic Crystals for Stable, Long-Wavelength Near-Infrared Nanolasers
articles.abstract: The development of near-infrared (NIR) organic lasers has long been constrained by inefficient excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) and limited electronic delocalization, which restrict both performance and scalability. In this study, we demonstrate that subtle molecular modifications can improve laser properties. By introducing a π-bridge-enhanced donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) architecture in the molecule MDS-DHAQ, we improve molecular planarity and extend π-conjugation. This strategic adjustment is associated with predominantly K*-type emission, consistent with an ESIPT-based four-level lasing scheme. Through self-assembly, MDS-DHAQ molecules spontaneously form well-ordered micro/nanocrystals that serve as the gain medium and resonant cavity for lasing. These self-assembled crystals exhibit single-mode lasing at 940 nm, with a low threshold of 3.8 μJ cm−2 and a linewidth of approximately 0.37 nm. Furthermore, they show a 10% reduction in lasing intensity after 10,000 pump pulses. This work highlights how molecular alterations can tune the physical properties of materials, offering an approach that integrates molecular engineering and self-assembly. The resulting NIR organic lasers have potential applications in integrated photonics and optoelectronics.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.
