Monolayer photonic-crystal manganese halide gel scintillator for full-vision imaging
articles.abstract: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.

articles.title: The camtrapR R package: From data management to interactive ecological analysis of camera trap data
articles.abstract: Camera trapping has become an indispensable tool in wildlife ecology, generating vast datasets that require efficient and robust analytical workflows. The R package camtrapR was originally developed for preparing camera trap data for analysis in external packages and has since become a standard tool for this purpose. The analyses themselves, however, still had to be conducted elsewhere. Here, we present a major update that transforms camtrapR into an end‐to‐end analytical platform that unifies data import, exploration, covariate preparation, activity pattern estimation, occupancy modelling and spatial prediction. All new functionality is available as R functions and through surveyDashboard(), a new code‐free graphical user interface that guides users through the entire analytical pipeline. Data import supports widely used formats, including exports from the Wildlife Insights platform and datasets conforming to the Camtrap DP data standard. Exploratory tools generate species accumulation curves, maps of species detections and activity patterns for up to two species. Covariates can be extracted at camera trap sites from user‐supplied rasters or online sources, providing inputs for model fitting and, as raster layers, for spatial predictions. Users can fit single‐species and community occupancy models, some of the most widely adopted analytical frameworks in wildlife ecology, and map predicted occupancy across space. Community occupancy models are fitted in a Bayesian framework using JAGS or NIMBLE. These hierarchical models estimate species‐ and community‐level responses to environmental predictors and improve inference for rare species. The workflow includes convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for model assessment and produces spatial predictions of species occupancy and species richness. The workflow can be implemented both in code and within the dashboard. By combining a code‐free interface with advanced modelling capabilities, camtrapR now makes robust camera trap data analysis accessible to a wider audience of ecologists, wildlife managers and students. This paper accompanies camtrapR version 3 and serves as the reference for its expanded functionality.

articles.title: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3′UTR shortening in proliferating cells
articles.abstract: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.

articles.title: Independent Major‐Effect Loci and Limited Trait Associations Characterize Warning Colour Variation Across Sexes and Life Stages in the Wood Tiger Moth (Arctia plantaginis)
articles.abstract: Variation in warning colouration is common, despite strong positive frequency‐dependent selection favouring the most common morph and may arise from spatially or temporally variable selection or associations with other traits. We investigated the maintenance of warning colour variation in the wood tiger moth, Arctia plantaginis, which shows sexual dimorphism in colouration: two distinct male morphs controlled by a single locus, and continuous variation in female hindwing colour and larval warning signal size. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 657 individuals from a laboratory stock derived from a wild polymorphic population, we examined the genetic basis of multiple life‐history traits, chemical defence, pheromones and male activity. We specifically tested for associations with male colour and aimed to identify the genetic basis of female and larval colour variation. We detected separate major‐effect loci for female colour and larval signal size, which were different from the male colour locus. Hindwing melanism was the only trait associated with male colour, mapping to a nearby major‐effect locus and showing a link to reduced activity at higher temperatures. Female colour was phenotypically correlated with pheromone amount. However, apart from melanism, none of the traits measured showed an association with any of the loci controlling warning colours and we found no evidence that male colour is part of a ‘supergene’ or complex co‐adapted phenotype. Instead, our results indicate largely independent genetic architectures for warning colours, suggesting that variable selection rather than genetic associations may contribute to the maintenance of colour polymorphisms in this species.

articles.title: Hybrid synchronous triboelectric sensors for roller self-rotation and cage revolution in spherical roller bearings with rolling–sliding mechanism elucidation

Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
articles.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

articles.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

articles.title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease
articles.abstract: Khatri and colleagues assembled a single-cell atlas of 1 million human neutrophils based on the integration of 43 independent single-cell transcriptome datasets to define multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and disease states.

articles.title: A tolerogenic function for gut TFH cells
articles.abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells maintain immunological tolerance, but the cellular niches sustaining them across tissues are poorly defined. Work now identifies T follicular helper cells as a source of IL-2 that supports Treg cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue and promotes intestinal immune homeostasis.

articles.title: IL-2-producing TFH cells sustain Treg cell homeostasis and immune tolerance in the gut
articles.abstract: Ballesteros-Tato and colleagues identify a spatially restricted follicular helper T cell-dependent interleukin-2 niche critical for regulatory T cell stability in gut-associated lymphoid tissues.

articles.title: Spatial confinement promotes germinal center diversity and tempers immunodominance
articles.abstract: Chen et al. examine why germinal centers (GCs) are confined to isolated islands in reactive lymph nodes during an immune response. They find that spatial confinement of GC B cells leads to greater antibody diversity by limiting the exchange and expansion of dominant B cell clones.

articles.abstract: Updates to the Global Burden of Disease Study showed that although global measles incidence and mortality had declined in 1990−2019, its resurgence since 2020 reflects stalled vaccination progress worldwide.

articles.title: Global, regional and national burden of pertussis in 1990–2023: a Global Burden of Disease study
articles.abstract: Updates to the Global Burden of Disease study showed that while global trends in pertussis (whooping cough) declined from 1990 to 2023, the rebound in incidence and mortality since 2020, particularly in high-income regions, reflects stalled vaccination progress worldwide.

articles.title: The need for resilience in global vaccination programs
articles.abstract: New studies of trends in the global burden of measles and pertussis offer a reminder of how much vaccination has achieved and a warning of the need to build more resilient and sustainable vaccination programs.

articles.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
articles.abstract: Tang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

articles.title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
articles.abstract: SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

articles.title: Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
articles.abstract: The breakdown of Hooke’s law marks the onset of nonlinear behaviour: when displacements become large, restoring forces weaken and Hookean proportionality fails. In quantum materials, intense optical excitation can drive the crystal lattice into a similar regime, where established linear relations between light, electrons and phonons no longer hold. Displacive excitation of coherent phonons, the principal mechanism for launching structural motion, typically assumes that lattice-driving forces scale linearly with the photo-excited carrier density. At high excitation, however, this linearity can break down, which fundamentally limits accessible lattice displacements. Here we show that such nonlinear limitations can be surpassed in a sliding ferroelectric by timing, rather than strengthening the optical drive. Time-resolved second-harmonic generation reveals that the interlayer-sliding phonon governing ferroelectricity saturates and even diminishes under single-pulse excitation. By means of first-principles calculations, we attribute this nonlinearity to band-specific electron–phonon coupling that induces competing forces on the lattice. By splitting the optical energy into two well-timed pulses that avoid populating counteracting states, we achieve markedly larger phonon amplitudes at fixed total fluence. The resulting enhanced sliding motion exposes a regime of anharmonic phonon coupling that emerges only far from equilibrium.

articles.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
articles.abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

Helicobacter pylori Infection — Advances, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
articles.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

articles.title: IVUS-Guided PCI in Left Main Coronary Disease
Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren’s Disease
articles.abstract: BackgroundSjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.MethodsWe conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.ResultsOverall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.ConclusionsIn these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

articles.title: Ianalumab in Sjögren’s Disease — A First Step
In Vivo Aquaporin-1 Circular RNA Therapy for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia
