Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs).ObjectiveTo evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations.DesignBenchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective.SettingProduction application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026.ParticipantsNo human participants were involved.MeasurementsCo-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action).ResultsThe rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%).LimitationsSingle prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use.ConclusionThe LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations.Primary funding sourceNone.

articles.title: Projected Effect of 2026 Federal Changes to the Childhood Immunization Schedule on Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infections in the United States
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination.ObjectiveTo project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections.DesignMarkov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection.Data sourcesPublished data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection.Target populationOne-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million).Time horizon20 years.InterventionUniversal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making.Outcome measuresNumbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis.Results of base-case analysisCompared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. These strategies would also increase the number of HBV-susceptible people at year 20 (474 000 and 1 806 000) compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (232 000).Results of sensitivity analysisIn a scenario with lower vaccine coverage (84.5%) and higher HBV prevalence (maternal prevalence of 0.72% and higher risk for horizontal infection), chronic HBV infections would increase to 1700 and 2192, respectively, with the deferred and shared decision-making strategies.LimitationUncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk.ConclusionProposed policy changes for vaccination through shared decision making are projected to result in an 83% increase in childhood HBV infections, and between 50% and 70% of children entering adulthood annually would be susceptible to HBV infection. Policymakers should reimplement recommendations for universal birth-dose vaccination.Primary funding sourceNational Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

articles.title: Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes: Fundamentals, Characterization, Strategies, and Applications
articles.abstract: Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of interface engineering in PeLEDs, beginning with the fundamental principles that govern carrier injection, transport, and recombination at heterojunctions between perovskite emitters and charge-transport layers. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.

articles.title: Tuning Interfacial Electron Transfer for Boosting Electrochemiluminescence: Methods, Mechanisms, and Bioanalytical Applications
articles.abstract: The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. Currently, harnessing diverse nanomaterials has driven significant advances in the development of novel ECL luminophores and the activation of coreactants. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

articles.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk
articles.abstract: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care. We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1 . Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants’ effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case–control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed. Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case–control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants. This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

articles.title: Divergent Spatial and Temporal Sensitivities of Forest Biomass to Climate Challenge Space‐For‐Time Assumptions and Models
articles.abstract: Understanding and projecting forest carbon responses to climate change remains challenging. The widely used space‐for‐time substitution (SFTS) approach assumes that ecological responses along spatial climate gradients can substitute for temporal relationships, yet agreement among spatial, temporal, and mechanistic approaches remains largely unknown. Using global satellite‐derived aboveground biomass (AGB) data, we quantified forest AGB sensitivities to spatial versus temporal climate variability, projected climate‐driven AGB changes under future emission scenarios, and compared results with Earth system models (ESMs). Spatial climate gradients explain substantially more AGB variation than temporal anomalies, with strong divergence across regions and forest ages. ESMs better reproduce spatial sensitivities than temporal ones. Temporal extrapolation generally projects future AGB gains, whereas spatial extrapolation often indicates AGB declines. These contrasts demonstrate that spatial, temporal, and model‐based approaches capture distinct facets of forest–climate coupling, and integrating them can better constrain uncertainty in carbon–climate feedbacks and improve future ecosystem projections.

articles.title: Functional Diversity Responses to Temperature Vary Spatially and With Protection Status in Wintering Waterbird Assemblages
articles.abstract: Wetlands support disproportionately high biodiversity, including waterbirds, which underpin key ecological functions and regulatory services. This has led to efforts to protect these crucial sites, but whether these protections can maintain waterbird assemblages in the face of new threats such as climate change is poorly understood. Here, we calculated functional redundancy and three metrics of functional diversity from over 45,000 waterbird censuses, spanning four decades of rising winter temperatures for 2792 protected and unprotected sites in Europe. We modelled the effect of average winter temperature and the trend over time for each of these metrics. Our results suggest functional diversity generally increased in warmer winters and over time, but redundancy declined, and the effect of temperature varied spatially and between levels of protection. This suggests abundance and distribution shifts due to climate change are altering functional diversity and resilience of waterbird assemblages both inside and outside protected areas across Europe.

articles.title: From sediment pulse to ecological recovery: a nine-year study of benthic macroinvertebrate response to Elwha River dam removal
articles.abstract: Large dam removals are increasingly important river restoration actions, but long-term ecological responses remain poorly understood, especially for removals involving large sediment releases. We evaluated benthic macroinvertebrate (BMI) responses following removal of the Elwha and Glines Canyon dams on the Elwha River, Washington, USA. At the time of removal (2011–2014), these were the largest dams to be dismantled worldwide. Dam removal reconnected over 90% of the watershed to anadromous fish, released more than 20 megatonnes of reservoir sediment downstream, and restored natural sediment and wood transport processes. Using nine years of monitoring data spanning periods before, during, and after dam removal, we quantified changes in BMI density, taxa richness, and community composition across five river sections exposed to different combinations of sediment disturbance, reservoir succession, and fish reintroduction. Sediment release substantially altered downstream physical habitat and was accompanied by pronounced declines in BMI density and richness, particularly downstream of both dams. Density declined by up to 95% during active dam removal but rebounded to near baseline levels within three years after peak sediment transport subsided. In contrast, taxa richness and community composition remained significantly altered three years after dam removal, with persistent reductions particularly evident among Trichoptera and long-lived taxa. Fine sediment was the environmental variable most strongly associated with changes in BMI community structure. Our results demonstrate that large dam removal can cause severe but largely transient reductions in BMI abundance while producing longer-lasting changes in taxonomic diversity and community composition. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between numerical and ecological recovery and suggest that recovery trajectories following large dam removal extend well beyond the period of active sediment release.

articles.title: Period-specific waterbird associations with wetland landscape configuration and InVEST-based habitat quality in Dongting Lake, China
articles.abstract: Seasonal lake wetlands perform multiple ecological functions, including flood regulation, maintenance of land-water ecotonal habitats, and support for migratory waterbirds, and therefore play a critical role in regional biodiversity conservation. However, integrated assessments linking long-term wetland landscape reconfiguration, changes in habitat quality, and waterbird community responses remain scarce. Focusing on the Dongting Lake wetland, this study integrated land-use data, landscape metrics, habitat quality (HQ) and habitat degradation (DEG) estimated with InVEST, and waterbird species richness and community composition. Habitat-waterbird response models were developed using negative binomial generalized linear models and partial permutational multivariate analysis of variance. The results showed that the total wetland area increased from 5,019.03 km2 in 2000 to 5,118.04 km2 in 2020, whereas area of lake decreased by 533.87 km2 and reservoir/pond and marsh increased by 317.70 and 227.41 km2, respectively. For lake, percentage of landscape (PLAND) and largest patch index (LPI) both declined, indicating that wetland change was primarily characterized by internal class replacement and reconfiguration of dominant patches. Over the same period, mean HQ decreased from 0.47827 to 0.45371, whereas mean DEG increased from 0.17985 to 0.19445. Waterbird species richness showed generally weak associations with HQ, DEG, and landscape variables, although wetland LPI exhibited a positive but not significant trend during ER (IRR = 1.3763, FDR q = 0.0632). In contrast, community composition during ER was significantly associated with wetland LPI (semi-partial R2 = 0.1027, permutation p = 0.0078, FDR q = 0.0468). By jointly evaluating wetland landscape configuration, InVEST-based habitat quality, and waterbird response models, this study identified differences in habitat–waterbird associations between two recession periods. These findings provide an evidence base for adaptive management, ecological restoration of river-connected lake wetlands, and conservation of wintering waterbird habitats.

articles.title: Improved use of deep soil water promotes radial growth during drought
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Increasingly frequent seasonal droughts under rapid climate change threaten the growth stability of subtropical mixed forests across the mid‐subtropical monsoon region. In this study, we combined stable hydrogen and oxygen isotope analyses with high‐precision radial growth monitoring to explore how water source use influences the radial growth of four subtropical tree species. Three contrasting functional strategies were identified based on rooting depth and water uptake plasticity. The shallow water‐dependent species (Cupressus funebris Endl.) featured a root system concentrated in the upper soil layer and obtained 38.3% of its water from shallow layers. During the drought period, declining surface soil water availability was accompanied by low stomatal conductance and photosynthetic rates, and the species experienced net stem shrinkage of 1.1 mm. The deep‐rooted species (Michelia maudiae Dunn and Abies fabri Craib) exhibited a dual rooting strategy: Deep taproots accessed stable water in the 80–100 cm soil layer, which contributed 67.2%–75.8% of water uptake during drought, while shallow fine roots captured sporadic rainfall in the upper soil layers. During the drought period, these species maintained relatively high water potentials and positive cumulative radial growth, with annual radial growth 1.9–2.5 times that of C. funebris. The balanced‐strategy species (Liquidambar formosana Hance) displayed a relatively uniform root distribution throughout the soil profile, enabling flexible water acquisition across soil layers and sustaining the highest cumulative radial growth during the drought period. Structural equation models revealed that access to stable water sources, particularly deeper reserves as surface soils dried, sustained radial growth indirectly by maintaining stomatal conductance and photosynthesis. This pathway provides a mechanistic explanation for contrasting drought adaptation among subtropical tree species. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Anthropogenic Effects on Elementomes Across Organisms, Ecosystems, and the Biosphere
articles.abstract: The elemental composition of organisms and ecosystems, termed the “elementome,” fundamentally determines biological function and ecosystem processes. These elemental profiles, historically relatively stable over geological timescales, have been profoundly altered by human activity, especially since the Industrial Revolution, giving rise to a novel “human elementome.” The number and amounts of elements used biologically and nonbiologically by humans, We synthesized multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating this critical shift, characterized by pervasive imbalances in the ratios of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus driven by extensive anthropogenic inputs, together with the unprecedented mobilization of a wide spectrum of elements, from critical raw materials and fossil fuels to novel technological elements such as rare‐earth metals. This shift in the human elementome is therefore at the root of many of the environmental changes observed today, as it profoundly alters the cycling, distribution, and availability of chemical elements across ecosystems. These elemental perturbations have not acted in isolation but have interacted synergistically with physiological stresses induced by elevated concentrations of CO2, warming, and drought, generating complex emergent effects on life. Our findings highlight a rapid transformation of the fundamental elemental makeup of the biosphere driven by humans, with cascading ecological consequences for ecosystem function and species composition globally. This elemental perspective offers a robust framework for understanding and predicting ecosystem responses in the Anthropocene, informing strategies for conserving biodiversity and managing ecosystems.

articles.title: Environmental and human‐related gradients shape the community structure of medium and large terrestrial mammals in a central Amazonian white‐sand Forest
articles.abstract: This novel study examines how environmental and human‐related gradients influence habitat use and the community structure of medium and large terrestrial mammals in Central Amazonian white‐sand forests (campinaranas), one of the naturally rarest and least studied ecosystems in the Amazon region. Using camera traps deployed in RAPELD modules, combined with NMDS ordination and structural equation modelling, we demonstrate that anthropogenic factors, particularly proximity to human settlements, exert stronger effects on mammal assemblages than the environmental gradients evaluated. Abstract Medium‐ and large‐sized terrestrial mammals play key ecological roles in tropical forests; however, the relative importance of environmental filters and anthropogenic disturbances in structuring their assemblages in Amazonian campinarana (white‐sand) ecosystems remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated the influence of these factors on species composition and habitat use by medium‐ and large‐sized terrestrial mammals, as well as by the frugivore–herbivore guild in Amazonian campinarana ecosystems. We used camera traps and structural equation modelling. We recorded 22 species over 4721 camera‐trap days, with assemblages dominated by frugivore–herbivores and by dietary and habitat generalists, such as the common opossum (Didelphis marsupialis). Habitat use by the overall mammal assemblage was higher in areas with lower vegetation height, whereas terrain elevation relative to the nearest drainage (HAND index) had an indirect effect mediated by vegetation structure. In contrast, frugivore–herbivore species showed more selective responses, with higher habitat‐use intensity in areas farther from human influence. Mammal assemblages were predominantly influenced by distance to houses, whereas the composition of the frugivore–herbivore guild was associated with distance to houses and tree height. Our results demonstrate that even low levels of human presence are sufficient to structure mammal assemblages, reinforcing the need for spatially explicit management strategies aimed at conserving the functional integrity of these unique and highly sensitive ecosystems.

articles.title: Human hunters—still poorly understood—likely cannot mimic the roles of disappearing top predators
articles.abstract: We highlight a new paper that asks whether hunters can replace the roles of large carnivores, and argue that more insight is needed into the planet's ‘super predator’—humans. Abstract Research Highlight: Geng, Y., Mammides, C., He, R.‐C., Wang, L., Luo, K., Zhang, Z.‐Y., Wang, B., & Quan, R.‐C. (2026). Human hunters are no substitute for vanishing apex predators. Journal of Animal Ecology, 1–13. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365‐2656.70306. As large carnivores decline and humans rise to become the planet's most influential predator, scant consideration has been given to the functional roles of hunters (and fishers) in ecological communities. In novel, landscape‐scale work, Geng et al. (2026) ask whether hunters can serve similar roles as the predators they are replacing. Camera‐trap records from 400 sites characterized as apex predator‐dominated, hunter‐dominated and predator‐absent were analysed across multiple ecological measures. Apex predator‐dominated sites hosted ~30% more species and nearly 50% greater abundances of mammals. Network measures of prey populations were most robust at apex predator sites and weakest at hunter‐dominated sites. Finally, prey showed up to 2.6 times longer avoidance times following hunter presence. These striking patterns suggest that hunters do not replicate the ecological influence of the area's vanishing predators. Work like this can benefit from much more data about human predators. Specifically, ecologists can confront in careful ways the conceptual, methodological and ethical constraints of studying our own species as predators. Outcomes could include greater knowledge about the ecological influence of the planet's ‘super predator’, the underlying mechanisms, and related insight to apply to mitigation.

articles.title: Megafaunal engineering in the tropical rainforest: African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduce avian species richness but elevate functional diversity
articles.abstract: Our paper investigates the crucial role of African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) on the functioning of rainforest ecosystems, through the lens of bird communities. It reveals that the critically endangered megaherbivores are inextricably linked to survival of another key group imperilled by land‐use change: understory invertivore birds. Abstract African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) are critically endangered ecosystem engineers of African tropical forests. Despite their rapidly declining population trend, little is known of how forest elephants interact with other vertebrate assemblages. To explore this, we studied avian communities within a continuous tropical rainforest on the slopes of Mt. Cameroon. The area's topography allowed us to survey birds in elephant‐grazed primary forest and in adjacent portions that elephants avoid, isolating the effect of megafaunal grazing within an otherwise intact system. We additionally surveyed nearby secondary forests fragmented by human activity, contrasting the disappearance of a single ecosystem engineer against the reshaping of forest by anthropogenic disturbance. We assessed the taxonomic diversity (species richness, Shannon index), functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy), functional redundancy (species overlap in functional space), and composition of functional traits (abundance‐weighted trait averages). Previous research suggested that loss of forest elephants would negatively impact avian assemblages through reduced habitat heterogeneity. In contrast, we show that elephant grazing itself significantly reduced species richness, to levels comparable with heavily disturbed secondary forests. Functional diversity nevertheless increased in both the grazed and secondary forest, but at the cost of functional redundancy: in both of these habitats, the avian assemblages were taxonomically impoverished, yet functionally more dispersed, with some foraging niches negatively affected. The elephant‐grazed forest was dominated by understory and terrestrial invertivores, whereas the ungrazed forest supported frugivores and larger birds. The secondary forest, in turn, harboured a functionally distinct assemblage of open‐habitat species with high dispersal ability and divergent foraging strategies. Together these patterns show that although elephant grazing reduces taxonomic diversity to a degree comparable with anthropogenic disturbance, it reshapes functional composition in fundamentally different ways. The presence of forest elephants facilitates stable populations of forest specialist birds, such as terrestrial invertivores. Conversely, the adverse effects of elephant grazing on frugivores and large birds could be minimized by establishing larger reserves of lightly grazed forest, possibly alongside ungrazed refuges. Overall, our results show that loss of keystone megaherbivores has widespread consequences for other rainforest vertebrates, potentially resulting in a cascading restructuring of key ecosystem functions.

articles.title: The missing metric in ecological studies: Land tenure system of territorial carnivores
articles.abstract: The article provides the first conceptual framework and testable hypotheses of land tenure system in territorial carnivores across various landscape scenarios. The authors synthesise existing literature, identify conceptual and methodological gaps and highlight how tenure strength can inform population stability and responses to environmental change. Abstract Land tenure is a fundamental ecological process in territorial animals; it reflects how individuals establish and maintain access to space and resources. First conceptualised by Hornocker in 1969, it provides an early understanding of population dynamics. However, this critical aspect for interpreting the stability, predictability and exclusivity of a population is rarely evaluated. To date, there has been no clear ecological definition of the land tenure system. To understand this concept, we review more than 50 years of research on territorial carnivores and synthesise how land tenure has been quantified across taxa. We examine how this aspect links population and demographic processes that lead to species conservation in various landscape scenarios. The goal is to develop a standardised approach across species and landscapes to evaluate land tenure by providing a framework and testable hypotheses. As land tenure provides critical insights into the spatial stability of populations and informs conservation planning, its limited integration into ecological studies remains concerning despite advances in population ecology and monitoring technologies. We attempted to build a foundation for future research that aims to measure population stability and species persistence. सारांश इलाके पर कब्ज़ा (लैंड टेन्योर) उन जानवरों के लिए एक बुनियादी पारिस्थितिक प्रक्रिया है जो अपने इलाके की रक्षा करते हैं; यह बताता है कि कैसे कोई जानवर जगह और संसाधनों तक अपनी पहुँच बनाता है और उसे बनाए रखता है। हॉर्नॉकर ने 1969 में सबसे पहले इस अवधारणा को पेश किया था, जिससे जनसंख्या गतिकी की गतिविधियों (पॉपुलेशन डायनामिक्स) को शुरुआती तौर पर समझने में मदद मिलती है। हालाँकि, किसी आबादी की स्थिरता, पूर्वानुमान और विशिष्टता को समझने के लिए इस अहम पहलू का शायद ही कभी मूल्यांकन किया जाता है। अब तक, ‘लैंड टेन्योर सिस्टम’ की कोई स्पष्ट पारिस्थितिक परिभाषा नहीं दी गई है। इस कॉन्सेप्ट को समझने के लिए, हम अपने इलाके पर कब्ज़ा रखने वाले मांसाहारी जानवरों पर पिछले 50 से ज़्यादा सालों की इकोलॉजिकल स्टडीज़ का रिव्यू करते हैं और यह समझते हैं कि अलग‐अलग तरह के जानवरों के लिए लैंड टेन्योर को कैसे मापा गया है। हम यह देखते हैं कि यह पहलू जनसंख्या गतिकी और डेमोग्राफिक प्रक्रियाओं को कैसे जोड़ता है, जिससे अलग‐अलग तरह के लैंडस्केप में प्रजातियों के संरक्षण में मदद मिलती है। इसका मकसद एक ऐसा तरीका विकसित करना है जो अलग‐अलग प्रजातियों और इलाकों में लैंड टेन्योर का मूल्यांकन करने के लिए एक ढांचा और जांचने योग्य परिकल्पनाएं प्रदान करे। चूंकि लैंड टेन्योर आबादी की स्थानिक स्थिरता के बारे में महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी देता है और संरक्षण की योजना बनाने में मदद करता है, इसलिए आबादी की पारिस्थितिकी और निगरानी तकनीकों में प्रगति के बावजूद पारिस्थितिक अध्ययनों में इसका सीमित एकीकरण चिंता का विषय बना हुआ है। हमने भविष्य के शोध के लिए एक आधार बनाने की कोशिश की है जिसका मकसद आबादी की स्थिरता और प्रजातियों के बने रहने को मापना है।

articles.title: Coverage-controlled NH3 selectivity in NO/H2 reactions over Pt and Pd catalysts for passive SCR
Elevated plant colonisation shifts soil microbes towards faster‐growing decomposition‐oriented communities
articles.abstract: Our findings indicate that elevated plant colonisation drives shifts towards faster‐growing, decomposition‐oriented microbial communities. Associations between plant colonists and microbial communities were stronger at the late succession site, even though colonist cover was higher in the early succession site. Practitioners should therefore consider belowground impacts of plant colonisation across all grasslands, and not only where effects on plant community composition are most visible. Abstract Colonisation by previously absent plants is increasing under global environmental change. Colonist establishment can alter plant community composition and could subsequently affect soil microbial communities. Using a 9‐year seed addition experiment, we ask: (i) how do colonists influence plant community composition; and (ii) do these vegetation changes drive shifts in soil prokaryote and fungal communities? We introduced 23 colonist species, divided into ‘fast’ and ‘slow’ resource acquisition strategies, into two grassland sites that differed in successional age and community composition. We manipulated local disturbance and colonist seed additions and examined how site and colonist characteristics influenced microbial community composition. Plant and microbial communities were surveyed 9 years after initial seed addition. Colonist cover was higher in the early succession site. Across both sites, evidence indicated that higher colonist cover led to communities with faster growth strategies, altered belowground resource acquisition strategies, and—at the early succession site—lowered taxonomic diversity. Through these changes in plant community composition, higher colonist cover was associated with less diverse prokaryote communities characterised by elevated metabolic activity and cellular replication, and a higher abundance of fungal saprotrophs. Additional associations between colonists and microbial composition depended on site characteristics and colonist characteristics. Colonist cover was only weakly linked to other microbial functional groups at the early succession site, with no observed links to obligate fungi, despite colonist abundance being highest there. At the late succession site, higher cover of fast‐growing colonists was associated with prokaryote communities exhibiting lower metabolic activity and greater obligate fungal abundance. Also at the late succession site, plots with more colonist seed additions supported higher prokaryote diversity and greater abundance of fungal obligates than unsown plots, regardless of current plant composition. Synthesis: Our findings indicate that elevated plant colonisation drives shifts towards faster‐growing, decomposition‐oriented microbial communities. However, associations between plant colonists and microbial communities were stronger at the late succession site, even though colonist cover was higher in the early succession site. Practitioners should therefore consider belowground impacts of plant colonisation across all grasslands, and not only where effects on plant community composition are most visible.

articles.title: Increasing exotic dominance generates soil microbial legacies that favour exotic over native plants
articles.abstract: Exotic dominance can leave behind soil microbial legacies that favour exotic plants over natives. In a two‐phase greenhouse experiment, increasing exotic dominance enriched arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and progressively enhanced exotic growth, while competition strength remained unchanged. A complementary field survey showed that exotic abundance was positively associated with AMF richness, supporting a potential microbial feedback that reinforces invasion. Abstract Ecosystems worldwide are undergoing a pervasive transition toward exotic‐dominated states, a shift that threatens biodiversity and disrupts key ecosystem functions. Although positive abiotic feedbacks are frequently cited as drivers of these transitions, the microbial mechanisms involved remain poorly understood. In a two‐phase greenhouse experiment, we conditioned soils along a gradient of increasing exotic plant dominance using 10 exotic and 10 native species. We then assessed plant performance on these soil microbial inocula under no, intraspecific and interspecific competition. We found that increasing exotic dominance progressively reshaped soil microbial communities in ways that favoured exotic over native growth, without altering competitive strengths. This growth asymmetry was tightly linked to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF), whose richness increased with exotic dominance and was positively correlated with exotic performance. Complementary field surveys of the same exotic species confirmed a positive correlation between their abundance and AMF richness in natural communities. Synthesis. Our findings demonstrate that increasing dominance of exotic plants can generate microbial legacies that progressively favour exotic plants over native plants. These microbial legacies provide a mechanism linking changes in plant community structure to subsequent competitive interactions and offer a framework for understanding how biotic interactions, particularly those involving soil mutualists, can contribute to the persistence and spread of invasive plants. 中文摘要 全球生态系统正在普遍向外来植物占优势的状态转变，这一转变威胁生物多样性并扰乱关键生态系统功能。尽管正向非生物反馈常被认为是这类生态转变的驱动因素，但其中涉及的微生物机制仍知之甚少。 本研究开展两阶段温室实验，选取10种外来植物和10种本地植物，沿外来植物优势度递增梯度完成土壤驯化处理。随后在无竞争、种内竞争和种间竞争条件下，评估植物在上述土壤微生物接种环境中的生长表现。 研究发现，外来植物优势度的增加会逐步重塑土壤微生物群落结构，形成利于外来植物生长、而非本地植物生长的格局，且不会改变物种竞争强度。这种生长不对称性与丛枝菌根真菌密切相关:丛枝菌根真菌丰富度随外来植物优势度升高而增加，且与外来植物生长表现呈正相关。针对相同外来物种的野外补充调查进一步证实，自然群落中外来植物多度与丛枝菌根真菌丰富度存在显著正相关关系。 综上，外来植物优势度的增加可以形成有利于外来植物而非本土植物的土壤微生物遗留效应，而且这种作用会随外来植物优势度提高而增强。这些遗留效应揭示了植物群落结构变化影响后续竞争关系的潜在机制，并为理解生物相互作用，尤其是土壤互惠生物介导的相互作用，如何促进入侵植物的持续存在和扩散提供了理论框架。

articles.title: Plants regulate the soil biodiversity–ecosystem stability relationship by mediating green‐brown food web coupling: Evidence from a removal experiment
articles.abstract: Collectively, these findings provide direct experimental evidence that plants act as central hubs that reconfigure the biodiversity‐stability relationship by mediating green‐brown food web coupling, and emphasise that maintaining plant integrity is critical for sustaining high multifunctionality and biologically buffered stability under global change. Abstract Direct evidence of how plants regulate soil biodiversity–ecosystem stability relationships remains scarce, as the coupling between aboveground and belowground components makes it methodologically challenging to isolate plant‐mediated effects from the independent role of soil biota. Using a long‐term multifactorial semiarid grassland experiment with plant removal nested within grazing, nitrogen addition and water addition, we directly tested whether weakening plant‐derived green inputs reconfigures the soil biodiversity–ecosystem stability relationship through altered green‐brown food web coupling. By contrasting plant‐present and plant‐removal plots, we found that plants fundamentally reconfigured the biodiversity‐stability relationship. In the coupled state, plant presence shifted ecosystem stability towards biotic regulation: multifunctionality was supported by soil biota richness, while functional stability depended on biotic insurance via soil biota asynchrony and compositional stability. After plant removal, multifunctionality weakened and control shifted towards abiotic factors (soil pH/moisture); the observed increase in calculated stability reflected reduced temporal variability at a lower functional level rather than enhanced ecological resilience. Water availability was the strongest moderator of these plant‐mediated effects, whereas grazing primarily reduced the magnitude of multifunctionality and soil biota richness, and nitrogen addition had comparatively weak effects. Synthesis. Collectively, these findings provide direct experimental evidence that plants act as central hubs that reconfigure the biodiversity‐stability relationship by mediating green‐brown food web coupling, and emphasise that maintaining plant integrity is critical for sustaining high multifunctionality and biologically buffered stability under global change.

articles.title: Predictably context dependent: A 12‐year grassland experiment into plant colonisation
articles.abstract: Context dependence can sometimes seem overwhelming in ecology, but—in this study—trends were largely predictable when we considered how causal drivers and limiting factors likely vary across different ecological conditions. Our study highlights the value of long‐term multifactorial experiments and suggests that the interplay of limiting factors can help predict mechanistic context dependence in plant colonisation. Abstract Context dependence can impede accurate prediction in ecology, including plant colonisation. Although it is well established that ecology is complicated, most studies in ecology focus on one or two factors at a time and most experiments run for less than 3 years. As such, most studies only provide a partial picture, and sometimes those pictures can appear contradictory, leading researchers and practitioners to question what factors are important and when. Using a 12‐year multifactorial grassland seed addition experiment, we tested whether we could accurately predict drivers of sown colonist abundance based on the species, sites and conditions in question. Up to 15 grassland species, divided into resource‐acquisitive (‘fast’) or resource‐conservative (‘slow’) life history groups, were added at two different seed rates, with and without the other colonist group, into grassland plots in Minnesota, USA. The plots represented early, mid and late successional communities, and half of the plots were regularly disturbed. We surveyed sown ‘colonist’ cover six times over 12 years. None of the five factors examined (colonist life history group, colonist group composition, seed rate, community successional age, disturbance—plus time) had a consistent relationship with colonist abundance, but general trends did emerge. Resource‐acquisitive colonists with fast life histories were most successful soon after seed addition while resource‐conservative slow colonists reached peak abundances in later years. Colonist cover was higher in early successional than late successional communities, reflecting soil N limitation in late succession. Physical disturbance facilitated colonisation when soil N was limiting, especially for resource‐acquisitive colonists, but disturbance otherwise impeded colonisation as it exacerbated effects of low soil moisture and reduced microhabitat suitability. When sown together into communities not already limited by resource competition, there was some evidence that fast colonists impeded slow colonists through niche pre‐emption. Synthesis: Context dependence can sometimes seem overwhelming in ecology, but—in this study—trends were largely predictable when we considered how causal drivers and limiting factors likely vary across different ecological conditions. Our study highlights the value of long‐term multifactorial experiments and suggests that the interplay of limiting factors can help predict mechanistic context dependence in plant colonisation.

articles.title: Covalency-driven amorphization in dual-anion-doped Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes enables long-life all-solid-state batteries
articles.abstract: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. This bond-covalency-mediated strategy enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries and provides a general design principle for high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes.

articles.title: Proteome-wide C-degron activity profiling connects conditional regulation of the CTLH E3 ligase complex to ribosome biogenesis
articles.abstract: Exploiting ORFeome libraries with different C-terminal architectures, Grant et al. perform comparative stability profiling to identify a conditionally regulated C-degron pathway governed by the CTLHMuskelin E3 ligase complex. Its substrate AAMP is the human ortholog of yeast Sqt1 and acts similarly as a uL16 chaperone, connecting nutrient status to control of ribosome biogenesis.

articles.title: Regulatable in vivo gene expression via adaptamers
articles.abstract: Bryant et al. develop adaptamers, compact RNA switches that use FDA-approved drugs to control gene expression by co-opting endogenous RNA-editing machinery rather than relying on foreign proteins. In mice, this approach safely tuned a metabolic hormone to reverse obesity, pointing to a simpler path toward programmable, drug-controlled gene therapies.

articles.title: Genome‐Wide Analyses Reveal Spatially Structured Genetic Diversity in Indian Rice Shaped by Ancestry, Geography and Environment
articles.abstract: India is a major centre of rice diversity, where long‐term cultivation across contrasting environments has generated substantial genomic and phenotypic variation. We analysed genome‐wide SNP variation in 313 Indian rice accessions to resolve ancestry structure, regional diversity, spatial genetic processes, environmental associations and haplotype variation at key domestication and adaptation genes. Population structure analyses resolved eight ancestry groups corresponding to indica, aus, aromatic and japonica lineages. Ancestry explained substantially more genomic differentiation than biogeographic regionalization, while there is extensive historical connectivity among lineages and regions. Genetic diversity considerably varied across biogeographic zones. After balanced resampling, the Himalayan region showed the highest standardized allelic diversity and private‐allele richness, whereas the North‐East region retained high observed heterozygosity and broad ancestry representation. Isolation‐by‐distance was weak overall but strongly lineage‐ and region‐dependent. Spatial principal component analysis identified significant ancestry‐independent broad‐scale genetic gradients, demonstrating geography‐influenced structure beyond lineage composition. Redundancy analysis detected significant genome–environment associations (F = 3.07, p = 0.001), with climate explaining more independent genomic variation (2.7%) than soil (0.9%). District‐level tribal population proportion showed only a weak negative association with individual heterozygosity (Spearman ρ = −0.155, p = 0.006), although PTP classes exhibited low‐to‐moderate genetic differentiation. Haplotype analysis revealed strong locus‐specific ancestry and geographic structuring at sd1, Wx, GS3 and DRO1. Together, the results show that Indian rice diversity is a reticulate genomic mosaic shaped by ancestry, geography, historical gene flow and environmental heterogeneity. This study provides a landscape‐genomic framework for conservation and targeted germplasm utilization in breeding programmes.

articles.title: When Hybrids Take an Intermediate Route: Genetic Ancestry Shapes Migration Across a Seabird Contact Zone
articles.abstract: Contact zones, where related taxa breed sympatrically, provide natural laboratories for studying phylogeography and speciation. In migratory species, these systems offer unique opportunities to disentangle the relative roles of genetic and social factors in migratory behaviour. Cory's (Calonectris borealis) and Scopoli's shearwaters (C. diomedea) are closely related long‐distance migrants that breed allopatrically across most of their ranges but occur sympatrically in the Alboran Sea. Here, we tested whether the migratory strategies of these shearwaters are determined primarily by their genetic ancestry or by the social environment of their breeding colony. We used light‐level geolocators to track the annual migration of 50 individuals (127 tracks) from six breeding colonies: four sympatric colonies within the Alboran contact zone and one allopatric colony of each species. We also generated whole‐genome sequencing data for 58 individuals (including all 50 tracked birds) to infer species ancestry and identify hybrids. Most Cory's shearwaters wintered in subtropical Atlantic upwelling systems along the African and South American coasts, whereas most Scopoli's shearwaters wintered in tropical waters off West Africa. The two taxa partially overlapped in the Sahelian upwelling and Angolan waters. Individuals breeding in the contact zone exhibited migration strategies that matched their genomic ancestry rather than the colony's predominant pattern. Most importantly, we identified seven recent hybrids between the two taxa, representing 17.5% of the sampled individuals in the contact zone. These hybrids exhibited intermediate migratory strategies, indicating a strong genetic determination of migratory behaviour. The overlap in wintering areas may increase opportunities for interspecific interactions before arrival at the breeding colonies, potentially promoting hybridisation. Our study demonstrates that migratory strategies are strongly influenced by genetic background in long‐distance migratory seabirds and suggests that weak migratory connectivity among populations facilitates hybridisation in contact zones.

Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
articles.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.

articles.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
articles.abstract: The noncanonical amino acid O-methyl-L-tyrosine is used as a tool to control microbial protein synthesis across diverse plants.

articles.title: Electrolytes that mind bridging the gap
articles.abstract: Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.

articles.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
articles.abstract: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.

articles.title: Genes take control of active matter
articles.abstract: Gene expression reconstituted outside the cell controls the composition and dynamics of cytoskeletal networks, bringing the tools of synthetic biology to active matter and opening a route to genetically programmed biomaterials.

articles.title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In2Se3 for ferroelectric homojunctions
articles.abstract: Stacking-controllable 2D In2Se3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. A 2H/3R homojunction memristor achieves an on/off ratio one order of magnitude higher than that of pure-phase devices, offering opportunities for advanced ferroelectric memory applications.

articles.title: Supramolecular chemical ligation of helical polymers
articles.abstract: Chemical ligation of synthetic polymers is achieved via supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation in a process that does not require thermal activation.

articles.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease
articles.abstract: This study identifies ABCA1 as a driver of dysregulated cholesterol trafficking in Parkinson’s disease, showing that reducing ABCA1 in astrocytes and neurons decreases cholesterol accumulation, α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in mice.

articles.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus
articles.abstract: Sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus arise from two early-diverging lineages, with sensory neurons progressing through shared intermediate states, revealing how thalamic organization emerges during development.

articles.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
articles.abstract: Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

articles.title: Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
articles.abstract: How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

articles.title: Urea reshuffles soil microbial balance
articles.abstract: In this study, Wu and colleagues demonstrate that long-term nitrogen fertilization acidifies soils, altering soil properties and bacterial community composition in Tibetan alpine grasslands.

articles.title: Manipulating dissolved gases with porous liquids
articles.abstract: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids. Here, we reflect on how the porous liquid concept, beyond simply imparting fluidity to a porous solid, provides a promising platform for overcoming long-standing challenges with manipulating dissolved gases.

articles.title: A single amino‐acid switch reprograms ROP6 signaling to drive functional evolution in plants
articles.abstract: A single amino‐acid substitution reprograms ROP6 from PIN stabilization to endocytic degradation. Summary Rho‐related GTPases of plants (ROPs) are evolutionarily conserved molecular switches that typically maintain PIN‐formed proteins at the plasma membrane (PM), yet their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that a single amino‐acid substitution at residue 194 acts as a core determinant, driving the evolutionary split between Brassicaceae and Malvaceae ROP6 orthologs: glycine enforces PM stabilization, whereas alanine licenses endocytic function. In cotton, the Malvaceae‐predominant alanine mutated GhROP6 displays an auxin‐independent manner. The distinct activity is attributed to the recruitment of three GhRIC effectors that directly bind the actin cytoskeleton and promote F‐actin assembly and bundling. The resulting actin reorganization facilitates GhPIN3a internalization and proteolysis, consequently enhancing cotton fiber elongation. Our findings demonstrate that a single amino‐acid change can reprogram ROP signaling and uncover a molecular switch underlying the functional evolution of ROP6 in regulating plant development.

articles.title: Comparative genomics of dark septate endophytes: shedding light on the enigmatic lifestyle and biology of DSEs
articles.abstract: Ancestral lifestyle reconstruction across the phylogeny of the 107 analysed fungal genomes. Summary Dark septate endophytes (DSE) are widespread root‐colonising fungi with poorly understood lifestyle and ecological functions. We investigated their genomic traits, sexual reproduction signatures, carbohydrate‐active enzyme (CAZyme) and secondary metabolites profiles, and tested whether genomic features distinguish DSEs and other endophytes from fungi with other lifestyles. We also reconstructed ancestral states to clarify the evolutionary origins of DSEs. We analysed 107 Ascomycota genomes representing diverse lifestyles, including nine newly sequenced DSE genomes. The dataset allowed us to test whether secreted enzyme profiles differ between fungi colonising roots vs shoots and those associated with grass vs nongrass hosts. DSEs evolved through multiple independent trajectories and diverse lifestyles and show remarkable metabolic diversity. They possess extensive degradative capacities and some of the largest biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) richness among fungi. Despite sharing BGC richness with other endophytes, DSEs form a distinct subgroup with fewer cellulose‐ and more hemicellulose‐targeting enzymes. Genomes also revealed genomic signatures associated with fungi colonising grass vs nongrass hosts and root‐ vs shoot‐associated niches. Our comparative genomics approach highlights how genome‐level data can deepen our understanding of endophytic lifestyle and the biology of the enigmatic DSE fungi.

articles.title: Tropical leaf phenology as a thermoregulation trait: how changes in crown structure modulate thermal dynamics for two dominant Hawaiian trees
articles.abstract: Study site and focal species. Summary Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress. While leaf traits are known to affect heat exchange, how changes in crown structure interact with environmental drivers to regulate canopy thermal dynamics is poorly understood, particularly in tropical forests. In a Hawaiian wet tropical montane forest, we used repeated UAV‐based (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) thermal and LiDAR (light detection and ranging) measurements of sunlit leaves within and across 397 tree crowns of Acacia koa and Metrosideros polymorpha to investigate (1) seasonal and species‐specific variation in crown traits; (2) how crown traits and environmental drivers interact to determine canopy–air temperature differences (Tdiff), within‐crown thermal variability (TcanSD), and maximum leaf temperatures (TcanMAX); and (3) whether crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibit enhanced thermoregulation. All crown traits showed species‐specific seasonal dynamics, with trait–trait and trait–environment interactions shaping thermal metrics differently across species. In M. polymorpha, crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibited lower relative Tdiff, whereas A. koa did not show this buffering effect. These results indicate that canopy thermoregulation emerges from interacting crown traits dynamically reshaped across phenological and seasonal cycles. Seasonal crown dynamics provide partial thermal buffering in some species, highlighting species‐specific pathways of thermal acclimation or vulnerability under climate change.

articles.title: On the future of science and its wise pursuit
articles.abstract: Science’s endless frontier is a changing frontier. It requires a dynamic approach to governance, collaboration, and investment.

articles.title: Originating from nature: a review of the design, fabrication, and applications of cantilever bio-inspired sensors
Modern research group leaders in the biomedical sciences
articles.abstract: Modern-day group leaders are expected to excel not only in scientific research and teaching but also in leadership and in providing a safe and intellectually stimulating environment for the next generation of budding scientists. In this article, we explore the evolution of a modern-day group leader within and beyond the scientific community.

articles.title: Bispecific antibodies in NSCLC: immune reengineering to neutralize adaptive tumor resistance
articles.abstract: Over the past few decades, the emergence of immunotherapy and single-target drugs has brought new promise to the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Yet the high heterogeneity of NSCLC leads to both primary and acquired resistance that neither sequential monotherapy nor empirical combinations can effectively overcome. In contrast to the conventional coadministration of two separate monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) feature a series of molecular engineering designs that confer inherent synergistic antitumor effects. We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.

articles.title: The tumor macroenvironment as cancer metabolism’s next frontier
articles.abstract: The deregulated utilization of nutrients by tumors, first observed over a century ago, is recognized as a hallmark of cancer and continues to be exploited clinically to image neoplastic disease. Despite this historic focus on cancer cells and, more recently, their neighbors, metabolic reprogramming is not limited to the tumor microenvironment. Tumors also have the capacity to rewire the metabolism of cells throughout the body, including those at distant sites, often referred to as the tumor macroenvironment. Alterations in the metabolism of noncancerous tissues outside the local tumor ecosystem are gaining attention, but their origins and consequences remain incompletely defined. A deeper understanding of these changes may reveal previously unrecognized signatures of disease and unexplored opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: The ongoing urgency of diversity science
articles.abstract: Efforts to extinguish DEI provoke questions about the ongoing significance of diversity science. We argue that this evolving context makes such research increasingly pressing, and we pose four questions that this environment both calls for and newly allows research to answer. Such science remains indispensable to society’s capacity to manage social differences.

articles.title: Colloidal ALD Epitaxial Shelling Enhances Stability and Photoluminescence of Blue Perovskite Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.

articles.title: Electrolyte-Derived Chemical Activation Enables Reversible Cathode Chemistry in Magnesium Batteries
articles.abstract: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.

articles.title: Manipulating Li2MnO3-Like Domain Dispersion in Lithium-Rich Layered Oxides Inherited from Precursor
articles.abstract: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

articles.title: Shear-Driven Structural Ordering Enables High Energy Density in Ferroelectric Polymer Capacitors
articles.abstract: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion
articles.abstract: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.

articles.abstract: First-in-class selective chemical targeting of USP32 uncovers its role in endosomal ubiquitin signaling. articles.abstract: Zhang et al. demonstrate that isobavachalcone targets the deubiquitinase OTUB1 to promote PD-L1 ubiquitination and degradation in cancer cells. This regulation enhances T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment to suppress tumor growth.

articles.title: Targeting oncogenic SOX2 condensates suppresses squamous cell carcinoma progression
articles.abstract: Luan et al. reveal that SOX2 condensates promote squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) progression by regulating chromatin organization and oncogene expression. The FDA-approved drug ixazomib selectively disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner, offering an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy with high translational potential.

articles.title: Ligand-protected copper nanoclusters enable room-temperature semihydrogenation of terminal alkynes
articles.abstract: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.

articles.title: Selective upcycling of polyesters to dicarboxylic acids via tandem depolymerization-dehydrogenative oxidation
articles.abstract: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.

articles.title: Artificial photosynthetic cells: bridging chemical energization with biological functionalization
articles.abstract: This review summarizes the bioinspired design principles, core modules, assembly strategies, unique functions, advances, and bottlenecks of artificial photosynthetic cells, and outlines future opportunities for synthetic photobiological systems.

articles.abstract: This review summarizes molecular design strategies for shifting molecular motors from UV to visible and near-infrared operation, with emphasis on recent advances and emerging applications.

ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED. We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%–16%; P <0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33–61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P =0.54). Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing. URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au ; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.
